reason: With only about 30 patients per arm, the trial would need MW-III to nearly double the healing rate against silver sulfadiazine to reach significance, well beyond the effect seen for MEBO-type ointments in earlier controlled trials.
rationale: Sixty-patient pilot against silver sulfadiazine, which heals partial-thickness burns slowly, so a modest advantage for MW-III (a MEBO-type botanical ointment) is plausible, but an earlier randomized trial found MEBO only similar to conventional care. With about 50 healing events the trial needs a hazard ratio near 2 for p<0.05; I expect about 1.2. The sponsor is small and private, registered the trial in 2011, started it in 2022 and is still recruiting, so disclosure by mid-2027 is unlikely and an early statement could be a stop.
evidence: Ang et al. 2001 (MEBO vs conventional burn care)
Wasiak et al. 2013 Cochrane review of burn dressings
Caruso et al. 2006 (Aquacel Ag vs silver sulfadiazine)

assumptions.claim: A randomized trial of 115 patients with partial-thickness burns found healing with MEBO similar to conventional management, with no significant difference.
A Cochrane review found silver sulfadiazine consistently associated with poorer healing than biosynthetic, silver-containing and silicone-coated dressings in superficial and partial-thickness burns.
assumptions.source: Wasiak et al., Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2013, CD002106

assumptions.claim: The trial was first registered in 2011, started in March 2022 and was still recruiting toward 60 patients in October 2026.

reason: The CT-density benefit of augmentation is real but small against between-patient noise, so a weaker-than-RAPID effect or extra noise from 12 years of multi-country scanning could leave the difference short of significance.
rationale: Three earlier randomized trials (Danish-Dutch, EXACTLE, RAPID) each showed slower CT density loss with augmentation, about 0.7-0.9 g/L per year, borderline significant every time. SPARTA has about 113 per arm, three years instead of two, TLC-only densitometry and a double-dose arm, so a RAPID-sized effect gives an expected z near 3. Discounts: 12 years of conduct in 17 countries, scanner changes, COVID-era missed scans, placebo dropout during three years of weekly infusions, and multiplicity across two doses.
evidence: Stockley et al. 2010 pooled CT analysis

assumptions.claim: In RAPID, annual lung density decline at total lung capacity was 1.45 g/L per year with alpha1 proteinase inhibitor versus 2.19 g/L per year with placebo (difference 0.74 g/L per year, p=0.03).
RAPID's combined total lung capacity plus functional residual capacity density endpoint did not reach significance (p=0.06).
A pooled analysis of two randomized trials (119 patients) found lung density fell 2.297 g/L less with augmentation than with placebo (p=0.006).

reason: Patients given radiotherapy plus 30 months of GnRH agonist already have few metastases and many non-cancer deaths, so the added effect of apalutamide on MFS may be near a hazard ratio of 0.8 and miss significance, as in ENZARAD.
rationale: Apalutamide for 30 months added to GnRH agonist plus radiotherapy, against short-course bicalutamide. STAMPEDE showed a large MFS gain from abiraterone in very-high-risk M0 disease, but ENZARAD, the closest analogue, found a hazard ratio near 0.8 that missed significance, with benefit concentrated in node-positive patients. ATLAS is mostly node-negative, counts non-cancer deaths as events, and has run to its 108-month limit with no announced interim success. About 400 events give roughly 50% power at a hazard ratio of 0.8.

assumptions.claim: In high-risk non-metastatic prostate cancer in STAMPEDE, adding abiraterone to ADT gave a metastasis-free survival hazard ratio of 0.53, with 6-year MFS of 82% versus 69%.
ENZARAD reported no statistically significant improvement in metastasis-free survival overall from adding enzalutamide to ADT plus radiotherapy (hazard ratio about 0.8).
In SPARTAN, apalutamide improved metastasis-free survival in non-metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer with a hazard ratio of 0.28.
assumptions.source: Smith et al., N Engl J Med 2018 (SPARTAN)

reason: Completed pediatric study from a sponsor that routinely posts results; posting is expected around the July 2027 due date, with a possible delay certification or late submission the main uncertainty for the 31 August 2027 read.
rationale: Completed in July 2026 by a large sponsor with a consistent record of posting results; a pediatric study with descriptive efficacy outcomes. Results are due on ClinicalTrials.gov by 21 July 2027, and results submitted on time are normally public within about 30 days, so the read date leaves a small margin. A delay certification for a pediatric labeling submission is possible. A completed trial is very unlikely to change status. Outcome wording may be tidied at posting, but a change in substance is unlikely.

reason: Spleen response should be met comfortably, but the second listed primary, 50% symptom-score reduction at week 24, may miss because low-dose ruxolitinib in the control arm improves symptoms and pacritinib's symptom effect has been inconsistent.
rationale: Pacritinib reliably shrinks spleens: SVR35 was 22% vs 3% in PERSIST-2 and 29% vs 3% below 50,000 platelets, so with 271 vs 136 patients the spleen endpoint is very likely met. The record lists a second primary, TSS50 at week 24, and the round's rule needs both. Symptom response was 32% vs 14% for the twice-daily arm in PERSIST-2 but missed in the pooled analysis, and low-dose ruxolitinib in the control arm helps symptoms. Open-label design without crossover should increase control dropouts counted as non-responders. I put TSS50 success near 70-75%.

assumptions.claim: In PERSIST-2, spleen volume reduction of at least 35% at week 24 occurred in 22% of patients on pacritinib 200 mg twice daily versus 3% on best available therapy.
assumptions.source: Mascarenhas et al., JAMA Oncol 2018 (PERSIST-2, NCT02055781)

assumptions.claim: In PERSIST-2, a 50% or greater reduction in total symptom score occurred in 32% on pacritinib 200 mg twice daily versus 14% on best available therapy, while the pooled pacritinib arms (25% vs 14%) did not reach significance.
assumptions.source: Mascarenhas et al., JAMA Oncol 2018 (PERSIST-2, NCT02055781)

assumptions.claim: Among PERSIST-2 patients with platelets below 50 x 10^9/L, 29% on pacritinib 200 mg twice daily versus 3% on best available therapy had a spleen volume reduction of at least 35%.

reason: The BPD benefit rests on a secondary finding from a small phase 2 trial that missed its primary endpoint, so the true reduction in severe BPD or death is probably smaller than the roughly 11 points this trial needs.
rationale: The BPD hypothesis comes from a secondary endpoint (severe BPD 21.3% vs 44.9%, p=0.04) of a 121-infant phase 2 trial that missed its ROP primary; such signals usually shrink. With about 148 per arm and a control rate near 45%, an absolute reduction of about 11 points is needed for significance; I expect about 5. Enrollment took seven years across a sponsor change. A private sponsor is more likely to announce a positive result early, so the probability given early disclosure is above my unconditional 18%.

assumptions.claim: The phase 2 trial of rhIGF-1/rhIGFBP-3 in 121 extremely preterm infants did not meet its primary endpoint of reducing the severity of retinopathy of prematurity.
In that phase 2 trial severe bronchopulmonary dysplasia occurred in 21.3% of treated infants versus 44.9% with standard care (p=0.04), a secondary endpoint.
This trial is open-label, with 295 infants of 23 to 27 weeks gestational age randomized between OHB-607 and standard neonatal care alone.

reason: A four-week exploratory dose-ranging study with patients spread over several dose and age groups has little power against the high placebo response typical of pediatric functional bowel trials, and may report no formal test at all.
rationale: Exploratory four-week dose-ranging study whose stated aim is to explore the therapeutic effect, so a formal significance claim is uncertain. Eluxadoline improved stool consistency in two adult phase 3 trials, so a pharmacodynamic effect on p-BSFS is plausible, but 272 children are split over several dose arms and two age groups, treatment lasts four weeks, and placebo response in pediatric functional bowel trials is high. The adult phase 2 trial did not separate at week 4 for 100 mg. Disclosure will mostly be a registry posting.

assumptions.claim: In two adult phase 3 trials, the composite response over weeks 1-12 with eluxadoline 100 mg twice daily was 25.1% and 29.6%, versus 17.1% and 16.2% with placebo.
assumptions.source: Lembo et al., N Engl J Med 2016 (IBS-3001, IBS-3002)

assumptions.claim: In the adult phase 2 trial, clinical response at week 4 was significantly higher than placebo (5.7%) for eluxadoline 25 mg (12.0%) and 200 mg (13.8%) but not for 100 mg.
The registry record describes the primary objective as exploring the therapeutic effect of eluxadoline in children, with a 4-week treatment period.

reason: The sponsor has limited resources and has been recruiting since 2018, so the trial may stop or never reach its event target; if analysed, adding an HDAC inhibitor to pazopanib is unlikely to give a large PFS gain.
rationale: Small, financially constrained sponsor; the trial started in 2018 and is still recruiting toward 413 patients, so a final PFS analysis by mid-2027 is unlikely and any public statement by then is more likely a stop than a readout. Evidence for the combination is a phase 1b study with a 27% response rate in a small RCC subset; HDAC inhibitor combinations have not succeeded in phase 3 solid-tumour trials, and pazopanib alone is no longer a standard first-line comparator. If analysed, I expect a hazard ratio near 0.85.

assumptions.claim: In the phase 1b study of abexinostat plus pazopanib, the objective response rate was 21% overall and 27% in the renal cell carcinoma subset.
assumptions.source: Aggarwal et al., J Clin Oncol 2017

assumptions.claim: In COMPARZ, median progression-free survival with first-line pazopanib was 8.4 months by independent review.
assumptions.source: Motzer et al., N Engl J Med 2013 (COMPARZ)

assumptions.claim: The trial started in July 2018 and was still listed as recruiting, with a planned enrollment of 413, in October 2026.

reason: Placebo response in adolescent schizophrenia trials is large and variable, and with about 110 patients per arm recruited over seven years across many countries a 5-6 point PANSS difference could miss significance.
rationale: Cariprazine separated from placebo in three adult 6-week trials (differences about 6-10 PANSS points), and most atypical antipsychotics have succeeded in adolescent schizophrenia trials (aripiprazole, lurasidone, quetiapine, risperidone, paliperidone; not asenapine or ziprasidone). The likely design is two fixed doses versus placebo with about 110 per arm, giving roughly 60% power for a 6-point difference with SD 19. Risks: rising placebo response in adolescents, a low dose arm, and seven years of recruitment across Russia, Ukraine and Latin America with possible data-quality problems.

assumptions.claim: In the 6-week adolescent schizophrenia trial of aripiprazole, PANSS total fell by 26.7 and 28.6 points with 10 mg and 30 mg versus 21.2 with placebo, both doses significant.
assumptions.source: Findling et al., Am J Psychiatry 2008

assumptions.claim: In the 6-week adolescent schizophrenia trial of lurasidone, PANSS total fell by 18.6 and 18.3 points with 40 and 80 mg per day versus 10.5 with placebo.
assumptions.source: Goldman et al., J Child Adolesc Psychopharmacol 2017

assumptions.claim: Cariprazine was superior to placebo on PANSS total change at week 6 in three adult acute schizophrenia trials.
assumptions.source: Durgam et al. 2014; Durgam et al. 2015; Kane et al. 2015

reason: Ipilimumab's incremental benefit over nivolumab alone is probably modest (hazard ratio about 0.85, about 10 points of response), too small for about 440 patients to show on both PFS and response rate.
rationale: No randomized data isolate ipilimumab's contribution in RCC. Cross-trial comparisons suggest about 40% vs 30% response and a PFS hazard ratio around 0.85 (CheckMate 067 in melanoma gave about 0.74-0.79 with a higher ipilimumab dose). With about 300 events power for PFS is under 50%, and the record lists ORR as a second primary that the round's rule also requires. Enrollment finished years ago with no public result, which hints that any earlier analysis was not clearly positive. Disclosure before mid-2027 is unlikely.

assumptions.claim: In intermediate- or poor-risk patients in CheckMate 214, nivolumab plus ipilimumab gave an objective response rate of 42% and median PFS of 11.6 months, versus 27% and 8.4 months with sunitinib (PFS hazard ratio 0.82, not significant at the prespecified threshold).
assumptions.source: Motzer et al., N Engl J Med 2018 (CheckMate 214)

assumptions.claim: First-line nivolumab monotherapy in clear cell RCC gave an objective response rate of 34.1% and median PFS of 8.3 months.
assumptions.source: Atkins et al., J Clin Oncol 2022 (HCRN GU16-260)

assumptions.claim: In CheckMate 067 in melanoma, the exploratory PFS hazard ratio for nivolumab plus ipilimumab versus nivolumab alone was 0.74.
assumptions.source: Larkin et al., N Engl J Med 2015 (CheckMate 067)

reason: Last 144-week visits fall around the registered October 2026 date, so the record should move to completed, with results posted near the 12-month deadline, after the read date.
rationale: Dose-comparison post-marketing study with enrolment complete and both completion dates registered for October 2026, so an orderly close is likely; termination would need a sponsor decision, possible after the ESSENCE miss and the 2025 restructuring. Results fall due about October 2027 and industry sponsors usually submit near the deadline, so posting by 31 August 2027 is unlikely. Three registered primary outcomes, one tied to a conditional interim analysis, leave some room for restructuring when results are prepared.

reason: Dropouts over six months and a wider between-patient spread in Kt/V than planned could leave the confidence interval crossing the non-inferiority margin even if XyloCore truly matches glucose solutions.
rationale: Non-inferiority on total weekly Kt/V urea is a forgiving target: both arms are prescribed to keep Kt/V above 1.7, urea clearance follows drained volume, and the 10-patient FIRST study showed adequacy maintained on XyloCore. 85 per arm fits a margin near 0.25 with SD 0.5. The trial was still recruiting two months before its registered completion, so a public result by June 2027 is unlikely and part of that probability is an unexplained stop, which lowers the conditional p_met below the roughly 0.75 I give a completed trial.
evidence: FIRST study of XyloCore (Rago et al., Toxins 2021)
ELIXIR rationale and design paper (Bonomini et al., Perit Dial Int 2025)
L-carnitine peritoneal dialysis solution trial (Bonomini et al., AJKD 2013)

assumptions.claim: The FIRST phase 2 study treated 10 CAPD patients with XyloCore for 4 weeks and reported it well tolerated, with dialysis adequacy (Kt/V) maintained.
The ELIXIR protocol defines the primary objective as non-inferiority of XyloCore to glucose-only solutions on total weekly Kt/V urea at 6 months.
assumptions.source: Bonomini et al., ELIXIR rationale and design, Peritoneal Dialysis International 2025; NCT03994471

reason: Enrolment closed at 58 and both completion dates are registered for October 2026, so the record should move to completed, with results posted about a year later, after the read date.
rationale: Open-label paediatric study with a descriptive week-12 PediACR30 endpoint; enrolment closed at 58 and both completion dates are registered for October 2026, so an orderly close is likely. Lilly normally submits results close to 12 months after primary completion, which would fall after the 31 August 2027 read date unless the actual completion was earlier than registered. Lilly rarely alters registered primary outcomes, and a single week-12 responder measure leaves little to restructure.

reason: A case-driven analysis on roughly 20 to 30 oral infections leaves little room if efficacy in the mouth is nearer 65% than 85%, for instance through reactivated latent infection.
rationale: HPV vaccines have shown about 90% efficacy against oral infection wherever it has been measured (Costa Rica Vaccine Trial, ACTG A5298), and the per-protocol analysis excludes men already infected. The trial is case-driven with a small case target, so a true efficacy near 85% gives a clear split, while efficacy near 65%, possible if latent infections reactivate or oral-rinse PCR is noisy, would leave it borderline. Primary completion is January 2027; Merck is more likely to present at a congress or post results later in 2027 than to speak by June.
evidence: Costa Rica Vaccine Trial oral HPV analysis (Herrero et al., 2013)
V503-049 design paper (Giuliano et al., Contemp Clin Trials 2022)
NHANES oral HPV by vaccination status (Chaturvedi et al., 2018)

assumptions.claim: Four years after vaccination, the bivalent HPV vaccine showed 93% efficacy against prevalent oral HPV16/18 infection in the Costa Rica Vaccine Trial.
assumptions.source: Herrero et al., PLoS One 2013 (Costa Rica Vaccine Trial)

assumptions.claim: In ACTG A5298, quadrivalent HPV vaccine efficacy against persistent oral HPV infection in HIV-infected adults aged 27 or older was 88%.
assumptions.source: Wilkin et al., Clin Infect Dis 2018 (ACTG A5298)

assumptions.claim: The V503-049 design is case-driven, with efficacy analysed once at least 20 primary endpoint cases have accrued.
assumptions.source: Giuliano et al., Contemp Clin Trials 2022 (design paper for NCT04199689)

reason: Adding a PD-1 inhibitor to concurrent chemoradiotherapy has usually produced hazard ratios of 0.8 to 0.9, too small for a 520-patient trial to detect.
rationale: Checkpoint inhibitors given with chemoradiotherapy have mostly failed in phase 3 (KEYNOTE-412, JAVELIN Head and Neck 100, PACIFIC-2), with KEYNOTE-A18 in cervical cancer the main exception. Bladder cancer does respond to PD-1 blockade in the curative setting (CheckMate 274, NIAGARA), which lifts the prior above the class rate. No early efficacy stop has been announced after more than six years, which argues against a large effect. I expect a hazard ratio near 0.85 with about 250 events, which needs roughly 0.78 or better to reach significance.

assumptions.claim: KEYNOTE-A18 showed that pembrolizumab added to chemoradiotherapy improved progression-free survival in high-risk locally advanced cervical cancer, with a hazard ratio of 0.70.
KEYNOTE-412 found no significant improvement in event-free survival from adding pembrolizumab to chemoradiotherapy in locally advanced head and neck cancer (hazard ratio 0.83).
In BC2001, two-year locoregional disease-free survival with chemoradiotherapy for muscle-invasive bladder cancer was 67%.
assumptions.source: James et al., N Engl J Med 2012 (BC2001)

reason: Diacerein has no convincing structural effect in the knee, and any true slowing of cartilage loss is likely too small to show in 128 patients, let alone on all four primary outcomes.
rationale: Evidence that diacerein slows structural damage is thin: ECHODIAH showed a modest effect on hip joint-space narrowing over three years, while a one-year knee trial found none, and IL-1 blockers have failed as disease modifiers. With 64 per arm, two years of dropout and MRI cartilage volume change that varies widely between patients, power is low. The record lists four primary outcomes, all of which must be met under the round's rules. A single-site sponsor-run study is unlikely to publish by June 2027.
evidence: Pham et al., Ann Rheum Dis 2004
Cochrane review of diacerein for osteoarthritis (Fidelix et al., 2014)

assumptions.claim: In ECHODIAH, three years of diacerein in hip osteoarthritis lowered the share of patients with joint-space loss of at least 0.5 mm to 50.7%, against 60.4% on placebo.
A one-year randomised trial in knee osteoarthritis found no effect of diacerein on joint-space narrowing compared with placebo.
assumptions.source: Pham et al., Ann Rheum Dis 2004

reason: With 50 patients per arm, the modest symptom and medication benefit usual for mite immunotherapy is unlikely to reach significance, and a slow trial may stop before reporting.
rationale: House dust mite immunotherapy gives modest symptom-medication benefits, typically a 15-20% relative reduction, and 50 patients per arm gives low power even with two active doses each able to win. The phase 2 programme with mannan-conjugated mite allergoids rested on nasal provocation, not field symptom scores. The trial has run since 2020 and is still listed as recruiting, with 12 months of treatment per patient, so a result by June 2027 is unlikely; a stop without explanation makes up much of the small chance of a public outcome, which pulls the conditional probability down.
evidence: MM09 phase 2 dose-finding trial (Nieto et al., Allergy 2022)
MT-06 house dust mite SLIT tablet trial (Demoly et al., 2016)
P001 house dust mite SLIT tablet trial (Nolte et al., 2016)

assumptions.claim: The phase 2 dose-finding trial of mannan-conjugated mite allergoids used nasal provocation testing as its primary efficacy measure and found improvement at the higher doses by the subcutaneous and sublingual routes.
In the MT-06 trial of the house dust mite SLIT tablet, the total combined rhinitis score was about 16-18% lower than on placebo.
assumptions.source: Demoly et al., J Allergy Clin Immunol 2016 (MT-06)

reason: The benefit of BTK inhibition with R-CHOP seen in PHOENIX was confined to younger patients and particular genetic subtypes, so an all non-GCB population up to age 75 dilutes it.
rationale: PHOENIX tested the same idea with ibrutinib and failed overall (EFS hazard ratio 0.93), with benefit confined to patients under 60. ESCALADE enrols up to age 75, which dilutes the group that benefited, and most R-CHOP add-on trials in DLBCL have been negative. No early efficacy stop has been announced after six years. Acalabrutinib is better tolerated than ibrutinib, so R-CHOP delivery should hold up. I expect a hazard ratio near 0.86 on about 185 events, short of the roughly 0.75 needed.
evidence: Wilson et al., Cancer Cell 2021 (PHOENIX genetic subtypes)

assumptions.claim: In PHOENIX, ibrutinib plus R-CHOP did not improve event-free survival in non-GCB DLBCL overall (hazard ratio 0.934) but did in patients younger than 60 (hazard ratio 0.579).
assumptions.source: Younes et al., J Clin Oncol 2019 (PHOENIX)

assumptions.claim: In POLARIX, two-year progression-free survival in the R-CHOP control arm was 70.2%.
assumptions.source: Tilly et al., N Engl J Med 2022 (POLARIX)

assumptions.claim: In ROBUST, adding lenalidomide to R-CHOP did not significantly improve progression-free survival in ABC-type DLBCL (hazard ratio 0.85).
assumptions.source: Nowakowski et al., J Clin Oncol 2021 (ROBUST)

reason: Randomisation ended at about 54 patients, so even a hazard ratio like SOLAR-1's 0.65 would leave the confidence interval crossing 1.
rationale: SOLAR-1 gave a PFS hazard ratio of 0.65 in the PIK3CA-mutant cohort, and a similar true effect is plausible in Chinese patients. But randomisation stopped near 54 patients against a plan of 120, so with about 44 events an observed hazard ratio below roughly 0.56 is needed for two-sided significance, which a true 0.70 delivers about one time in four. A lenient bridging criterion would raise that. Results will most likely appear through registry posting during 2027, and a small share of early public outcomes would be a stop.

assumptions.claim: In the PIK3CA-mutant cohort of SOLAR-1, median progression-free survival was 11.0 months with alpelisib plus fulvestrant and 5.7 months with placebo plus fulvestrant (hazard ratio 0.65).
assumptions.source: Andre et al., N Engl J Med 2019 (SOLAR-1)

assumptions.claim: In SOLAR-1, alpelisib was permanently stopped for adverse events in 25% of patients, against 4.2% stopping placebo.
assumptions.source: Andre et al., N Engl J Med 2019 (SOLAR-1)

reason: The survival effect of arginine deprivation in unselected glioblastoma is probably modest, well short of the hazard ratio near 0.6 that a 100-patient trial needs.
rationale: Overall survival in a 100-patient phase 2 needs an observed hazard ratio near 0.62 or better with about 70 deaths, and almost no agent added to radiotherapy and temozolomide has improved survival in newly diagnosed glioblastoma. Arginine deprivation has a rationale in ASS1-deficient tumours and ADI-PEG 20 lengthened survival in mesothelioma (ATOMIC-meso, hazard ratio 0.71), but glioblastoma evidence is limited to a small single-arm phase 1b. I expect a hazard ratio near 0.86. Polaris, a listed company, should disclose topline results within months of the February 2027 completion.
evidence: Stupp et al., N Engl J Med 2005
Phase 1b portion of NCT04587830 (ADI-PEG 20 plus radiotherapy and temozolomide)

assumptions.claim: Median overall survival with radiotherapy plus temozolomide in newly diagnosed glioblastoma was 14.6 months in the EORTC-NCIC trial.
assumptions.source: Stupp et al., N Engl J Med 2005

assumptions.claim: In ATOMIC-meso, ADI-PEG 20 plus chemotherapy gave a median overall survival of 9.3 months against 7.7 months with placebo plus chemotherapy in nonepithelioid mesothelioma (hazard ratio 0.71).

reason: The primary analysis is confined to patients with baseline CNS metastases (perhaps 80-100 of 217, about 60-70 events), so only a large effect (hazard ratio near 0.6 or better) reaches significance, while cross-trial data suggest entrectinib's PFS edge over crizotinib in these patients is moderate.
rationale: Entrectinib and crizotinib have similar systemic activity in ROS1 NSCLC; entrectinib's advantage is CNS penetration. Cross-trial, PFS with baseline CNS disease was 13.6 months on entrectinib (integrated analysis) versus about 10 months on crizotinib (OO12-01), implying a hazard ratio near 0.7. The primary analysis uses only the CNS subgroup of a 217-patient trial, perhaps 60-70 events, giving roughly 35% power at that effect. Frequent CNS-first progression on crizotinib and Roche's choice of this population argue for a larger effect. Positive results would reach congresses sooner.
evidence: Drilon et al., Lancet Oncol 2020 (entrectinib ROS1 integrated analysis: ALKA-372-001, STARTRK-1, STARTRK-2)
Wu et al., J Clin Oncol 2018 (crizotinib East Asian ROS1 phase 2, OO12-01)
PROFILE 1001 ROS1 cohort (Shaw et al., 2014 and 2019 update)
Patil et al., J Thorac Oncol 2018 (CNS progression on crizotinib in ROS1 NSCLC)

assumptions.claim: In the integrated analysis of entrectinib in ROS1 fusion-positive NSCLC, median PFS was 13.6 months in patients with baseline CNS disease and 26.3 months in those without.
assumptions.source: Drilon et al., Lancet Oncol 2020 (ALKA-372-001, STARTRK-1, STARTRK-2), PMID 31838015

assumptions.claim: In the East Asian phase 2 trial of crizotinib in ROS1-positive NSCLC, median PFS was 15.9 months overall and 10.2 months in patients with brain metastases at baseline.
assumptions.source: Wu et al., J Clin Oncol 2018 (OO12-01, NCT01945021)

assumptions.claim: The CNS was the first and sole site of progression in about 47% of ROS1-positive NSCLC patients treated with crizotinib.
assumptions.source: Patil et al., J Thorac Oncol 2018

reason: Adjuvant PD-(L)1 plus anti-VEGF therapy delays early recurrence, but the benefit faded with follow-up in IMbrave050; a mature final analysis here may give a hazard ratio near 0.8-0.85 that misses significance.
rationale: Camrelizumab plus rivoceranib is active in advanced HCC (CARES-310) and improved event-free survival perioperatively (CARES-009, HR 0.59). But the RFS gain from adjuvant atezolizumab-bevacizumab in IMbrave050 (HR 0.72 at interim) faded to about 0.90 with longer follow-up, and I know of no announced interim success for this 687-patient trial, which points to a mature analysis with a diluted effect. Unconditional success is about one in three; conditioning on a public result by mid-2027 raises it, because Hengrui presents positive phase 3 data promptly and seldom publicises failures.
evidence: Wang et al., Nat Med 2024 (adjuvant sintilimab in HCC with microvascular invasion)

assumptions.claim: In IMbrave050, adjuvant atezolizumab plus bevacizumab gave an RFS hazard ratio of 0.72 at the first interim analysis, which attenuated to about 0.90 at the updated analysis with longer follow-up.
assumptions.source: IMbrave050 (NCT04102098): Qin et al., Lancet 2023; updated analysis ESMO 2024

assumptions.claim: In CARES-009, perioperative camrelizumab plus rivoceranib improved event-free survival versus surgery alone (median 42.1 vs 19.4 months, HR 0.59).
In CARES-310, about 24% of patients on camrelizumab plus rivoceranib discontinued any study treatment because of treatment-related adverse events.

reason: Fully enrolled Roche phase 3b with fixed visit schedules should finish on its registered date, run to completion, and post results about a year after primary completion, which is after the August 2027 read date.
rationale: Enrolment is complete (451) and the remaining work is scheduled visits, so the day-specific completion date of 4 February 2027 is unlikely to slip by more than 90 days. Roche rarely stops fully enrolled trials, and the port delivery system returned to use after the 2022 recall. Roche usually posts results close to 12 months after primary completion, so posting by 31 August 2027 is unlikely. The primary outcome (BCVA change averaged over weeks 68 and 72) is settled.

reason: SV2A ligands have only modest anti-absence efficacy (levetiracetam 24% vs 5% seizure-free at 2 weeks, not significant), and seizure freedom on a 24-hour EEG with hyperventilation is a strict bar, so brivaracetam's responder rate may be too low to separate from placebo in about 150 patients.
rationale: Brivaracetam is an SV2A ligand like levetiracetam, which gave 23.7% versus 4.8% two-week seizure freedom in absence epilepsy (Fattore 2011; p=0.08, n=59). A similar true difference in about 150 patients gives roughly 80% power, but seizure freedom on a 24-hour EEG is stricter and brivaracetam's absence efficacy is unproven, so true rates of 10-25% are plausible. The trial ran to completion through its adaptive dose-finding stage rather than stopping, a mildly favourable sign. Placebo response should be very low in untreated patients with frequent seizures.
evidence: Fattore et al., Epilepsia 2011 (levetiracetam in childhood and juvenile absence epilepsy)
Glauser et al., N Engl J Med 2010 (Childhood Absence Epilepsy trial, NCT00088452)
Kasteleijn-Nolst Trenite et al., Neurology 2007 (brivaracetam and photoparoxysmal EEG response)

assumptions.claim: In a double-blind placebo-controlled trial of levetiracetam in newly diagnosed childhood or juvenile absence epilepsy, 23.7% of levetiracetam patients and 4.8% of placebo patients were seizure-free responders after 2 weeks (p=0.08).
In the Childhood Absence Epilepsy trial, 16-week freedom-from-failure rates were 53% with ethosuximide, 58% with valproate and 29% with lamotrigine.
assumptions.source: Glauser et al., N Engl J Med 2010 (NCT00088452)

reason: Small France-only phase 2 from a Korean sponsor with dosing finished: likely to run to its end without stopping, with no results posted on ClinicalTrials.gov by August 2027 and no change to its safety primary outcome.
rationale: The trial is active, not recruiting, with 43 patients and its primary completion date already passed, so only follow-up remains and a stop is unlikely. It has no US sites and Il-Yang has little history of posting results on ClinicalTrials.gov, so posting by 31 August 2027 is improbable. A single safety primary outcome (adverse events over 12 months) is unlikely to be changed in substance this late.

reason: A slowly enrolling open-label phase 2 with about 37 patients per arm and an overall-survival endpoint has little power, pembrolizumab is inactive in MSS colorectal cancer, and anything public by mid-2027 is more likely an interim descriptive report or a stop than a formally met primary endpoint.
rationale: Teclison's randomized mCRC cohort is small (roughly 74 patients), open-label, at 3 sites and still recruiting after 5.5 years, so a formal overall-survival readout by June 2027 is improbable. PD-1 blockade alone is inactive in MSS mCRC and liver metastases blunt immunotherapy; the case for hypoxia-activated tirapazamine embolization rests on small single-arm data. Anything public by the deadline is likely interim or descriptive, which counts as not met. Control survival on TAS-102 or regorafenib should be about 7-10 months.
evidence: KEYNOTE-016 (Le et al., N Engl J Med 2015)

assumptions.claim: In RECOURSE, TAS-102 gave a median overall survival of 7.1 months versus 5.3 months with placebo in refractory metastatic colorectal cancer.
assumptions.source: Mayer et al., N Engl J Med 2015 (RECOURSE)

assumptions.claim: In LEAP-017, the regorafenib or TAS-102 control arm had a median overall survival of 9.3 months in previously treated non-MSI-H metastatic colorectal cancer.
assumptions.source: LEAP-017 (NCT04776148): Kawazoe et al., J Clin Oncol 2024

assumptions.claim: Pembrolizumab produced no objective responses in mismatch-repair-proficient colorectal cancer.
assumptions.source: Le et al., N Engl J Med 2015 (KEYNOTE-016)

reason: Non-inferiority could fail if a subset of gene-therapy eyes loses vision after subretinal surgery or delayed rescue injections, pulling the mean 2-3 letters below monthly ranibizumab and the confidence bound past the margin.
rationale: BCVA non-inferiority trials in previously treated nAMD usually succeed when rescue anti-VEGF is allowed, as here. Subretinal RGX-314 gave stable vision with far fewer injections in phase 1/2a and in the phase 2 bridging study at the pivotal doses. With about 210 per arm and SD near 11-12 letters, the confidence half-width is about 2.2 letters, so a likely 4.5-letter margin tolerates a true deficit of 1-2 letters, and either dose can succeed. Risks are surgical complications, pigmentary changes and undertreatment against monthly ranibizumab. Topline is expected around the turn of 2026/27.
evidence: NCT03066258 (subretinal RGX-314 phase 1/2a; Campochiaro et al., Lancet 2024)
Subretinal RGX-314 phase 2 pharmacodynamic bridging study, 2022-2023

assumptions.claim: In Archway, the port delivery system with ranibizumab was non-inferior to monthly ranibizumab on BCVA change averaged over weeks 36 and 40 (+0.2 vs +0.5 letters; difference -0.3).
Archway's pre-specified non-inferiority margin for BCVA change against monthly ranibizumab was 4.5 ETDRS letters.
In the phase 1/2a trial of subretinal RGX-314, mean BCVA change at 2 years was +14 letters in cohort 3 and +1 letter in cohort 4.

reason: Placebo response on the CDRS-R in pediatric bipolar depression is large and variable (quetiapine XR failed for this reason) and cariprazine's adult effect is modest, so a 2-3 point difference may not reach significance.
rationale: Cariprazine's adult bipolar depression effect is modest (MADRS difference about 2.5 points, effect size near 0.3, one of four trials negative). Pediatric precedents split: lurasidone succeeded (CDRS-R difference -5.7) while quetiapine XR failed against a large placebo response. With 190 per arm and SD about 13.5, significance needs roughly a 2.8-point difference; I expect about 2.3. Flexible dosing with escalation for poor responders helps slightly. The trial is still recruiting after 5.5 years, so a result by mid-2027 is unlikely and completion will probably slip.
evidence: DelBello et al., J Am Acad Child Adolesc Psychiatry 2017 (lurasidone in pediatric bipolar depression)
Findling et al., J Child Adolesc Psychopharmacol 2014 (quetiapine XR in pediatric bipolar depression)
Detke et al., J Am Acad Child Adolesc Psychiatry 2015 (olanzapine/fluoxetine in pediatric bipolar depression)
Earley et al., Am J Psychiatry 2019 (cariprazine RGH-MD-54)
Durgam et al., Am J Psychiatry 2016 (cariprazine RGH-MD-56)

assumptions.claim: In pediatric bipolar depression, lurasidone reduced the CDRS-R total score by 21.0 points versus 15.3 with placebo at week 6 (difference -5.7).
assumptions.source: DelBello et al., J Am Acad Child Adolesc Psychiatry 2017

assumptions.claim: Quetiapine XR did not separate from placebo in pediatric bipolar depression (CDRS-R change -29.6 vs -27.3 at week 8).
assumptions.source: Findling et al., J Child Adolesc Psychopharmacol 2014

assumptions.claim: In adults with bipolar I depression, cariprazine 1.5 mg/day improved the MADRS total score by about 2.5 points more than placebo at week 6.
assumptions.source: Earley et al., Am J Psychiatry 2019 (RGH-MD-54)

reason: With about 40 patients per arm, high expected patency in the sham arm and three primary outcomes, this pilot cannot plausibly show statistical superiority; it is also still recruiting close to its registered completion date.
rationale: This is a phase 2 pilot from a small device company with NHLBI support: 80 patients, three primary outcomes (patency, post-thrombotic syndrome, safety) and no stated hypothesis. Symptomatic patency in the sham arm after successful thrombus removal is probably 70-85%, leaving room for a gain of only 5-15 points, far below what 40 per arm can detect. It is still recruiting two months before its registered completion with a 6-month endpoint, so the date must slip and a result by June 2027 is unlikely; any early report would be descriptive.
evidence: ATTRACT (Vedantham et al., N Engl J Med 2017)

assumptions.claim: In ATTRACT, pharmacomechanical catheter-directed thrombolysis did not reduce post-thrombotic syndrome over 24 months (47% vs 48% with anticoagulation alone).
assumptions.source: Vedantham et al., N Engl J Med 2017 (ATTRACT)

reason: Atezolizumab added little to T-DM1 in metastatic HER2-positive disease (KATE2) and to neoadjuvant HER2 therapy (IMpassion050); in a PD-L1-unselected trial cut to 1188 patients the IDFS hazard ratio is likely near 0.9 and not significant.
rationale: Evidence for PD-L1 blockade in HER2-positive breast cancer is weak: KATE2 missed PFS (HR 0.82) with a signal only in PD-L1-positive tumours, and IMpassion050 showed no pCR gain. ASTEFANIA enrols regardless of PD-L1 and stopped accrual at 1188 patients, short of plan, so power is reduced; about 200 events need an observed HR below roughly 0.76. I expect a true HR near 0.9. Control 3-year IDFS should resemble T-DM1 in DESTINY-Breast05 (83.7%). Primary completion is March 2027, so a statement by June 2027 is unlikely.
evidence: IMpassion030/ALEXANDRA (adjuvant atezolizumab in triple-negative breast cancer), 2023

assumptions.claim: In KATE2, adding atezolizumab to T-DM1 did not significantly improve PFS in previously treated HER2-positive advanced breast cancer (median 8.2 vs 6.8 months, HR 0.82).
assumptions.source: Emens et al., Lancet Oncol 2020 (KATE2, NCT02924883)

assumptions.claim: In DESTINY-Breast05, 3-year invasive disease-free survival in the T-DM1 arm was 83.7% in high-risk HER2-positive patients with residual invasive disease.
assumptions.source: DESTINY-Breast05 (NCT04622319), ESMO 2025 and N Engl J Med 2025

assumptions.claim: In IMpassion050, adding atezolizumab to neoadjuvant chemotherapy with trastuzumab and pertuzumab did not improve pathological complete response (62.4% vs 62.7%).
assumptions.source: Huober et al., J Clin Oncol 2022 (IMpassion050, NCT03726879)

reason: Background therapy and steroids lift placebo SRI-4 to the low-to-mid 40s at week 52, so a true gain of about 10 points would land right at the significance boundary with about 183 patients per arm.
rationale: Litifilimab (anti-BDCA2) showed SRI-4 56% vs 29% at week 24 in phase 2 LILAC-A, but that was a small trial with a joint-count primary (p=0.04), and effects usually shrink in phase 3. The type I interferon pathway is validated by anifrolumab, yet TULIP-1 missed SRI-4 and pDC-depleting daxdilimab failed phase 2. About 183 per arm gives 80% power only for a 15-point gain; I expect about 10 points over a 43% placebo rate. Adjudicated entry criteria and two doses help. Roughly a coin flip, matching the phase 3 record in lupus.

assumptions.claim: In the phase 2 LILAC Part A trial, SRI-4 response at week 24 was 56% with litifilimab 450 mg versus 29% with placebo.
assumptions.source: LILAC Part A, Furie et al., NEJM 2022 (NCT02847598)

assumptions.claim: LILAC Part A met its primary endpoint of change in total active joint count at week 24 with a difference of -3.4 joints versus placebo (p=0.04).
assumptions.source: LILAC Part A, Furie et al., NEJM 2022 (NCT02847598)

assumptions.claim: In TULIP-2, SRI-4 response at week 52 was 55.5% with anifrolumab versus 37.3% with placebo.

reason: Dosing of the 100 healthy volunteers ended long ago; the 2027-01-01 date looks like a rolled-forward placeholder while assay work and the post-exposure filing plan are pending, so another roll-forward is about as likely as a clean close.
rationale: Healthy-volunteer study of 100 subjects with 59 days of follow-up that started in April 2022; dosing ended long ago and the registered completion date looks like a placeholder that has been rolled forward while immunogenicity assays and the post-exposure prophylaxis filing strategy are pending. Roughly even odds it is rolled forward again rather than closed with an earlier actual date. Results posting within the window is unlikely, since posting follows completion by up to a year. Termination is unlikely because data collection is done. The vague immunogenicity outcome could be tightened, but substantive change is rare.

reason: JAK1 inhibition is very likely to separate from placebo on ACR20; the residual risk is an unusually high placebo response at week 24 in a slow-enrolling single-country study.
rationale: JAK inhibitors reliably beat placebo on ACR20 in psoriatic arthritis (tofacitinib OPAL, upadacitinib SELECT-PsA, filgotinib EQUATOR), and ivarmacitinib itself beat placebo by about 30 points on ACR20 at week 24 in its phase 3 rheumatoid arthritis trial. With about 139 per arm, power exceeds 95% for a 20-point difference. Chinese placebo arms tend to be modest (30-40%). Residual risks are a high placebo rate at week 24 or conduct problems in a slow-enrolling study. Hengrui rarely issues topline releases, so timing of disclosure is the main uncertainty, not the result.

assumptions.claim: In SELECT-PsA 1, ACR20 response at week 12 was 70.6% with upadacitinib 15 mg versus 36.2% with placebo.
In the phase 3 rheumatoid arthritis trial of ivarmacitinib, ACR20 response at week 24 was 70.4% (4 mg) and 75.1% (8 mg) versus 40.4% with placebo.
assumptions.source: Ivarmacitinib RA phase 3, Ann Rheum Dis 2025

assumptions.claim: In OPAL Broaden, ACR20 response at month 3 was 50% with tofacitinib 5 mg twice daily versus 33% with placebo.
assumptions.source: OPAL Broaden, Mease et al., NEJM 2017

reason: Placebo SRI-4 on background therapy typically reaches the low 40s at week 52, so a true gain of about 10 points would sit at the edge of significance with about 187 patients per arm.
rationale: Same design and drug as TOPAZ-1, run in different countries (Asia, western Europe, Canada, Latin America). Phase 2 LILAC-A showed SRI-4 56% vs 29% at week 24 in a small trial whose primary was joint count (p=0.04). The interferon pathway is validated by anifrolumab, but TULIP-1 missed on SRI-4 and pDC-depleting daxdilimab failed phase 2. With about 187 per arm, a 10-point true gain over a 42% placebo rate sits at the significance boundary. Two doses and adjudicated eligibility help; phase 3 lupus trials succeed about half the time.

assumptions.claim: In the phase 2 LILAC Part A trial, SRI-4 response at week 24 was 56% with litifilimab 450 mg versus 29% with placebo.
assumptions.source: LILAC Part A, Furie et al., NEJM 2022 (NCT02847598)

assumptions.claim: In TULIP-1, anifrolumab missed its SRI-4 primary endpoint at week 52, with 36% responders versus 40% with placebo.
assumptions.source: TULIP-1, Furie et al., Lancet Rheumatology 2019

assumptions.claim: In TULIP-2, SRI-4 response at week 52 was 55.5% with anifrolumab versus 37.3% with placebo.

reason: Adolescents with chronic migraine improve by about 6 migraine days a month after a placebo infusion, leaving roughly 1.5 days of drug effect to detect with only about 95 patients per arm.
rationale: Eptinezumab 300 mg cut monthly migraine days by 2.6 more than placebo in adults with chronic migraine (PROMISE-2). In youth, placebo responses are large, especially after an infusion: onabotulinumtoxinA failed in adolescent chronic migraine, and paediatric CGRP antibody trials have been mixed, with fremanezumab SPACE succeeding on a 1.1-day gain. I expect about -1.6 days against a placebo change near -6, SD about 6; with 95 per arm the detectable difference is about 1.7 days, so slightly under even odds. Five years of slow enrolment adds noise.

assumptions.claim: In PROMISE-2, the change in monthly migraine days over weeks 1-12 was -8.2 with eptinezumab 300 mg versus -5.6 with placebo in adults with chronic migraine.
In the SPACE trial in children and adolescents with episodic migraine, fremanezumab reduced monthly migraine days by 2.5 versus 1.4 with placebo.
OnabotulinumtoxinA did not separate from placebo on headache days in adolescents with chronic migraine, with a placebo reduction of about 6.8 days at week 12.

reason: Cell-based immunotherapy has not improved adjuvant outcomes in pancreatic cancer, and the trial needs an observed recurrence hazard ratio below about 0.80, beyond the effect I expect (about 0.87).
rationale: Immuncell-LC (autologous cytokine-induced killer cells) improved recurrence-free survival after curative liver cancer treatment (HR 0.63) and progression-free survival in glioblastoma in the sponsor's earlier open-label Korean trials, but pancreatic adenocarcinoma is immunologically cold and no immunotherapy has improved adjuvant outcomes there. With about 290 events among 408 patients, the observed HR must fall below about 0.80; I centre the true HR near 0.88. Gemcitabine alone should give 12-14 months, longer by independent review as in APACT. Independent review limits open-label bias. Roughly a one-in-four chance.

assumptions.claim: In the phase 3 trial after curative treatment of hepatocellular carcinoma, Immuncell-LC improved recurrence-free survival with a hazard ratio of 0.63 (median 44.0 versus 30.0 months).
In PRODIGE 24, median disease-free survival in the adjuvant gemcitabine arm was 12.8 months.
In APACT, independently assessed median disease-free survival in the adjuvant gemcitabine arm was 18.8 months.
assumptions.source: APACT, Tempero et al., J Clin Oncol 2023

reason: Enrolment is closed and the registered end sits exactly 67 months after start, matching the outcome time frame; Merck usually keeps such dates or closes earlier, and posts results about a year after completion.
rationale: Merck signal-finding basket study with no formal hypothesis, enrolment closed, registered end at 67 months after start, the same as the outcome time frame. Merck usually keeps such dates or closes earlier and moves remaining patients to rollover studies, so a slip beyond June 2027 is unlikely. Merck rarely labels studies terminated, even when cohorts close. Results are normally posted about 12 months after primary completion, so posting by August 2027 is unlikely. Cohort changes by protocol amendment are possible but rarely alter the registered primary outcomes in substance.

reason: Single-arm rPFS signals for a BET inhibitor plus enzalutamide may not hold in a randomised comparison, and the Cohort A sample (about 100 events) can only detect a hazard ratio near 0.6.
rationale: ZEN-3694 plus enzalutamide gave a median rPFS of 9.0 months in a single-arm phase 1b/2a in ARSI-resistant prostate cancer, longer than expected for a switch of androgen-receptor inhibitor (3.7-5.6 months in CARD and PSMAfore controls). Cohort A selects poor abiraterone responders, where enzalutamide alone should do badly (about 4 months), leaving room for a BET inhibitor to add benefit. But single-arm rPFS signals often fail when randomised, BET inhibitors have a thin record, and the trial is open-label, small and slow to enrol. About one in three.

assumptions.claim: In the phase 1b/2a study of ZEN-3694 plus enzalutamide in 75 patients with ARSI-resistant mCRPC, median radiographic progression-free survival was 9.0 months.
assumptions.source: Aggarwal et al., Clin Cancer Res 2020 (NCT02711956)

assumptions.claim: In PSMAfore, median rPFS in the control arm that switched androgen-receptor pathway inhibitor was about 5.6 months.
In CARD, median rPFS was 3.7 months in the arm given the alternative androgen-receptor inhibitor (abiraterone or enzalutamide).
assumptions.source: CARD, de Wit et al., NEJM 2019

reason: Standard-dose octreotide LAR or lanreotide already gives long progression-free survival and no randomised evidence shows that higher octreotide exposure adds antitumour effect, so an observed hazard ratio below 0.75 is a stretch.
rationale: SORENTO tests whether higher octreotide exposure (CAM2029 every 2 weeks) beats standard-dose octreotide LAR or lanreotide on progression-free survival. Somatostatin analogues clearly delay progression versus placebo (PROMID, CLARINET), but no randomised evidence shows a dose-response above standard doses; CLARINET FORTE was uncontrolled. With 194 events the observed HR must be below about 0.75, the design assumed 0.67, and I centre the true HR near 0.87. Slow event accrual signals an indolent population, not necessarily a treatment effect. About one in four.

assumptions.claim: In CLARINET, lanreotide 120 mg reduced the risk of progression or death versus placebo with a hazard ratio of 0.47, with median PFS not reached versus 18.0 months.
In PROMID, median time to tumour progression was 14.3 months with octreotide LAR 30 mg versus 6.0 months with placebo.
assumptions.source: PROMID, Rinke et al., J Clin Oncol 2009

assumptions.claim: CLARINET FORTE, which tested lanreotide 120 mg every 14 days after progression on the standard dose, was a single-arm study with median PFS of 8.3 months in midgut and 5.6 months in pancreatic tumours.
assumptions.source: CLARINET FORTE, Pavel et al., Eur J Cancer 2021

reason: No randomised efficacy data exist for clemizole in Lennox-Gastaut syndrome; a serotonergic effect of about 8 points over placebo would not reach significance with 130 per arm and highly variable seizure counts.
rationale: Clemizole (EPX-100) is a serotonin-receptor modulator found in a zebrafish Dravet screen; it has no published randomised efficacy data in Lennox-Gastaut syndrome, and the outcome of the Dravet phase 3 (ARGUS) is unknown to me. The serotonergic precedent is fenfluramine, about 19 points better than placebo on drop seizures, but soticlestat showed new mechanisms can miss in this syndrome. With 130 per arm and SD near 50, a difference of 13-14 points is needed; I expect about 8. An early statement could also be a stop.
evidence: Baraban et al. zebrafish clemizole screen 2013

assumptions.claim: In the phase 3 fenfluramine trial in Lennox-Gastaut syndrome, the median reduction in drop seizure frequency was 26.5% with 0.7 mg/kg/day versus 7.6% with placebo.
The phase 3 SKYWAY trial of soticlestat in Lennox-Gastaut syndrome missed its primary endpoint of reduction in major motor drop seizures.
Clemizole was identified as a suppressor of seizures in scn1a mutant zebrafish, a model of Dravet syndrome.

reason: Prolonged seizures often stop on their own within 90 seconds of dosing (placebo responders were 42.5% in phase 2b) and home dosing by caregivers during a seizure may blunt delivery, so the drug-placebo gap could be too small for both primaries.
rationale: Phase 2b StATES showed 65.8% versus 42.5% responders (p=0.039) in a monitored unit; inhaled alprazolam peaks in plasma within about two minutes and benzodiazepines reliably terminate seizures. Phase 3 is larger (350) but moves to outpatient caregiver dosing, tightens the window to 90 seconds and requires two primaries: termination, and no recurrence or rescue to two hours. The phase 2 effect was borderline, so some shrinkage is expected. Enrolment has slipped for years; readout is likely mid-2027, so a result by June is uncertain.

assumptions.claim: In the phase 2b StATES trial, responder rates (seizure cessation within 2 minutes and no recurrence within 2 hours) were 65.8% for both Staccato alprazolam 1 mg and 2 mg versus 42.5% for placebo.
assumptions.source: StATES phase 2b, French et al., Epilepsia 2023

assumptions.claim: StATES treated 116 patients in an inpatient epilepsy monitoring unit, not at home.
assumptions.source: StATES phase 2b, French et al., Epilepsia 2023

reason: The fixed 0-, 48-month schedule with enrolment closed makes the last visits predictable, so completion near March 2027 is likely, with results posted around GSK's usual 12-month mark, after the read date.
rationale: GSK-run schedule study with enrolment closed; the last 48-month dose and one-month blood draw fall in early 2027 by design, so slippage beyond 90 days is unlikely. GSK usually posts results about 12 months after primary completion, later than the August 2027 read date. Primary outcomes are descriptive and stable; the vaccine is licensed, so a stop is unlikely.

reason: The class effect on EFS is consistent, so failure would most likely come from an immature interim analysis or from only the stage III primary being reported while the ITT primary is still pending.
rationale: Perioperative PD-(L)1 plus chemotherapy improved EFS in every phase 3 so far (HR 0.40 to 0.68), including Chinese PD-1 trials Neotorch (0.40, stage III) and RATIONALE-315 (0.56). ORIENT-99 follows Neotorch's stage III-first hierarchy with 506 patients, so a true HR near 0.55 is well powered. A statement by June 2027 would most likely be a positive interim at a congress or an sNDA acceptance. I discount for two listed primaries (stage III, then ITT) that may not both be reported, and for stale registry dates.

assumptions.claim: In Neotorch (perioperative toripalimab plus chemotherapy, stage III NSCLC), the EFS hazard ratio was 0.40 and median EFS in the placebo arm was about 15 months.
KEYNOTE-671 reported an EFS hazard ratio of 0.58 for perioperative pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy versus placebo plus chemotherapy.
RATIONALE-315 reported an EFS hazard ratio of 0.56 for perioperative tislelizumab plus chemotherapy versus placebo plus chemotherapy.

reason: A 60-patient phase 2a from a small sponsor with enrolment closed and the registered completion date already passed will most likely move to completed, with results posted late or not by the read date.
rationale: Phase 2a that began in 2021 for COVID-19 and was broadened to pneumonia; now active, not recruiting with the registered completion (September 2026) already passed. Small private sponsor: results posting within 11 months is uncertain, and an early close could be relabelled terminated. A safety primary is unlikely to change.

reason: As a DHODH inhibitor vidofludimus may cut relapses by only 20-30%, and with about 250 first relapses a true hazard ratio above 0.75 leaves the trial short of significance.
rationale: EMPhASIS phase 2 showed 62-70% fewer active MRI lesions at 24 weeks, comparable to teriflunomide, which cut relapses 31-36% versus placebo. With about 1,100 patients and roughly 250 first relapses, power is near 80% at HR 0.70 and 60% at 0.75. The October 2024 interim passed futility with no sample-size increase, which favours the planned effect. CALLIPER missed its brain-volume primary but supports activity. Topline for both ENSURE trials was guided for end of 2026, so the result should be public early in the window.

assumptions.claim: In EMPhASIS, vidofludimus calcium 45 mg reduced cumulative combined unique active MRI lesions over 24 weeks by about 62% versus placebo, and 30 mg by about 70%.
assumptions.source: EMPhASIS phase 2, Fox et al., Ann Clin Transl Neurol 2022

assumptions.claim: In October 2024 the independent data monitoring committee, after an unblinded interim analysis of the ENSURE programme, recommended continuing both trials as planned with no sample-size increase.
Teriflunomide 14 mg reduced the annualized relapse rate by about 31% versus placebo in TEMSO.

reason: The phase 2 trial missed its primary and the 14-point complete-response gain for the intensified regimen came from about 45 patients per arm, so the true gain may be under the 10 points this trial can detect.
rationale: TULIP-LN missed its UPCR primary; the intensified regimen gave complete renal response 45.5% versus 31.1% at week 52 (not significant) while the basic regimen fell below placebo, so the signal is noisy. Shrinking it gives a true gain of 7-9 points; IRIS needs about 10 observed points with 181 per arm. Add-on lupus nephritis trials have a mixed record. Primary completion is February 2027 and AstraZeneca usually announces positive phase 3 results within three months, so results public by June skew positive; by December the probability falls to about 0.37.

assumptions.claim: TULIP-LN did not meet its primary endpoint (change in 24-hour UPCR for combined anifrolumab versus placebo at week 52).
assumptions.source: TULIP-LN, Jayne et al., Ann Rheum Dis 2022

assumptions.claim: In TULIP-LN, complete renal response at week 52 was 45.5% with the intensified anifrolumab regimen versus 31.1% with placebo.
assumptions.source: TULIP-LN, Jayne et al., Ann Rheum Dis 2022

assumptions.claim: In REGENCY, complete renal response at week 76 was 46.4% with obinutuzumab plus standard therapy versus 33.1% with placebo plus standard therapy.

reason: About 37 patients per arm and a 24-week FVC endpoint with a between-patient SD near 200 mL give low power unless the treatment difference exceeds 100 mL.
rationale: HEC585 is a pirfenidone analogue; that class slows FVC decline in progressive fibrosing ILD by about half, roughly 40-50 mL over 24 weeks against a placebo decline near 75-90 mL. With three arms of about 37 and SD near 200 mL, each dose has 15-25% power, and either dose can win. Recruiting since February 2023 and still open with primary completion listed for December 2026, the trial will run late; a public result by June 2027 is unlikely and could as easily be a stop.

assumptions.claim: In INBUILD, the adjusted annual rate of FVC decline on placebo was -187.8 mL per year in progressive fibrosing ILD.
In the unclassifiable ILD phase 2 trial, mean 24-week FVC change by site spirometry was -17.8 mL with pirfenidone versus -113.0 mL with placebo.
assumptions.source: Maher et al., Lancet Respir Med 2020

reason: Only 69 patients for two primaries (HbA1c and triglycerides at month 6) with wide between-patient variability, and open-label HbA1c falls of 0.6-0.9 points may shrink against placebo on optimized background therapy.
rationale: Open-label NIH data in partial lipodystrophy showed HbA1c falls of 0.6-0.9 points and triglyceride falls of 21-37% at 12 months without a control; Simha 2012 found triglyceride but not HbA1c benefit in familial partial lipodystrophy. Against placebo I expect about -0.45 points with SD near 1.3, roughly 40% power for HbA1c in 69 patients, and both listed primaries may be required. The leptin cap of 20 ng/mL enriches somewhat. A positive result is more likely to be announced early, so results public by June skew positive.
evidence: Oral et al., Endocrine 2019 (NIH metreleptin partial lipodystrophy)

assumptions.claim: In the NIH open-label study, the partial lipodystrophy subgroup with baseline HbA1c of 6.5% or more and/or triglycerides of 5.65 mmol/L or more had a mean HbA1c change of -0.9 percentage points at month 12 on metreleptin.
In familial partial lipodystrophy (Dunnigan variety), metreleptin lowered triglycerides but did not significantly change HbA1c.
assumptions.source: Simha et al., J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2012

reason: Stage Two splits a small sample across several light fluences and vehicle and the analysis may be descriptive, so a clear statement that the efficacy primary was met is uncertain despite a strong drug effect.
rationale: Hemoporfin PDT is approved in China, where the phase 3 showed 89.7% versus 24.5% with at least some improvement at week 8, so a real effect versus vehicle on face and neck lesions is very likely. Risks are small Stage Two arms split across fluences, a US adult population with possibly more resistant lesions, an undefined IGA analysis and a safety outcome listed first. Still recruiting with up to 44 weeks of follow-up, the trial will finish after January 2027; a public result by June 2027 is unlikely and could reflect a stop.
evidence: Zhao et al., PLoS One 2016 (hemoporfin PDT phase 3, China)

assumptions.claim: In the Chinese phase 3 trial, 89.7% of hemoporfin PDT patients versus 24.5% of placebo PDT patients achieved at least some improvement at week 8.

reason: Enrolment is closed at 66 and the primary is a 24-hour safety outcome, so completion by the end of 2026 is likely, and the small sponsor is unlikely to post results on ClinicalTrials.gov by August 2027.
rationale: Enrolment closed at 66 with a 24-hour primary outcome and completion listed for 31 December 2026, so a slip beyond March 2027 would need recruitment to restart for the second part. Small Taiwanese sponsor; posting on ClinicalTrials.gov within eight months of completion is unlikely. A safety primary is unlikely to change.

reason: The relapse effect may be only teriflunomide-like or smaller (hazard ratio near 0.8) while low modern placebo relapse rates leave too few first-relapse events to show it.
rationale: DHODH inhibition is a validated relapse mechanism: teriflunomide cut relapses by about a third against placebo (TEMSO, TOWER). Vidofludimus calcium 30 mg reduced active MRI lesions by about 70% in EMPhASIS, and the 2024 unblinded interim analysis found no futility and no need to upsize. With 1,100 patients, power is roughly 75-88% for a hazard ratio of 0.65-0.70, but recent trials show low relapse rates (teriflunomide ARR 0.11-0.15), so events may be thin. Top-line was guided for end of 2026, so a result by March 2027 is likely.

assumptions.claim: Teriflunomide 14 mg reduced the annualized relapse rate by about 31% versus placebo (0.37 vs 0.54) in TEMSO.
In EMPhASIS, vidofludimus calcium 30 mg and 45 mg reduced cumulative combined unique active lesions over 24 weeks by about 70% and 62% versus placebo.
assumptions.source: EMPhASIS, Fox et al., Ann Clin Transl Neurol 2022 (NCT03846219)

assumptions.claim: After an unblinded interim analysis of the ENSURE programme in October 2024, the independent data monitoring committee recommended continuing both trials without a sample size increase.

reason: Carisbamate showed only modest, inconsistent efficacy in focal epilepsy and has no controlled data in Lennox-Gastaut syndrome, so its drop-seizure effect may not clear a 10-20% placebo response.
rationale: Carisbamate has no controlled LGS data; phase 3 followed an open-label pharmacokinetic study. In focal epilepsy it was inconsistent (400 mg/day positive in one of two trials; a higher-dose trial failed), suggesting modest potency. Broad-spectrum antiseizure drugs usually beat placebo on drop seizures (clobazam, rufinamide, cannabidiol, fenfluramine), but soticlestat and perampanel missed. With 252 patients and placebo response of 10-20%, a 15-point median difference is detectable. Enrolment has run since 2022 and is still open, so the February 2027 completion will probably slip and a result before mid-2027 is uncertain.
evidence: Carisbamate partial-onset seizure trials (Sperling et al.), 2010

assumptions.claim: Placebo patients had a median 21.8% reduction in drop seizures in GWPCARE4, versus 43.9% with cannabidiol.
Placebo patients had a median 7.6% reduction in drop seizures in the fenfluramine LGS trial, versus 26.5% with 0.7 mg/kg/day.
In two phase 3 trials in partial-onset seizures, carisbamate 400 mg/day was significantly better than placebo in one trial but not in the other.

reason: The COAST signal came from about 60 patients per arm against an underperforming durvalumab arm, and the true add-on benefit of oleclumab is probably too small (hazard ratio near 0.85) to reach significance.
rationale: PACIFIC-9 rests on COAST, an open-label randomized phase 2 with about 60 patients per arm where both add-ons looked similarly good against an underperforming durvalumab arm (median PFS about 6 months versus 17 in PACIFIC). Shrinking that signal gives a true hazard ratio near 0.85, below what roughly 350 patients per arm can detect. Phase 3 add-ons to PD-(L)1 around chemoradiation have repeatedly failed (SKYSCRAPER-03, PACIFIC-2, KEYLYNK-012, CheckMate-73L), and monalizumab failed INTERLINK-1. The registered completion date has passed, so AstraZeneca should disclose by early 2027.

assumptions.claim: In COAST, durvalumab plus oleclumab gave a PFS hazard ratio of 0.44 versus durvalumab alone at the interim analysis, with about 60 patients per arm.
assumptions.source: COAST, Herbst et al., J Clin Oncol 2022 (NCT03822351)

assumptions.claim: Median PFS with durvalumab after chemoradiation was 16.8 months by blinded central review in PACIFIC, versus 5.6 months with placebo.
The phase 3 INTERLINK-1 trial of monalizumab plus cetuximab in head and neck cancer was stopped for futility in 2022.

reason: Oral systemic factor B inhibition is unproven in the retina, and a proof-of-concept study of about 73 per arm needs roughly a halving of conversion to iRORA or late AMD to succeed.
rationale: Small proof-of-concept (about 73 per arm) that needs roughly a halving of conversion to iRORA or late AMD to reach significance. Complement inhibitors injected into the eye slowed geographic atrophy only modestly, and oral alternative-pathway inhibition has not shown benefit in AMD. Iptacopan in earlier disease is plausible from genetics but unproven. Novartis rarely press-releases negative phase 2 results; disclosure will most likely come through registry posting about 12 months after the August 2026 completion, so a statement before July 2027 is unlikely.

assumptions.claim: In OAKS, monthly intravitreal pegcetacoplan reduced geographic atrophy lesion growth by about 21% versus sham at 12 months, while DERBY did not reach significance at 12 months.
assumptions.source: OAKS and DERBY, Heier et al., Lancet 2023

assumptions.claim: In GATHER2, avacincaptad pegol 2 mg reduced geographic atrophy growth by about 14% versus sham over 12 months.
The registry description plans about 146 treated participants, 73 per arm, randomized 1:1 to iptacopan or placebo.

reason: Only 64 men were enrolled across three arms (about 21 each), too few to show a plausibly small effect of fenugreek extract on both IIEF and Erection Hardness Score over a sizeable placebo response.
rationale: Single-site nutraceutical trial that enrolled 64 men across three arms (about 21 each), far below the power needed for a plausible small effect of fenugreek extract on IIEF. Two primary outcomes (IIEF and Erection Hardness Score) must both be met by the same dose. Earlier Testofen studies reported improvements in libido and ageing-male symptom scores, not erectile function in men with erectile dysfunction. Placebo response on IIEF is sizeable. Publication, if any, will likely come after mid-2027 and favour positive framing.
evidence: Rao et al., Testofen in healthy ageing males (Aging Male), 2016
Steels et al., Testofen and male libido (Phytother Res), 2011

assumptions.claim: A 12-week placebo-controlled trial of Testofen 600 mg/day in 120 healthy men aged 43-70 reported improved Ageing Male Symptom and DISF-SR scores versus placebo.
The registry record gives an enrolment of 64 participants for a three-arm trial.

reason: With about 80 patients per arm, a chance deficit of around 10 points in remission, or slightly lower efficacy at the trough of twice-yearly dosing, could push the confidence bound past the non-inferiority margin.
rationale: Depemokimab targets IL-5 like mepolizumab, with sustained eosinophil suppression over 26 weeks and asthma exacerbation reductions (SWIFT) similar to mepolizumab's. The design mirrors MANDARA, where benralizumab was non-inferior to mepolizumab (59% vs 56% remission) with a 25-point margin; about 80 per arm gives roughly 90% power if the drugs are truly equal. Risks: the margin is not in the record, week 52 falls at the trough of twice-yearly dosing against mepolizumab 300 mg monthly, and the sample is small. Completion was September 2026, so read-out is near.

assumptions.claim: In MANDARA, remission at weeks 36 and 48 occurred in 59% of benralizumab and 56% of mepolizumab patients, meeting non-inferiority against a margin of -25 percentage points.
In MIRRA, 32% of mepolizumab patients versus 3% of placebo patients were in remission at both weeks 36 and 48.
Depemokimab given every 26 weeks reduced the annualized asthma exacerbation rate by about 54% versus placebo in the pooled SWIFT-1 and SWIFT-2 trials.

reason: The study is completed and results are due on the registry around 10 August 2027, so whether they show by 31 August depends on AstraZeneca submitting on time and on processing lag.
rationale: Completed AstraZeneca paediatric study designed with FDA; primary completion was 10 August 2026, so results are due on ClinicalTrials.gov around 10 August 2027. AstraZeneca usually submits close to the 12-month deadline and posting follows within weeks, so appearance by 31 August 2027 is a little better than even. A completed trial cannot be stopped, and outcome changes at posting are usually rewording.

reason: Induced-sputum neutrophil counts are highly variable and ensifentrine's anti-inflammatory effect in COPD airways is unproven, so 56 crossover patients may not show a significant fall at week 8.
rationale: Evidence that ensifentrine reduces airway neutrophils comes from an LPS-challenge study in healthy volunteers, not from COPD patients; its PDE4 activity is weaker than its PDE3 bronchodilator activity. Roflumilast cut sputum neutrophils by about a third in a similar crossover, so an effect is plausible, but induced-sputum counts are highly variable and 56 enrolled patients (fewer with paired samples in both periods) give limited power. Background once-daily maintenance therapy may blunt differences. Results will probably appear only at a congress or on the registry after mid-2027.
evidence: Franciosi et al., RPL554 LPS-challenge study (Lancet Respir Med), 2013
Grootendorst et al., roflumilast sputum study (Thorax), 2007

assumptions.claim: Inhaled RPL554 (ensifentrine) reduced sputum neutrophil counts after LPS challenge in healthy volunteers.
assumptions.source: Franciosi et al., Lancet Respir Med 2013

assumptions.claim: Roflumilast reduced absolute sputum neutrophil numbers by about 36% versus placebo in a 4-week crossover study of 38 COPD patients.
Ensifentrine 3 mg twice daily improved average FEV1 AUC0-12h at week 12 by 87 mL in ENHANCE-1 and 94 mL in ENHANCE-2 versus placebo.
assumptions.source: ENHANCE-1/2, Anzueto et al., Am J Respir Crit Care Med 2023

reason: The 11-month PFS in a 27-patient, single-arm, largely single-centre phase 2 is likely to shrink in a randomized multicentre trial, leaving a benefit too small for 186 patients to show.
rationale: The case rests on VIRO-15, a single-arm, largely single-centre phase 2 in 27 patients (ORR 54%, median PFS 11 months), far above the 4-5 months expected with chemotherapy plus bevacizumab after three or more lines. Such signals usually shrink in randomized multicentre trials; I assume a true hazard ratio around 0.7, with real uncertainty either way. The experimental arm also gets a platinum doublet while controls get single-agent chemotherapy, which may help slightly. About 186 patients give adequate power only for a hazard ratio near 0.6. Open-label design adds drop-out risk.

assumptions.claim: In the single-arm phase 2 VIRO-15 trial of 27 patients, Olvi-Vec followed by platinum-based chemotherapy with or without bevacizumab gave an objective response rate of 54% and a median PFS of 11.0 months.
assumptions.source: VIRO-15, Holloway et al., JAMA Oncol 2023 (NCT02759588)

assumptions.claim: In AURELIA, chemotherapy plus bevacizumab gave a median PFS of 6.7 months versus 3.4 months with chemotherapy alone in platinum-resistant ovarian cancer.
assumptions.source: AURELIA, Pujade-Lauraine et al., J Clin Oncol 2014

assumptions.claim: In MIRASOL, investigator's-choice single-agent chemotherapy gave a median PFS of about 4.0 months in platinum-resistant ovarian cancer.

reason: Enrolment is closed and follow-up should finish close to the registered November 2026 date, with results posting due only in late 2027.
rationale: Small NINDS-funded feasibility study with enrolment finished and 24-month safety follow-up ending around November 2026; there is a modest risk the date slips past February 2027. Results are due about 12 months after primary completion (late 2027) and the indication is not yet approved, so posting by August 2027 is unlikely. Termination is unlikely for an implanted-device study in follow-up.

reason: CCTA total atheroma volume includes calcified plaque, which rises under intensive LDL lowering, and reading noise over 24 months could shrink a real regression effect below significance.
rationale: Inclisiran roughly halves LDL-C on top of statins, and PCSK9 antibodies produced plaque regression on IVUS (GLAGOV, PACMAN-AMI) and on CCTA (ARCHITECT). With 610 patients over 24 months the trial should detect a 3-4 point difference in percent change of total atheroma volume. Risks: CCTA total volume includes calcified plaque, which grows under intensive lipid lowering; reading noise; statin optimisation blunting placebo progression; and patients entering with LDL-C only modestly above 55 mg/dL.

assumptions.claim: In GLAGOV, evolocumab added to statin changed percent atheroma volume on IVUS by -0.95% versus +0.05% with placebo over 76 weeks.
In ORION-10 and ORION-11, inclisiran lowered LDL-C by about 50% versus placebo at day 510.
In ARCHITECT, alirocumab plus high-intensity statin lowered coronary plaque burden on CCTA from 34.6% to 30.4% over 78 weeks in familial hypercholesterolaemia.

reason: Breg induction of at least 3% plus completed immunosuppression reduction without rejection may be reached by too few MIC patients; a result by mid-2027 is also unlikely because the trial is still listed as recruiting.
rationale: Composite is built so that standard-of-care patients almost cannot qualify: they stay on steroids and full-dose MPS and rarely reach Breg of 3%. Phase 1 (TOL-1) showed Breg induction and stable grafts on reduced immunosuppression in the 4 high-dose patients, so even a 30% response among 42 MIC patients beats near-zero control. Risks: Breg threshold missed, rejection during minimisation, small multi-centre manufacture. A result by mid-2027 is unlikely (still listed as recruiting, 12-month endpoint), and an early statement could be a stop.
evidence: Morath et al. 2023 (TOL-1 three-year follow-up, J Am Soc Nephrol)

assumptions.claim: In the phase 1 TOL-1 trial, the patients given the highest MIC dose 7 days before transplantation showed a marked rise in CD19+CD24hiCD38hi regulatory B cells and no rejection in the first year.
Three-year follow-up of TOL-1 reported the high-dose patients on reduced immunosuppression without rejection or de novo donor-specific antibodies.
assumptions.source: Morath et al., J Am Soc Nephrol 2023

reason: If the hypothesis is superiority, 85 patients per arm cannot show a difference when about 90% of surgical patients keep the limb at 30 days; success depends on a non-inferiority design with a wide margin.
rationale: Sponsor's earlier Fortelyzin trials against active comparators (FRIDOM, FRIDA) were non-inferiority designs, so FORAT probably tests non-inferiority to surgery; the record states no hypothesis. Historic thrombolysis-versus-surgery trials (Rochester, STILE, TOPAS) found similar limb salvage, so non-inferiority with 85 per arm is plausible given a wide margin, while superiority on a 30-day amputation-free rate near 90% is unlikely. I weight about 65% non-inferiority design (success about 0.7) and 35% superiority (success about 0.1). Open-label, sponsor-run in Russia.

assumptions.claim: In TOPAS, amputation-free survival at 6 months was similar with intra-arterial urokinase (71.8%) and surgery (74.8%).
In FRIDA, non-immunogenic staphylokinase was tested for and met non-inferiority to alteplase on favourable outcome (mRS 0-1) at day 90 in ischaemic stroke.
FRIDOM compared non-immunogenic staphylokinase with tenecteplase in STEMI as a non-inferiority trial.

reason: The agitation signal comes from post hoc phase 2 subgroups; a 5-HT6 antagonist may not beat the large placebo response seen in Alzheimer's agitation trials.
rationale: Masupirdine, a 5-HT6 antagonist, failed its phase 2 cognition endpoint; the agitation hypothesis comes from post hoc subgroup analyses of NPI agitation/aggression, which seldom replicate. The 5-HT6 class has no confirmed efficacy in Alzheimer's disease. Agitation trials show large placebo responses (about 17 CMAI points in brexpiprazole trials), and effective drugs separate by only 3-5 points. Two doses give two chances, and 125 per arm detects roughly a 0.35 SD effect. I put success at about 17%.
evidence: Nirogi et al. 2022 (post hoc agitation/aggression analysis)

assumptions.claim: The phase 2 trial of masupirdine added to donepezil and memantine in moderate Alzheimer's disease did not meet its primary endpoint, ADAS-Cog 11 at week 26.
Post hoc analyses of that phase 2 trial reported lower NPI agitation/aggression scores with masupirdine in patients who had agitation symptoms at baseline.
assumptions.source: Nirogi et al., Int J Geriatr Psychiatry 2022

assumptions.claim: In the fixed-dose brexpiprazole trial, CMAI total score at week 12 fell by about 22.6 points on brexpiprazole and 17.3 on placebo.

reason: Gene therapy eyes may lose letters from surgery or from under-suppressed disease before rescue, pushing the lower confidence bound past the non-inferiority margin.
rationale: Non-inferiority on BCVA in previously treated, anti-VEGF-responsive eyes, with supplemental anti-VEGF injections allowed in the gene therapy arms, favours success: vision is protected by rescue, as in Archway. Phase 1/2a showed stable vision for years at the pivotal dose range. Two doses give two chances. Risks: vitrectomy and subretinal delivery complications, late rescue causing letter loss (as in DAZZLE), and a tight margin with about 240 per arm, where a true deficit beyond 2-2.5 letters would fail.

assumptions.claim: In the phase 1/2a trial of subretinal RGX-314, the three higher dose cohorts kept stable or improved BCVA through 2 years with few supplemental anti-VEGF injections.
In Archway, the port delivery system with ranibizumab, with supplemental injections allowed, was non-inferior to monthly ranibizumab in BCVA change (difference about -0.3 letters).
In DAZZLE, tarcocimab tedromer on extended dosing failed to show non-inferiority to aflibercept in BCVA change.
