reason: With 64 patients split across ascending doses and placebo, and anticoagulation alone already lowering RV/LV by about 0.2 at 48 hours, only a large drug effect would be significant.
rationale: First patient efficacy test of alpha2-antiplasmin inactivation. Anticoagulation alone already lowers RV/LV by about 0.2 within 48 hours (STORM-PE), leaving limited room, and the 64 patients are spread across ascending doses and placebo, so only a large effect (about 0.15 or more) would reach significance. Mechanism is plausible from animal models and phase 1 pharmacodynamics, but lower dose cohorts may dilute the pooled comparison. Small company, NIH-funded; reporting may be slow.

assumptions.claim: In STORM-PE, anticoagulation alone reduced the RV/LV ratio by about 0.24 at 48 hours, versus about 0.52 with computer-assisted vacuum thrombectomy.
In ULTIMA, heparin alone reduced the RV/LV ratio by 0.03 at 24 hours, versus 0.30 with ultrasound-assisted catheter-directed thrombolysis.

reason: Both ADAS-Cog and CDR-SB must be met at 28 weeks in 60 patients per arm, which needs a large effect from an unproven agent; slow single-site recruitment also threatens completion.
rationale: Unknown oral agent from a small Taiwanese sponsor, single site, 120 patients, with ADAS-Cog and CDR-SB both primary at 28 weeks; both must be met. Placebo patients on cholinesterase inhibitors change little in 28 weeks, so a symptomatic drug would need a large effect on both scales in 60 per arm. Recruitment has run since 2022 and the record still says recruiting, so a result by mid-2027 is unlikely and could be a stop. Base rate for phase 2 Alzheimer's trials is low.

assumptions.claim: In the idalopirdine phase 3 trials, placebo patients with mild-to-moderate Alzheimer's disease on cholinesterase inhibitors worsened by less than about 1 ADAS-Cog point over 24 weeks.

reason: Lowering liver fat and stiffness may not translate into fewer decompensation, MELD or death events within about 3 years in cirrhosis, and 3:1 randomisation leaves few placebo events.
rationale: Resmetirom improved histology in F2-F3 (MAESTRO-NASH) and lowered liver stiffness in open-label compensated cirrhosis, but no drug has yet reduced clinical events in NASH cirrhosis (selonsertib, simtuzumab, obeticholic acid failed surrogate endpoints). With 3:1 randomisation and roughly 110-130 events, significance needs an observed hazard ratio near 0.66 or lower, a large effect for about 3 years of treatment; the composite also includes all-cause death and MELD rises that the drug may not change. I assume a true hazard ratio near 0.73.
evidence: Sanyal et al. 2019 (simtuzumab in NASH cirrhosis, NCT01672879)

assumptions.claim: In MAESTRO-NASH, resmetirom 80 mg gave NASH resolution in 25.9% versus 9.7% on placebo and fibrosis improvement in 24.2% versus 14.2% at week 52.
In the simtuzumab trial in compensated NASH cirrhosis, about 19% of patients had a liver-related clinical event over a median of about 29 months.
Selonsertib did not improve fibrosis versus placebo at week 48 in compensated NASH cirrhosis.

reason: Small NMDAR cohort with a sizeable placebo response to first-line immunotherapy; a 20-25 point responder difference is needed, and the LGI1 cohort primary must also succeed if both count.
rationale: IL-6 receptor blockade has only retrospective support in autoimmune encephalitis (tocilizumab in rituximab-refractory cases). Satralizumab works in AQP4 NMOSD but gave a small effect in myasthenia gravis. The NMDAR cohort is small (perhaps 40 per arm), many placebo patients improve by one mRS point within 24 weeks on first-line therapy, and a 20-25 point difference is needed. The basket has a second cohort primary (LGI1, week 52); if both must be met the chance falls further. I blend to about 0.25.
evidence: Lee et al. 2016 (tocilizumab in autoimmune encephalitis)

assumptions.claim: In a retrospective cohort of rituximab-refractory autoimmune encephalitis, tocilizumab-treated patients had better mRS outcomes than those given further rituximab or no additional therapy.
Satralizumab lowered relapse risk versus placebo in AQP4-IgG-positive NMOSD.
In generalised myasthenia gravis, satralizumab gave a statistically significant but small MG-ADL improvement over placebo at week 24.

reason: Twenty infants per arm cannot show a significant difference in death or disability unless the effect is very large; the 24-month endpoint will not be ready by mid-2027.
rationale: Forty neonates give almost no power on death or moderate/severe disability at 24 months: with a control rate near 45% the sovateltide arm would need a rate near 10%. No prior clinical data in neonatal encephalopathy; support is preclinical plus the sponsor's Indian stroke trials. The record still says recruiting with a 24-month endpoint, so the primary result cannot be ready by mid-2027; any statement by then would be a stop or a short-term update without the primary endpoint.

assumptions.claim: In HELIX, death or moderate/severe disability at 18 months occurred in about 50% of cooled and 47% of non-cooled infants with neonatal encephalopathy in South Asia.
In the Indian phase 3 trial in acute ischaemic stroke, more sovateltide than placebo patients reached mRS 0-2 at day 90.

reason: PVd may do well in this proteasome-inhibitor-sensitive population with 1-3 prior lines, so swapping pomalidomide for mezigdomide has to deliver a clear PFS gain despite more neutropenia, infections and dose reductions.
rationale: Head-to-head CELMoD-for-IMiD substitution on a bortezomib-dexamethasone backbone, 810 patients, open label. Mezigdomide is active in pomalidomide-refractory myeloma, and the MeziVd expansion cohort of CC-92480-MM-002 gave a response rate near 86% and median PFS near 17.5 months, against 11-13 months for PVd in OPTIMISMM and DREAMM-8, pointing to a hazard ratio near 0.7. I also recall, unverified, a positive SUCCESSOR-2 readout in 2026. Risks: PVd does better in a PI-sensitive population, extra neutropenia and infections, and a record still marked recruiting, which may delay the event-driven analysis.

assumptions.claim: In OPTIMISMM, median PFS was 11.2 months with PVd versus 7.1 months with Vd (hazard ratio 0.61).
assumptions.source: OPTIMISMM, Richardson et al., Lancet Oncol 2019 (NCT01734928)

assumptions.claim: In DREAMM-8, the PVd control arm had a median PFS of 12.7 months.
In CC-92480-MM-002, the MeziVd dose-expansion cohort had an overall response rate of about 86% and a median PFS of about 17.5 months.
assumptions.source: CC-92480-MM-002 (NCT03989414), ASH 2023 abstract, Oriol et al.

reason: Renal sinus fat on MRI is a noisy measure in a small trial, and weight loss is blunted in CKD patients with type 2 diabetes, so the fall could be too small or too variable to reach significance.
rationale: Tirzepatide gives roughly 12-18% weight loss over a year and large MRI-measured falls in liver and visceral fat (SURPASS-3 MRI); renal sinus fat tracks visceral fat and fell with far smaller weight loss in lifestyle trials. A placebo-adjusted fall of 15-20% should be detectable with 50-60 completers per arm unless between-patient noise in the percent change is very large. Weight loss is blunted in CKD with type 2 diabetes, and missed scans cut power. The trial completed in July 2026, so a congress report or the registry posting should come by mid-2027.
evidence: CENTRAL MRI trial, Zelicha et al. 2018

assumptions.claim: In SURPASS-3 MRI, pooled tirzepatide 10 and 15 mg reduced liver fat content by about 8 percentage points at week 52 versus about 3 points with insulin degludec.
assumptions.source: SURPASS-3 MRI, Gastaldelli et al., Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol 2022 (NCT03882970)

assumptions.claim: In SURMOUNT-2 (obesity with type 2 diabetes), tirzepatide 15 mg reduced body weight by 14.7% versus 3.2% with placebo at 72 weeks.
In the 18-month CENTRAL MRI weight-loss trial, renal sinus fat decreased with moderate weight loss.
assumptions.source: Zelicha et al., Clin Nutr 2018 (CENTRAL MRI trial)

reason: With about 11 artesunate and 6 placebo patients, only a near-complete separation in response rates would be statistically significant, and some placebo lesions regress after biopsy.
rationale: Only 17 patients were enrolled and randomized 2:1, about 11 versus 6. Even if artesunate gives the high histologic response suggested by the open-label phase 1, Fisher's exact test needs something like 9/11 versus 1/6 to reach p<0.05, and placebo lesions do regress after biopsy (SPANC clearance 22 per 100 person-years, more once partial response counts). A small sponsor may report descriptively, which counts as not met. A public result by June 2027 is unlikely; the registry posting is due only at the end of 2027.
evidence: Artesunate suppositories phase 1 in anal HSIL, Fang et al. 2023 (NCT03100045)

assumptions.claim: In the SPANC cohort, anal HSIL cleared spontaneously at about 22 per 100 person-years.
assumptions.source: SPANC, Poynten et al., Lancet Infect Dis 2021

assumptions.claim: The phase 1 trial of intra-anal artesunate suppositories for anal HSIL was open label with no placebo arm and reported histologic responses in most evaluable participants.

reason: Twelve patients per arm on top of full-dose acetylcysteine cannot separate the arms on a highly skewed ALT percent change that one or two late presenters dominate.
rationale: Exploratory single-site study, 12 per arm, on top of full-dose IV acetylcysteine. Most patients treated early have little ALT rise, while a few late presenters rise many hundred percent, so the mean percent change at day 3 is driven by one or two patients and a significant difference is very unlikely even if the CYP2E1-inhibiting ingredients work. Enrolment has been open since May 2023 at one hospital and is not finished, so completion will probably slip and a public result before 2028 is unlikely.
evidence: Smilkstein et al., NEJM 1988 (oral acetylcysteine in acetaminophen overdose)

assumptions.claim: In patients at probable risk, hepatotoxicity developed in about 6% when acetylcysteine was started within 10 hours of ingestion and about 26% when started at 10-24 hours.

reason: A single intracoronary AAV dose has to improve death, NYHA class, LVEF and walk distance together against a blinded placebo arm that usually improves on the soft measures, and earlier calcium-cycling gene therapy failed.
rationale: Four primaries are listed (cardiovascular death, NYHA class, LVEF and 6-minute walk at 52 weeks), probably analysed as a hierarchical composite; either way AB-1002 must win with 30-50 patients per arm. The evidence so far is a small open-label phase 1. Cardiac gene therapy has a poor record: CUPID 2 (AAV1/SERCA2a), aimed at the same calcium-cycling pathway, was neutral in 250 patients. Blinded placebo arms improve on NYHA class and walk distance, and cardiovascular death alone cannot reach significance with a handful of events.

assumptions.claim: CUPID 2 randomized 250 patients to intracoronary AAV1/SERCA2a or placebo and found no reduction in recurrent heart-failure events (hazard ratio 0.93).
The first-in-human trial of AB-1002 was open label with no control arm.

reason: Adding LAG-3 blockade to PD-1 gave no relapse-free survival gain in adjuvant melanoma in RELATIVITY-098, and pembrolizumab is a strong active control.
rationale: The closest precedent is negative: RELATIVITY-098, adjuvant relatlimab plus nivolumab versus nivolumab in resected stage III-IV melanoma, showed no relapse-free survival benefit. Fianlimab plus cemiplimab must beat pembrolizumab, an active control with 12-month RFS of 75% in stage III and 90% in stage IIB/C. I also recall, unverified, that Regeneron's first-line metastatic phase 3 missed significance on PFS in 2026. The registered primary completion passed in July 2026 with no announcement, which is not what an early win looks like.
evidence: Fianlimab plus cemiplimab first-line melanoma phase 3 (NCT05352672)

assumptions.claim: RELATIVITY-098, adjuvant nivolumab plus relatlimab versus nivolumab in resected stage III-IV melanoma, did not meet its primary endpoint of relapse-free survival.
In KEYNOTE-054, 12-month relapse-free survival was 75.4% with adjuvant pembrolizumab versus 61.0% with placebo.
In KEYNOTE-716 (stage IIB/IIC), 12-month relapse-free survival was about 90% with pembrolizumab versus 83% with placebo.

reason: A placebo SRI(4) rate in the mid-40s, common in global lupus trials on background therapy, would shrink the phase 2 difference below what 516 patients can detect.
rationale: PAISLEY phase 2 was unusually strong for lupus: SRI(4) at week 32 was 58% with deucravacitinib 3 mg twice daily versus 34% with placebo, with BICLA, LLDAS, skin and joint measures agreeing and the gain held to week 48. TYK2 inhibition blocks type I interferon signalling, a pathway validated by anifrolumab. With about 258 per arm the trial needs roughly 8.5 points; I expect 10-14 after shrinkage. Against that, lupus phase 3 pairs often split (TULIP-1, SLE-BRAVE-II) when placebo response reaches the mid-40s, and PAISLEY showed no dose-response.

assumptions.claim: In PAISLEY, SRI(4) response at week 32 was 58% with deucravacitinib 3 mg twice daily versus 34% with placebo.
assumptions.source: PAISLEY, Morand et al., Arthritis Rheumatol 2023 (NCT03252587)

assumptions.claim: In TULIP-2, the placebo SRI(4) response at week 52 was about 37%.
In SLE-BRAVE-II, baricitinib 4 mg did not differ from placebo on SRI-4 at week 52 (about 47% versus 46%).

reason: A high placebo SRI(4) rate in a global trial on stable background therapy, as in TULIP-1 and SLE-BRAVE-II, could leave the difference below the roughly 8.5 points this sample can detect.
rationale: Twin of POETYK SLE-1 with the same dose, endpoint and size. Phase 2 PAISLEY gave a 24-point SRI(4) gain at week 32 for 3 mg twice daily and a 22-point BICLA gain at week 48, consistent across skin, joints and low disease activity. Even halved, that effect clears the roughly 8.5 points needed with 513 patients. The main threat is a high placebo rate on background therapy, as in TULIP-1 and SLE-BRAVE-II, plus the absent dose-response in phase 2. I give both trials the same odds; one of two failing is plausible.

assumptions.claim: In PAISLEY, BICLA response at week 48 was about 47% with deucravacitinib 3 mg twice daily versus about 26% with placebo.
assumptions.source: PAISLEY, Morand et al., Arthritis Rheumatol 2023 (NCT03252587)

assumptions.claim: TULIP-1 did not meet its primary endpoint: SRI(4) at week 52 was 36% with anifrolumab versus 40% with placebo.
assumptions.source: TULIP-1, Furie et al., Lancet Rheumatol 2019 (NCT02446912)

assumptions.claim: In SLE-BRAVE-I, SRI-4 at week 52 was 57% with baricitinib 4 mg versus 46% with placebo.

reason: A subjective voice-handicap score in 62 patients with a sham injection control leaves little room: placebo improvement may be large and the true HGF effect on established scar modest.
rationale: The only earlier evidence is an open-label phase 1/2 in 18 patients with no placebo arm, where VHI-10 improved across dose groups, a pattern an injection or placebo effect would also produce. This trial has 31 per arm, a patient-reported endpoint and a sham intracordal injection that can itself change the voice for a while. Established scar and sulcus are hard to remodel. An antifibrotic effect of HGF is plausible from animal work, so success is possible, but small sham-controlled confirmatory trials after uncontrolled data fail more often than not.
evidence: Intracordal HGF phase I/II for vocal fold scar, Hirano et al. 2018
KP-100IT phase 1/2 in acute spinal cord injury, Nagoshi et al. 2020

assumptions.claim: The phase I/II study of intracordal recombinant human HGF for vocal fold scar and sulcus enrolled 18 patients, was open label and had no placebo arm.
assumptions.source: Hirano et al., J Tissue Eng Regen Med 2018

reason: The trial has about 145 patients per arm, so a true SRI-4 gain of around 12 points over a placebo rate near 40% could miss significance by chance.
rationale: Phase 2 was small but clear: the week-28 composite of SRI-4 with steroid reduction was 44% with monthly ianalumab versus 9% with placebo. B-cell targeting has phase 3 support in SLE (belimumab BLISS trials, obinutuzumab ALLEGORY), and ianalumab adds BAFF-receptor blockade to depletion; its Sjogren's phase 3 trials were positive. With about 145 per arm the trial needs roughly 11 points over a placebo rate near 40%, so a true gain of 12-16 points leaves real risk of a chance miss. Readout follows primary completion in late March 2027.

assumptions.claim: In the phase 2 trial, the week-28 composite of SRI-4 with sustained corticosteroid reduction was reached by 44.1% on ianalumab versus 9.1% on placebo.
assumptions.source: NCT03656562, Shen et al., ACR Convergence 2023 abstract

assumptions.claim: In BLISS-52, SRI response at week 52 was 58% with belimumab 10 mg/kg versus 44% with placebo.
ALLEGORY, obinutuzumab versus placebo in SLE, met its primary endpoint of SRI-4 response at week 52.

reason: Slow paediatric enrolment across four sequential age cohorts (down to 9 months) makes a slip of the March 2027 primary completion date about as likely as not; termination and early results posting are unlikely.
rationale: Operations only. Pfizer paediatric phase 2a with four sequential age cohorts of 12 and 3:1 randomisation, recruiting since April 2023 at 22 sites and still open after 3.5 years. Paediatric gram-negative infection PK studies often slip, especially the cohort under 2 years, so I put about even odds on completion moving beyond June 2027. Regulatory paediatric commitments are rarely terminated. Posting results within five months of primary completion is unlikely. The primary outcomes are standard PK and safety measures with little reason to change.

reason: About 60 patients per arm against an adult effect of only 8-13 percentage points and a variable paediatric placebo response leaves power well under 50%.
rationale: Adult T3MPO trials showed only 8-13 pp gains on the 6/12-week combined responder endpoint with about 300 patients per arm. This trial has about 60 per arm, so power is roughly 25-45% even if the adult effect carries over, and paediatric functional bowel trials show high, variable placebo response. Two active doses give a modest second chance. The study mainly fulfils a paediatric regulatory commitment and may not be powered for significance. It completed in August 2026; disclosure probably comes through a filing, DDW or the registry.

assumptions.claim: In T3MPO-1 the 6/12-week combined responder rate was 27.0% with tenapanor 50 mg twice daily versus 18.7% with placebo.
assumptions.source: T3MPO-1, Chey et al., Am J Gastroenterol 2020

assumptions.claim: In T3MPO-2 the 6/12-week combined responder rate was 36.5% with tenapanor versus 23.7% with placebo.
assumptions.source: T3MPO-2, Chey et al., Am J Gastroenterol 2021

assumptions.claim: In T3MPO-2, 6.5% of tenapanor patients versus 0.7% of placebo patients discontinued because of diarrhoea.
assumptions.source: T3MPO-2, Chey et al., Am J Gastroenterol 2021

reason: Alpelisib plus fulvestrant is an active same-class comparator and cross-trial efficacy looks similar, so the hazard ratio may not be far enough below 1 to reach significance with about 270 events.
rationale: Head-to-head against an active PI3K-alpha inhibitor. Cross-trial, inavolisib plus fulvestrant (phase 1, PFS about 7 months) resembles alpelisib plus fulvestrant after CDK4/6 inhibitors (BYLieve 7.3 months), so superiority must come from better tolerability and dose intensity (alpelisib discontinuation 20-25% versus about 6%) and mutant p110-alpha degradation. I centre the true HR near 0.83; with about 270 events the trial needs an observed HR below about 0.79. The registered primary completion of November 2026 points to a readout in early 2027.

assumptions.claim: In BYLieve cohort A (after a CDK4/6 inhibitor plus aromatase inhibitor), alpelisib plus fulvestrant gave a median PFS of 7.3 months.
assumptions.source: BYLieve, Rugo et al., Lancet Oncol 2021

assumptions.claim: In SOLAR-1, 25% of patients stopped alpelisib because of adverse events.
assumptions.source: SOLAR-1, Andre et al., N Engl J Med 2019

assumptions.claim: In INAVO120, 6.8% of patients in the inavolisib arm stopped any trial agent because of adverse events, and the PFS hazard ratio versus placebo was 0.43.
assumptions.source: INAVO120, Turner et al., N Engl J Med 2024

reason: The phase 2b signal was small and only nominally significant at 4 mg, so the true SRI-4 gain over a placebo rate near 45% may be too small to reach significance.
rationale: Cenerimod's phase 2b CARE study missed its multiplicity-adjusted primary; only 4 mg showed a nominal 1.2-point mSLEDAI-2K gain at 6 months, with stronger signals in interferon-high patients. Phase 3 tests 4 mg for 12 months in about 470 patients, which gives good power only if the SRI-4 difference reaches 10-12 pp; I expect about 6 pp against a placebo rate near 45% in regions with high placebo response. SLE phase 3 history on SRI-4 (baricitinib, TULIP-1) adds caution. Twin trial OPUS-2 shares the risk.

assumptions.claim: In the phase 2b CARE study, cenerimod 4 mg changed mSLEDAI-2K at month 6 by -4.04 versus -2.85 with placebo (difference -1.19, nominal p=0.029), which was not significant after multiplicity adjustment.
assumptions.source: CARE, NCT03742037, Askanase et al., Lancet Rheumatol 2025

assumptions.claim: Placebo SRI-4 response at week 52 was about 40% in TULIP-1 and 37% in TULIP-2.
assumptions.source: TULIP-1 (Furie et al., Lancet Rheumatol 2019) and TULIP-2 (Morand et al., N Engl J Med 2020)

assumptions.claim: In SLE-BRAVE-II, baricitinib 4 mg did not beat placebo on SRI-4 at week 52 (47% versus 46%).

reason: With about 75 patients per arm, two doses sharing alpha and a stringent 12-month off-treatment endpoint, a real benefit of 15-20 points could still miss significance.
rationale: B-cell depletion added to first-line steroids has precedent: rituximab plus dexamethasone raised 6-month sustained response from 36% to 63%. Ianalumab was positive in second-line VAYHIT2 (time to treatment failure HR 0.55; stable response 62% versus 39%). The primary was switched in May 2026, before unblinding, to a stringent 12-month off-treatment stable response. With about 75 per arm and two doses sharing alpha, a true difference near 20 pp gives roughly 65-75% power. Novartis has guided to an ITP filing in 2027 that includes this trial.

assumptions.claim: In VAYHIT2, ianalumab 9 mg/kg plus eltrombopag prolonged time to treatment failure versus placebo plus eltrombopag with a hazard ratio of 0.55.
assumptions.source: VAYHIT2, NCT05653219, ASH 2025 / N Engl J Med 2025

assumptions.claim: In VAYHIT2, stable response at 6 months was 62.0% with ianalumab 9 mg/kg versus 39.2% with placebo.
assumptions.source: VAYHIT2, NCT05653219, ASH 2025 / N Engl J Med 2025

assumptions.claim: In newly diagnosed ITP, rituximab plus dexamethasone gave a sustained response at 6 months in 63% versus 36% with dexamethasone alone.

reason: PANOVA-3 suggests only a modest survival effect (HR 0.82), so a trial of this size could easily miss significance; the final analysis is also unlikely to be ready by mid-2027.
rationale: PANOVA-3 showed a modest OS gain for tumor treating fields plus gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel in locally advanced pancreatic cancer (HR 0.82, p=0.039) without a significant PFS gain, so the true effect is probably HR 0.85-0.90. A 512-patient trial has about 35-50% power for that. The record still shows recruiting two months before its registered completion at five Chinese sites, so a final OS analysis by mid-2027 is unlikely; an early public result would most likely be a positive interim or company announcement.

assumptions.claim: In PANOVA-3, tumor treating fields plus gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel gave a median OS of 16.2 versus 14.2 months (HR 0.82, p=0.039).
assumptions.source: PANOVA-3, NCT03377491, Babiker et al., J Clin Oncol 2025

assumptions.claim: In PANOVA-3, progression-free survival was not significantly improved (median 10.6 versus 9.3 months).
assumptions.source: PANOVA-3, NCT03377491, Babiker et al., J Clin Oncol 2025

reason: Equivalence is very likely if the product is truly similar; the main risk is a chance difference in response rates pushing the confidence interval outside the margin.
rationale: Bevacizumab biosimilar equivalence trials in first-line non-squamous NSCLC using ORR at about week 18 have almost uniformly met their margins (ABP 215, PF-06439535, SB8). With 620 patients and expected ORR near 40%, power is around 85-90% for typical margins if the products are truly similar. Residual risk is chance imbalance or product differences from a newer manufacturer. The record still shows recruiting with completion due December 2026, so delay is likely, and public reporting by a Russian sponsor is usually slow.

assumptions.claim: In the ABP 215 biosimilar trial in non-squamous NSCLC, ORR was 39.0% with ABP 215 versus 41.7% with reference bevacizumab, within the equivalence margin.
assumptions.source: MAPLE, Thatcher et al., Clin Cancer Res 2019

assumptions.claim: In the PF-06439535 biosimilar trial, ORR by week 19 was 45.3% versus 44.6% with reference bevacizumab.
In E4599, adding bevacizumab to carboplatin and paclitaxel raised the response rate to 35% from 15%.
assumptions.source: E4599, Sandler et al., N Engl J Med 2006

reason: Efficacy rests on an uncontrolled open-label study; against a placebo arm that improves naturally by 72 hours with rescue analgesia, the true difference may be only a few millimetres.
rationale: Evidence for dapansutrile in flares is one open-label, uncontrolled phase 2a study (52-68% pain reduction by day 3), which cannot be separated from natural resolution. IL-1 blockade works in flares, but NLRP3 inhibition acts upstream and neutrophil proteases can activate IL-1 beta independently. Placebo patients enrolled up to 96 hours after onset with rescue analgesia improve substantially by 72 hours. With 200 versus 100 patients and SD about 27 mm, a true 6-8 mm difference gives 45-65% power. Recruitment since January 2023 has been slow.
evidence: Kluck et al., dapansutrile phase 2a, Lancet Rheumatol 2020

assumptions.claim: In the open-label phase 2a study, mean target-joint pain fell by 52-68% at day 3 across dapansutrile doses of 100-2000 mg/day, with no placebo arm.
In the beta-RELIEVED trials, mean 72-hour pain on a 100-mm VAS was 25.0 mm with canakinumab versus 35.7 mm with triamcinolone (difference -10.7 mm).
assumptions.source: beta-RELIEVED and beta-RELIEVED II, Schlesinger et al., Ann Rheum Dis 2012

reason: The phase 2b signal was small and only nominally significant at 4 mg, so the true SRI-4 gain over a placebo rate near 45% may be too small to reach significance.
rationale: Cenerimod's phase 2b CARE study missed its multiplicity-adjusted primary; only 4 mg showed a nominal 1.2-point mSLEDAI-2K gain at 6 months, with stronger signals in interferon-high patients. Phase 3 tests 4 mg for 12 months in about 450 patients, which gives good power only if the SRI-4 difference reaches 10-12 pp; I expect about 6 pp against a placebo rate near 45% in regions with high placebo response. SLE phase 3 history on SRI-4 (baricitinib, TULIP-1) adds caution. Twin trial OPUS-1 shares the risk.

assumptions.claim: In the phase 2b CARE study, cenerimod 4 mg changed mSLEDAI-2K at month 6 by -4.04 versus -2.85 with placebo (difference -1.19, nominal p=0.029), which was not significant after multiplicity adjustment.
assumptions.source: CARE, NCT03742037, Askanase et al., Lancet Rheumatol 2025

assumptions.claim: Placebo SRI-4 response at week 52 was about 40% in TULIP-1 and 37% in TULIP-2.
assumptions.source: TULIP-1 (Furie et al., Lancet Rheumatol 2019) and TULIP-2 (Morand et al., N Engl J Med 2020)

assumptions.claim: In SLE-BRAVE-II, baricitinib 4 mg did not beat placebo on SRI-4 at week 52 (47% versus 46%).

reason: Only 100 patients (2:1) and three registered primary measures: the itch score, with the smallest adult effect, could miss significance even if UAS7 succeeds.
rationale: Remibrutinib gave consistent UAS7 gains of 6-8 points over placebo at week 12 in adult REMIX-1 and REMIX-2, and BTK inhibition should work similarly in adolescents at matched exposure. With 67 versus 33 patients and SD about 12.5, power is about 70-80% for UAS7 alone; requiring ISS7 and HSS7 as well lowers it, because the itch component had the smaller adult effect. Adolescent placebo response is uncertain. Enrolment is complete and primary completion was due in November 2026.

assumptions.claim: In REMIX-1 the change in UAS7 at week 12 was -20.0 with remibrutinib versus -13.8 with placebo, and in REMIX-2 it was -19.4 versus -11.7.
assumptions.source: REMIX-1 and REMIX-2, Metz et al., N Engl J Med 2025

assumptions.claim: UAS7 of 6 or less at week 12 was reached by 49.8% versus 24.8% in REMIX-1 and 46.8% versus 19.6% in REMIX-2.
assumptions.source: REMIX-1 and REMIX-2, Metz et al., N Engl J Med 2025

reason: Mixed non-clear-cell histologies (papillary, unclassified, translocation) may dilute the TKI plus checkpoint-inhibitor benefit, and early censoring in an open-label sunitinib arm under central review could narrow the PFS gap in a 317-patient trial.
rationale: Sunitinib is a weak comparator in non-clear-cell RCC (median PFS about 5.6-8 months in PAPMET, ESPN and ASPEN). Cabozantinib beat sunitinib in papillary RCC (HR 0.60), and TKI plus PD-1 combinations gave response rates near 50% and median PFS of 12-18 months in single-arm studies. Zanzalintinib is cabozantinib-like and active with nivolumab in clear-cell disease. About 190 events give high power for a hazard ratio of 0.6-0.7. ORR, the second primary, should clearly favour the combination. Slow event accrual against the registered time frame is neutral to favourable.
evidence: Cabozantinib plus nivolumab in nccRCC, phase 2, Lee 2022 (NCT03635892)
STELLAR-002 zanzalintinib plus nivolumab clear-cell cohort (NCT05176483)

assumptions.claim: In SWOG S1500 (PAPMET), median PFS in metastatic papillary RCC was 5.6 months with sunitinib and 9.0 months with cabozantinib (hazard ratio 0.60).
Cabozantinib plus nivolumab gave an objective response rate of 47.5% and a median PFS of 12.5 months in the papillary, unclassified and translocation-associated cohort of a phase 2 nccRCC trial.
assumptions.source: Lee et al., J Clin Oncol 2022 (NCT03635892)

assumptions.claim: First-line lenvatinib plus pembrolizumab gave an objective response rate of about 49% in non-clear-cell RCC in KEYNOTE-B61.
assumptions.source: KEYNOTE-B61, Albiges et al., Lancet Oncol 2023 (NCT04704219)

reason: With only 94 children and an event-driven time-to-first-exacerbation endpoint, the trial has power only for a very large effect, while anti-IL-5 pathway drugs have shown modest or no exacerbation benefit in children and adolescents.
rationale: Benralizumab cut exacerbations by 28-51% in adults (SIROCCO, CALIMA), but the pooled adolescent subgroup showed no benefit, and mepolizumab gave only a 27% rate reduction in children (MUPPITS-2). A 94-patient event-driven trial with about 45 first exacerbations has roughly 80% power only for a hazard ratio near 0.4; at a more plausible 0.65-0.7, power is 25-35%. Enrichment for eosinophilia and frequent exacerbations helps somewhat. Small paediatric trials also show strong placebo-arm improvement and chance imbalance.

assumptions.claim: In SIROCCO, benralizumab every 8 weeks reduced the annual asthma exacerbation rate by 51% versus placebo in patients with blood eosinophils of at least 300 cells per microlitre.
In MUPPITS-2, mepolizumab reduced the annualised exacerbation rate in urban children aged 6-17 years with eosinophilic exacerbation-prone asthma from 1.30 to 0.96 per year (rate ratio 0.73).
Among adolescents aged 12-17 years in the SIROCCO and CALIMA trials, benralizumab did not reduce the exacerbation rate versus placebo (rate ratio above 1).
assumptions.source: Fasenra US prescribing information, paediatric use section; SIROCCO and CALIMA 2016

reason: Milvexian 25 mg twice daily gives less factor XIa inhibition than the asundexian dose that worked in OCEANIC-STROKE, the same dose was futile in LIBREXIA-ACS, and the trial includes lacunar strokes, so the stroke reduction may be too small to reach significance.
rationale: Factor XIa inhibition is validated in this setting: asundexian cut ischemic stroke by about a quarter (HR 0.74) in OCEANIC-STROKE, a similar design. In AXIOMATIC-SSP, symptomatic ischemic stroke was about 30% lower at 25-100 mg twice daily. With roughly 870 events, power exceeds 85% for a hazard ratio of 0.80 and is about 60% for 0.85. The monitoring committee let the trial continue in November 2025 when it stopped LIBREXIA-ACS. The main doubts are the low 25 mg dose and a broader, lower-risk population.

assumptions.claim: In OCEANIC-STROKE, asundexian 50 mg once daily on top of antiplatelet therapy reduced ischemic stroke versus placebo (6.2% vs 8.4%; hazard ratio 0.74).
assumptions.source: OCEANIC-STROKE, presented at the International Stroke Conference 2026 (NCT05686070)

assumptions.claim: In AXIOMATIC-SSP, milvexian showed no dose-response on the composite of symptomatic ischemic stroke or covert brain infarction at 90 days, but symptomatic ischemic stroke was numerically lower than placebo at 25 to 100 mg twice daily.
assumptions.source: AXIOMATIC-SSP, Sharma et al., Lancet Neurol 2024 (NCT03766581)

assumptions.claim: In November 2025 LIBREXIA-ACS was stopped for futility at an interim analysis, while the independent data monitoring committee recommended that LIBREXIA-STROKE and LIBREXIA-AF continue.
assumptions.source: Bristol Myers Squibb and Johnson & Johnson announcement, November 2025 (NCT05754957)

reason: The trial is still recruiting a rare FGFR2-rearranged population weeks before its registered December 2026 primary completion, so the date will most likely slip well into 2027; termination is unlikely because the study is a post-approval commitment.
rationale: The record is still recruiting in late October 2026 with primary completion registered for December 2026. ORR by central review needs months of follow-up after the last patient, so a move past March 2027 is likely. The study confirms futibatinib's accelerated approval and tests a lower dose, so the sponsor has a regulatory reason to finish it. Posting results by August 2027 would need completion and a fast submission. The single ORR primary outcome is unlikely to change.

assumptions.claim: Futibatinib 20 mg daily gave an objective response rate of 42% in previously treated intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma with FGFR2 fusions or rearrangements, the basis of its accelerated approval.
assumptions.source: FOENIX-CCA2, Goyal et al., N Engl J Med 2023 (NCT02052778)

reason: Factor XIa inhibition may protect less against cardioembolic stroke than factor Xa inhibition, as asundexian showed in OCEANIC-AF, so even a modest excess of strokes over apixaban would breach the non-inferiority margin.
rationale: Asundexian was clearly inferior to apixaban in OCEANIC-AF (HR 3.79), so the class prior is poor. Against that, milvexian is dosed higher (100 mg twice daily), and LIBREXIA-AF has run to its planned end through repeated monitoring reviews, including November 2025, which argues against gross inferiority. Non-inferiority still needs an observed hazard ratio at or below roughly 1.15 with about 480 events against a strong comparator; the margin is not in the record. Bleeding should be clearly lower. I put success slightly below even.

assumptions.claim: OCEANIC-AF was stopped early because asundexian 50 mg once daily was inferior to apixaban for stroke or systemic embolism (hazard ratio 3.79).
assumptions.source: OCEANIC-AF, Piccini et al., N Engl J Med 2024 (NCT05643573)

assumptions.claim: In OCEANIC-AF, ISTH major bleeding was lower with asundexian than with apixaban (hazard ratio 0.32).
assumptions.source: OCEANIC-AF, Piccini et al., N Engl J Med 2024 (NCT05643573)

assumptions.claim: In ARISTOTLE, the rate of stroke or systemic embolism with apixaban was 1.27% per year.
assumptions.source: ARISTOTLE, Granger et al., N Engl J Med 2011 (NCT00412984)

reason: Boosting the glucagon response with a somatostatin receptor 2 antagonist may blunt rather than prevent CGM-defined events below 54 mg/dL, leaving a rate reduction too small to detect over a 28-day crossover period.
rationale: ZT-01 raised glucagon during clamped hypoglycemia in a phase 1b study in type 1 diabetes, so the target is engaged, but I know of no public outpatient efficacy data. Night-time lows are driven mainly by insulin excess, and a restored counter-regulatory response may shorten events more than prevent them. The crossover design, three doses (one is enough) and a hypoglycemia-prone population help power. First-in-class phase 2a base rates argue for under even odds; a small private sponsor is more likely to publicise a positive result.
evidence: ZT-01 phase 1b hypoglycemic clamp study in type 1 diabetes, 2022

assumptions.claim: In a phase 1b crossover study in adults with type 1 diabetes, ZT-01 increased the glucagon response to insulin-induced hypoglycemia compared with placebo.
assumptions.source: Zucara Therapeutics phase 1b study of ZT-01, reported 2022 and published 2024

reason: An oral microbiome product is unlikely to cut 12-month all-cause mortality by the 35-40% that a 387-patient trial needs, since relapse and causes unrelated to the gut microbiota account for many deaths after reduced-intensity transplant.
rationale: Low gut microbiota diversity predicts mortality after allogeneic transplant (Peled 2020), but no randomized trial has shown that restoring it improves survival, and a placebo-controlled oral FMT trial did not reduce infections. Twelve-month overall survival is a hard endpoint: about 100 deaths give adequate power only for a hazard ratio near 0.6. Safety board reviews letting the trial continue say little about efficacy. The trial was still recruiting in late 2026, so the 12-month readout probably falls in late 2027 or later.
evidence: Peled et al., N Engl J Med 2020
Rashidi et al., J Clin Oncol 2023 (NCT03678493)
ARES phase 3 of MaaT013 in GvHD (NCT04769895)

assumptions.claim: Higher intestinal microbiota diversity around engraftment was associated with a lower risk of death after allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation (hazard ratio about 0.71 in the first cohort).
assumptions.source: Peled et al., N Engl J Med 2020

assumptions.claim: A randomized, placebo-controlled trial of oral third-party fecal microbiota transplantation after allogeneic transplant or AML induction did not reduce the infection rate, its primary endpoint.
assumptions.source: Rashidi et al., J Clin Oncol 2023 (NCT03678493)

reason: Diary-based incontinence endpoints show large placebo and sham-injection responses, which sank the sponsor's earlier stress urinary incontinence trial, so a real cell effect may not separate from placebo at 12 months.
rationale: Autologous muscle cell injection has small-trial support in fecal incontinence: a French randomized study found a 12-month response of 58% versus 8% with placebo. But the same sponsor's product failed to beat placebo in stress urinary incontinence because most placebo patients improved, and sham responses of 30% or more are usual in fecal incontinence trials. Selecting women with obstetric sphincter injury and a 12-month endpoint help, and 200 patients give moderate power for a diary-based outcome.
evidence: Autologous muscle-derived cells in stress urinary incontinence, Jankowski 2018

assumptions.claim: In a randomized placebo-controlled phase 2 trial of intrasphincteric autologous myoblasts for fecal incontinence, the response rate at 12 months was 58% with cells versus 8% with placebo.
assumptions.source: MIAS trial, Boyer et al., Ann Surg 2018

assumptions.claim: A randomized placebo-controlled trial of autologous muscle-derived cells for female stress urinary incontinence stopped enrolment at 150 patients because of a very high placebo response and showed no difference on its primary endpoint.
assumptions.source: Jankowski et al., Int Urol Nephrol 2018

assumptions.claim: In the randomized sham-controlled trial of NASHA/Dx for fecal incontinence, 52% of treated patients versus 31% of sham patients had at least a 50% reduction in incontinence episodes.

reason: The registered December 2026 date implies an early look when invasive disease events are still few, so a true benefit of the size seen with abemaciclib or ribociclib may not yet cross an interim boundary.
rationale: Continuously dosed CDK4/6 inhibitors improve adjuvant IDFS: abemaciclib (monarchE, HR 0.75 then 0.68) and ribociclib (NATALEE, HR 0.75); palbociclib did not. TQB3616 is given continuously, is active in advanced disease, and the trial has 1,946 patients randomized 2:1. A result public by mid-2027 would most likely be a positive interim analysis, because a negative interim would continue without announcement; that raises the conditional probability. The final analysis probably needs about 300 events and may come later.

assumptions.claim: In monarchE, adjuvant abemaciclib plus endocrine therapy improved invasive disease-free survival versus endocrine therapy alone (hazard ratio 0.75 at the first interim analysis).
assumptions.source: monarchE, Johnston et al., J Clin Oncol 2020 (NCT03155997)

assumptions.claim: In NATALEE, ribociclib plus a nonsteroidal aromatase inhibitor improved invasive disease-free survival (hazard ratio 0.75), with 3-year rates of 90.4% versus 87.1%.
assumptions.source: NATALEE, Slamon et al., N Engl J Med 2024 (NCT03701334)

assumptions.claim: In PALLAS, adding two years of palbociclib to adjuvant endocrine therapy did not improve invasive disease-free survival.
assumptions.source: PALLAS, Mayer et al., Lancet Oncol 2021 (NCT02513394)

reason: Lupus trials on background therapy often see placebo BICLA responses of 30-40%, and with two replicate studies of about 250 per arm one of them could miss even if the drug works, as happened with baricitinib.
rationale: Upadacitinib 30 mg met the phase 2 SLEek primary endpoint (54.8% versus 37.3%) and showed large week-48 gains on BICLA, SRI-4, flares and LLDAS. Placebo BICLA at week 52 is usually 30-35% (TULIP-2: 31.5%), so a 13-15 point difference gives roughly 80-90% power per study. Baricitinib's split result across two phase 3 studies is the caution. The record covers two replicate studies, so a mixed outcome is possible; my estimate weights both succeeding.

assumptions.claim: In the phase 2 SLEek trial, upadacitinib 30 mg met the primary endpoint at week 24 (SRI-4 with a glucocorticoid dose of 10 mg/day or less: 54.8% versus 37.3% with placebo).
assumptions.source: SLEek, Merrill et al., Arthritis Rheumatol 2024 (NCT03978520)

assumptions.claim: In TULIP-2, the BICLA response at week 52 was 31.5% with placebo and 47.8% with anifrolumab.
assumptions.source: TULIP-2, Morand et al., N Engl J Med 2020 (NCT02446899)

assumptions.claim: Baricitinib 4 mg met the SRI-4 primary endpoint in SLE-BRAVE-I but not in SLE-BRAVE-II.

reason: Small non-comparative Novartis phase 2 with enrolment closed at 49 and a fixed end date of 23 Dec 2026; it should end on schedule, with some chance it is labelled terminated and little chance results post before late 2027.
rationale: Active, not recruiting, with primary and study completion both set to one specific day (2026-12-23), which reads as a planned last-visit date, so slippage beyond 90 days is unlikely. Enrolment of 49 across 31 sites looks curtailed, so a 'terminated' label at closure is possible. Novartis usually posts results about 12 months after primary completion, which is after the 31 Aug 2027 read date. The primary outcome wording is unlikely to change in substance.

reason: About 62 patients per arm gives a standard error near 70 mL on FEV1, so a dose must show roughly 140 mL over placebo; an oral JAK1 inhibitor in a population not enriched for eosinophilic disease may deliver only about 100 mL.
rationale: JAK1 inhibition blocks IL-4/IL-13/TSLP signalling, so a lung-function effect is biologically plausible, and povorcitinib was positive in HS phase 3. But there is no prior oral JAK1 asthma efficacy trial, the population is not T2-selected, placebo FEV1 gains are often 100-200 mL, and each arm has only ~62 patients. Dupilumab's FEV1 gain in an all-comer population was ~130-140 mL. Three doses give several chances. Incyte usually discloses phase 2 toplines within months.

assumptions.claim: In LIBERTY ASTHMA QUEST, dupilumab improved pre-bronchodilator FEV1 at week 12 by about 0.13-0.14 L over placebo in the overall population.
Placebo arms in LIBERTY ASTHMA QUEST gained about 0.18-0.21 L in pre-bronchodilator FEV1 by week 12.
Povorcitinib met the primary endpoint (HiSCR50 at week 12) in both phase 3 hidradenitis suppurativa trials.

reason: Adding LAG-3 blockade to PD-1 has not clearly beaten PD-1 alone outside melanoma, and with 83 patients a hazard ratio near 0.6 would be needed for significance against an active pembrolizumab control.
rationale: An 83-patient phase 2 against pembrolizumab plus nab-paclitaxel is an estimation study: about 55-60 PFS events need an observed HR near 0.6 for two-sided p<0.05. LAG-3 co-blockade has added to PD-1 clearly only in melanoma (RELATIVITY-047), and Roche has not moved tobemstomig into phase 3. Control median PFS should sit near KEYNOTE-355's 9.7 months for CPS>=10. Results most likely appear through registry posting about a year after primary completion or a minor congress abstract.

assumptions.claim: In KEYNOTE-355, pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy gave a median PFS of 9.7 months versus 5.6 months with chemotherapy alone in PD-L1 CPS>=10 tumours.
Relatlimab plus nivolumab improved PFS over nivolumab alone in untreated advanced melanoma with a hazard ratio of about 0.75.
In IMpassion130, adverse events led to discontinuation of any study treatment in about 16% of patients on atezolizumab plus nab-paclitaxel.

reason: A fully enrolled post-marketing dose-comparison study that should complete normally; BMS tends to post results close to the 12-month mark, which falls after the 31 Aug 2027 read date.
rationale: KRYSTAL-21 compares 600 mg and 400 mg twice-daily adagrasib descriptively, as a dose-optimisation study; 200 patients are enrolled and the trial is active, not recruiting, so an early stop is unlikely. Primary completion is registered for 30 Oct 2026, making results due around the end of October 2027; posting by 31 Aug 2027 needs an early submission plus registry review. The BICR-assessed ORR primary is unlikely to be redefined.

reason: Earlier positive OM-85 wheeze data come from small single-centre trials; in a rigorous multinational trial the true reduction may be nearer 15-20% than 38%, which 148 children per arm cannot reliably detect.
rationale: Razi 2010 showed a 38% fall in wheezing attacks with OM-85 in 75 preschoolers and the MV130 lysate trial showed about 40%, but prevention trials in infants (Sly 2019, ORBEX) were mixed. I assume a true rate ratio near 0.8, giving roughly 40% power with ~390 episodes; daily dosing for 6 months is more intensive than the usual regimen. A private sponsor is likelier to publicise a positive result early, which lifts the probability conditional on disclosure by June 2027.
evidence: Razi et al. 2010, J Allergy Clin Immunol (OM-85 in preschool wheeze)
Nieto et al. 2021, MV130 in recurrent wheezing (NCT01734811)
Sly et al. 2019, OM-85 in at-risk infants

assumptions.claim: OM-85 reduced the cumulative rate of wheezing attacks by 37.9% versus placebo over 12 months in 75 children aged 1-6 years with recurrent wheezing.
assumptions.source: Razi et al., J Allergy Clin Immunol 2010

assumptions.claim: The sublingual bacterial preparation MV130 reduced wheezing attacks by about 40% versus placebo in 120 children with recurrent wheezing.
assumptions.source: Nieto et al., Am J Respir Crit Care Med 2021 (NCT01734811)

assumptions.claim: In at-risk infants OM-85 did not significantly reduce the overall frequency of severe lower respiratory illnesses, although time to the first episode was longer.
assumptions.source: Sly et al., J Allergy Clin Immunol 2019

reason: Continuing CDK4/6 inhibition after progression on a CDK4/6 inhibitor has given at best a modest benefit (postMONARCH HR 0.73; PACE and PALMIRA negative), and the trial lists both ORR and PFS as primary outcomes.
rationale: SPH4336 is a CDK4/6 inhibitor tested with endocrine therapy after progression on a CDK4/6 inhibitor. In this setting postMONARCH and MAINTAIN were modestly positive, PACE and PALMIRA negative, so a true PFS hazard ratio around 0.75-0.8 and an ORR gain of 5-10 points seem likely; 254 patients give moderate power. The trial is still recruiting three years in at 22 Chinese sites, so a readout by mid-2027 is unlikely and would more probably be an early or partial disclosure.

assumptions.claim: In postMONARCH, abemaciclib plus fulvestrant improved PFS over fulvestrant alone after progression on a CDK4/6 inhibitor with a hazard ratio of 0.73.
In postMONARCH, the objective response rate in patients with measurable disease was about 17% with abemaciclib plus fulvestrant versus about 7% with fulvestrant alone.
In PACE, adding palbociclib to fulvestrant after progression on a CDK4/6 inhibitor did not improve PFS over fulvestrant alone.

reason: Nearly every drug tested to prevent cardiac-surgery AKI has failed in controlled trials, and with 120 per arm LSALT would need an absolute reduction of about 12 points on a noisy creatinine and urine-output endpoint.
rationale: LSALT (a DPEP-1 inhibitor) has no positive controlled efficacy data; its COVID-19 phase 2 showed no significant primary benefit. Cardiac-surgery AKI prevention has a poor record: teprasiran looked good in phase 2 and failed in phase 3, and ANG-3777 failed. With a placebo AKI rate near 35% and 120 per arm, significance needs roughly a 12-point absolute reduction. Arch is a micro-cap that press-releases toplines, but enrolment has been slow and the March 2027 completion may slip.

assumptions.claim: In the teprasiran phase 2 trial in high-risk cardiac surgery, AKI occurred in about 37% of teprasiran patients versus about 50% on placebo.
The phase 2 trial of LSALT peptide in hospitalised COVID-19 patients did not show a significant difference from placebo on its primary endpoint.
The phase 3 trial of teprasiran for prevention of major adverse kidney events after cardiac surgery did not meet its primary endpoint.

reason: Both primaries must be met: non-inferior 18-month rPFS, with few events and an unstated margin, and a diary-based percent change in hot-flash score that depends on how quickly testosterone recovers after ADT is stopped.
rationale: Randomised patients are deep PSA responders (<0.2 ng/mL after 6 months), so 18-month rPFS should exceed 90% in both arms, and apalutamide continues in the intermittent arm; EMBARK showed AR-inhibitor monotherapy controls disease well. Non-inferiority is likely unless the margin is tight. Stopping ADT should let testosterone recover and cut hot flashes clearly versus continuous castration. Both primaries must be met, which trims the joint probability. Primary completion was October 2026, so a 2027 congress presentation is expected.

assumptions.claim: In TITAN, 24-month radiographic progression-free survival was 68.2% with apalutamide plus ADT versus 47.5% with placebo plus ADT.
In EMBARK, enzalutamide monotherapy improved metastasis-free survival over leuprolide alone with a hazard ratio of 0.63.
In TITAN, patients reaching a PSA of 0.2 ng/mL or lower on apalutamide had markedly longer radiographic progression-free and overall survival than those who did not.
assumptions.source: Chowdhury et al., Ann Oncol 2023 (TITAN post hoc analysis)

reason: 1 mg is a low dose; if its gain over placebo is nearer 6 than 10 hairs/cm2 the 1% significance level is at risk, and the trial also wants oral minoxidil to match topical 2% within an unstated margin.
rationale: Minoxidil is an established hair-growth drug; topical 2% beats vehicle by roughly 10 hairs/cm2 and oral 1 mg matched topical 5% in Ramos 2020. With 208 vs 104 patients and an SD near 22, a 9-hair difference gives high power even at alpha 0.01. The residual risks are the low oral dose, a non-inferiority comparison with topical 2% that the sponsor may also need, and limited disclosure by a private sponsor, which is likelier to publicise a positive result.
evidence: Ramos et al. 2020, J Am Acad Dermatol (oral minoxidil 1 mg vs topical 5% in women)
Lucky et al. 2004, J Am Acad Dermatol (topical minoxidil 5% and 2% vs placebo in women)
Blume-Peytavi et al. 2011 (5% foam vs 2% solution in women)
Penha et al. 2024, JAMA Dermatol (oral 5 mg vs topical 5% in men)

assumptions.claim: In a 24-week randomised trial in women, oral minoxidil 1 mg increased total hair density by about 12% versus about 7% with topical minoxidil 5%, with no significant difference.
assumptions.source: Ramos et al., J Am Acad Dermatol 2020

assumptions.claim: At week 48, non-vellus hair count rose by about 20.7 per cm2 with topical minoxidil 2% versus about 9.4 per cm2 with placebo in women.
assumptions.source: Lucky et al., J Am Acad Dermatol 2004

assumptions.claim: In men, oral minoxidil 5 mg daily was not superior to topical minoxidil 5% twice daily after 24 weeks.

reason: Adding a PI3K-alpha inhibitor to pertuzumab/trastuzumab adds hyperglycaemia, diarrhoea and stomatitis over a long maintenance period, which can erode dose intensity; a result by mid-2027 could also be an early stop for slow accrual.
rationale: PIK3CA mutation marks HER2-positive disease that does worse on trastuzumab/pertuzumab (CLEOPATRA), and inavolisib gave a PFS hazard ratio of 0.43 in INAVO120, so a benefit around HR 0.6 is plausible; I put underlying success near 55-60%. The trial is still recruiting with a placeholder December 2026 date, so a readout by June 2027 is unlikely and would be either an early positive topline or a stop, which lowers the conditional probability.

assumptions.claim: In INAVO120, inavolisib plus palbociclib and fulvestrant improved PFS over placebo plus palbociclib and fulvestrant with a hazard ratio of 0.43.
In CLEOPATRA, patients with PIK3CA-mutated tumours in the pertuzumab arm had a median PFS of 12.5 months versus 21.8 months for wild-type.
assumptions.source: Baselga et al., J Clin Oncol 2014 (CLEOPATRA biomarker analysis)

assumptions.claim: In HER2CLIMB-05, median PFS on trastuzumab plus pertuzumab maintenance with placebo was about 16 months, versus about 25 months with added tucatinib.

reason: Equivalence must be shown several times over (two PK AUC windows in patients against both EU and US Ocrevus, plus near-zero lesion counts), so a variance-driven miss on any one comparison is the main way to fail.
rationale: CT-P53 is an ocrelizumab biosimilar from a sponsor whose phase 3 biosimilar trials have consistently met equivalence. Ocrelizumab suppresses gadolinium-enhancing lesions by about 90-95%, so counts in both arms should sit near zero and efficacy equivalence is easy if the margin is absolute. The residual risk is PK equivalence in patients across three products and two AUC windows. The record still says recruiting with a 24-week endpoint and February 2027 completion, so a public result by June 2027 is unlikely and a filing by end-2027 is a stretch.
evidence: Kappos et al. 2011 (ocrelizumab phase 2 in RRMS, Lancet)

assumptions.claim: In the phase 2 trial of ocrelizumab in relapsing-remitting MS, gadolinium-enhancing lesions over weeks 12 to 24 were about 89% lower with ocrelizumab 600 mg than with placebo.
In OPERA I and II, ocrelizumab reduced gadolinium-enhancing T1 lesions by about 94-95% versus interferon beta-1a.
assumptions.source: Hauser et al., NEJM 2017 (OPERA I and II)

assumptions.claim: Celltrion's ustekinumab biosimilar CT-P43 met its phase 3 equivalence primary endpoint against reference ustekinumab in plaque psoriasis.

reason: A 21-patient safety study inherited from Telavant with a year-end placeholder date; it will most likely close around then or be pushed a few months, with results posted about a year after completion.
rationale: Only 21 patients were enrolled, far short of a normal phase 2, so Roche evidently curtailed the study once afimkibart moved into phase 3 in Crohn's disease. Primary and study completion share the same 31 December 2026 date while the safety outcome runs to end of study, about 5 years, so the date may still be pushed or the study closed as terminated. Roche usually posts results close to 12 months after completion, which falls after the 31 August 2027 read date.

reason: PFS should be won comfortably, so the realistic way to miss is the second primary: overall survival may be immature or short of its interim boundary when PFS is first reported in a trial of only 412 patients.
rationale: RC48-C016 gave disitamab vedotin plus toripalimab a PFS HR of 0.36 and OS HR of 0.54 against the same chemotherapy in the same HER2-expressing first-line population, and EV-302 showed 0.45 for a sister MMAE conjugate with pembrolizumab. Phase 2 response rates with pembrolizumab were about 75%. A global control arm with avelumab maintenance and more HER2 1+ patients should dilute the effect only modestly. I put PFS success near 95% and discount for OS, the second primary, needing to be significant at the same report.
evidence: RC48-C016 2025 (disitamab vedotin + toripalimab vs chemotherapy, NEJM)

assumptions.claim: In RC48-C016, disitamab vedotin plus toripalimab gave a PFS hazard ratio of about 0.36 versus platinum chemotherapy (median about 13.1 vs 6.5 months) in HER2-expressing first-line urothelial cancer.
In RC48-C016 the overall survival hazard ratio was about 0.54 (median about 31.5 vs 16.9 months).
In EV-302, median PFS in the platinum-gemcitabine arm was 6.3 months and the PFS hazard ratio for enfortumab vedotin plus pembrolizumab was 0.45.

reason: Agomelatine's edge over placebo is small (around 2 MADRS points) and the EEG biomarker was derived from open-label data, so the enriched subgroup may not separate enough from a high US placebo response.
rationale: ALTO-300 is agomelatine 25 mg, a modest antidepressant (SMD about 0.24 versus placebo). The EEG biomarker came from an open-label phase 2a, the same approach that failed for ALTO-100 in a placebo-controlled phase 2b. The 2025 interim analysis led to a larger biomarker-positive sample, which suggests a promising but not decisive interim effect. With about 100 per arm in the primary subgroup and SD near 9.5, the trial needs roughly 2.6 points; I expect about 2.

assumptions.claim: Alto's ALTO-100 phase 2b in biomarker-defined major depression missed its primary MADRS endpoint.
assumptions.source: Alto Neuroscience press release, October 2024 (ALTO-100 phase 2b)

assumptions.claim: A meta-analysis of published and unpublished trials found a standardized mean difference of about 0.24 for agomelatine versus placebo in acute depression.
After a planned interim analysis in early 2025, the ALTO-300 phase 2b continued with a larger sample of EEG-biomarker-positive patients and stopped enrolling biomarker-negative patients.

reason: Anifrolumab reached phase 3 in systemic sclerosis with no randomized phase 2, and placebo patients on background mycophenolate often improve enough to reach CRISS-25, leaving little room for a modest drug effect.
rationale: No controlled efficacy data exist for anifrolumab in systemic sclerosis; the case rests on the interferon signature and an open-label phase 1. Late-stage scleroderma trials have a poor record (tocilizumab, lenabasum, riociguat and abatacept all missed skin or composite primaries), partly from strong placebo improvement on background immunosuppression. Revised CRISS-25 is more sensitive but untested as a prospective primary. With 157 per arm the trial needs about an 11-point difference; I expect 7 to 8, giving roughly 30%.
evidence: RESOLVE-1 2023 (lenabasum phase 3 in diffuse cutaneous SSc)
Goldberg et al. 2014 (anifrolumab phase 1 in SSc)

assumptions.claim: The phase 3 focuSSced trial of tocilizumab in systemic sclerosis did not meet its primary endpoint of change in modified Rodnan skin score at week 48.
assumptions.source: Khanna et al., Lancet Respir Med 2020 (focuSSced, NCT02453256)

assumptions.claim: Before DAISY, anifrolumab had only an open-label phase 1 study in systemic sclerosis (34 patients) and no randomized phase 2 efficacy trial in the disease.
assumptions.source: Goldberg et al., Arthritis Res Ther 2014 (NCT00930683)

assumptions.claim: In RESOLVE-1, placebo patients, most on background immunosuppression, reached a median ACR-CRISS score of about 0.89 at week 52 and lenabasum did not beat placebo.
assumptions.source: Spiera et al., Arthritis Rheumatol 2023 (RESOLVE-1, NCT03398837)

reason: An EGFR x HER3 antibody added to docetaxel is unlikely to move overall survival much in unselected post-immunotherapy NSCLC, where nearly every docetaxel combination or replacement has failed on survival.
rationale: Phase 2 response rates with SI-B001 plus docetaxel (about 31-45%) looked better than docetaxel alone, but EGFR antibodies with chemotherapy have given only small survival gains in NSCLC and most second-line docetaxel-comparator trials after PD-1 therapy missed OS. Registered completion passed in July 2026 with no announcement, and Baili has shifted attention to its ADC. Negative Chinese trials often stay unpublished, so a result public by mid-2027 is more likely positive than my 20% unconditional estimate; both OS and PFS are primary.
evidence: SI-B001 plus chemotherapy phase 2 in EGFR/ALK wild-type NSCLC (ASCO 2023)

assumptions.claim: In a phase 2 study, SI-B001 plus docetaxel gave an objective response rate of about 45% (10 of 22) in the best dose group of EGFR/ALK wild-type NSCLC patients previously treated with PD-1/PD-L1 therapy and platinum.
assumptions.source: Zhao et al., ASCO 2023 abstract (SI-B001 plus chemotherapy, phase II)

assumptions.claim: Median overall survival with docetaxel was about 11.5 months in CONTACT-01 after checkpoint inhibitor and platinum chemotherapy.
assumptions.source: CONTACT-01, Neal et al., J Clin Oncol 2024

assumptions.claim: Sacituzumab govitecan did not significantly improve overall survival over docetaxel in EVOKE-01 (HR about 0.84).
assumptions.source: EVOKE-01, Paz-Ares et al., J Clin Oncol 2024

reason: With no phase 2 in Sjogren's, TYK2 inhibition may add only about a point over a placebo arm that typically improves 4 to 5 ESSDAI points by week 52.
rationale: Deucravacitinib blocks type I interferon signalling, central to Sjogren's, and worked in phase 2 lupus. Recent trials in anti-Ro-positive patients with ESSDAI of 5 or more have been positive for several mechanisms (ianalumab, nipocalimab, dazodalibep, iscalimab), though effects are small (1-2.5 points) and a JAK1 inhibitor failed. With 258 per arm and SD about 5.5, a difference near 1 point is significant, so the trial is well powered for a modest effect; the question is whether there is one. Two doses give two chances.
evidence: NEPTUNUS-1 and NEPTUNUS-2 2025 (ianalumab phase 3 in Sjogren's)
Dazodalibep phase 2 in Sjogren's 2024 (St Clair et al.)
Price et al. 2022 (filgotinib, lanraplenib, tirabrutinib in Sjogren's)

assumptions.claim: In the phase 2 PAISLEY trial in SLE, SRI-4 response at week 32 was about 58% with deucravacitinib 3 mg twice daily versus 34% with placebo.
assumptions.source: Morand et al., Arthritis Rheumatol 2023 (PAISLEY, NCT03252587)

assumptions.claim: In the phase 2 DAHLIAS trial, nipocalimab 15 mg/kg lowered clinESSDAI at week 24 by about 6.4 points versus about 3.7 points with placebo.
The JAK1 inhibitor filgotinib did not meet the primary endpoint in a phase 2 trial in Sjogren's syndrome.

reason: Part B is small with a 2:1 split, so if the true hazard ratio is nearer 0.7 than 0.55 against chemotherapy in a slow-growing FGFR2-fusion population, the BICR PFS analysis may not reach significance.
rationale: Phase 2 tinengotinib gave median PFS about 5.3 months and responses in roughly a third of patients with acquired resistance to a prior FGFR inhibitor, against an expected 2.5-3.5 months with third-line chemotherapy. That supports a hazard ratio near 0.55-0.6. Risks are the small Part B sample (perhaps 150 patients, about 110 events), weaker activity in primary-resistant disease, open-label early censoring in the control arm, and dose interruptions from multi-kinase toxicity.
evidence: Tinengotinib phase 2 in FGFR inhibitor-refractory cholangiocarcinoma (NCT04919642)
ABC-06 2021 (second-line FOLFOX in biliary tract cancer)
NIFTY 2021 (liposomal irinotecan in biliary tract cancer)

assumptions.claim: In the phase 2 study, tinengotinib gave a median PFS of about 5.3 months in cholangiocarcinoma patients with FGFR2 fusions who had progressed on a prior FGFR inhibitor.
assumptions.source: Javle et al., tinengotinib phase 2 (NCT04919642), ASCO GI 2024

assumptions.claim: In ABC-06, second-line FOLFOX gave a median progression-free survival of about 4.0 months in advanced biliary tract cancer.
Part B randomizes 2:1 to tinengotinib or physician's choice, with about 200 patients planned across Parts A and B.

reason: The stent non-inferiority test should pass, but the paired bleeding superiority test for 1-month DAPT has only about 100 events and a control arm in which many patients will stop DAPT early anyway.
rationale: Angiolite is a thin-strut cobalt-chromium sirolimus stent that matched Xience on late lumen loss, and modern drug-eluting stent non-inferiority trials with over 2,000 patients usually succeed; I put that at about 85%. The trial's second primary, BARC 2, 3 or 5 bleeding with 1-month versus 12-month DAPT, has precedent (MASTER DAPT, STOPDAPT-2, TWILIGHT) but power near 60-65% in all-comers. My number blends the stent test alone with the stricter reading that both primaries must be met.

assumptions.claim: In the randomized ANGIOLITE trial of 223 patients, the Angiolite stent was non-inferior to Xience for 6-month in-stent late lumen loss.
In MASTER DAPT, major or clinically relevant non-major bleeding occurred in 6.5% with abbreviated versus 9.4% with standard antiplatelet therapy.
In TALENT, the 12-month device-oriented composite endpoint occurred in about 5.3% of patients in the Xience arm.

reason: Saline injected with a needle three times has a real subcision effect, so if the control response on the blinded 5-grade scale is high the 39-patient saline arm leaves limited power.
rationale: A space-filling tropoelastin-hyaluronic acid gel should mechanically lift rolling and boxcar scars, and the PMMA-collagen filler pivotal trial showed 64% versus 33% responders against saline at 6 months. Risks are durability at Day 181 (four months after the last session), the requirement for improvement on both cheeks, and the small control arm. The study is complete; results will most likely surface through registry posting around mid-2027, which makes a public result by June 2027 uncertain.
evidence: Karnik et al. 2014 (PMMA-collagen filler for atrophic acne scars, JAAD)

assumptions.claim: In the pivotal trial of PMMA-collagen filler for atrophic acne scars, 64% of treated versus 33% of saline-control participants were responders at 6 months.
assumptions.source: Karnik et al., J Am Acad Dermatol 2014;71:77-83

assumptions.claim: Participants have a 1 in 4 chance of saline, giving about 118 ELAPR002f and 39 saline-control participants out of 157.

reason: A herbal tablet may add too little over a sizeable placebo response on the largely subjective ASAS20 at only 8 weeks in patients washed out of NSAIDs.
rationale: Company-sponsored, placebo-controlled Chinese herbal-medicine phase 3 with 204 per arm gives about 90% power for a 15-point ASAS20 gap, and such trials, usually run after a positive phase 2, mostly report success. The short 8-week endpoint, NSAID washout and subjective components leave room for a 30-35% placebo response. An early public statement would most likely be a positive company announcement. Still recruiting weeks before the registered completion date, so the result will probably come late.
evidence: Etoricoxib in ankylosing spondylitis, van der Heijde (2005)

assumptions.claim: In MEASURE 2, the placebo ASAS20 response at week 16 was 28% versus 61% with secukinumab 150 mg.
In COAST-V, the placebo ASAS20 response at week 16 was about 40%.
assumptions.source: COAST-V, van der Heijde et al., Lancet 2018

reason: With about 100 patients and under 80 PFS events, only a hazard ratio near 0.63 or better would be significant, and the record frames PFS as an estimate, not a tested hypothesis.
rationale: Only 103 patients (about 78 PFS events) and a record that describes the hazard ratio as a measure of interest, not a tested hypothesis. POSEIDON subgroup data suggest CTLA-4 blockade helps STK11/KEAP1-mutant tumours, but mainly through late overall-survival tails, and KRAS-only patients do well on pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy. A true PFS hazard ratio near 0.85 leaves roughly a one-in-seven chance of a significant result.
evidence: Skoulidis et al., Nature 2024 (CTLA-4 blockade in STK11/KEAP1-mutant NSCLC)

assumptions.claim: In POSEIDON, tremelimumab plus durvalumab plus chemotherapy improved overall survival versus chemotherapy alone with a hazard ratio of 0.77.
assumptions.source: POSEIDON, Johnson et al., J Clin Oncol 2022

assumptions.claim: In KEYNOTE-189, median PFS was 8.8 months with pembrolizumab plus pemetrexed-platinum versus 4.9 months with chemotherapy.

reason: The single-arm phase 1b signal (response near 50%, PFS about 6 months) may shrink under blinded randomization and central review, leaving a hazard ratio short of the roughly 0.65 needed.
rationale: Phase 1b single-arm data for IN10018 plus PLD showed a response rate near 50% and median PFS about 6 months against roughly 3.5 months expected with PLD alone, earning breakthrough status in China. Single-arm signals often shrink in blinded randomized testing with central review; 168 patients at 2:1 give about 80% power only for a hazard ratio near 0.6. A small company is more likely to publicise a positive result early, which lifts the conditional probability a little.
evidence: IN10018 plus PLD phase 1b in platinum-resistant ovarian cancer (ASCO 2022)

assumptions.claim: In JAVELIN Ovarian 200, median PFS with pegylated liposomal doxorubicin alone was 3.5 months.
assumptions.source: JAVELIN Ovarian 200, Pujade-Lauraine et al., Lancet Oncol 2021

assumptions.claim: The phase 1b study of IN10018 plus PLD in platinum-resistant ovarian cancer reported an objective response rate of about 57% and median PFS of 6.2 months.

reason: Cutaneous lupus trials can show a high placebo response on background therapy, and scarring discoid lesions may not clear enough for a 70% CLASI-A reduction by week 24.
rationale: Type I interferon drives cutaneous lupus; anifrolumab gave consistent skin responses in TULIP-1/2 and MUSE (about 46% vs 25% CLASI-50 at week 12), strong real-world responses in refractory discoid and subacute disease, and the subcutaneous regimen succeeded in TULIP-SC. With about 170 per arm, power exceeds 90% for a 17% vs 38% CLASI-70 split. Main risks are a high placebo response on background therapy and scarring discoid lesions.
evidence: LILAC part B, litifilimab in cutaneous lupus (2022)

assumptions.claim: In TULIP-2, among patients with baseline CLASI-A of 10 or more, a 50% or greater CLASI-A reduction at week 12 occurred in 49% with anifrolumab versus 25% with placebo.
The phase 3 TULIP-SC trial of subcutaneous anifrolumab in systemic lupus met its primary endpoint.

reason: TPL2 inhibition has no clinical proof of concept in ulcerative colitis and the earlier compound's phase 2 was stopped, so the effect in advanced-therapy failures may be too small for arms of about 40.
rationale: First-in-class TPL2 inhibitor without clinical proof of concept; the parent compound tilpisertib's earlier ulcerative colitis phase 2 was terminated. All patients have failed advanced therapy, which lowers placebo response but also drug response. Dose-ranging arms of roughly 35-45 patients need about a 25-30 point response gain for significance. The base rate for novel oral mechanisms in ulcerative colitis phase 2 is about one in three, and I shade it down.

assumptions.claim: The earlier phase 2 trial of tilpisertib (GS-4875) in moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis was terminated early.
In UNIFI induction, the placebo clinical response rate at week 8 was 31.3%.

reason: Paediatric heart transplants are rare in Germany, so the 15-patient target at three sites will probably slip past the registered date; results posting on ClinicalTrials.gov by the read date is very unlikely.
rationale: Fifteen children at three German centres since August 2023, and the record still shows recruiting three months before the registered primary completion, which needs a 3-month follow-up after the last transplant. Germany performs only a few dozen paediatric heart transplants a year and the exclusions are restrictive, so a delay is more likely than not. A small German sponsor with a safety primary rarely posts results quickly or rewrites outcomes.

reason: A single-site pilot with perhaps 15-30 PTSD patients per arm, compared against an active couple therapy, has limited power to show a CAPS-5 difference of 6-7 points.
rationale: A single-site pilot whose listed primaries are mostly feasibility and safety; CAPS-5 is compared against an active, evidence-based couple therapy, so the increment from MDMA should be smaller than the 9-12 points seen against inactive placebo with supportive therapy in MAPP1 and MAPP2. With perhaps 15-30 PTSD patients per arm, power is roughly 30-50%, less if enrolment falls short. Publication by mid-2027 is unlikely.
evidence: Monson et al., MDMA-facilitated cognitive-behavioural conjoint therapy pilot (2020)
Monson et al., CBCT for PTSD randomized trial, JAMA (2012)

assumptions.claim: In MAPP1, mean CAPS-5 change was -24.4 with MDMA-assisted therapy versus -13.9 with placebo plus therapy.
assumptions.source: MAPP1, Mitchell et al., Nat Med 2021

assumptions.claim: In MAPP2, mean CAPS-5 change was -23.7 with MDMA-assisted therapy versus -14.8 with placebo plus therapy.
assumptions.source: MAPP2, Mitchell et al., Nat Med 2023

reason: With about 22 patients per arm, significance needs a remission gap of roughly 35 points, which only a large, so far unproven, effect of JAK1 inhibition in EGPA would deliver.
rationale: JAK1 inhibition is unproven in EGPA and about 22 patients per arm need a remission gap of roughly 35 points for significance. Placebo remission with a forced steroid taper was very low in MIRRA, which helps, but allowing background mepolizumab or benralizumab enrols refractory patients. I give about a 30% chance of a large true effect and only moderate power even then.

assumptions.claim: In MIRRA, remission (BVAS 0 and prednisolone 4 mg/day or less) at both weeks 36 and 48 occurred in 32% of mepolizumab patients versus 3% on placebo.
In MANDARA, remission at weeks 36 and 48 occurred in 59% of benralizumab and 56% of mepolizumab patients.

reason: The trial repeats a post hoc winning subgroup of a failed phase 3; if the true reduction in new facial BCCs is nearer 30% than 50%, 113 patients with overdispersed counts will not reach significance.
rationale: The earlier phase 3 of patidegib gel missed its primary endpoint overall; this trial repeats the post hoc winning subgroup (PTCH1-confirmed adults with at least 10 facial BCCs) and endpoint (all new facial BCCs). Hedgehog blockade clearly prevents BCCs systemically and phase 2 was positive, but subgroup-derived effects usually shrink. With 113 patients and overdispersed counts, power is about 90% for a halving but only about 40% for a 30% reduction.
evidence: Patidegib gel phase 2 in Gorlin syndrome (NCT02762084)
Tang et al., vismodegib in basal-cell nevus syndrome, NEJM (2012)

assumptions.claim: The earlier phase 3 trial of patidegib gel 2% in Gorlin syndrome did not meet its primary endpoint in the overall population.
Oral vismodegib reduced new surgically eligible BCCs in basal-cell nevus syndrome to about 2 versus 29 per patient per year on placebo.

reason: If as-needed fluticasone through the dry powder device delivers less anti-inflammatory benefit than budesonide did in MANDALA, the hazard ratio could drift toward 0.85-0.9 and miss significance.
rationale: As-needed inhaled corticosteroid with albuterol is a validated concept: MANDALA showed a hazard ratio of 0.74 for budesonide/albuterol against albuterol in a similar exacerbation-prone population, and BATURA confirmed it in milder asthma. This event-driven trial has about 920 per arm, so power is near 90% for a hazard ratio of 0.75. Residual risks are the dry powder device, the fluticasone dose choice and the inclusion of young children.

assumptions.claim: In MANDALA, as-needed budesonide/albuterol 180/160 micrograms lowered the risk of severe asthma exacerbation versus albuterol with a hazard ratio of 0.74 (95% CI 0.62-0.89).
In MANDALA, the lower-dose budesonide/albuterol arm did not reach significance (hazard ratio 0.84, P=0.052).

reason: With 18 versus 9 patients, artesunate needs about 7 of 18 complete histologic responses against none on placebo; a real but moderate effect would miss, and a single placebo regression raises the bar further.
rationale: Vulvar HSIL rarely regresses spontaneously (0/26 complete responses on placebo in the imiquimod RCT), so placebo should show 0-1 of 9. Artesunate produced histologic regression in cervical HSIL and clinical responses in the vulvar phase 1, but I assume a complete histologic response rate near 35%, which gives roughly even odds of the 7/18 or more needed for significance against zero placebo responders. Power is low with 27 patients randomized 2:1. The record was still recruiting two months before registered primary completion, so a readout by mid-2027 is unlikely.
evidence: van Seters 2008 (imiquimod for vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia, RCT)

assumptions.claim: In the placebo-controlled trial of imiquimod for vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia, no placebo patient (0 of 26) had a complete response at 20 weeks, against 9 of 26 (35%) on imiquimod.
assumptions.source: van Seters et al., N Engl J Med 2008

assumptions.claim: In the phase 1 study of intravaginal artesunate for CIN2/3, histologic regression occurred in 19 of 28 treated women (68%).
The record was still listed as recruiting in the October 2026 snapshot, with registered primary completion in December 2026 and an 18-week primary endpoint.

reason: Likely to run late: enrolling 54 patients with rapid-test-positive Acinetobacter HABP/VABP in about ten months at 15 sites is ambitious for a small sponsor; results posting by August 2027 is very unlikely.
rationale: Phase 2a started May 2026 and must enrol 54 patients with hospital-acquired or ventilator-associated pneumonia and rapid-test-positive Acinetobacter baumannii at 15 sites in Greece and Israel by March 2027; pathogen-specific pneumonia trials enrol slowly, so a delay beyond 90 days is likely. The sponsor is a small private company, so results posting by August 2027 is very unlikely and a funding- or recruitment-driven stop is possible. Five safety and PK primary outcomes leave modest room for registry edits.
