reason: Change in eGFR at month 24 includes any acute haemodynamic dip from the endothelin antagonist, so a roughly 30% albuminuria reduction may translate into only about 1 mL/min/1.73 m2, close to what the trial can detect.
rationale: Zibotentan added to dapagliflozin cut UACR by 27-34% in ZENITH-CKD, and endothelin antagonists slowed kidney decline in SONAR and PROTECT. In a fast-progressing high-proteinuria population (control near -7 mL/min/1.73 m2 over two years), I expect about 1.2 mL/min/1.73 m2 preserved at month 24 after an acute haemodynamic dip; with 1,835 patients the standard error is about 0.55, so power is moderate. Total change at a fixed time is a demanding endpoint (PROTECT total slope p=0.058). AstraZeneca is likelier to announce quickly if positive, which raises the conditional probability.

assumptions.claim: Zibotentan 0.25 mg plus dapagliflozin 10 mg lowered UACR by about 27%, and zibotentan 1.5 mg plus dapagliflozin by about 34%, versus dapagliflozin alone at week 12.

Sparsentan's two-year eGFR total slope advantage over irbesartan in IgA nephropathy was about 1.0 mL/min/1.73 m2 per year and missed significance (p=0.058), while the chronic slope difference of 1.1 was significant.
The dapagliflozin arm's total eGFR slope was about -2.9 mL/min/1.73 m2 per year, against about -3.8 on placebo.
assumptions.source: DAPA-CKD, Heerspink et al., N Engl J Med 2020 (NCT03036150)

reason: IL-6 blockade mainly calms inflammation; its proptosis effect looks smaller than that of IGF-1R antibodies, and with about 26 patients per arm the trial needs a gain of roughly 25 points or more over placebo.
rationale: IL-6 pathway blockade improves inflammatory activity in thyroid eye disease (tocilizumab RCT), but its proptosis effect appears smaller than that of IGF-1R antibodies. I assume about 37% proptosis responders on 50 mg versus 16% on placebo at week 20; with roughly 26 per arm that difference would usually miss significance, though a pooled-dose comparison or either dose winning helps. Tourmaline deprioritized this indication before Novartis bought it for cardiovascular use, and the readout slipped repeatedly, so disclosure may wait for registry posting, which favours no selective good news.

assumptions.claim: In the randomized trial of tocilizumab in corticosteroid-resistant Graves orbitopathy (32 patients), 93% on tocilizumab versus 59% on placebo improved the Clinical Activity Score by at least 2 points at week 16.
assumptions.source: Perez-Moreiras et al., Am J Ophthalmol 2018

assumptions.claim: The placebo proptosis response rate at week 24 in the teprotumumab phase 3 trial was about 10%, against 83% on teprotumumab.
assumptions.source: OPTIC, Douglas et al., N Engl J Med 2020 (NCT03298867)

assumptions.claim: Novartis agreed to acquire Tourmaline Bio in September 2025, with pacibekitug's cardiovascular programme as the stated rationale.

reason: Should run to plan as an open-label PK and safety study of an approved product; the main uncertainty is whether results are posted by the end of August 2027, about a year after primary completion.
rationale: Open-label PK, safety and acceptability study of approved twice-yearly lenacapavir in US cisgender women. Primary completion passed in July 2026 and the study continues to January 2028, so termination is unlikely. Results fall due about July 2027 under the 12-month rule and Gilead generally submits on time, but posting by 31 August 2027 depends on timely submission and registry processing. Seven primary outcomes could be edited when results are entered, though a change in substance is uncommon.

reason: Past primary completion and likely to finish as planned; results fall due around late July 2027, so posting by 31 August 2027 is somewhat better than even odds.
rationale: Open-label PK and safety study of approved twice-yearly lenacapavir in people who inject drugs, run with HPTN. Primary completion passed in July 2026 with 181 enrolled, and the study continues to January 2028, so termination is unlikely. Results fall due about late July 2027 and Gilead generally submits on time, but posting by 31 August 2027 depends on timely submission and registry processing. The four PK and safety primary outcomes are unlikely to change in substance.

reason: Patients stable on a BTK inhibitor progress slowly, so few PFS events will have accrued by mid-2027; an early look could be immature or show no clear separation yet, and added toxicity could offset early benefit.
rationale: Adding a BCL-2 inhibitor to ongoing BTK inhibitor therapy should deepen responses and lengthen PFS substantially (hazard ratio around 0.45), and lisaftoclax is already approved in China for BTK-inhibitor-pretreated CLL. But patients stable on a BTK inhibitor for at least a year progress slowly, the trial was still recruiting in October 2026, and the registered December 2026 primary completion is unrealistic. A result by mid-2027 would most likely come from an early positive interim or from a stop, hence a probability below my estimate for the final analysis.
evidence: Lisaftoclax China pivotal phase 2 in relapsed/refractory CLL (2025 approval)

assumptions.claim: Lisaftoclax received conditional approval in China in July 2025 for adults with CLL/SLL previously treated with at least one systemic therapy including a BTK inhibitor.
The record was still listed as recruiting in the October 2026 snapshot, with a registered primary completion date of 2026-12-31.

reason: No clinical proof of the mechanism in alopecia areata and a 12-week endpoint that is early even for JAK inhibitors; a small trial needs a difference of about 14 points in percent SALT change.
rationale: NXC736 is a first-in-class oral immunomodulator without clinical proof in alopecia areata, and another oral immunomodulator class tested there (the S1P modulator etrasimod) showed no significant SALT benefit in phase 2. Week 12 is early even for JAK inhibitors, whose effects build through weeks 24-36. With roughly 36 per arm and a between-patient SD near 30 points, the drug must beat placebo by about 14 points. Small Korean sponsor, two sites, still recruiting at registered primary completion, so disclosure by mid-2027 is uncertain.

assumptions.claim: In the baricitinib phase 3 trials, only 6.2% (BRAVE-AA1) and 3.3% (BRAVE-AA2) of placebo patients reached a SALT score of 20 or less at week 36.
assumptions.source: King et al., N Engl J Med 2022

assumptions.claim: The phase 2 trial of etrasimod in alopecia areata did not show a statistically significant improvement in SALT over placebo at week 24.
The record was still listed as recruiting in the October 2026 snapshot, with a registered primary completion date of 2026-10-31.

reason: Loss of 15 or more letters is rare when aflibercept is available, so eye drops can at best match the comparator on this endpoint; statistical superiority is very unlikely.
rationale: The registered endpoint, losing 15 or more letters through week 36, is rare when aflibercept is available (under 2% at one year in VIVID/VISTA), so showing statistical superiority of tivozanib eye drops on it is very unlikely; the realistic best case is comparable vision with fewer injections, which does not count as meeting a superiority hypothesis. Earlier topical kinase-inhibitor drops (pazopanib, regorafenib) failed in retinal disease. Kyowa Kirin reports pipeline changes quarterly, so some statement by mid-2027 is fairly likely.

assumptions.claim: In VISTA and VIVID, under 2% of eyes treated with aflibercept lost 15 or more letters at week 52, against about 9-11% of laser-treated eyes.
Regorafenib eye drops in neovascular AMD gave visual results below those expected with anti-VEGF injections, and the phase 2 programme was stopped.
assumptions.source: DREAM study, Joussen et al., Br J Clin Pharmacol 2019

reason: Acute MI patients not selected on hsCRP and treated with modern therapy may gain only about a 10% relative reduction in MACE, less than the roughly 12% the trial needs to observe; colchicine and other post-MI strategies have recently been neutral.
rationale: Ziltivekimab lowers hsCRP by about 90% (RESCUE), and IL-6 signalling has genetic and CANTOS support (hazard ratio 0.85 with IL-1 beta blockade). But ARTEMIS takes acute MI patients without hsCRP selection, and anti-inflammatory or early post-MI strategies have often failed (CLEAR SYNERGY colchicine hazard ratio 0.99; AEGIS-II). I expect a true hazard ratio near 0.90; with roughly 950 events the trial needs an observed ratio below about 0.88, giving about 40%. Novo Nordisk announces headline outcomes results promptly, so a statement by mid-2027 is likely.

assumptions.claim: Ziltivekimab reduced hsCRP at 12 weeks by 77%, 88% and 92% at 7.5 mg, 15 mg and 30 mg, against 4% with placebo.
Canakinumab 150 mg reduced major adverse cardiovascular events with a hazard ratio of 0.85 in patients with prior MI and hsCRP of 2 mg/L or more.
assumptions.source: CANTOS, Ridker et al., N Engl J Med 2017 (NCT01327846)

assumptions.claim: Colchicine started soon after myocardial infarction did not reduce the primary cardiovascular composite (hazard ratio 0.99).
assumptions.source: CLEAR SYNERGY, Jolly et al., N Engl J Med 2025 (NCT03048825)

reason: Fully enrolled BMS phase 2a with about 24 weeks of follow-up and a completion date weeks away; it should close on schedule, with registry results following roughly a year after completion.
rationale: Status is active, not recruiting with 227 enrolled and primary completion registered for December 2026, so little can delay it beyond March 2027. Large sponsors rarely terminate a fully enrolled safety study this close to the end. BMS usually posts results near the 12-month legal deadline, so posting by August 2027 (about 8.5 months after completion) is unlikely. Safety primary outcomes are standard and unlikely to be rewritten.

reason: About 105 patients per arm at most (fewer if several doses were randomized) gives modest power for a pirfenidone-sized FVC benefit, and slow recruitment of a placebo-only IPF trial in China adds dropout and timing risk.
rationale: Sufenidone is a pirfenidone-like pyridone, so the mechanism is validated: pirfenidone and nintedanib each cut annual FVC loss by roughly 100-190 mL against placebo. But this is a small seamless phase 2/3 (210 patients, possibly split over several doses) without background antifibrotics, still recruiting three years after start, run by a small Chinese sponsor with no public phase 2 efficacy data. Power for a ~80 mL/year difference is modest. A result public by mid-2027 would probably be an early, favourable announcement.

assumptions.claim: In ASCEND, mean FVC decline at week 52 was about 235 mL with pirfenidone versus about 428 mL with placebo.
In INPULSIS-1 and INPULSIS-2, the adjusted annual rate of FVC decline on placebo was -239.9 and -207.3 mL/year, versus about -114 mL/year on nintedanib.

reason: Placebo response in dementia-related psychosis over 12 weeks is large and variable across 150+ sites, so a real but small KarXT effect (d about 0.2) could fall short of significance, especially if tolerability limits dosing in the elderly.
rationale: Xanomeline reduced hallucinations and delusions in a 1997 Alzheimer's trial and KarXT has large effects in schizophrenia monotherapy, but effect sizes in dementia psychosis are usually small (d about 0.2-0.3) with high placebo response over 12 weeks across many countries. Sample size was raised to 500 after site irregularities, giving about 80% power for d=0.25. Tolerability in frail elderly patients at lower doses adds risk; the adjunctive schizophrenia trial ARISE missed. I put success near a coin flip.
evidence: Bodick et al. 1997 (xanomeline in Alzheimer's disease)
Ballard et al. 2018 (pimavanserin in AD psychosis, NCT02035553)

assumptions.claim: In EMERGENT-2, KarXT lowered the PANSS total score by 9.6 points more than placebo at week 5 in schizophrenia.
In a 6-month trial in 343 patients with Alzheimer's disease, xanomeline produced dose-dependent reductions in hallucinations, delusions and agitation.
In the phase 2 trial of pimavanserin in Alzheimer's disease psychosis, the NPI-NH psychosis score fell 3.76 points with pimavanserin versus 1.93 with placebo at week 6, with no difference at week 12.

reason: Single-dose benzimidazoles other than albendazole cure only a minority of hookworm and Trichuris infections, so with about 57 evaluable hookworm cases per arm and a primary covering each species, one species could miss significance.
rationale: ZP5-9676 is a single-dose chewable benzimidazole tested against placebo with a day-14 test of cure. Benzimidazoles reliably beat placebo for Ascaris, and albendazole cures about 80% of hookworm, but mebendazole-like agents cure only about a third as a single dose, and placebo 'cure' from egg-count variability can reach 15-25%. Only about 57 evaluable hookworm cases per arm are guaranteed, and the primary covers each species, including hard-to-cure Trichuris. Tiny sponsor; reporting by mid-2027 is unlikely.
evidence: Moser, Schindler and Keiser 2017 (BMJ network meta-analysis of anthelmintics)
Silber et al. 2017 (mebendazole chewable phase 3, NCT02034162)

assumptions.claim: Single-dose albendazole 400 mg cures about 80% of hookworm infections, while single-dose mebendazole 500 mg cures about a third.
In the phase 3 trial of chewable mebendazole 500 mg, cure rates were 83.7% versus 11.1% with placebo for Ascaris and 33.9% versus 7.6% for Trichuris.

reason: Eighty patients cannot detect the small functional gain, if any, that intravenous stem cells add to large and variable spontaneous recovery, and both Barthel Index and mRS must be met.
rationale: Intravenous mesenchymal or progenitor cell trials in ischemic stroke (MASTERS, TREASURE, the investigators' own earlier Malaysian trial) have not shown functional benefit on mRS or Barthel Index. This study has 80 patients, enrolls up to 4 weeks after onset, lists two co-primary scales at several time points without a defined primary time, and is still recruiting with 12-month follow-up needed. Spontaneous recovery in the placebo arm is large and variable. Success on both co-primaries is improbable and timely reporting unlikely.
evidence: Law et al. 2021 (Cytotherapy, bone marrow MSC in subacute MCA infarct)

assumptions.claim: In MASTERS, intravenous multipotent adult progenitor cells did not improve global stroke recovery at 90 days versus placebo.
In TREASURE, intravenous MultiStem given 18-36 hours after ischemic stroke did not increase the share of patients with an excellent outcome at 90 days.

The Malaysian randomized trial of intravenous autologous bone marrow MSCs in subacute MCA infarct found no significant difference in NIHSS, mRS or Barthel Index at 12 months, only a change in infarct volume.

reason: Crizotinib is unusually durable in ROS1 disease (median PFS up to about 19-20 months in some series), so with only about 100 events a strong control arm could leave the hazard ratio short of significance.
rationale: Repotrectinib gave a median PFS of 35.7 months in TKI-naive ROS1 NSCLC in TRIDENT-1 versus roughly 16-19 months historically for crizotinib, and it controls brain disease, where crizotinib fails. That implies a hazard ratio near 0.5; with about 100 events among 190 patients, an observed HR below roughly 0.67 is significant. Next-generation TKIs have consistently beaten crizotinib head-to-head in ALK disease. Risks are a strong crizotinib arm by central review and a small event count.
evidence: Wu et al. 2018 (crizotinib in East Asian ROS1 NSCLC, NCT01945021)

assumptions.claim: In TRIDENT-1, median PFS with repotrectinib in TKI-naive ROS1-positive NSCLC was 35.7 months.
In the updated PROFILE 1001 ROS1 cohort, median PFS with crizotinib was 19.3 months.
In the East Asian phase 2 study of crizotinib in ROS1-positive NSCLC, median PFS by independent review was 15.9 months.
assumptions.source: Wu et al. 2018, J Clin Oncol (NCT01945021)

reason: Failure would most likely need pembrolizumab-chemotherapy to perform far better in HER2-mutant disease than the 6-8 months seen in retrospective series, combined with early censoring in an open-label design.
rationale: Zongertinib produced a 77% response rate in treatment-naive HER2-mutant NSCLC and a 12.4-month median PFS in pretreated patients in Beamion LUNG-1, while chemo-immunotherapy in HER2-mutant disease typically gives a PFS of about 6-8 months. A hazard ratio around 0.45 in a 428-patient trial leaves very high power. The trial is fully enrolled with primary completion registered for December 2026, so a congress presentation around mid-2027 is plausible. Residual risks are an unexpectedly strong control arm or informative censoring in an open-label design.

assumptions.claim: In previously treated HER2-mutant NSCLC in Beamion LUNG-1, zongertinib gave a 71% objective response rate and a median PFS of 12.4 months.
assumptions.source: Heymach et al. 2025, N Engl J Med (NCT04886804)

assumptions.claim: In the treatment-naive cohort of Beamion LUNG-1, the objective response rate with zongertinib was 77%.
In KEYNOTE-189, median PFS with pembrolizumab plus pemetrexed-platinum in unselected non-squamous NSCLC was about 9 months.

reason: LAG-3 blockade has added little to PD-1 plus chemotherapy in lung cancer, and a phase 2 with under 100 patients per arm needs a pCR gain of about 15 points over an active cemiplimab-chemotherapy control.
rationale: Cemiplimab-chemotherapy control should give a pCR near 20-24%, as with other PD-1 perioperative regimens. Adding a LAG-3 antibody to PD-1 plus chemotherapy has shown little incremental activity in lung cancer, and with roughly 65-100 patients per arm an absolute pCR gain of about 15 points is needed for significance. A phase 2 may report descriptively without a formal claim. Primary completion has passed; Regeneron may disclose at a 2027 congress or in pipeline updates, or stay quiet if negative.

assumptions.claim: In CheckMate 816, pCR was 24.0% with neoadjuvant nivolumab plus chemotherapy versus 2.2% with chemotherapy alone.
In KEYNOTE-671, pCR was 18.1% with perioperative pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy versus 4.0% with placebo plus chemotherapy.
In RELATIVITY-047, relatlimab plus nivolumab improved median PFS to 10.1 months versus 4.6 months with nivolumab alone in advanced melanoma (HR 0.75).

reason: Fully enrolled 52-week extension whose participants rolled over on a fixed schedule from the parent study; it should complete on time, with results posted about a year after completion.
rationale: Fully enrolled extension of Pfizer's 52-week vitiligo study; every participant rolled over within 30 days of finishing the parent trial, so the last 52-week visit is predictable and the March 2027 date should hold. Pfizer rarely stops fully enrolled extensions absent a safety signal and typically posts results close to 12 months after primary completion, well after August 2027. Safety primary outcomes are unlikely to be changed.

reason: If CLDN18.2 positivity is defined more broadly than in the zolbetuximab trials, the benefit may be diluted in low expressers and the PFS hazard ratio could drift toward 0.85 and miss significance.
rationale: CLDN18.2 antibody plus chemotherapy is a validated approach: zolbetuximab improved PFS in SPOTLIGHT (HR 0.75) and GLOW (HR 0.69, same CAPOX backbone, 6.8-month control PFS). M108 showed high response rates with CAPOX in early studies, and 486 patients give good power for HR 0.7. Uncertainty comes from the CLDN18.2 positivity cut-off, which may be broader than zolbetuximab's, and independent-review PFS. The trial is still listed as recruiting, so a readout by mid-2027 is unlikely.

assumptions.claim: In GLOW, zolbetuximab plus CAPOX gave a median PFS of 8.21 months versus 6.80 months with placebo plus CAPOX (HR 0.687).
In SPOTLIGHT, zolbetuximab plus mFOLFOX6 gave a median PFS of 10.61 months versus 8.67 months with placebo plus mFOLFOX6 (HR 0.75).

reason: The LAG-3 add-on may raise pCR by only 10-15 points over cemiplimab alone, as with response rates in metastatic melanoma, and about 75 patients per arm cannot reliably detect that.
rationale: Neoadjuvant PD-1 alone yields pCR near 20-25% (S1801, pooled INMC), while single-arm relatlimab plus nivolumab reached 57%, so a LAG-3 add-on plausibly lifts pCR to about 40-45%. With roughly 75 per arm, an observed gap of about 15 points is needed. Offsetting: LAG-3 adds only about 10 points of response in metastatic disease, adjuvant relatlimab failed (RELATIVITY-098), blinded central review and multicentre intent-to-treat analysis usually shrink single-centre rates, and the arm split is not confirmed. pCR data should be mature by late 2026; ASCO 2027 is the likely venue.
evidence: Amaria et al. 2022, neoadjuvant relatlimab plus nivolumab (NCT02519322)

assumptions.claim: Neoadjuvant relatlimab plus nivolumab gave a pathological complete response rate of 57% in a single-arm phase 2 trial of resectable stage III/IV melanoma.
Neoadjuvant pembrolizumab alone gave a pathological complete response rate of about 21% in SWOG S1801.
assumptions.source: SWOG S1801, Patel et al., NEJM 2023 (NCT03698019)

assumptions.claim: Adjuvant nivolumab plus relatlimab did not improve recurrence-free survival over nivolumab alone in resected melanoma.

reason: An anti-angiogenic multi-kinase inhibitor may improve response and PFS without a clear survival gain over active third-line chemotherapy, as happened with anlotinib in ESCC.
rationale: KC1036 (AXL/VEGFR2 inhibitor) showed response rates near 26-30% in pretreated ESCC in single-arm phase 2, well above third-line chemotherapy, so a PFS gain is likely. Overall survival superiority over active chemotherapy is a harder bar: anlotinib improved PFS but not survival in ESCC (ALTER1102). Control survival should be about 5-6 months; I expect a hazard ratio near 0.8, giving roughly even odds at final analysis. The trial was still recruiting in October 2026, so a result by mid-2027 would mostly mean an interim stop, lowering the conditional probability.
evidence: KC1036 phase Ib/II in advanced ESCC, ASCO 2023

assumptions.claim: KC1036 monotherapy gave an objective response rate of roughly 26-30% in previously treated advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma in its phase Ib/II study.
Anlotinib improved median PFS (3.0 vs 1.4 months) but not overall survival versus placebo in previously treated advanced ESCC.
Second-line chemotherapy gave a median overall survival of 6.3 months in advanced ESCC.
assumptions.source: RATIONALE-302, Shen et al., J Clin Oncol 2022 (NCT03430843)

reason: Single-site, sequential-cohort study from a small biotech that started about 2.5 years after registration; finishing up to 90 women by December 2026 looks optimistic, so the primary completion date will probably slip.
rationale: Registered in January 2024 but first dosing listed only for July 2026; three sequential dose cohorts totalling up to 90 postmenopausal women with confirmed atrophy at one phase 1 unit are unlikely to finish by December 2026. A small private sponsor adds funding and record-keeping risk; results posting within eight months of completion would be unusual for a phase 2a safety and PK study.

reason: Only 48 patients randomized 2:1, with spontaneous regression and a loose partial-response definition likely to inflate the placebo rate, so even a real effect may miss significance.
rationale: Evidence is limited to small open-label phase 1 studies (anal suppositories; vaginal inserts in CIN2/3 with 68% regression), without placebo controls. Anal HSIL regresses spontaneously, and biopsy plus a loosely defined partial response could give placebo rates of 20-35%. With 32 versus 16 patients, even a true 25-30 point difference yields under 50% power. Recruitment has been slow (started January 2024, still recruiting), and the private sponsor is unlikely to report before late 2027.
evidence: Trimble et al. 2020, intravaginal artesunate for CIN2/3 (NCT02354534)
Fang et al. 2023, intra-anal artesunate suppositories phase I (NCT03100045)
SPANC cohort 2021, natural history of anal HSIL

assumptions.claim: Intravaginal artesunate was followed by histologic regression in 19 of 28 (67.9%) women with CIN2/3 in a first-in-human trial.
A phase I dose-escalation study of intra-anal artesunate suppositories in anal HSIL reported the treatment as safe with histologic responses in a majority of evaluable participants.
Anal HSIL cleared spontaneously at about 22 per 100 person-years in a cohort of gay and bisexual men.
assumptions.source: SPANC, Poynten et al., Clin Infect Dis 2021

reason: The added benefit of a CLDN18.2 antibody on top of chemotherapy plus PD-1 blockade may be smaller than zolbetuximab's benefit over chemotherapy alone, especially in a broader CLDN18.2-positive population.
rationale: CLDN18.2 antibodies added to chemotherapy improved PFS twice (SPOTLIGHT HR 0.75, GLOW HR 0.69). ASKB589 has enhanced ADCC and phase 1b/2 response rates near 80% with CAPOX plus PD-1. With 780 patients and roughly 500 events, the trial detects hazard ratios below about 0.84. Risks: benefit on top of a PD-1 inhibitor is unproven in phase 3, a broader CLDN18.2 cut-off may dilute the effect, and nausea/vomiting may reduce chemotherapy exposure. Control PFS should be near 7 months (RATIONALE-305). A listed sponsor should announce topline in 2027.
evidence: ASKB589 plus CAPOX plus PD-1 phase Ib/II, ASCO 2024

assumptions.claim: Zolbetuximab plus CAPOX improved PFS over placebo plus CAPOX with a hazard ratio of 0.687 (median 8.21 vs 6.80 months).
assumptions.source: GLOW, Shah et al., Nat Med 2023 (NCT03653507)

assumptions.claim: Zolbetuximab plus mFOLFOX6 improved PFS with a hazard ratio of 0.75 (median 10.61 vs 8.67 months).
Tislelizumab plus chemotherapy gave a median PFS of 6.9 months in first-line gastric or gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma.

reason: At most 33 patients and a noisy self-reported symptom endpoint dominated by lingering fatigue leave the trial with little power, even if tafenoquine speeds parasite clearance.
rationale: Tafenoquine has anti-Babesia activity in mouse models and case reports, but this trial has at most 33 patients and a noisy self-reported endpoint requiring seven days free of eleven symptoms, including fatigue, which persists for weeks to months on standard therapy. Even a true hazard ratio of 1.5 gives well under 30% power. Enrolment is seasonal and has been slow since June 2024; an interim after 24 patients is possible. The micro-cap sponsor will press-release any outcome, likely emphasising parasitological endpoints.
evidence: Krause et al. 2000, atovaquone plus azithromycin for babesiosis
Mordue and Wormser 2019, tafenoquine in B. microti mouse model
Marcos et al. 2022, tafenoquine for relapsing babesiosis case report
Rogers et al. 2023, tafenoquine in immunocompromised babesiosis case series

assumptions.claim: Three months after starting therapy, symptoms had resolved in about 65% of babesiosis patients given atovaquone plus azithromycin.
assumptions.source: Krause et al., N Engl J Med 2000

assumptions.claim: Tafenoquine rapidly reduced Babesia microti parasitemia in immunodeficient mice.
assumptions.source: Mordue and Wormser, J Infect Dis 2019

assumptions.claim: Adding tafenoquine was followed by resolution of relapsing babesiosis in an immunocompromised patient who had failed standard regimens.

reason: Extension study with closed enrolment should finish on schedule around December 2026; results are likely to be posted near the 12-month deadline, after the read date.
rationale: Extension of STOP-HS1/2, whose 54-week periods ended around late 2025, so a 52-56 week extension finishing in December 2026 fits; enrolment is closed at 617. Incyte keeps its records current. Risks are a protocol extension while povorcitinib awaits approval. Results are normally posted about 12 months after primary completion, so posting by August 2027 is unlikely.

reason: Completed GSK vaccine study; results are due about August 2027 and public posting may fall just before or just after the 31 August 2027 read date.
rationale: Already completed (August 2026), so a stop is essentially excluded. GSK reliably submits results about 12 months after primary completion (due early August 2027); for a study outside the United States, public posting follows registry quality review, which with 44 primary outcomes may run past 31 August 2027. Outcome wording may be tidied at results entry, rarely in substance.

reason: Both co-primaries must be met; the likeliest miss is the HbA1c comparison, if baseline HbA1c is low or arms are smaller than assumed, leaving the 12-week difference short of significance.
rationale: The coded products appear to be fimasartan (BR1019A) and an oral glucose-lowering drug, probably dapagliflozin (BR1019B), in a factorial design. Each co-primary tests an established drug against its placebo on its own target: an ARB typically lowers systolic pressure by about 10 mmHg beyond placebo, and an SGLT2 inhibitor lowers HbA1c by 0.5-0.7 points; with about 70-90 per arm both comparisons have over 90% power. Failure would need an unexpectedly small HbA1c effect. Publication by mid-2027 is unlikely: still recruiting, results usually appear years later.
evidence: Lee et al. 2012, fimasartan vs losartan phase 3
Sjostrom et al. 2015, dapagliflozin blood pressure pooled analysis

assumptions.claim: Dapagliflozin 10 mg monotherapy lowered HbA1c by 0.89 percentage points versus 0.23 with placebo at 24 weeks.
Fimasartan 60/120 mg lowered sitting diastolic blood pressure by about 11.3 mmHg versus 8.6 mmHg with losartan 50/100 mg at 12 weeks.
Dapagliflozin 10 mg lowered systolic blood pressure by roughly 3-4 mmHg more than placebo in pooled phase 3 data.
assumptions.source: Sjostrom et al., Diab Vasc Dis Res 2015

reason: With about 30 patients per arm and no clear formal hypothesis in phase II, the response-rate gap over paclitaxel may not reach, or not be reported as reaching, statistical significance.
rationale: In phase II (about 30 per arm), disitamab vedotin plus cadonilimab should reach response rates of 40-50% (DV plus toripalimab 43%; DV alone about 25%) against 10-16% for second-line paclitaxel, a gap that is often but not always significant at this size. The bigger uncertainty is labelling: phase II probably has no formal hypothesis, the record also lists phase III PFS and OS as primaries, and a descriptive congress abstract may not state the objective as met. Enrolment remains 90, suggesting phase III has not opened.

assumptions.claim: Placebo plus paclitaxel gave an objective response rate of 16% in second-line advanced gastric cancer.
assumptions.source: RAINBOW, Wilke et al., Lancet Oncol 2014 (NCT01170663)

assumptions.claim: Disitamab vedotin monotherapy gave an objective response rate of 24.8% in HER2-overexpressing gastric cancer after at least two prior lines.
assumptions.source: RC48-C008, Peng et al., Cancer Commun 2021 (NCT03556345)

assumptions.claim: Disitamab vedotin plus toripalimab gave an objective response rate of 43% in the HER2-expressing gastric cancer cohort of a phase 1 trial.

reason: TYK2 inhibition has not yet shown efficacy in Crohn's disease (deucravacitinib failed in LATTICE-CD), so zasocitinib may not reach an endoscopic effect large enough to be significant with about 67 patients per arm.
rationale: Zasocitinib gives near-complete, sustained TYK2 inhibition and biologic-like efficacy in psoriasis, and IL-23 blockade yields 20-30 point gains in endoscopic response at week 12 in Crohn's disease. Against that, deucravacitinib failed in LATTICE-CD, while Ventyx's VTX958 missed on CDAI but showed a dose-related endoscopic signal. With placebo near 12% and 67 per arm, a 20-point gain gives roughly 85% power, and three doses add chances. I weight a real effect at about 60%. Recruitment was still open in October 2026, so a public readout before mid-2027 is uncertain.

assumptions.claim: Placebo endoscopic response at week 12 was 12% in ADVANCE and 11% in MOTIVATE, against 40% and 29% with risankizumab 600 mg.
Deucravacitinib did not meet its co-primary endpoints of clinical remission and endoscopic response at week 12 in the phase 2 LATTICE-CD trial.
Zasocitinib 30 mg gave PASI 75 in 67% of patients at week 12 versus 6% on placebo in the phase 2b psoriasis trial.

reason: Enrolment is closed with completion registered for November 2026, so the study most likely finishes close to schedule; a small private sponsor makes early results posting unlikely.
rationale: Active, not recruiting, with primary completion registered for November 2026 and 24-week safety follow-up, so a slip beyond February 2027 needs a record update showing late follow-up; I put that near one in four. ReCode is a small private company dependent on financing, which gives a modest termination risk. Results are due a year after completion, and small sponsors rarely post early. The multi-part design has already been extended once, so another primary-outcome change is possible but unlikely.

reason: Methotrexate acts slowly in atopic dermatitis, so EASI 75 at week 16 may come too early to separate clearly from a placebo response of 10-20%.
rationale: Methotrexate is an established off-label systemic for atopic dermatitis; open trials show about 40% SCORAD reduction by week 12, with responses still building to week 20 and beyond. I expect roughly 30% EASI 75 at week 16 on subcutaneous dosing against about 14% on placebo; with 138 per arm that gap gives over 85% power, but slow onset could shrink it to 10 points. The record still shows recruiting with completion in November 2026, so the date will slip, and a private sponsor is unlikely to report by mid-2027.

assumptions.claim: Methotrexate reduced mean SCORAD by 42% at week 12 in adults with severe atopic eczema, similar to azathioprine (39%).
assumptions.source: Schram et al., J Allergy Clin Immunol 2011

assumptions.claim: Placebo EASI 75 at week 16 was 15% in SOLO 1 and 12% in SOLO 2.
assumptions.source: Simpson et al., N Engl J Med 2016 (SOLO 1 and SOLO 2)

assumptions.claim: At week 8 only 8% of adults on methotrexate 15 mg weekly reached SCORAD 50 versus 42% on ciclosporin, showing slow onset.
assumptions.source: Goujon et al., J Allergy Clin Immunol Pract 2018

reason: With 83 patients and roughly 60 events, only a hazard ratio near 0.5 is reliably significant, and dropouts before cell infusion or in the open-label gemcitabine arm could blur the comparison.
rationale: Single-agent chemotherapy after first-line failure in cervical cancer gives median PFS under 3 months and response rates near 10%, a weak control. TIL therapy has produced response rates of 30-45% in small cervical cohorts with some durable responses, so a hazard ratio of 0.5-0.6 is plausible. With about 60 events, power is around 75% at 0.5 but only 50% at 0.6. The trial was still recruiting three months before its registered completion, so delay is likely and a public result by mid-2027 is improbable.

assumptions.claim: Median PFS on investigator's-choice single-agent chemotherapy was 2.9 months in recurrent cervical cancer after platinum.
assumptions.source: EMPOWER-Cervical 1, Tewari et al., N Engl J Med 2022

assumptions.claim: The TIL product LN-145 gave an objective response rate of 44% (12 of 27) in previously treated advanced cervical cancer.
TIL therapy halved the risk of progression or death versus ipilimumab in advanced melanoma (hazard ratio 0.50).
assumptions.source: M14TIL, Rohaan et al., N Engl J Med 2022

reason: A patient-reported endpoint over 48 weeks in a 26-country trial invites a large placebo response, and both ESSPRI and the new DASPRI diary must be met, so the phase 2 gap of 1.3 points could shrink below significance.
rationale: In phase 2, the symptomatic population (ESSPRI 5 or more, ESSDAI under 5) improved by 1.80 ESSPRI points on dazodalibep versus 0.53 on placebo at day 169 (P=0.0002), with gains in fatigue and dryness. Even if the effect halves to about 0.7 points, 217 per arm gives over 85% power for ESSPRI. Risks are a larger placebo response at week 48 across 194 sites and the need to win on the DASPRI diary as well. Primary completion passed in October 2026, so Amgen should report topline by early 2027.
evidence: Dazodalibep phase 2 NCT04129164 (St Clair et al., Nat Med 2024)

assumptions.claim: In phase 2 population 2, ESSPRI fell by 1.80 points on dazodalibep versus 0.53 on placebo at day 169 (difference -1.27, P=0.0002).
assumptions.source: St Clair et al., Nat Med 2024 (NCT04129164)

assumptions.claim: In phase 2 population 1, ESSDAI fell by 6.3 points on dazodalibep versus 4.1 on placebo at day 169 (P=0.017).
assumptions.source: St Clair et al., Nat Med 2024 (NCT04129164)

reason: The comparator is an approved anti-LAG-3 plus anti-PD-1 combination of the same class, so a response-rate advantage large enough for superiority (about 12 points true difference) is unlikely.
rationale: Fianlimab plus cemiplimab and relatlimab plus nivolumab share one mechanism. The phase 1 response rate of 57% looked better than Opdualag's 43% in RELATIVITY-047, but cross-trial gaps of that kind usually shrink in a randomized comparison, and as I recall Regeneron's first-line phase 3 against pembrolizumab missed statistical significance on PFS in 2026. Superiority on ORR needs roughly an 8-point observed difference with 280 per arm; I expect a few points at most. Recruitment is still open, so a result by mid-2027 is unlikely unless the trial is stopped.
evidence: Fianlimab plus cemiplimab phase 1 NCT03005782 (Hamid et al., JCO 2024)
Fianlimab plus cemiplimab vs pembrolizumab phase 3 NCT05352672

assumptions.claim: Relatlimab plus nivolumab gave an objective response rate of 43.1% by blinded central review in first-line advanced melanoma.
assumptions.source: RELATIVITY-047, Tawbi et al., N Engl J Med 2022; Long et al., NEJM Evid 2023

assumptions.claim: Fianlimab plus cemiplimab gave an objective response rate of 57% in 98 patients with PD-(L)1-naive advanced melanoma in phase 1.
assumptions.source: Hamid et al., J Clin Oncol 2024 (NCT03005782)

assumptions.claim: The phase 3 trial of fianlimab plus cemiplimab versus pembrolizumab in first-line melanoma did not reach statistical significance on progression-free survival.
assumptions.source: Regeneron announcement, 2026 (NCT05352672); recalled from memory, not verified

reason: SP-624 showed no overall separation from placebo in its first phase 2 trial, and a four-week MADRS endpoint against a typical placebo fall of 9-10 points leaves little room for a novel mechanism of unproven efficacy.
rationale: SP-624, a SIRT6 activator, did not separate from placebo overall in its first phase 2 depression trial; the signal came from a post hoc analysis in women, and subgroup-led follow-up trials seldom confirm. Novel-mechanism antidepressants succeed in perhaps a quarter of phase 2 trials, and US placebo responses at week 4 are large. The trial completed in July 2026 with no result known to me, a mild negative sign for a private sponsor. A result made public by mid-2027 is more likely to be a positive announcement, which lifts the conditional probability slightly.

assumptions.claim: The first phase 2 trial of SP-624 in major depressive disorder did not show a significant overall difference from placebo on MADRS; a post hoc analysis suggested benefit in women.

reason: The trial is almost certainly a non-inferiority comparison with dulaglutide; the risk is that an exendin-4 based agonist lowers HbA1c less than dulaglutide, as weekly exenatide did against liraglutide, and misses the margin.
rationale: Open-label Chinese phase 3 trials of new GLP-1 agonists against dulaglutide are usually built for non-inferiority with a margin of 0.3-0.4%, and doses are chosen from phase 2 to match the comparator, so most succeed. Dulaglutide 1.5 mg lowers HbA1c by about 1.4-1.7 points in Chinese patients at this baseline. With 200 per arm and a standard deviation near 1.0, non-inferiority is likely unless JY09 is truly 0.15 points or more weaker. Superiority, as the card assumes, would be unlikely. The sponsor is unlikely to publish before mid-2027.

assumptions.claim: Dulaglutide 1.5 mg lowered HbA1c by 1.73 percentage points at week 26 in mainly Chinese patients on metformin and/or a sulfonylurea.
assumptions.source: AWARD-CHN2, Wang et al., Diabetes Obes Metab 2019

assumptions.claim: Once-weekly exenatide lowered HbA1c by 1.28 points versus 1.48 with liraglutide and did not meet non-inferiority.

reason: Enrolment is closed and the week 56 visit of the last participant fixes the timeline, so the study should complete near February 2027; results are unlikely to be posted before the one-year deadline.
rationale: Active, not recruiting, with primary completion set by the last participant's week 56 visit in February 2027, so a slip of more than 90 days is unlikely. Guselkumab is approved for adult ulcerative colitis and this is a required paediatric study, so early termination is improbable. Janssen usually posts results close to the 12-month deadline, which falls in early 2028, after the read date. The primary outcome is a standard descriptive week 56 remission rate with little reason to change.

reason: No anti-tau antibody has yet met a primary endpoint; bepranemab slowed tau PET accumulation only as a secondary measure, and BMS-986446 may not slow tau spread enough to show on PET with about 100-155 patients per arm.
rationale: N-terminal tau antibodies (semorinemab, gosuranemab, tilavonemab) did nothing to tau PET, but the mid-region antibody bepranemab slowed tau PET accumulation by 33-58% over 80 weeks in phase 2, and the MTBR antibody E2814 lowered tau biomarkers in dominantly inherited disease. BMS-986446 binds the microtubule-binding region that seeds aggregation, so a PET effect is plausible, and a biomarker primary is more sensitive than a clinical scale. I put a true effect near 55% and power near 75%. Last visits come in March 2027, so topline is more likely in the second half of 2027.
evidence: E2814 phase 1b/2 in dominantly inherited Alzheimer's disease (2024)

assumptions.claim: Bepranemab missed its CDR-SB primary endpoint but slowed tau PET accumulation by 33% to 58% versus placebo over 80 weeks.
Semorinemab did not slow tau PET accumulation or clinical decline in prodromal to mild Alzheimer's disease.
assumptions.source: TAURIEL, Teng et al., JAMA Neurol 2022

reason: With only 100 vs 50 patients and a large saline injection response in the shoulder, a knee-sized effect of about 1 point at week 12, the edge of the drug's duration, gives roughly 60-70% power.
rationale: ZILRETTA beat saline at week 12 in the knee phase 3 (difference about -1.0 on average daily pain, about 160 per arm) but missed week 12 in the smaller phase 2b, so week 12 sits at the edge of its duration. Here only 100 vs 50 patients, a shoulder joint with no randomized efficacy data, rotator cuff pathology allowed and a large expected saline response. If the knee effect carries over, power is about 70%; with a smaller shoulder effect it drops below 50%. Enrolment is complete, so topline should come in the first half of 2027.
evidence: Kwon et al. 2013 (hyaluronate vs saline in glenohumeral OA)

assumptions.claim: In the knee OA phase 3 trial, ZILRETTA 32 mg changed average daily pain at week 12 by -3.12 vs -2.14 with saline placebo, a difference of about -0.98.
assumptions.source: Conaghan et al., J Bone Joint Surg Am 2018; NCT02357459

assumptions.claim: In the phase 2b knee OA trial, ZILRETTA 32 mg did not reach statistical significance against saline placebo at the week 12 primary time point.
assumptions.source: Conaghan et al., Arthritis Rheumatol 2018; NCT02116972

assumptions.claim: ZILRETTA is approved by the FDA only for osteoarthritis pain of the knee (approval October 2017).

reason: The trial is built to estimate an effect size with 30 patients per arm, so a statistically significant difference in wound closure is unlikely even if the beads help.
rationale: Open-label phase 2 of 60 patients whose stated aim is to estimate the between-group effect size, not to test a hypothesis. Wound closure after flap surgery is already frequent with standard care (roughly 55-70% by 8 weeks), so 30 per arm would need a difference of about 25 points for significance; calcium sulfate beads can also cause wound drainage. The trial is still recruiting a month before its registered completion date, so it will run late and a result by June 2027 is unlikely.
evidence: Bamba et al. 2017 (flap reconstruction for pressure ulcers, outcomes analysis)

assumptions.claim: After flap reconstruction of pressure ulcers, wound dehiscence occurs in roughly 30% of flaps.
assumptions.source: Bamba et al., Plast Reconstr Surg Glob Open 2017

assumptions.claim: The registry record states the purpose as assessing safety, tolerability and the between-group effect size, with 60 patients randomized 1:1.

reason: Failure would most likely come from a strong placebo arm under basal insulin titration or from a disclosure that does not state the primary endpoint, not from lack of glucose lowering.
rationale: Retatrutide lowered HbA1c by about 2 points in phase 2; against placebo on basal insulin the expected difference is well over 1 point with 320 patients, so power is near 100%. Tirzepatide in the same setting (SURPASS-5) gave a 1.2-1.5 point difference. The remaining risks are a strong placebo arm through insulin titration, tolerability in renal impairment and a first disclosure that only calls the result positive. Primary completion was October 2026, so Lilly should report within months.

assumptions.claim: In the phase 2 trial in type 2 diabetes, retatrutide 12 mg lowered HbA1c by about 2.0 percentage points at 24 weeks versus about 0 with placebo.
In SURPASS-5, placebo added to titrated insulin glargine lowered HbA1c by about 0.9 points at 40 weeks and tirzepatide by 2.1 to 2.4 points.

reason: Still recruiting two months before its registered primary completion with a 24-week treatment period, so the date will slip well past March 2027 if the record is updated, and results posting is unlikely.
rationale: Small phase 2 at five Chinese sites, still recruiting in late October 2026 with a 24-week treatment period and a December 2026 primary completion date; the last patient cannot finish in time, so an updated record will show a later date. Small sponsors of this kind rarely post results on ClinicalTrials.gov within a year and seldom change a safety primary outcome.

reason: A single-site trial that started in March 2025 and is still recruiting 63 patients cannot complete 24 weeks of follow-up by December 2026, so the primary date will move later if the record is updated.
rationale: Open-label dose-ranging phase 2 at one Chinese site, started March 2025, still recruiting in late October 2026 with response assessed over 24 weeks and a December 2026 primary completion date. Lower-risk MDS patients enrol slowly at a single site, so a delay beyond March 2027 is likely. Results posting on ClinicalTrials.gov by August 2027 is very unlikely; the descriptive primary outcome with three cohorts has a small chance of being reworded in substance.

reason: The phase 1/2 trial is still recruiting with response followed for up to two years, so primary completion in December 2026 is not credible and the date should move well past March 2027.
rationale: Phase 1/2 with dose escalation, expansion and a randomized stage against sorafenib alone, 60 patients at nine sites in China and Hong Kong, still recruiting in late October 2026. Second-line HCC after immunotherapy enrols slowly and response follow-up is long, so the December 2026 date will slip if the record is updated. A small Chinese sponsor is unlikely to post results by August 2027; a multi-stage protocol carries a modest chance of a change to the primary outcome.

reason: BHV-7000 has no efficacy data in epilepsy patients and may engage brain Kv7 channels too weakly at 75 mg to beat a placebo response of about 20% over a short 8-week treatment phase.
rationale: Kv7 opening is a validated mechanism in focal epilepsy (ezogabine; XEN1101 cut seizures by a median 53% vs 18% with placebo in X-TOLE). BHV-7000 has no patient efficacy data in epilepsy, only phase 1 EEG target engagement, and it failed in bipolar mania; its clean tolerability raises doubt about brain exposure at 75 mg. The treatment phase is only 8 weeks, at 150 sites in 16 countries, which invites a high placebo response. About 130 per arm detects a difference of roughly 12 points. Primary completion was October 2026, so topline is near.

assumptions.claim: In X-TOLE, XEN1101 25 mg reduced monthly focal seizure frequency by a median 52.8% versus 18.2% with placebo.
assumptions.source: French et al., JAMA Neurol 2023; NCT03796962

assumptions.claim: BHV-7000 did not separate from placebo on the primary endpoint of its phase 2/3 trial in bipolar mania, reported in 2025.
The record names BHV-7000 75 mg versus placebo as the primary comparison, measured over an 8-week double-blind phase after an 8-week observation phase.

reason: Sema3A blockade has not been shown to regress retinopathy lesions, and with about 35 patients per arm only an anti-VEGF-sized effect on DRSS would be significant.
rationale: First efficacy test of an anti-Sema3A antibody on retinopathy severity; the endpoint (2-step DRSS improvement) was built around anti-VEGF drugs, which reach 65-80% vs about 15% for sham, and nothing shows Sema3A blockade regresses lesions. About 35 per arm needs a difference near 20 points. The record still says recruiting although a week-52 endpoint cannot complete by March 2027, so the primary date will slip into late 2027; a result by June 2027 would mostly mean an early stop.

assumptions.claim: In PANORAMA, about 15% of sham-treated eyes had a 2-step or greater DRSS improvement at week 52, versus 65% and 80% with the two aflibercept regimens.
assumptions.source: Brown et al., JAMA Ophthalmol 2021; NCT02718326

assumptions.claim: BI 764524 has earlier clinical data only from a phase 1/2a trial in diabetic macular ischaemia, not from a trial with a DRSS endpoint.

reason: Two co-primary histology endpoints in 48 patients leave very little power, and HSD17B13 knockdown has no proven effect on fibrosis or NASH activity within 52 weeks.
rationale: Two co-primary biopsy endpoints in 48 patients: even an effective drug would rarely reach significance on both (resmetirom needed hundreds per arm for 10-12 point differences). HSD17B13 knockdown lowered ALT in phase 1 but has no proven histological effect, and it does not lower liver fat, so the key secondary is unlikely too. Visirna is a private company; disclosure would come through a congress abstract or a partner statement, with the primary completion date already passed in July 2026.

assumptions.claim: In the phase 1/2 trial of ARO-HSD, the top dose lowered hepatic HSD17B13 mRNA by about 93% and ALT by about 42% in patients with suspected NASH.
assumptions.source: Mak et al., J Hepatol 2023; NCT04202354

assumptions.claim: In MAESTRO-NASH, fibrosis improved by at least one stage without worsening of NASH in 14% of placebo patients and 24-26% of resmetirom patients at week 52.
assumptions.source: Harrison et al., N Engl J Med 2024

reason: The class effect is reliable, so the main threat is a low exacerbation rate in the placebo arm that would shrink the number of events and the power.
rationale: Anti-IL-5 antibodies have cut severe exacerbations by about half in every pivotal trial in eosinophilic asthma (mepolizumab, reslizumab, depemokimab), and by more in Chinese patients (mepolizumab China phase 3, benralizumab MIRACLE). 610 showed lung function gains in phase 2. With 480 patients over 52 weeks, power is above 90% unless the placebo exacerbation rate is very low. The record still says recruiting with a February 2027 completion date, so timing is uncertain; a result by June 2027 requires enrolment to have ended by early 2026.

assumptions.claim: In MENSA, subcutaneous mepolizumab reduced the rate of clinically significant exacerbations by 53% versus placebo.
assumptions.source: Ortega et al., N Engl J Med 2014

assumptions.claim: In MIRACLE, in mainly Chinese patients, benralizumab reduced the annual exacerbation rate by 74% (0.49 vs 1.38 per year with placebo).
assumptions.source: Lai et al., Respir Med 2024; NCT03186209

assumptions.claim: In SWIFT-1 and SWIFT-2, depemokimab lowered the annualized exacerbation rate to 0.46 and 0.56 versus 1.11 and 1.08 with placebo.
assumptions.source: Jackson et al., N Engl J Med 2024

reason: With about 100 patients and fairly high six-month retention among take-home-eligible methadone patients, too few dropouts will occur to show a retention difference, and both primaries must favour Sonara.
rationale: Single-site SBIR trial of 100 patients comparing an app-monitored take-home workflow with usual take-homes. Only about 25-30 dropout events are expected over 24 weeks, giving little power unless the hazard ratio is below about 0.4. Both primaries (retention and take-home doses received) must favour Sonara. A public result before mid-2027 is unlikely: primary completion is March 2027, the trial was still recruiting in late 2026 and the sponsor is a small company.
evidence: Timko 2016 systematic review of retention in medication treatment for opioid dependence
ROME I pilot of Sonara video-observed methadone take-homes (SBIR phase I)

assumptions.claim: Retention in methadone treatment at 6 months varies widely across studies, with typical values around 50-70% for patients starting treatment.
assumptions.source: Timko et al., J Addict Dis 2016, systematic review of retention in medication-assisted treatment for opiate dependence

reason: IL-13 blockade alone may add only about half a TNSS point over a large placebo response on background nasal steroids, near the edge of what 450 patients can detect.
rationale: No phase 2 in rhinitis; Lilly went straight to phase 3 on mechanism. IL-4R-alpha blockade (stapokibart) improved TNSS in eosinophil-high seasonal rhinitis, but dupilumab alone and the anti-IL-13 QAX576 did not cut allergen-challenge symptoms, and IL-13-only blockade leaves IL-4 signalling intact. Placebo response on background INCS is large (about -2.4 points). With about 225 per arm and SD near 2.6 the trial detects roughly 0.7 points; I expect a true effect near 0.4-0.5, so slightly under even odds.
evidence: Stapokibart phase 3 in seasonal allergic rhinitis, Nature Medicine 2025
QAX576 nasal allergen challenge study, Nicholson 2011
ADvocate1 and ADvocate2 lebrikizumab atopic dermatitis 2023
LAVOLTA I and II lebrikizumab asthma 2016

assumptions.claim: Stapokibart, an anti-IL-4R-alpha antibody, significantly reduced the daily reflective total nasal symptom score versus placebo on background intranasal corticosteroid in a phase 3 trial in seasonal allergic rhinitis patients with blood eosinophils of at least 300 per microlitre.
assumptions.source: Stapokibart phase 3 SAR trial (MERAK), Nature Medicine 2025

assumptions.claim: Dupilumab monotherapy for 16 weeks did not significantly reduce the total nasal symptom score after nasal allergen challenge compared with placebo.
assumptions.source: Corren et al., J Allergy Clin Immunol 2021 (NCT03558997)

assumptions.claim: A single dose of the anti-IL-13 antibody QAX576 lowered nasal IL-13 but did not reduce nasal symptoms after allergen challenge in allergic rhinitis.
assumptions.source: Nicholson et al., J Allergy Clin Immunol 2011

reason: The record lists start, primary completion and study completion all as December 2026 although follow-up is 12 months, so the dates will almost certainly be pushed back if the sponsor updates the record at all.
rationale: Small private sponsor with a history of slow trial starts. The record gives start, primary completion and study completion all as December 2026 while the primary outcome needs 12 months of follow-up in 40 implant recipients at 6 sites. Any record update must move primary completion well past March 2027; without an update the lateness question voids. Results posting by August 2027 is essentially impossible. Modest risk of withdrawal if the study never enrols; the single safety primary is unlikely to be redefined.

reason: PFS should be met comfortably against paclitaxel alone, but overall survival is a second primary and may be immature or not significant when the first result is reported.
rationale: Adding VEGFR2 blockade to paclitaxel improved PFS in RAINBOW (HR 0.64) and RAINBOW-Asia (HR 0.77); the phase 2 triplet after immunochemotherapy failure showed ORR near 48% and PFS near 6.8 months versus about 3 months expected with paclitaxel alone. With 506 patients PFS success is very likely (about 0.9). The discount is for overall survival, the second primary: it may be immature or miss at the first report, and the round requires all primaries to be met.
evidence: Cadonilimab plus pulocimab plus paclitaxel phase 2, ASCO 2024

assumptions.claim: In RAINBOW, median PFS was 2.9 months with placebo plus paclitaxel and 4.4 months with ramucirumab plus paclitaxel (hazard ratio 0.635).
assumptions.source: RAINBOW, Wilke et al., Lancet Oncol 2014 (NCT01170663)

assumptions.claim: In RAINBOW-Asia, ramucirumab plus paclitaxel improved PFS (4.14 vs 3.15 months, hazard ratio 0.765) while the overall survival hazard ratio was 0.963.
assumptions.source: RAINBOW-Asia, Xu et al., Lancet Gastroenterol Hepatol 2021 (NCT02898077)

assumptions.claim: In a phase 2 study, cadonilimab plus pulocimab plus paclitaxel gave an objective response rate of about 48% and median PFS of about 6.8 months in gastric cancer patients who had failed first-line immunochemotherapy.
assumptions.source: Akeso phase 2 study of AK104 plus AK109 plus paclitaxel, ASCO 2024 abstract

reason: TIGIT blockade has failed in larger HCC and lung trials, and with about 39 patients per arm only a response-rate gain above 20 points would reach significance.
rationale: Randomised phase 2 with about 39 per arm; significance on ORR needs roughly a 22-point gain, and PFS is a second primary. TIGIT blockade has failed repeatedly in phase 3, including tiragolumab added to atezolizumab-bevacizumab in HCC after a promising MORPHEUS-Liver signal. Control ORR with serplulimab plus bevacizumab should be near 25-30%. A public result by mid-2027 is unlikely because the trial was still recruiting in late 2026.

assumptions.claim: Atezolizumab plus bevacizumab gave an objective response rate of 27.3% by independent review per RECIST 1.1 in first-line HCC.
In MORPHEUS-Liver, tiragolumab plus atezolizumab-bevacizumab gave an objective response rate of 42.5% versus 11.1% with atezolizumab-bevacizumab alone.
The phase 3 IMbrave152/SKYSCRAPER-14 trial of tiragolumab added to atezolizumab-bevacizumab in first-line HCC did not meet its primary endpoints.

reason: No tau-directed or OGA-inhibitor therapy has slowed PSP or Alzheimer's progression, so the most likely outcome is no difference from placebo on the PSPRS.
rationale: Every disease-modifying trial in PSP has failed (davunetide, tideglusib, gosuranemab, tilavonemab), and the OGA-inhibitor class missed in Alzheimer's disease (ceperognastat). FNP-223 has target-engagement data only, no clinical efficacy signal. Placebo decline of about 10-11 PSPRS points over 52 weeks is well established, and 241 patients give power only for roughly a 35-40% slowing. I put success under 10%.

assumptions.claim: In PASSPORT, PSPRS worsened by about 10.5 points over 52 weeks in the placebo group, with no difference between gosuranemab and placebo.
assumptions.source: PASSPORT, Dam et al., Nature Medicine 2021 (NCT03068468)

assumptions.claim: Tilavonemab did not slow PSPRS worsening versus placebo over 52 weeks in a phase 2 PSP trial.
assumptions.source: ARISE, Hoglinger et al., Lancet Neurol 2021 (NCT02985879)

assumptions.claim: The OGA inhibitor ceperognastat did not meet its primary endpoint in the phase 2 PROSPECT-ALZ trial in early Alzheimer's disease.

reason: The survival gain over physician's-choice chemotherapy may be modest (hazard ratio near 0.8), leaving the trial at about even odds with roughly 360 deaths.
rationale: Sac-TMT showed ORR about 22% and OS near 7.5 months in a single-arm Chinese cohort of pretreated gastric cancer; third-line chemotherapy gives 5-6 months. I expect a true OS hazard ratio near 0.8, which with about 360 deaths gives roughly even odds. TROP2 ADCs have a mixed survival record (EVOKE-01 and TROPION-Lung01 missed; sac-TMT won in TNBC). The control includes irinotecan, a same-class payload. No early efficacy stop was announced before the planned completion date.

assumptions.claim: In TAGS, median overall survival was 5.7 months with trifluridine-tipiracil versus 3.6 months with placebo in heavily pretreated gastric cancer.
assumptions.source: TAGS, Shitara et al., Lancet Oncol 2018 (NCT02500043)

assumptions.claim: Third-line chemotherapy (paclitaxel or irinotecan) gave a median overall survival of 5.0 months in JAVELIN Gastric 300.
assumptions.source: JAVELIN Gastric 300, Bang et al., Ann Oncol 2018

assumptions.claim: Sacituzumab tirumotecan gave an objective response rate of about 22% in previously treated gastric or gastroesophageal junction cancer in a phase 2 cohort.

reason: Subjective relief within 4 hours occurs in about 40% of placebo-treated attacks, so a high placebo response in a small trial is the main way an effective C1-INH concentrate could miss.
rationale: Plasma-derived C1-INH replacement is a validated treatment for acute HAE attacks: Berinert (IMPACT-1) and Cinryze both beat placebo on time to onset of relief with fewer patients than planned here. The endpoint copies the Cinryze trial's unequivocal-relief definition, where placebo relief within 4 hours was about 40%. The main risk is a high placebo response on a subjective endpoint. Octapharma is private and the trial was still recruiting, so a public result by mid-2027 is unlikely.

assumptions.claim: In the nanofiltered C1-INH acute-attack trial, median time to onset of unequivocal relief was 2 hours with C1-INH versus more than 4 hours with placebo (p=0.02).
In IMPACT-1, C1-INH 20 U/kg shortened median time to onset of symptom relief to 0.5 hours versus 1.5 hours with placebo.
assumptions.source: IMPACT-1, Craig et al., J Allergy Clin Immunol 2009 (NCT00168103)

reason: Enrolment is complete and the primary window is 18 weeks, so the trial should finish on time; results posting by August 2027 is unlikely.
rationale: AbbVie-run supportive-care study, already closed to enrolment with a primary window of 18 weeks, so the February 2027 primary completion looks safe. AbbVie usually posts results close to the 12-month deadline, which falls after the read date. Little reason for termination since the drug is marketed and the study addresses a labelled toxicity; the primary outcome is a simple safety count unlikely to be redefined.

reason: Survival differences against docetaxel can be diluted by active later-line therapy and by toxicity-related dose reductions, even if PFS and response clearly favour BL-B01D1.
rationale: BL-B01D1 gave response rates of roughly 30-45% and PFS over 5 months in pretreated EGFR wild-type NSCLC, against about 12% and 3.5 months for docetaxel, and has won phase 3 trials versus chemotherapy in nasopharyngeal and oesophageal cancer. With 698 patients the trial has good power for an OS hazard ratio near 0.75. Risks are OS dilution by later therapy and haematological toxicity. The sponsor announces positive interims promptly, so an early public result is more likely positive.
evidence: BL-B01D1 phase 1, Ma et al., Lancet Oncol 2024 (NCT05194982)
BL-B01D1 phase 3 in second-line oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma 2025

assumptions.claim: Docetaxel gave a median overall survival of 11.8 months in previously treated advanced NSCLC in TROPION-Lung01.
assumptions.source: TROPION-Lung01, Ahn et al., J Clin Oncol 2024 (NCT04656652)

assumptions.claim: In the first-in-human study, BL-B01D1 produced objective responses in roughly 30-45% of previously treated patients with EGFR wild-type NSCLC.
The sponsor reported that the phase 3 trial of BL-B01D1 versus chemotherapy in second-line oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma met its PFS and OS endpoints at an interim analysis.

reason: The anti-CD70 add-on has not clearly beaten venetoclax-azacitidine response rates in earlier studies, and about 120 patients randomized 2:1 can only detect a hazard ratio near 0.6 on overall survival.
rationale: Cusatuzumab (anti-CD70) disappointed after early promise: CULMINATE with azacitidine gave CR rates of 27% and 14%, and the ELEVATE triplet's response rate (about 77%) was in line with venetoclax-azacitidine alone. Part A randomizes only about 120 patients 2:1; with roughly 65-70 deaths the trial needs an observed hazard ratio near 0.6 for two-sided 0.05 (about 0.72 under a relaxed phase 2 alpha). My prior true HR is about 0.9. Control should mirror VIALE-A (median OS about 14 months). A private sponsor may report late.

assumptions.claim: In VIALE-A, median overall survival was 14.7 months with venetoclax plus azacitidine versus 9.6 months with azacitidine alone.
In CULMINATE, cusatuzumab plus azacitidine gave complete remission rates of 27% at 10 mg/kg and 14% at 20 mg/kg.
In the phase 1b ELEVATE study, cusatuzumab with venetoclax and azacitidine produced an overall response rate of about 77% in 44 patients.

reason: The gene-agnostic modifier mechanism is unproven and phase 1/2 support was small and uncontrolled; similar retinal gene therapies failed mobility endpoints in phase 3.
rationale: OCU400 is a gene-agnostic NR2E3 modifier therapy supported only by a small open-label phase 1/2 (18 RP patients, 'stabilization or improvement' claims). Comparable retinal gene-therapy phase 3 trials with mobility-course endpoints mostly failed (LUMEOS, XIRIUS, STAR); voretigene succeeded with a much stronger mechanism. Untreated, unmasked controls and a sponsor-specific LDNA test add some bias toward treatment, and 140 patients give adequate power if a real effect exists. Enrollment is complete with fixed 52-week follow-up, so a spring 2027 topline is likely; Ocugen plans a BLA.

assumptions.claim: In the voretigene neparvovec phase 3 trial with an untreated control arm, mean bilateral multi-luminance mobility test change at 1 year was 1.8 light levels with treatment versus 0.2 in controls.
The phase 3 LUMEOS trial of botaretigene sparoparvovec in X-linked retinitis pigmentosa did not meet its primary endpoint on the vision-guided mobility assessment.
The OCU400 phase 1/2 study was open-label, without a randomized control, and treated 18 retinitis pigmentosa participants.

reason: Ruxolitinib alone should already produce a high 6-month response rate in new-onset cGVHD, leaving a gain of about 10 points that roughly 65 patients per arm cannot prove.
rationale: Axatilimab is clearly active in refractory cGVHD (AGAVE-201 ORR 74%) and ruxolitinib gave a 50% week-24 ORR in REACH3, so both arms should respond well in new-onset disease. I expect about 55% 6-month ORR on ruxolitinib and 65-70% on the combination. With at most 65 per arm a 10-12 point gain is not significant, and this open-label phase 2 is framed as preliminary efficacy and contribution of components, so a formal 'primary met' statement is uncertain. First-line cGVHD add-on trials (ibrutinib, itacitinib) have failed before.

assumptions.claim: In AGAVE-201, axatilimab 0.3 mg/kg every 2 weeks gave an overall response rate of 74% within the first 6 cycles in recurrent or refractory chronic GVHD.
In REACH3, the overall response rate at week 24 was 49.7% with ruxolitinib versus 25.6% with best available therapy in steroid-refractory chronic GVHD.
In AGAVE-201, 6% of patients receiving axatilimab 0.3 mg/kg every 2 weeks discontinued treatment because of adverse events.

reason: Failure would need an unexpectedly low early EASI 90 rate on upadacitinib 15 mg in dupilumab-refractory patients, since week 8 is an early read of a demanding endpoint.
rationale: Patients enter with active disease (EASI at least 12) despite at least 4 months of dupilumab, so continued dupilumab should give very few EASI 90 responses by week 8 (about 5%). Upadacitinib acts fast: EASI 90 was 61% vs 39% at week 16 in Heads Up and 41% vs 23% in LEVEL UP with a 15 mg start and escalation. Even in a refractory population at week 8 I expect 30-35% on upadacitinib, a difference near 28 points that 92 per arm detects easily.

assumptions.claim: In LEVEL UP, EASI 90 at week 16 was reached by 40.8% of patients on upadacitinib (15 mg with escalation to 30 mg) versus 22.5% on dupilumab.
assumptions.source: LEVEL UP, Silverberg et al., Br J Dermatol 2025 (NCT05601882)

assumptions.claim: In Heads Up, EASI 90 at week 16 was reached by 60.6% of patients on upadacitinib 30 mg versus 38.7% on dupilumab.
assumptions.source: Heads Up, Blauvelt et al., JAMA Dermatol 2021 (NCT03738397)

assumptions.claim: SWITCH-UP requires at least 4 months of current dupilumab use with an inadequate response and a baseline EASI of 12 or more.

reason: Enrolment is closed and the PSA50 read is short, so the trial should reach its data cut near the registered date; the sponsor may still shift the date or reprioritise, and results posting is not due until late 2027.
rationale: AstraZeneca-run (Fusion) dose-optimisation study with enrolment closed at 110 patients; PSA50 is read 12 weeks after first dose, so the December 2026 date is plausible, though data cut-offs often move and the safety outcome runs for years. Results are not due on ClinicalTrials.gov until late 2027. Strategic termination is possible given actinium supply and pipeline reprioritisation but unlikely while patients remain in follow-up. The descriptive primary outcomes are unlikely to be rewritten.

reason: The top dose may lower Abeta42 production too little, or over too short a time, to separate amyloid PET change from a placebo accumulation of only a few Centiloids.
rationale: RG6289 is a gamma-secretase modulator that lowered CSF Abeta42 dose-dependently in phase 1. Production-lowering drugs have reliably moved amyloid PET: lanabecestat cut plaque by roughly 13-18 Centiloids over two years (AMARANTH), while untreated amyloid-positive people accumulate about 4 CL per year (A4). I expect placebo +5 CL at week 72 and the top dose to halt or modestly reverse accumulation (difference about -6.5 CL); with SD near 9 and about 64 per arm that is well powered. Risks: under-dosing, dropouts, and no prior GSM with PET proof.

assumptions.claim: In the A4 study, mean amyloid PET rose by 19.3 Centiloids over 240 weeks in the placebo group.
In AMARANTH, the BACE inhibitor lanabecestat reduced florbetapir amyloid PET by roughly 13 to 18 Centiloids over 104 weeks at 20 and 50 mg.
assumptions.source: AMARANTH, Wessels et al., JAMA Neurol 2020 (NCT02245737)

assumptions.claim: The trial enrolls cognitively unimpaired or MCI participants with a positive amyloid PET of at least 24 Centiloids.

reason: PSD-95 inhibition with nerinetide failed to improve 90-day outcome in three large trials, and the plasmin-resistant successor has no clinical efficacy evidence alongside thrombolysis.
rationale: NoNO-42 is a plasmin-resistant successor to nerinetide, whose PSD-95 inhibition did not improve 90-day mRS in ESCAPE-NA1, ESCAPE-NEXT or FRONTIER; the only signals were subgroup findings. No clinical data yet show the new peptide works alongside thrombolysis, so I give about 9% for a positive shift analysis. The trial is still recruiting at nine Canadian sites toward up to 600 patients with a 90-day endpoint, so the December 2026 date will be missed and a result by mid-2027 is unlikely unless an adaptive interim stops the domain.

assumptions.claim: In ESCAPE-NA1, 61.4% of nerinetide patients versus 59.2% of placebo patients reached mRS 0-2 at 90 days, a non-significant difference.
ESCAPE-NEXT found no improvement in 90-day functional independence with nerinetide in thrombectomy patients not given thrombolysis.
FRONTIER found no overall benefit of prehospital nerinetide on 90-day functional outcome.

reason: Solriamfetol's catecholamine effect is weaker than lisdexamfetamine's and placebo responses in binge eating disorder are large, so the drug-placebo gap may be too small to reach significance.
rationale: Solriamfetol is a dopamine-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor with TAAR1 agonism. Related mechanisms work in BED (lisdexamfetamine: -3.9 vs -2.5 binge days per week; dasotraline positive), but solriamfetol is weaker, has no sponsor phase 2 in BED, and in adult ADHD was significant only at 150 mg. I assume about a 0.5 episode/week advantage over a large placebo response (about -2.9), SD near 2.2, giving roughly 60-70% power per dose with 150 per arm; either dose can win. Axsome reliably press-releases toplines.

assumptions.claim: In the two phase 3 lisdexamfetamine trials in binge eating disorder, binge days per week fell by about 3.9 on drug versus 2.5 and 2.3 on placebo.
In the FOCUS trial in adult ADHD, solriamfetol 150 mg met the primary endpoint while the 300 mg dose did not reach statistical significance.
Flexible-dose dasotraline reduced binge days per week more than placebo (about -3.7 vs -2.8) over 12 weeks.
assumptions.source: McElroy et al., J Clin Psychiatry 2020 (NCT02564588)

reason: Forty-five patients yield about 30 events, so only a very large event-free survival effect could be significant, and CDK4/6 inhibition has shown modest activity in glioma.
rationale: A 45-patient randomized paediatric study, probably run to meet paediatric regulatory obligations, cannot show conventional superiority unless the EFS hazard ratio is about 0.45 or better with roughly 30 events. Abemaciclib reaches the CNS and modestly prolonged PFS in adult unmethylated glioblastoma (INSIGhT, HR about 0.72) without a survival gain; CDK4/6 inhibitors have shown little in paediatric high-grade glioma. I expect a true HR near 0.85 and control median EFS about 6.5 months from post-radiotherapy randomization. Lilly is unlikely to publicise results before registry posting.

assumptions.claim: In HERBY, median event-free survival in paediatric high-grade glioma was 11.8 months with radiotherapy plus temozolomide versus 8.2 months with added bevacizumab.
assumptions.source: HERBY, Grill et al., J Clin Oncol 2018 (NCT01390948)

assumptions.claim: In INSIGhT, abemaciclib prolonged progression-free survival versus temozolomide control in MGMT-unmethylated glioblastoma (hazard ratio about 0.72) without an overall survival benefit.
assumptions.source: INSIGhT, Rahman et al., J Clin Oncol 2023 (NCT02977780)

reason: With about 21 patients per arm, a 1-2 point QMG advantage after 21 days can easily miss significance against a variable placebo response.
rationale: NMD670, a ClC-1 chloride channel inhibitor, improved QMG after single doses in a 12-patient crossover study, so a symptomatic gain of 1-2 QMG points over placebo at day 21 is plausible. With about 21 per arm and SD near 3.6, a pairwise comparison needs roughly 2.3 points for two-sided 0.05; three doses give several chances and a phase 2b may use a pooled or dose-response test. I put success near 38%. Recruitment has been slow (84 patients since May 2024, still recruiting), so topline will probably slip into 2027.
evidence: NMD670 phase 1/2a in myasthenia gravis, Sci Transl Med 2024

assumptions.claim: A single-dose crossover study in 12 patients with myasthenia gravis reported improved QMG total score with NMD670 versus placebo.
assumptions.source: Ruijs et al., Sci Transl Med 2024

assumptions.claim: The trial plans 84 participants across three NMD670 dose levels and placebo, dosed twice daily for 21 days.

reason: Dato-DXd could add only a modest PFS gain over a platinum doublet, as HER3-DXd did (HR 0.77), with ILD and stomatitis discontinuations and alpha split across two comparisons eroding the margin.
rationale: Post-osimertinib platinum-pemetrexed gives BICR PFS near 4.2-5.4 months (MARIPOSA-2, HERTHENA-Lung02). TROP2 ADCs are active in EGFRm NSCLC: sac-TMT beat the same control with HR 0.49 (OptiTROP-Lung04); Dato-DXd had ORR about 43% in pretreated EGFRm disease (TROPION-Lung05/01). Adding osimertinib gave median PFS 9.5-11.7 months in ORCHARD and keeps CNS control. With 256 per arm and about 340 events, an HR near 0.55 is amply powered. Risks: ILD and stomatitis discontinuations, open-label censoring, alpha split across dual comparisons.

assumptions.claim: In MARIPOSA-2 the platinum-pemetrexed arm had a median PFS by BICR of 4.2 months after osimertinib.
In OptiTROP-Lung04 the TROP2 ADC sacituzumab tirumotecan gave a PFS hazard ratio of about 0.49 versus platinum-pemetrexed after EGFR TKI failure.
In HERTHENA-Lung02 patritumab deruxtecan gave a PFS hazard ratio of 0.77 versus platinum-pemetrexed.

reason: Nineteen patients cannot show a 24-week liver iron difference unless it exceeds about 2.5 mg Fe/g, and hepcidin elevation mainly redistributes iron rather than removing it.
rationale: Only 19 patients were randomized across 26 sites, and primary and study completion coincide, suggesting a curtailed study. Raising hepcidin blocks absorption and sequesters iron but offers no excretion route, so a 24-week LIC fall beyond MRI noise (SD about 2-3 mg/g) is doubtful; placebo LIC drifts up only about 0.4 mg/g per year (THALASSA). The TMPRSS6 antisense sapablursen disappointed in NTDT. With about 10 vs 9 patients, significance needs a difference near 2.5 mg/g. Disclosure is likely via registry posting in late 2027.

assumptions.claim: Placebo-treated NTDT patients in THALASSA had a mean liver iron rise of about 0.38 mg Fe/g dw over 52 weeks.
The record lists an enrolment of 19 across 26 sites.

reason: Both AUC ratios must fall inside the margins; patient PK variability and missing steady-state samples in an adjuvant population are the main threats.
rationale: Amgen has a long record of biosimilar PK similarity studies meeting standard 80-125% margins (ABP 215, ABP 980, ABP 959). Pembrolizumab PK is linear with moderate variability, and 163 resected patients without tumour burden reduce target-mediated noise. Two co-primary AUCs (first dose and steady state) must both pass; dropout before weeks 16-19 and immune-related discontinuations thin the steady-state set. Public disclosure before mid-2027 is uncertain; registry posting may be delayed for an unapproved product.

assumptions.claim: ABP 215 met PK similarity to bevacizumab within the 80-125% margin in its phase 1 study.

reason: An unvalidated add-on to weekly paclitaxel must reach an observed HR near 0.62 with about 68 events, which few agents besides anti-angiogenics have achieved in platinum-resistant disease.
rationale: B013's target is not stated in the record and I cannot confirm it; the base rate for a randomized phase 2 add-on to weekly paclitaxel in platinum-resistant ovarian cancer is low. Paclitaxel alone gives median PFS near 4 months (AURELIA 3.9). With 90 patients and about 68 events, significance needs an observed HR near 0.62, so only a bevacizumab-like effect would succeed. Still recruiting two months before registered completion; a Chinese phase 2 rarely reports within months, so public results by mid-2027 are unlikely.

assumptions.claim: In AURELIA, weekly paclitaxel alone gave a median PFS of 3.9 months in platinum-resistant ovarian cancer.
