reason: The very large effect seen in the China phase 3 may shrink in a global population with a stronger placebo response, leaving a difference too small to separate.
rationale: China phase 3 showed a very large effect (MG-ADL -5.74 vs -0.91 at week 24), supported by phase 2 and by BLyS/APRIL biology. A global, placebo-controlled trial should see a stronger placebo response (-2 to -3 as in MINT, Vivacity-MG3) and a smaller effect, but 191 patients give over 90% power for a 1.7-point difference (SD about 3.6). Even heavy discounting of the Chinese effect leaves a likely win. Enrolment is complete; week-24 data lock around March 2027, topline guided for H1 2027.

assumptions.claim: In the China phase 3 trial, MG-ADL fell by 5.74 points with telitacicept versus 0.91 with placebo at week 24.
In MINT, MG-ADL fell by about 2.2 points on placebo and 4.2 on inebilizumab at week 26.
In Vivacity-MG3, placebo patients improved by about 3.25 MG-ADL points over weeks 22-24.

reason: Ulcerative colitis efficacy may not carry over to Crohn's disease, and a high, variable placebo CDAI response can swallow a modest drug effect at week 12.
rationale: Obefazimod worked in ulcerative colitis (ABTECT induction, placebo-adjusted remission about 16% at 50 mg), but this is its first controlled Crohn's test and UC activity translates unevenly (ozanimod, tofacitinib failed in CD). CDAI change is a sensitive continuous endpoint, yet placebo falls of 40-90 points and SD about 95 mean a dose arm of 50-70 needs roughly a 40-50 point advantage. I weigh 40% strong effect, 25% modest, 35% none. Thirteen registered primary outcomes add labelling ambiguity. Topline expected around the turn of 2026-27.

assumptions.claim: Obefazimod 50 mg gave a pooled placebo-adjusted clinical remission rate of 16.4% at week 8 in the ABTECT ulcerative colitis induction trials.
In GALAXI-1, placebo CDAI change at week 12 was about -36 points.
Ozanimod, approved in ulcerative colitis, failed its phase 3 Crohn's induction trial.

reason: Slow enrolment and thin funding make a fully powered BICR PFS analysis unlikely by the deadline; any early readout would be a small descriptive interim.
rationale: Open-label phase 2 from a cash-constrained small sponsor, still recruiting 142 patients at 15 US sites months before registered completion; a formal BICR PFS analysis by mid-2027 is unlikely, and any early disclosure would probably be descriptive interim data or a stop, both scored not met. Biologically the comparison is favourable: platinum rechallenge plus checkpoint inhibitor versus docetaxel (median PFS about 3.7 months), so an HR below 1 is plausible, but oncolytic vaccinia evidence comes from ovarian cancer (VIRO-15), not lung.

assumptions.claim: Docetaxel gave a median PFS of 3.7 months in previously treated NSCLC in TROPION-Lung01.

reason: Cirrhotic livers can carry little fat at baseline, which would shrink the absolute PDFF change, though the relative effect should stay large.
rationale: Glucagon co-agonism strips liver fat: efinopegdutide 10 mg cut liver fat 72.7% relative at 24 weeks in NAFLD versus 42.3% for semaglutide, and semaglutide itself lowered MRI-PDFF in compensated MASH cirrhosis. Even with lower baseline fat in cirrhosis, a 50-60% relative reduction against a near-flat placebo over 28 weeks should be highly significant with 85 patients. Trial completed August 2026; Merck usually posts registry results about 12 months after completion, with a congress presentation (EASL 2027) possible before mid-2027.

assumptions.claim: Efinopegdutide 10 mg weekly gave a 72.7% relative reduction in liver fat at week 24 versus 42.3% with semaglutide.
Semaglutide reduced liver fat on MRI versus placebo in NASH compensated cirrhosis.

reason: Still recruiting late in 2026 with a 36-week primary follow-up, so completion will slip past mid-2027; no results posting expected by the read date.
rationale: Safety-primary phase 2 from a private biotech. Week 36 primary follow-up means the last patient must have been dosed by about July 2026 for a March 2027 completion, yet the record still showed recruiting in late October 2026 across 50 sites, so the date very likely slips past June 2027. Adaptive design and venture funding give some stop risk. Results posting by August 2027 is implausible as it falls before or just after completion.

reason: If remission is read while cyclosporine is still being given (about 12 months), the control arm's remission rate may be too high to show superiority.
rationale: B007 appears to be a humanized anti-CD20 antibody (exclusions cite CD20 resistance). Anti-CD20 versus calcineurin inhibitor in membranous nephropathy wins when remission is read after the CNI is withdrawn: MENTOR 60% vs 20% at 24 months, MAJESTY obinutuzumab vs tacrolimus at week 104; at 12 months the gap is small (60% vs 52%). The approximately 2-year frame suggests a late read, favouring B007, but time point and hypothesis are unstated. Still recruiting, so no result by mid-2027 is likely.

assumptions.claim: In MENTOR, remission at 24 months was 60% with rituximab versus 20% with cyclosporine, and 60% versus 52% at 12 months.
In MAJESTY, obinutuzumab gave a higher complete remission rate at week 104 than tacrolimus.

reason: With about 20 patients per arm, only a very large gap in day-70 clinical cure (roughly 35 points or more) can reach significance, and standard antiviral-plus-steroid therapy already cures many patients by 10 weeks.
rationale: Phase 2a, 40 patients, single site, single-blind. Standard triple therapy resolves most stromal keratitis within 10 weeks (HEDS) and clears tear HSV-1, so control cure is probably near half or higher; BD111's human evidence is three transplant patients. A formal significant result needs a 35-40 point gap. Investigator-assessed cure in a partly unblinded design could inflate the difference, and any early publicity would likely be favourable. The record is still recruiting two months before registered completion, so delay and late or no disclosure are likely.

assumptions.claim: In the first-in-human study, three patients with refractory HSV-1 stromal keratitis given BD111 at corneal transplantation had no detectable HSV-1 and no recurrence over about 18 months.
assumptions.source: NCT04560790; Wei et al., Mol Ther 2023

assumptions.claim: In HEDS, adding topical prednisolone to trifluridine cut stromal keratitis treatment failure within 10 weeks from about 73% to about 26%.

reason: Both co-primaries must be met; navtemadlin's symptom effect was modest in BOREAS (TSS50 24% vs 12%) and its GI toxicity can blunt symptom gains, so TSS50 may miss even if SVR35 separates.
rationale: BOREAS showed modest monotherapy activity (SVR35 15% vs 5%, p=0.08; TSS50 24% vs 12%). The single-arm add-on study gave 32% SVR35 and TSS50, likely inflated. Placebo plus continued ruxolitinib should give few new SVR35 responders, so SVR35 probably separates, but TSS50 with roughly 180 randomized 2:1 is marginally powered, and both must be met. Still recruiting with a run-in of 18+ weeks plus 24 weeks, so primary completion will slip well into 2027; a readout by June 2027 would most likely be an early stop.

assumptions.claim: In BOREAS, navtemadlin gave SVR35 at week 24 in 15% versus 5% on best available therapy and TSS50 in 24% versus 12% in JAK inhibitor relapsed or refractory myelofibrosis.
In the phase 1b/2 add-on study, navtemadlin added to ruxolitinib in suboptimal responders gave SVR35 at week 24 in about 32% and TSS50 in about 32%.
POIESIS plans to enrol about 600 patients into the ruxolitinib run-in and to randomize about 180 suboptimal responders 2:1.

reason: Adjunctive antipsychotic-type agents have shown only small HAM-A gains in GAD (adjunctive quetiapine XR missed), and a large placebo response at 6 weeks can erase a 1-2 point effect.
rationale: Lumateperone, the parent compound, gave large adjunctive effects in MDD (about 4.5-4.9 MADRS points) with good trial conduct across similar sites, and 5-HT2A/D2 agents reduce anxiety. But adjunctive quetiapine XR failed in GAD, the expected HAM-A effect is about 1-2 points, and GAD placebo response is large. With about 235 per arm the study detects roughly 2 points; two doses give two chances. Slow enrolment since 2024 and J&J ownership make timely public disclosure uncertain.
evidence: Adjunctive quetiapine XR in GAD (Khan et al.), 2014

assumptions.claim: Adjunctive lumateperone 42 mg beat placebo on MADRS total at week 6 by about 4.9 points in Study 501 and about 4.5 points in Study 502 in MDD with inadequate antidepressant response.
Adjunctive quetiapine XR did not separate from placebo on HAM-A total at week 8 in GAD patients with inadequate response to SSRI or SNRI treatment (about -10.7 vs -9.6 points, p about 0.08).
assumptions.source: Khan et al., adjunctive quetiapine XR in GAD, 2014

reason: SGLT inhibitors typically add only 2-3 KCCQ points in heart failure; with a placebo gain near 5 points and an SD near 16, a 500-patient trial needs about 3 points to reach significance.
rationale: No randomized evidence for SGLT inhibition in HCM; support is extrapolated from HFpEF, where KCCQ gains ranged from about 1.5 (EMPEROR-Preserved) to 5.8 points (PRESERVED-HF). HCM trials show sizeable placebo KCCQ improvement (ODYSSEY-HCM about 10 points), and ODYSSEY missed with a 2.7-point difference. With 250 per arm the standard error is about 1.5, so a true 2.5-point effect gives roughly 40% power. Obstructive patients may gain less from a natriuretic drug. Enrolment is complete; Lexicon should report topline in early to mid 2027.

assumptions.claim: In PRESERVED-HF, dapagliflozin improved KCCQ clinical summary score by 5.8 points versus placebo at 12 weeks in HFpEF.
assumptions.source: PRESERVED-HF, Nassif et al., Nat Med 2021

assumptions.claim: In EMPEROR-Preserved, empagliflozin improved KCCQ clinical summary score versus placebo by only about 1.3 to 1.5 points.
In ODYSSEY-HCM, KCCQ clinical summary score rose about 10 points on placebo at week 48 and mavacamten's 2.7-point advantage was not significant.

reason: Small two-site Taiwanese cell-therapy trial still recruiting two months before its registered primary completion, so the date will probably slip and results are unlikely to be posted by the read date.
rationale: Ninety patients at two Taiwanese sites since June 2024 for a single-infusion MSC product; still recruiting at the October 2026 snapshot with primary completion registered for 30 December 2026 and a 90-day primary window, so slippage beyond March 2027 is more likely than not. Small sponsors of this kind rarely post results on ClinicalTrials.gov within a year, termination risk is modest, and the cluttered seven-item safety primary list has a small chance of being changed in substance.

reason: If the implant controls exudation less well than aflibercept every 8 weeks, some eyes lose vision before rescue and the BCVA gap could approach the non-inferiority margin.
rationale: Non-inferiority on BCVA against aflibercept 2 mg every 8 weeks in patients pre-selected after aflibercept loading, with OTX-TKI re-dosed at 24 weeks and rescue allowed. Sustained-release TKIs have tracked within about a letter of aflibercept (OTX-TKI phase 1, DAVIO 2), and roughly 330 per arm gives a standard error under one letter against a likely 4.5-letter margin. Failure needs a true deficit near 3 letters, as in under-treated arms such as DAZZLE. Enrolment is complete; week-48 topline is expected in early 2027.

assumptions.claim: In the US phase 1 trial, eyes given OTX-TKI kept BCVA and central subfield thickness comparable to aflibercept every 8 weeks through 12 months.
In DAVIO 2, both EYP-1901 arms were within about 0.3 to 0.4 letters of aflibercept every 8 weeks in BCVA change at weeks 28-32 and met non-inferiority.
SOL-R randomizes 2:2:1 to OTX-TKI re-dosed every 24 weeks, aflibercept 2 mg every 8 weeks, and a masking aflibercept 8 mg arm.

reason: About 36 patients per arm and highly variable eosinophil counts in a population not clearly selected for eosinophilia; a noisy placebo arm or descriptive-only reporting could leave the primary unconfirmed.
rationale: Solrikitug is an anti-TSLP antibody; TSLP blockade reliably lowers blood eosinophils within weeks (tezepelumab cut counts by about 130 cells/uL versus placebo in NAVIGATOR and at every PATHWAY dose). The primary is this pharmacodynamic marker, three doses give several chances, and 12 weeks of treatment suffice. Risks are small arms, skewed counts, and a private sponsor that may report selectively or without a formal primary statement. The trial is completed; disclosure timing depends on the company's financing and congress plans.

assumptions.claim: In NAVIGATOR, tezepelumab lowered blood eosinophil counts by about 170 cells/uL versus about 40 cells/uL on placebo at week 52.
In PATHWAY, every tezepelumab dose reduced blood eosinophil counts versus placebo from week 4 onward.

reason: Arms of about 60 and skewed eosinophil counts with regression to the mean in an eosinophil-enriched placebo group; failure would more likely come from noise or vague reporting than from lack of pharmacology.
rationale: Anti-TSLP antibodies lower blood eosinophils consistently (tezepelumab in NAVIGATOR and COURSE), and ZION enrols COPD patients with elevated eosinophils, giving a large baseline to reduce and about 60 per arm. The pharmacodynamic primary should be met at the high dose unless the drug is underdosed. FEV1 at 12 weeks is unlikely to reach significance at this size. Private sponsor; topline timing is uncertain after the September 2026 primary completion, likely with the asthma study or at a 2027 congress.

assumptions.claim: In NAVIGATOR, tezepelumab lowered blood eosinophil counts by about 170 cells/uL versus about 40 cells/uL on placebo at week 52.
In COURSE, tezepelumab reduced blood eosinophils and improved pre-bronchodilator FEV1 by about 55 mL versus placebo at week 52 in COPD.
assumptions.source: COURSE, Singh et al., Lancet Respir Med 2025

assumptions.claim: In BOREAS, dupilumab improved pre-bronchodilator FEV1 by about 83 mL versus placebo at week 12 in COPD with eosinophils of at least 300/uL, with about 470 patients per arm.

reason: Sixteen patients per arm cannot show a significant PFS-6 gain unless the difference is around 40 points, and opening the blood-brain barrier adds uncertain benefit to bevacizumab, which acts on tumour vessels.
rationale: Open-label 32-patient Taiwanese device trial. Bevacizumab alone gives PFS-6 of roughly 16-43% in recurrent glioblastoma (BELOB, BRAIN); here small residual tumours may put it near 30%. Bevacizumab acts intravascularly, so focused-ultrasound barrier opening has a weak rationale for a large gain, and only single-arm pilot data exist. Significance needs about a 40-point gap. Still recruiting two months before registered completion with a 6-month endpoint, so the date will slip; the sponsor would likely disclose topline once available.

assumptions.claim: Bevacizumab alone gave a 6-month progression-free survival rate of 42.6% in recurrent glioblastoma in the BRAIN trial.
assumptions.source: Friedman et al., J Clin Oncol 2009 (BRAIN)

assumptions.claim: Bevacizumab alone gave a 6-month progression-free survival rate of about 16% in the BELOB trial.

reason: Topotecan patients may live longer than history suggests through later lines, and BL-B01D1's marked haematological toxicity and shorter responses in platinum-resistant disease could shrink the survival gain below significance.
rationale: BL-B01D1 (iza-bren) gave ORR about 55% and median OS about 12 months in pretreated SCLC in phase 1, against 7-8 months expected for topotecan (RESILIENT and DeLLphi-304 controls 8.3), implying a hazard ratio near 0.7; 722 patients give ample power. The drug has met several other phase 3 interims in China. No interim success appears announced for this trial yet, which tempers confidence. Baili announces positive readouts promptly, so results public by mid-2027 lean positive.

assumptions.claim: In phase 1 data, BL-B01D1 gave an objective response rate of about 55% and median overall survival of about 12 months in previously treated small cell lung cancer.
In DeLLphi-304, median overall survival in the chemotherapy control arm (topotecan, lurbinectedin or amrubicin) was 8.3 months.
In RESILIENT part 2, topotecan gave median overall survival of 8.3 months in second-line small cell lung cancer.

reason: About 14-21 patients per arm with a highly variable proteinuria endpoint means only a large (roughly 35% relative) UPCR reduction would reach significance, and CD40L blockade has no proven effect in FSGS or MCD.
rationale: Phase 2a umbrella with only about 14-21 patients per arm and a noisy endpoint (UPCR percent change, SD around 45 points), so a significant frexalimab-placebo difference needs roughly a 35% relative reduction. CD40/CD40L blockade is unproven in FSGS/MCD: bleselumab did not significantly prevent recurrent FSGS. The steroid-responsive, immune-mediated population gives biological plausibility, and a lenient phase 2a criterion could help. Still recruiting two months before registered completion, so a readout by mid-2027 is unlikely; Sanofi tends to post small phase 2a results late.

assumptions.claim: The anti-CD40 antibody bleselumab did not significantly reduce recurrence of FSGS after kidney transplantation in its phase 2a trial.
The trial plans 84 participants across six arms, about 14 per arm if split evenly.
Frexalimab had a low rate of treatment discontinuation for adverse events in its phase 2 relapsing multiple sclerosis trial.

reason: Fully enrolled open-label biomarker study with a fixed week-48 biopsy endpoint; it should complete on schedule in March 2027, with results posted about a year later, after the read date.
rationale: Open-label, single-drug biomarker study that is fully enrolled (89 participants, active not recruiting) with a fixed week-48 biopsy endpoint, so the March 2027 primary completion should hold. Bimekizumab is approved with a known safety profile, so a stop is unlikely. UCB usually posts results close to 12 months after primary completion, which falls after August 2027. The primary outcome is a single gene-expression score with little reason to change.

reason: Failure would need the Part A dose to give a much smaller platelet rise than avatrombopag or lusutrombopag, for example in Child-Pugh B or very low baseline counts; placebo response on this endpoint is near zero.
rationale: TPO-receptor agonists reliably raise platelets before procedures in chronic liver disease: avatrombopag (ADAPT-1/2) and lusutrombopag (L-PLUS 1/2) beat placebo by 30-65 points. Herombopag is an approved agonist of the same class, the dose was chosen in Part A, and the endpoint (count at least 50 with a rise of at least 20, no transfusion) has a very low placebo response. Even with about 45 per arm, power is near 100%. The trial completed in August 2026; disclosure is most likely through an NDA-acceptance notice or a liver congress.

assumptions.claim: In ADAPT-1 and ADAPT-2, 66-88% of avatrombopag patients versus 23-38% of placebo patients needed no platelet transfusion or rescue procedure for bleeding.
In L-PLUS 2, 64.8% of lusutrombopag patients versus 29.0% of placebo patients met the primary endpoint of no pre-procedure platelet transfusion and no rescue therapy for bleeding.
In L-PLUS 1, 79% of lusutrombopag patients versus 13% of placebo patients needed no platelet transfusion before the procedure.
assumptions.source: Hidaka et al., Clin Gastroenterol Hepatol 2019 (L-PLUS 1)

reason: SG301 may be a weaker anti-CD38 antibody than daratumumab or isatuximab, and inclusion of CD38-exposed patients could dilute the PFS benefit over pomalidomide-dexamethasone.
rationale: Adding an anti-CD38 antibody to pomalidomide-dexamethasone has succeeded twice (APOLLO HR 0.63; ICARIA-MM HR 0.60), and about 340 randomized patients give ample power for HR 0.65. Risks: SG301 is less characterised than daratumumab or isatuximab, and only primary CD38-refractory patients are excluded, so CD38-exposed patients may dilute the effect. The trial was still recruiting in late 2026 and PFS is event-driven, so a result by mid-2027 would need an early interim; the registered March 2027 completion looks optimistic.

assumptions.claim: In APOLLO, daratumumab plus pomalidomide-dexamethasone gave median PFS of 12.4 versus 6.9 months with pomalidomide-dexamethasone alone, hazard ratio 0.63.
In ICARIA-MM, isatuximab plus pomalidomide-dexamethasone gave median PFS of 11.5 versus 6.5 months, hazard ratio 0.60.
The trial excludes only patients primary refractory to a prior CD38 antibody and those previously given pomalidomide.

reason: With about 36 patients per arm, a placebo responder rate of 30-40% from protocol-driven weaning could leave a real 25-30 point teduglutide-like effect short of significance.
rationale: PJ009 appears to be a teduglutide product (weight-based daily subcutaneous dosing; prior teduglutide excluded) and the endpoint mirrors STEPS, where teduglutide gave 63% versus 30% responders; study 004 gave 46% versus 6%. With about 36 per arm, power for a 30-point difference is roughly 70-80%, so the main risks are sample size and a high placebo response from parenteral-volume weaning rules. Primary completion passed in September 2026; disclosure would come through company announcements or an NDA filing in China.

assumptions.claim: In STEPS, 63% of teduglutide 0.05 mg/kg/day patients versus 30% of placebo patients had at least a 20% reduction in parenteral support volume at weeks 20 and 24.
In the earlier teduglutide phase 3 study, responder rates were 46% with 0.05 mg/kg/day versus 6% with placebo.
The trial excludes patients who have previously used teduglutide and doses PJ009 daily by body weight for 24 weeks.

reason: The strict composite (itch response plus near-clear nodules at week 24) with dropouts counted as non-responders is the only plausible way a strongly antipruritic JAK1 inhibitor misses.
rationale: JAK1 inhibition gave large, dose-dependent itch and lesion responses in the phase 2 PN trial (itch NRS4 54% at 75 mg versus 8% on placebo at week 16). In PRIME/PRIME2 the same week-24 composite was about 9% on placebo versus 32-39% on dupilumab, and povorcitinib should perform similarly. With 115-175 per arm, power is near 100%. Residual risks are phase 3 shrinkage (as in STOP-HS) and non-responder imputation for dropouts. Primary completion was October 2026, so Incyte topline should come within months.

assumptions.claim: In the phase 2 prurigo nodularis trial, a 4-point or greater itch NRS improvement at week 16 was reached by 36.1%, 44.4% and 54.1% on povorcitinib 15, 45 and 75 mg versus 8.1% on placebo.
assumptions.source: Incyte phase 2 povorcitinib prurigo nodularis trial, AAD 2024 late-breaker

assumptions.claim: In PRIME and PRIME2, the week-24 composite of itch NRS improvement of at least 4 points and IGA PN-S 0/1 was reached by 38.7% and 32.1% on dupilumab versus 9.2% and 8.5% on placebo.
assumptions.source: Yosipovitch et al., Nat Med 2023 (PRIME, PRIME2)

assumptions.claim: The phase 3 hidradenitis trials STOP-HS1 and STOP-HS2 of povorcitinib met their primary endpoint.

reason: The strict composite (itch response plus near-clear nodules at week 24) with dropouts counted as non-responders is the only plausible way a strongly antipruritic JAK1 inhibitor misses.
rationale: Replicate of STOP-PN1. JAK1 inhibition gave large, dose-dependent itch and lesion responses in the phase 2 PN trial (itch NRS4 54% at 75 mg versus 8% on placebo at week 16). In PRIME/PRIME2 the same week-24 composite was about 9% on placebo versus 32-39% on dupilumab, and povorcitinib should perform similarly. With 115-175 per arm, power is near 100%. Residual risks are phase 3 shrinkage (as in STOP-HS) and non-responder imputation for dropouts. Primary completion was October 2026, so topline should come within months.

assumptions.claim: In the phase 2 prurigo nodularis trial, a 4-point or greater itch NRS improvement at week 16 was reached by 36.1%, 44.4% and 54.1% on povorcitinib 15, 45 and 75 mg versus 8.1% on placebo.
assumptions.source: Incyte phase 2 povorcitinib prurigo nodularis trial, AAD 2024 late-breaker

assumptions.claim: In PRIME and PRIME2, the week-24 composite of itch NRS improvement of at least 4 points and IGA PN-S 0/1 was reached by 38.7% and 32.1% on dupilumab versus 9.2% and 8.5% on placebo.
assumptions.source: Yosipovitch et al., Nat Med 2023 (PRIME, PRIME2)

assumptions.claim: The phase 3 hidradenitis trials STOP-HS1 and STOP-HS2 of povorcitinib met their primary endpoint.

reason: PFS is likely positive; the risk is that the dual primary with OS is immature or not significant when PFS is reported, or that FDA018 is less active than other Trop2 ADCs.
rationale: Trop2 ADCs with topoisomerase payloads have decisively beaten single-agent chemotherapy in pretreated TNBC (ASCENT PFS HR 0.41; OptiTROP-Breast01 HR 0.31), and FDA018 is an SN-38 Trop2 ADC with phase 1 activity. 350 patients give high power even for HR 0.6. Residual risks: a weaker or less tolerable molecule, open-label assessment (mitigated by BICR), and the dual primary with OS, which may be immature when PFS reads out. Enrolment is complete, so a PFS readout by mid-2027 is plausible.

assumptions.claim: In ASCENT, sacituzumab govitecan gave median PFS of 5.6 versus 1.7 months with single-agent chemotherapy in patients without brain metastases, hazard ratio 0.41.
In OptiTROP-Breast01, sacituzumab tirumotecan reduced the risk of progression or death by BICR versus chemotherapy with a hazard ratio of about 0.31 in pretreated TNBC.
The trial registers PFS by BICR and overall survival as dual primary outcomes.

reason: VLP norovirus vaccines have not yet protected young children (HIL-214 failed in infants); antigenic drift in GII.4 and GII.17 and weak blocking-antibody responses could leave efficacy too low.
rationale: No norovirus vaccine has shown efficacy in a pivotal trial. The bivalent VLP HIL-214 failed in infants (about 5% efficacy), although a similar VLP gave about 62% against moderate-severe disease in adult recruits. Zhifei's vaccine is quadrivalent, uses three doses and enrols 2-13-year-olds primed by natural infection, which helps; genotype drift and weak infant responses are the main threats. Roughly 100-200 cases are expected, adequate if efficacy exceeds 40%. Two-year follow-up ends around March 2027, so a report by June 2027 is unlikely.

assumptions.claim: The bivalent norovirus VLP vaccine HIL-214 showed about 5% efficacy against moderate or severe norovirus gastroenteritis in infants and missed its primary endpoint.
A bivalent GI.1/GII.4 VLP vaccine showed 61.8% efficacy against moderate or severe norovirus gastroenteritis of any genotype in US Navy recruits.
The trial enrolled 6600 children in three age strata: 3000 aged 6-23 months, 2200 aged 2-5 years and 1400 aged 6-13 years, randomized 1:1.

reason: Plain bupivacaine plus rescue analgesia may leave little room for a significant 72-hour pain AUC difference with about 24-32 patients per arm.
rationale: Small dose-finding phase 2 (96 patients over probably three or four arms) against an active comparator, plain bupivacaine. Sponsor-run nerve-block trials of liposomal bupivacaine showed lower 72-96 hour pain AUC than bupivacaine HCl, but independent trials and meta-analyses find small differences, and rescue opioids after thoracoscopic surgery compress pain scores. The hypothesis is not stated, so a formal superiority claim is uncertain. Hengrui rarely publicises phase 2 results quickly; a public result by mid-2027 is unlikely.
evidence: Hussain et al. meta-analysis of perineural liposomal bupivacaine, Anesthesiology 2021
Liposomal bupivacaine sciatic nerve block for bunionectomy phase 3 (Schwartz 2024)

assumptions.claim: A meta-analysis of perineural liposomal versus plain bupivacaine found a statistically significant but clinically unimportant reduction in 24-72 hour pain AUC.
In a phase 3 bunionectomy trial, liposomal bupivacaine sciatic nerve block gave a significantly lower 0-96 hour pain AUC than bupivacaine HCl.
assumptions.source: Schwartz et al., J Clin Anesth 2024

assumptions.claim: The trial enrols 96 patients and compares liposomal bupivacaine doses with bupivacaine hydrochloride as active control.

reason: Still recruiting two months before the registered primary completion, with 178 planned patients and an optional randomized part 3, so the date will almost certainly slip; a cash-constrained, partner-funded sponsor adds some risk of an early stop.
rationale: Phase 2 started December 2024 with three parts and 178 planned patients; it was still recruiting in late October 2026 against a December 2026 primary completion and 12-month response time frames, so a slip beyond March 2027 is very likely unless the trial stops. Ryvu is cash-constrained and the trial depends on Menarini funding and an unproven PIM-inhibitor combination, so a stop is possible. Results posting by August 2027 is implausible. The multi-part primary outcomes could be trimmed if part 3 is dropped.

reason: Enrolment is closed and the primary safety window is only 17 weeks, so primary completion close to the registered December 2026 date is likely, while results posting on the registry by August 2027 is unlikely for a small sponsor.
rationale: Enrolment is closed at 46 patients and the primary outcome is adverse events to week 17, so the last primary visit should fall close to the registered December 2026 date. The sponsor has guided to top-line data in the second half of 2026, as I recall. An open-label extension runs to 2028, so the record should stay active; a stop would need a clear safety or efficacy disappointment. Results are not due on the registry until about a year after primary completion, and a safety primary is unlikely to be rewritten.

reason: Failure would most likely come from serum calcium falling below 8.0 mg/dL on half the elemental calcium, forcing dose increases so that too few AMOR-1 patients keep the 50% reduction.
rationale: The composite is built so the control arm, which keeps its full calcium dose, can hardly respond, while AMOR-1 patients respond whenever serum calcium stays within 8.0-10.0 mg/dL on half the elemental calcium without more active vitamin D. Active vitamin D drives serum calcium more than the supplement, and amorphous calcium carbonate showed about double absorption in earlier work, so a 30-60% response against near 0% is likely and 41 vs 21 patients suffice. Risks: rescue up-titration, dropouts, and a small private sponsor reporting vaguely.
evidence: Vaisman et al. 2014, J Bone Miner Res (amorphous calcium carbonate absorption)

assumptions.claim: In a double-blind crossover trial in postmenopausal women, fractional calcium absorption from amorphous calcium carbonate was about twice that from crystalline calcium carbonate.
assumptions.source: Vaisman et al. 2014, J Bone Miner Res

assumptions.claim: In this trial the control arm keeps its initial elemental calcium intake, while the AMOR-1 arm is switched to about 50% of it.
In the PaTHway phase 3 trial in hypoparathyroidism, about 5% of placebo patients met the composite primary endpoint, against about 79% on palopegteriparatide.

reason: The only real route to failure is a physician's-choice arm doing better than expected because of docetaxel, and I believe a positive primary result has already been announced.
rationale: My recollection is that Pfizer announced in December 2025 that MEVPRO-1 met its rPFS primary endpoint, with detail at ASCO GU 2026; if so the answer is yes and the card is void. Independently, the randomized phase 1 expansion gave HR 0.51 (14.3 vs 6.2 months) against enzalutamide alone, and a second ARPI after abiraterone is a weak control (about 4-6 months), partly offset by docetaxel as an option. 600 patients give ample power for HR 0.7 or better. The numbers given are estimates, not recalled values.
evidence: Pfizer press release on MEVPRO-1, December 2025 (as recalled)

assumptions.claim: In the randomized phase 1 dose expansion, mevrometostat plus enzalutamide gave a median rPFS of 14.3 months against 6.2 months for enzalutamide alone (HR 0.51).
Pfizer announced in December 2025 that MEVPRO-1 met its primary endpoint of radiographic progression-free survival.
In PSMAfore, the control arm switching to a second androgen receptor pathway inhibitor had a median rPFS of about 5.6 months.

reason: With about 10 patients on the top dose and about 12 on pooled placebo, the study cannot support a formal significant result on weekly stool frequency.
rationale: Dose-ranging paediatric study with 5:1 randomization: about 10 tenapanor patients per cohort and 2 placebo each, so no realistic power for a formal test of weekly SBM change (SD near 3, expected gain about 1 per week). The sponsor will probably report descriptively, on ClinicalTrials.gov or in a congress abstract, without claiming a met primary objective. Adult trials show a modest stool-frequency gain with diarrhoea as the main adverse event. A met result needs an unusually large observed difference plus a stated significance test.

assumptions.claim: In the adult T3MPO-1 trial, the combined responder rate was 27.0% with tenapanor against 18.7% with placebo.
Each cohort of 12 children is randomized 5:1 to tenapanor or placebo, so about 2 children per cohort receive placebo.
In the paediatric phase 3 trial of linaclotide in functional constipation, weekly SBM frequency rose by about 2.2 with linaclotide 72 micrograms against about 1.1 with placebo.
assumptions.source: Di Lorenzo et al. 2024, Lancet Gastroenterol Hepatol (NCT04026113)

reason: OX40L blockade is untested in celiac disease and may not protect the mucosa from gluten-driven injury enough to show against a modest, noisy placebo decline.
rationale: First test of OX40L blockade in celiac disease, with no earlier human efficacy data in this disease. The primary needs amlitelimab to blunt villous damage from simulated gluten exposure over 28 weeks; placebo decline under low-dose gluten is modest (about 0.2-0.3 in Vh:Cd) and variable (SD about 0.5), so about 38 per arm detects only near-complete protection. Most earlier immune or enzyme approaches in celiac disease failed in phase 2. I give about a one-in-three chance the drug works and about half power if it does.
evidence: Catassi et al. 2007 (low-dose gluten and Vh:Cd)

assumptions.claim: In the ZED1227 gluten-challenge trial, the three doses attenuated the fall in Vh:Cd ratio against placebo by 0.44 to 0.49 over 6 weeks of 3 g of gluten daily.
assumptions.source: Schuppan et al. 2021, N Engl J Med

assumptions.claim: The anti-IL-15 antibody AMG 714 did not meet its primary endpoint of change in Vh:Cd ratio in a gluten-challenge phase 2a trial in celiac disease.
assumptions.source: Lahdeaho et al. 2019, Lancet Gastroenterol Hepatol

reason: B-cell inhibition without depletion may give only a modest BICLA gain over a placebo response near 35% in 24 weeks, short of the roughly 14 points needed with 95 patients per arm.
rationale: Obexelimab inhibits B cells without depleting them. Its earlier SLE phase 2 missed the primary (42.0% vs 28.6%, p=0.18) although time to loss of improvement favoured it, and in IgG4-related disease the effect looked weaker than B-cell depletion. With 95 per arm and placebo BICLA near 35%, the trial needs an observed gap of about 14 points; a true 12-15 point effect gives roughly even odds, and 24 weeks is short for B-cell therapy in lupus. Lupus phase 2 trials of plausible mechanisms succeed about half the time; I shade lower.

assumptions.claim: In the earlier phase 2 trial of obexelimab in SLE, 42.0% of obexelimab patients against 28.6% of placebo patients had no loss of improvement at day 225 (p=0.18), so the primary endpoint was missed.
In TULIP-2, BICLA response at week 52 was 47.8% with anifrolumab against 31.5% with placebo.
In the phase 3 INDIGO trial in IgG4-related disease, obexelimab reduced the risk of flare by 56% against placebo.
assumptions.source: INDIGO (NCT05662241), Zenas BioPharma press release, early 2026

reason: A true effect near 2 MADRS points leaves the trial exposed to a high placebo response across many sites in Latin America and Eastern Europe.
rationale: Seltorexant 20 mg beat placebo by 2.6 MADRS points in MDD3001 and 3.1 in phase 2b, but it did not beat quetiapine XR in MDD3005 and effects in this class are small. True effect is probably about 2 points; with roughly 250-375 per arm power is 60-75%, eroded by high placebo response at Latin American and Eastern European sites. Given a statement by June 2027 the mix shifts: J&J rarely issues quick toplines, and an early stop after a failed part 1 would count as not met, so I set about even odds.

assumptions.claim: In MDD3001, seltorexant 20 mg improved MADRS total score at day 43 by a least-squares mean difference of 2.6 points over placebo (p=0.007) in patients with MDD and insomnia symptoms.
In MDD3005, seltorexant was not superior to quetiapine XR on response rate at week 26 (57.4% vs 53.4%).
In the phase 2b trial, seltorexant 20 mg improved MADRS at week 6 by a least-squares mean difference of 3.1 points over placebo.
assumptions.source: Savitz et al. 2021, Int J Neuropsychopharmacol

reason: The large phase 2 effect may shrink in a 45-site phase 3, as it did for psilocybin in COMP005, especially with patients staying on serotonergic antidepressants.
rationale: CYB003 16 mg given twice, against inactive placebo with psychological support, in MDD patients on a stable antidepressant. Phase 2 showed a 14-point MADRS advantage at 3 weeks in a small sample; phase 3 psilocybin data (COMP005, 3.6 points at week 6 in treatment-resistant depression) show much smaller but still significant effects, helped by functional unblinding. With about 110 per arm the trial detects about 3 points; I expect 4-8. Risks are effect shrinkage, blunting by concurrent SSRIs and a larger placebo response with support.

assumptions.claim: In the phase 2 trial, CYB003 12 mg reduced MADRS total score by 14.08 points more than placebo at 3 weeks (p=0.0005).
In COMP005, a single 25 mg dose of COMP360 psilocybin reduced MADRS by 3.6 points more than placebo at week 6 in treatment-resistant depression.
In a phase 2 trial in major depressive disorder, a single 25 mg psilocybin dose reduced MADRS by 12.3 points more than niacin placebo at day 43.

reason: NET inhibition is unproven in RA and may not move DAS28-CRP within 6 weeks by the 0.65 points that 24 patients per arm can detect.
rationale: First efficacy test of a NET-inhibiting antibody in RA: 24 patients per arm, 6 weeks, DAS28-CRP, no earlier patient efficacy data. With SD about 1.15 a single dose needs a gap of about 0.65 points over placebo, as much as established biologics achieve by week 6; three doses and a possibly lenient phase 2a test help somewhat. A private sponsor is more likely to publicise a win, which lifts the conditional probability, but vague 'positive' wording without a statement on the primary counts as not met.
evidence: CIT-013 phase 1 in healthy volunteers with LPS challenge (Citryll)

assumptions.claim: The trial compares three dose levels of CIT-013 with placebo in 96 patients, with change in DAS28-CRP at week 6 as the primary outcome.
Before this trial, CIT-013 had been tested in a phase 1 study in healthy volunteers, including an LPS challenge, and not for efficacy in RA patients.
assumptions.source: Citryll phase 1 study of CIT-013 in healthy volunteers

reason: PD-1 blockade has limited activity in MMR-proficient colon cancer, so the gain in major pathological response over CAPEOX alone may be too small for a 120-patient phase 2 to show.
rationale: Chemotherapy alone gives few major pathological responses in MMRp colon cancer (FOxTROT pCR about 4%; I expect about 12% mPR after four CAPEOX cycles). Anti-PD-1 adds little in MSS metastatic disease, but early-stage primaries respond more (NICHE: 4 of 15 pMMR tumours with nivolumab plus ipilimumab), so I assume roughly 22% with dostarlimab. A 10-point gain in about 120 patients gives under 40% power, and a signal-finding phase 2 may have no formal test. Still recruiting a month before the registered completion date, so data by mid-2027 are unlikely.

assumptions.claim: In FOxTROT, six weeks of neoadjuvant oxaliplatin-fluoropyrimidine chemotherapy gave a pathological complete response in about 4% of colon cancer patients.
assumptions.source: FOxTROT, Morton et al., J Clin Oncol 2023

assumptions.claim: In NICHE, 4 of 15 MMR-proficient colon tumours (27%) showed a pathological response after neoadjuvant nivolumab plus ipilimumab.
assumptions.source: NICHE, Chalabi et al., Nat Med 2020

assumptions.claim: In OPTICAL, three months of neoadjuvant mFOLFOX6 or CAPOX gave a pathological complete response in about 7% of locally advanced colon cancer patients.
assumptions.source: OPTICAL, Hu et al., J Clin Oncol 2024

reason: The wake-promoting effect on MWT is very likely, but the second primary outcome (CGI-S of sleepiness on the night shift) has a large placebo response in shift workers and must be met by the same dose.
rationale: Solriamfetol raised 40-minute MWT sleep latency by about 10 to 13 minutes over placebo at 150 and 300 mg in the TONES narcolepsy and sleep-apnoea trials, far more than armodafinil, which still won its shift work disorder trial on night-time sleep latency and clinical global impression. With about 173 patients per arm, even half that effect is detected on MWT. The risks are the second primary outcome (CGI-S, with a large placebo response in shift workers), dropouts at 300 mg, and site quality in a hard-to-recruit population; both outcomes must be met by the same dose.
evidence: Armodafinil in shift work disorder, Czeisler 2009
Modafinil in shift work sleep disorder, Czeisler 2005

assumptions.claim: In TONES 3 (obstructive sleep apnoea), solriamfetol 150 mg and 300 mg increased MWT sleep latency at week 12 by 11.0 and 13.0 minutes versus 0.2 minutes with placebo.
assumptions.source: TONES 3, Schweitzer et al., Am J Respir Crit Care Med 2019 (NCT02348606)

assumptions.claim: In TONES 2 (narcolepsy), solriamfetol 150 mg and 300 mg increased MWT sleep latency at week 12 by 9.8 and 12.3 minutes versus 2.1 minutes with placebo.
assumptions.source: TONES 2, Thorpy et al., Ann Neurol 2019 (NCT02348593)

assumptions.claim: In the armodafinil shift work disorder trial, night-time sleep latency rose 3.1 minutes versus 0.4 minutes with placebo and 79% versus 59% of patients were rated improved on CGI-C.
assumptions.source: Czeisler et al., Mayo Clin Proc 2009

reason: Complete debridement should be met easily, but the second primary outcome, time to complete wound closure over 12 weeks, showed only a trend in phase 2 and the trial has limited power for it.
rationale: In the phase 2 ChronEx trial in the same population, EscharEx achieved complete debridement in 63% versus 30% with gel vehicle, so the debridement outcome is very likely met with 216 patients. The trial has a second primary outcome, time to complete wound closure over 12 weeks; phase 2 showed only a trend there and the trial has limited power for closure even with sample-size re-estimation. Under the co-primary rule that outcome decides. Still recruiting in late October 2026, so topline is likely around mid-2027 or later.
evidence: EscharEx first phase 2 in hard-to-heal wounds, 2017

assumptions.claim: In the phase 2 ChronEx trial, complete debridement was achieved in 63% (29/46) of EscharEx patients versus 30.2% (13/43) on gel vehicle (p=0.004).
assumptions.source: ChronEx, NCT03588130; Shoham et al., eClinicalMedicine 2024

assumptions.claim: In ChronEx, the incidence of complete wound closure did not differ significantly between EscharEx and gel vehicle.

reason: If the unstated non-inferiority margin is 10 points, the roughly 400 microbiologically evaluable patients leave little room for chance variation unless HRS-8427 is truly better than imipenem.
rationale: HRS-8427 is a siderophore cephalosporin like cefiderocol, which beat imipenem-cilastatin on the same composite endpoint in APEKS-cUTI (72.6% versus 54.6%). Carbapenem comparators usually reach 55 to 70% at test of cure because of late bacteriological relapse, so a long-exposure cephalosporin should at least match imipenem. The record does not give the margin; with about 400 microbiologically evaluable patients a 15% margin is comfortable and a 10% margin needs a small advantage. The trial is completed, and Hengrui usually discloses pivotal results when its application is accepted.

assumptions.claim: In APEKS-cUTI, composite clinical and microbiological response at test of cure was 72.6% with cefiderocol versus 54.6% with imipenem-cilastatin (adjusted difference 18.6 points).
assumptions.source: APEKS-cUTI, Portsmouth et al., Lancet Infect Dis 2018 (NCT02321800)

assumptions.claim: In APEKS-cUTI, about 2% of patients in each arm stopped study drug because of an adverse event.
assumptions.source: APEKS-cUTI, Portsmouth et al., Lancet Infect Dis 2018 (NCT02321800)

reason: The efficacy contrast against on-demand treatment is very large for this class; the residual risk is a thrombotic safety signal or hold, as seen with other anti-TFPI antibodies, disrupting the trial.
rationale: KN057 is an anti-TFPI antibody, a class with large, consistent effects against on-demand treatment: concizumab cut treated bleeds by about 80 to 86% in explorer8 and marstacimab by about 92% in BASIS. Patients enter with at least six treated bleeds in 26 weeks, so the on-demand arm should bleed 20 to 30 times a year and even a small randomized comparison is decisive. The residual risks are a thrombotic safety signal or a hold. Primary completion has passed; Alphamab typically announces pivotal results or a filing through exchange announcements or congresses.

assumptions.claim: In explorer8, concizumab prophylaxis versus no prophylaxis gave an annualized bleeding rate ratio of 0.14 in hemophilia A and 0.21 in hemophilia B.
assumptions.source: explorer8, NCT04082429; Chowdary et al., Lancet Haematol 2024

assumptions.claim: In BASIS, marstacimab prophylaxis lowered the mean annualized bleeding rate from 38.0 on prior on-demand treatment to about 3.2, a reduction of about 92%.

reason: With about 40 patients per arm and missing week-48 biopsies counted as failures, only a difference above roughly 20 points reaches significance, and the potency of this FGF21 analogue is unproven.
rationale: Fc-fused or pegylated FGF21 analogues have given large biopsy effects: efruxifermin resolved NASH in 47 to 76% versus 15% on placebo at 24 weeks (HARMONY) and pegozafermin in 23 to 37% versus 2% (ENLIVEN). If TQA2225 is comparably potent, 48 weeks should separate from placebo, but its potency is unproven, arms are only about 40 patients, and missing biopsies count as failures. The primary is either NASH resolution or fibrosis improvement. The record still says recruiting with a 48-week biopsy, so completion in December 2026 looks optimistic.

assumptions.claim: In HARMONY, NASH resolution without worsening of fibrosis at week 24 occurred in 47% (28 mg) and 76% (50 mg) of efruxifermin patients versus 15% on placebo.
assumptions.source: HARMONY, NCT04767529; Harrison et al., Lancet Gastroenterol Hepatol 2023

assumptions.claim: In ENLIVEN, NASH resolution without worsening of fibrosis at week 24 occurred in 23 to 37% of pegozafermin patients versus 2% on placebo.
assumptions.source: ENLIVEN, NCT04929483; Loomba et al., N Engl J Med 2023

reason: Hyaluronate injections bring a large improvement in WOMAC on their own, leaving a small margin for the cells, and the MRI cartilage outcome at 24 weeks must also be met.
rationale: Earlier small trials from the same sponsor (autologous ReJoin against hyaluronate) reported better WOMAC and cartilage volume, and a Korean phase 3 of autologous adipose stem cells beat placebo on WOMAC at six months. But large blinded trials of cell injections show small differences against active comparators, hyaluronate arms improve substantially, and the trial also has an MRI cartilage primary outcome at 24 weeks that must be met too. I assume about 3 WOMAC points of benefit. With 520 patients, two listed sites and 48-week follow-up, the trial will not report by mid-2027.

assumptions.claim: In the ReJoin phase 2b trial of about 52 patients, autologous adipose-derived mesenchymal progenitor cells improved WOMAC and cartilage volume more than hyaluronic acid at 12 months.
assumptions.source: Lu et al., Stem Cell Res Ther 2019 (NCT02162693)

assumptions.claim: In the Korean phase 3 of autologous adipose-derived stem cells (261 patients), WOMAC improved more than with placebo at 6 months.
assumptions.source: Kim et al., Am J Sports Med 2023

reason: The trial was still recruiting at its registered primary completion date, so it will most likely run on with a late record update and no results posted on ClinicalTrials.gov.
rationale: A phase 2 from a small Chinese sponsor that was still recruiting at its registered primary completion date. Such trials rarely post results on ClinicalTrials.gov, are seldom formally terminated within a year, and seldom change a response-rate primary outcome, though a switch to progression-free survival is possible in a randomized first-line design.

reason: A bone-density gain over placebo is close to certain for a sclerostin-blocking antibody; the residual risk is a topline that only calls the data positive without a statement on the primary endpoint.
rationale: AGA2118 neutralizes sclerostin and DKK1. Sclerostin antibodies give very large 12-month spine gains: romosozumab 210 mg monthly +11.3% versus -0.1% on placebo, blosozumab up to +17.7%. Against a between-patient SD of about 4 to 5 points, 54 patients per arm detect a difference this size with near certainty, and several regimens get a chance. Enrollment is complete and the 12-month visit falls around December 2026; Angitia is private, so the date of a topline release or a congress presentation (ASBMR is in autumn) is the main uncertainty.

assumptions.claim: In the romosozumab phase 2 trial, 210 mg monthly increased lumbar spine BMD by 11.3% at 12 months versus a 0.1% decrease with placebo.
assumptions.source: McClung et al., N Engl J Med 2014 (NCT00896532)

assumptions.claim: In the blosozumab phase 2 trial, lumbar spine BMD rose by up to 17.7% at 52 weeks at the highest dose.
assumptions.source: Recker et al., J Bone Miner Res 2015

reason: Atropine is an effective comparator, so an unproven antisense eye drop would need a clear advantage in refraction change to show superiority in 140 children; comparable efficacy is the likelier report.
rationale: SHJ002 is an antisense oligonucleotide against a microRNA, with no published controlled evidence that it slows myopia more than atropine, an active comparator that slows progression by 30 to 60% depending on concentration (LAMP: -0.27 D a year at 0.05%, -0.59 D at 0.01%, -0.81 D on placebo). With 140 children and a between-child SD near 0.45 D, the trial could only show superiority with a difference above about 0.2 D. The study is described as exploratory relative to atropine, so a claim of comparable efficacy is the likelier outcome, which does not count as met.

assumptions.claim: In LAMP, mean spherical equivalent change over one year was -0.27 D with 0.05% atropine, -0.46 D with 0.025%, -0.59 D with 0.01% and -0.81 D with placebo.
In ATOM2, myopia progressed by about -0.49 D over two years with 0.01% atropine.

reason: Shingrix with AS01 gives CD4+ T-cell response rates above 90%, so superiority is out of reach; success depends on the sponsor having a non-inferiority objective and saying it was met, not just calling the data positive.
rationale: No formal hypothesis is registered and seven of the eight primaries are safety. Shingrix CD4(2+) response rates one month after dose 2 run about 90-95%, so JCXH-105 can at best match it; superiority is out of reach. Arm size fits a non-inferiority reading with a 10-point margin. Immorna moved from phase 1 to a 460-subject head-to-head, suggesting adequate cellular immunogenicity, but RNA zoster candidates have struggled to match AS01-adjuvanted gE. A private sponsor may only call the data positive, which counts as not met.

assumptions.claim: About 93% of Shingrix recipients in the ZOE-50 immunogenicity substudy had a gE-specific CD4(2+) T-cell vaccine response one month after the second dose.
assumptions.source: Cunningham et al., J Infect Dis 2018 (ZOE-50/ZOE-70 immunogenicity substudy)

assumptions.claim: JCXH-105 was tested against Shingrix in a phase 1 trial in adults aged 50 to 69 before this phase 2 began.

reason: Placebo improvement in dementia-psychosis trials is large and site quality across 296 sites is uneven, so a modest KarXT effect at the lower dose used in the elderly may not separate on NPI-C H+D.
rationale: Xanomeline reduced delusions and hallucinations dose-dependently in the 1997 Alzheimer's trial and KarXT is a proven antipsychotic in schizophrenia, but ADEPT uses lower doses in frail patients, adjunctive ARISE missed, and ADEPT-2 needed extra enrolment after site irregularities. Drug effects in Alzheimer's psychosis are usually small against large placebo improvement, and 406 patients power only about 0.3 SD. I put a clean readout near 42% and allow for an early stop if ADEPT-2 fails. The record still shows recruiting weeks before its completion date, so timing will slip.

assumptions.claim: In a 6-month trial in 343 patients with Alzheimer's disease, xanomeline produced dose-dependent reductions in hallucinations, delusions and agitation compared with placebo.
KarXT added to background antipsychotics did not significantly beat placebo on PANSS total score at week 6 in the ARISE trial.
In the phase 2 trial of pimavanserin in Alzheimer's disease psychosis, the NPI-NH psychosis score at week 6 improved by about 1.9 points on placebo and 3.8 points on drug.

reason: A miss would need a far smaller effect than the three phase 2 anti-TL1A trials showed, for example from the earlier week-12 read or loss of exposure to anti-drug antibodies.
rationale: Three anti-TL1A antibodies gave placebo-adjusted remission gains of 16 to 27 points in phase 2: afimkibart 32% v 12% at week 14 (TUSCANY-2), tulisokibart 26% v 1% (ARTEMIS-UC), duvakitug 36-48% v 20%. With 350 patients, a 12-point true gain over an 8% placebo rate still gives about 90% power. I shrink the effect to 16 points for phase 3, an earlier week-12 read and a mixed population. Residual risk is a changed regimen and anti-drug antibodies. Roche should announce topline in the first half of 2027.

assumptions.claim: In TUSCANY-2, clinical remission at week 14 was 32% with pooled doses of afimkibart (then RVT-3101) and 12% with placebo.
In ARTEMIS-UC cohort 1, clinical remission at week 12 was 26% with tulisokibart and 1% with placebo.
assumptions.source: Sands et al., N Engl J Med 2024 (ARTEMIS-UC)

assumptions.claim: In RELIEVE UCCD, clinical remission at week 14 in ulcerative colitis was 36% and 48% with two duvakitug doses versus 20% with placebo.
assumptions.source: RELIEVE UCCD phase 2b, Teva and Sanofi topline December 2024

reason: Both week 12 and week 52 remission must be met; the added risk is loss of response over a year of treat-through dosing, for example from anti-drug antibodies, on top of the induction risk.
rationale: Same drug and week-12 endpoint as Ametrine-2, plus a second primary, remission at week 52 in a treat-through design, and both must be met. TUSCANY-2 showed 32% v 12% remission at week 14 and 36% remission at week 56 on continued dosing; placebo treat-through remission at one year is usually near 10%. Power is high for both, so joint success is about 0.84; the extra risk is loss of response from anti-drug antibodies, which were frequent with this antibody. Completion in January 2027 points to topline in the second quarter.

assumptions.claim: In TUSCANY-2, clinical remission at week 14 was 32% with pooled doses of afimkibart (then RVT-3101) and 12% with placebo.
In the chronic period of TUSCANY-2, 36% of patients on continued afimkibart (RVT-3101) were in clinical remission at week 56.
In the phase 2a TUSCANY study, 82% of patients given the antibody (then PF-06480605) developed anti-drug antibodies.
assumptions.source: Danese et al., Clin Gastroenterol Hepatol 2021 (TUSCANY)

reason: If the margin is 10 points, 154 per arm gives only about 80% power with truly equal arms, and a small real deficit for once-daily dosing would cut that to about half.
rationale: Budesonide orodispersible 1 mg twice daily gives about 90% histological remission at 6 weeks (93% in EOS-1), and the dose-response is flat at the top, so 2 mg once daily should come within a few points. The sample (154 per arm) matches a 10-point margin with 80% power at equal 90% rates, so even a 2-3 point true deficit, as hinted by twice-daily beating once-daily fluticasone in FLUTE, cuts power to about half. A wider margin would make success likely. Falk reports through congresses, so results by mid-2027 are unlikely.

assumptions.claim: In EOS-1, budesonide orodispersible tablets 1 mg twice daily gave histological remission in 93% of patients at 6 weeks versus 0% on placebo.
In FLUTE, histological response was 80% with fluticasone orodispersible 1.5 mg twice daily and 67% with 3 mg once daily at bedtime.
assumptions.source: Dellon et al., Clin Gastroenterol Hepatol 2022 (FLUTE)

reason: Unproven mechanism in ulcerative colitis with small arms; enrolment of 143 across 207 sites suggests the adaptive study did not expand, so monotherapy likely shows little gain over placebo.
rationale: Eltrekibart neutralises ELR+ CXC chemokines to block neutrophil recruitment and has no earlier efficacy data in ulcerative colitis. Only 143 patients were enrolled across 207 sites in a study described as lasting 4-5 years, which suggests the adaptive design stopped enrolling instead of expanding. Arms of 30-50 give little power for monotherapy against placebo unless the gain exceeds 20 points. Lilly tends to present positive phase 2 data at congresses and post the rest on ClinicalTrials.gov at 12 months, so a result public by June 2027 is somewhat enriched for success.

assumptions.claim: In LUCENT-1, clinical remission at week 12 was 24.2% with mirikizumab and 13.3% with placebo.
assumptions.source: D'Haens et al., N Engl J Med 2023 (LUCENT-1)

assumptions.claim: The registry record lists 143 enrolled patients and 207 sites in 21 countries for this trial.

reason: Higher response and PFS may not carry through to survival against pembrolizumab, as in LEAP-010, and the CD47 component may add toxicity without much benefit.
rationale: Phase 2 gave a 60% response rate for ivonescimab plus ligufalimab in first-line PD-L1-positive disease, against about 19% for pembrolizumab alone in KEYNOTE-048, so PFS should improve. Survival is less sure: LEAP-010 raised response and PFS with lenvatinib plus pembrolizumab but not survival (HR 1.15), and CD47 blockade with evorpacept added little in this disease. I put the true HR near 0.78 and unconditional success near 55%. Akeso announces wins quickly, at interim or final analysis, and rarely announces misses, so a result public by mid-2027 is mostly a positive one.
evidence: Ivonescimab plus ligufalimab phase 2 in head and neck cancer (ESMO 2024)

assumptions.claim: Median overall survival with pembrolizumab alone was 12.3 months in the PD-L1 CPS 1 or higher population of KEYNOTE-048.
In LEAP-010, pembrolizumab plus lenvatinib improved response rate and PFS over pembrolizumab plus placebo but not overall survival (hazard ratio about 1.15).
Ivonescimab plus ligufalimab gave an objective response rate of 60% in 20 first-line patients with PD-L1-positive recurrent or metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.

reason: Small phase 2a already closed to recruitment should finish its 12-week blinded period on time; the main risk is early termination of the extension if the BIIB122 programme is ended after LUMA.
rationale: Fifty-patient phase 2a with a 12-week double-blind period, already closed to recruitment, so the last primary visit should fall by early 2027 and the March 2027 date should hold. The main operational risk is early termination of the open-label extension if the larger LUMA phase 2b study of BIIB122 in early Parkinson's disease reads out negative and Biogen and Denali end the programme. Results are not due on ClinicalTrials.gov until about a year after primary completion, so posting by August 2027 is unlikely.

assumptions.claim: BIIB122 is also being tested in LUMA, a placebo-controlled phase 2b study in early-stage Parkinson's disease run by Biogen with Denali.

reason: The CSF MTBR-tau243 assay may capture antibody-bound tau or move on lecanemab alone, blunting the dose-response, and Eisai may report late or only in general terms.
rationale: E2814 binds the microtubule-binding region of tau, and CSF MTBR-tau243 is close to a target-engagement readout: in the phase 1b/2 study in dominantly inherited Alzheimer's disease it fell by roughly half or more. A dose-response test including placebo, with about 35 per arm on a lecanemab background, should be significant unless the assay captures antibody-bound tau or lecanemab alone moves the marker as much. The risk lies more in how and when Eisai words the result: AAIC in July 2027 is the likely venue, after the main deadline.
evidence: E2814 Study 103 (phase 1b/2, dominantly inherited Alzheimer's disease) 2023

assumptions.claim: In Study 103, E2814 lowered CSF MTBR-tau243 in patients with dominantly inherited Alzheimer's disease.
assumptions.source: E2814 Study 103 (phase 1b/2), Eisai presentations at CTAD 2023 and AAIC 2024

assumptions.claim: E2814 is being given together with lecanemab in the DIAN-TU Tau NexGen trial in dominantly inherited Alzheimer's disease.

reason: PAR2 blockade has no prior clinical evidence in migraine prevention, so the most likely failure is simply too little effect on monthly migraine days.
rationale: MEDI0618 blocks PAR2, a target with only preclinical support in migraine; this is its first efficacy test. First-in-class preventive mechanisms succeed in phase 2 about a third of the time. The population (two or more failed oral preventives, mostly CGRP-naive) gives a low placebo response of about 1-1.5 days, which helps, and 100-150 per arm can detect about 1.3 days. AbbVie taking over sponsorship is weak positive evidence. A result public by June 2027, four months after completion, would more likely be a positive one, so I shade p_met up slightly.

assumptions.claim: In CONQUER, in patients with 2 to 4 prior preventive category failures, monthly migraine days fell by about 1.0 on placebo and 4.1 on galcanezumab over 3 months.
In LIBERTY, in episodic migraine with 2 to 4 prior preventive failures, monthly migraine days at weeks 9-12 fell by about 0.2 on placebo and 1.8 on erenumab.

reason: About 60 hepatic progression events with 2:1 allocation need an observed HR near 0.6 or better; melphalan is not an established colorectal drug and systemic therapy is delayed about 3 months in the experimental arm.
rationale: Melphalan/HDS gives strong liver control in uveal melanoma (FOCUS) and isolated hepatic perfusion data show activity in colorectal liver metastases. hPFS in an open-label trial favours a liver-directed arm, while TAS-102/bevacizumab controls refractory disease for about 5-6 months (SUNLIGHT). But 90 patients split 2:1 yield about 60 events, so the observed HR must be near 0.6; procedure toxicity and a 3-month delay to systemic therapy add risk. Delcath guided the hPFS readout to end 2027, so the registered date will slip and a result by June 2027 is unlikely.
evidence: Hughes et al. 2016, percutaneous hepatic perfusion phase 3 in melanoma liver metastases
van Iersel et al. 2008, isolated hepatic perfusion with melphalan for colorectal liver metastases

assumptions.claim: In SUNLIGHT, trifluridine-tipiracil plus bevacizumab gave a median PFS of 5.6 months in refractory metastatic colorectal cancer.
In FOCUS, melphalan/HDS gave an objective response rate of about 36% and a median PFS of 9.0 months in uveal melanoma liver metastases.
Delcath guided that the hepatic PFS primary readout of this phase 2 trial is expected by the end of 2027.

reason: The two-domain MHQ endpoint was chosen after a small phase 2, so the true effect is probably smaller than assumed, and 98 patients only detect a standardised difference near 0.6; most direct repairs recover well by week 24.
rationale: NTX-001 (PEG fusion) has animal data and a small phase 2 (NEUROFUSE) suggesting faster early recovery and less pain, but efficacy there was secondary and the phase 3 endpoint (MHQ ADL plus pain at week 24) looks selected from it. With 98 patients, power is good only for a difference near 0.6 SD; regression from a small selected signal is likely, and standard repair patients improve substantially by week 24. The record still recruits although its primary completion is March 2027, so the date will probably slip and topline is more likely in late 2027.
evidence: Bamba et al. 2016, PEG fusion in human digital nerve repair

assumptions.claim: A small human case series of PEG fusion in digital nerve repair reported faster early sensory recovery than standard repair.
assumptions.source: Bamba et al., J Trauma Acute Care Surg 2016

assumptions.claim: The phase 2 NEUROFUSE study of NTX-001 was a small randomised trial with safety as its primary endpoint and the Michigan Hand Questionnaire as an efficacy measure.
With 49 patients per arm, a two-sided 0.05 test has 80% power only for a standardised difference of about 0.57.
assumptions.source: NCT06616025 record (enrolment 98) and standard two-sample power formula

reason: The chronic placebo-controlled trough effect on PVR may be much smaller than the acute fall after one IV dose; the CpcPH primary subset is only part of 191 patients, and relaxin-class drugs have disappointed in heart failure.
rationale: TX45 (Fc-relaxin) lowered PVR about 30% acutely in CpcPH patients in phase 1b, with lower wedge pressure and higher cardiac output, so a 24-week PVR endpoint is mechanistically plausible. Against that: uncontrolled single-dose data, trough catheterisation at week 24, a primary subset of perhaps 35 per arm, and class setbacks (volenrelaxin in HFpEF; group 2 PH trials such as MELODY-1). I assume a true placebo-adjusted fall near 0.6-0.7 Wood units with SD about 1.7, giving roughly even odds. Primary completion is November 2026, so topline is likely in early 2027.

assumptions.claim: In the TX45 phase 1b study, a single intravenous dose lowered PVR by roughly 30% in patients with combined pre- and post-capillary pulmonary hypertension.
Lilly's long-acting relaxin volenrelaxin showed no benefit in its phase 2 HFpEF trial and its development was stopped.
In MELODY-1, macitentan did not improve PVR in combined pre- and post-capillary PH due to left heart disease and caused more fluid retention than placebo.

reason: Sugemalimab is an active PD-L1 comparator; adding CTLA-4 blockade to PD-1 has not clearly improved outcomes in NSCLC (KEYNOTE-598; BTCRC LUN16-081 consolidation) and may add pneumonitis-related discontinuation after chemoradiotherapy.
rationale: Head-to-head against an active, approved consolidation antibody (GEMSTONE-301: PFS 9.0 vs 5.8 months, HR 0.64). Evidence that CTLA-4 adds to PD-(L)1 in NSCLC is weak: KEYNOTE-598 was negative and nivolumab plus ipilimumab consolidation looked similar to nivolumab in BTCRC LUN16-081, with more toxicity. Cadonilimab's gains over PD-1 are clearest in PD-L1-low tumours, so I expect a true HR near 0.85 and about 30% unconditional success. The trial started November 2024 with 560 patients; a statement by June 2027 would most likely be a positive interim, which raises the conditional probability.

assumptions.claim: In GEMSTONE-301, sugemalimab consolidation gave a median PFS of 9.0 months versus 5.8 months with placebo (HR 0.64).
In KEYNOTE-598, adding ipilimumab to pembrolizumab did not improve PFS or OS in metastatic NSCLC with PD-L1 TPS of 50% or more.
In BTCRC LUN16-081, consolidation nivolumab plus ipilimumab and nivolumab alone gave similar 18-month PFS (about 67% vs 62%), with more grade 3 or higher toxicity in the combination.

reason: NaV1.8 inhibitors have matched but not beaten pregabalin (VX-548 phase 2), so a comparison with the active control would fail; if the primary is within-group change it is easily met, but Vertex may not frame a deprioritised drug that way.
rationale: The record mirrors the VX-548 DPN phase 2, whose primary endpoint was within-group change from baseline (about -2.1 to -2.3 points, pregabalin -2.09) and was reported as met. If VX-993 is analysed and reported the same way, the primary is near-certain to be significant; against pregabalin, superiority is very unlikely. VX-993 failed its bunionectomy phase 2 and Vertex has deprioritised it, so the result may be reported tersely, or the study stopped, without stating the primary was met. I put the labelled outcome near even. Primary completion March 2027 makes a statement by June uncertain.

assumptions.claim: In the VX-548 phase 2 DPN study, mean NPRS change at week 12 was -2.26, -2.11 and -2.18 across the VX-548 doses and -2.09 with pregabalin.
The primary endpoint of the VX-548 phase 2 DPN study was within-group change from baseline, with pregabalin as a reference arm and no formal comparison against it.
VX-993 did not meet the primary endpoint (SPID48 versus placebo) in its phase 2 bunionectomy study.

reason: Enzalutamide alone controls ARSi-naive disease for 18 months or more, so the added effect of EZH2 inhibition may be smaller than in post-abiraterone disease, and the rPFS analysis may be immature.
rationale: Mevrometostat plus enzalutamide roughly halved radiographic progression risk in randomised post-abiraterone data (phase 1 expansion: 14.3 vs 6.2 months, HR 0.51) and Pfizer reported MEVPRO-1 positive. MEVPRO-2 tests the same combination earlier, with 900 patients and ample power for an HR near 0.7. The risk is dilution in ARSi-naive disease, where enzalutamide alone gives a median rPFS around 18-22 months (TALAPRO-2 control 21.9), plus GI and haematological toxicity reducing exposure. I expect an HR near 0.67. Registered primary completion December 2026 points to topline in the first half of 2027.
evidence: Mevrometostat phase 1 randomised expansion, ASCO GU 2025 (NCT03460977)

assumptions.claim: In the randomised phase 1 dose-expansion, mevrometostat plus enzalutamide gave a median rPFS of 14.3 months versus 6.2 months with enzalutamide alone (HR 0.51) in abiraterone-pretreated mCRPC.
Pfizer announced that the phase 3 MEVPRO-1 trial met its primary rPFS endpoint.
assumptions.source: Pfizer press release on MEVPRO-1 (NCT06551324), December 2025

assumptions.claim: In TALAPRO-2, the placebo plus enzalutamide arm had a median rPFS of 21.9 months by blinded central review.

reason: About 100 patients and roughly 30 DFS events can only detect a very large effect; cancer vaccines have a poor record in prostate cancer, and an early public statement would more likely call interim data encouraging than report a met primary.
rationale: Cancer vaccines have repeatedly failed in prostate cancer (GVAX cell vaccine in VITAL-1/2; PROSTVAC in PROSPECT), and no adjuvant vaccine has reduced recurrence after prostatectomy. With 100 patients and a control recurrence rate near one third at 22 months, only about 30 events are expected, so significance needs an HR near 0.4. The open-label design with PSA-driven events and vaccine crossover for controls adds noise. The trial still recruits while its primary completion is February 2027 with 22 months of follow-up required, so it will run late; a small sponsor may issue only an interim 'encouraging' statement.

assumptions.claim: The GVAX prostate cell vaccine failed in the phase 3 VITAL-1 and VITAL-2 trials, both of which were stopped early.
PROSTVAC did not improve overall survival in the phase 3 PROSPECT trial in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer.

reason: The main risk is formal: CR/CRi needs marrow-confirmed remission within 16 months by independent review and the arms are small; if the analysis is descriptive, the sponsor may not state a met hypothesis.
rationale: BTK inhibitor monotherapy rarely produces complete remission early (zanubrutinib CR/CRi about 7% at 26 months in SEQUOIA), while sonrotoclax plus zanubrutinib gave 100% responses with deep, mostly MRD-negative remissions in the phase 1 TN CLL cohorts and BCL2-BTK doublets reach CR/CRi rates of 40-55%. A difference of roughly 30 points is detectable even with about 45 per arm. Residual risk is the IRC marrow requirement at month 16 and how formally the comparison is tested. Primary completion is November 2026; presentation is most likely at a 2027 congress.

assumptions.claim: In SEQUOIA, zanubrutinib monotherapy had a CR/CRi rate of about 7% at a median follow-up of about 26 months.
In the phase 1 BGB-11417-101 study, sonrotoclax plus zanubrutinib gave a 100% overall response rate in treatment-naive CLL.
In GLOW, fixed-duration ibrutinib plus venetoclax reached a CR/CRi rate of about 39% by independent review versus about 11% with chlorambucil-obinutuzumab.

reason: Efficacy risk is low; the main threat is an inflated placebo ACR50 response, as placebo response hurt sonelokimab's VELA-2 hidradenitis trial, or a weaker response in TNF-experienced patients.
rationale: IL-17A/F inhibition works in TNF-inadequate-responder psoriatic arthritis: bimekizumab reached ACR50 43% vs 7% at week 16 in BE COMPLETE. Sonelokimab itself gave ACR50 46-47% vs 20% at week 12 in the phase 2 ARGO trial. With roughly 150 per arm, a difference of 20 points or more gives power above 99%. I expect placebo near 10% and sonelokimab 120 mg near 38%. The only real risks are placebo inflation and regression from phase 2, as seen in hidradenitis. Primary completion January 2027 suggests topline in the first half of 2027.

assumptions.claim: In the phase 2 ARGO trial, ACR50 at week 12 was 46% with sonelokimab 60 mg and 47% with 120 mg versus 20% with placebo.
In BE COMPLETE, bimekizumab gave ACR50 at week 16 in 43% of patients versus 7% with placebo in TNF-inadequate-responder psoriatic arthritis.
In sonelokimab's VELA-2 hidradenitis trial, a high placebo response left the primary endpoint short of statistical significance in the primary analysis.

reason: Rimegepant's preventive effect is modest (0.8 days per month over placebo with every-other-day dosing) and perimenstrual attacks are hard to treat; a high placebo response over five cycles could shrink the difference.
rationale: Rimegepant is an established acute and preventive CGRP antagonist (prevention trial: -4.3 vs -3.5 monthly migraine days), and short-term perimenstrual prophylaxis works with triptans (frovatriptan). Daily dosing through the perimenstrual window should cut migraine days by about 0.3-0.4 per 5-day period over placebo; with several hundred randomised and SD near 1.3 that gives power around 85-90%. Risks are a modest drug effect and placebo response. The record still shows recruiting with primary completion November 2026 and five treatment cycles needed, so completion will likely slip into 2027 and results may not be public by June.
evidence: Croop et al. 2021, rimegepant prevention trial (NCT03732638)
Silberstein et al. 2004, frovatriptan menstrual migraine prophylaxis

assumptions.claim: In the rimegepant prevention trial, monthly migraine days fell by 4.3 with rimegepant every other day versus 3.5 with placebo.
Frovatriptan perimenstrual prophylaxis reduced the incidence of menstrual migraine to 41% (twice daily) and 52% (once daily) versus 67% with placebo.

reason: If cyclosporine is continued to week 76 instead of being stopped at about 12 months as in MENTOR, its responders do not relapse and 45 patients per arm cannot separate the arms.
rationale: Anti-CD20 therapy beat cyclosporine at 18-24 months in MENTOR because cyclosporine responders relapsed after withdrawal; a week-76 endpoint suggests the same design. If so, about 65% vs 30% gives roughly 85% power with 45 per arm, and two doses give two chances. Risks: unknown cyclosporine duration, good calcineurin-inhibitor response in Chinese patients, and an open-label exploratory phase 2 that may report no formal test. A private Chinese sponsor makes public results by mid-2027 unlikely.

assumptions.claim: In MENTOR, complete or partial remission was 60% with rituximab vs 52% with cyclosporine at 12 months and 60% vs 20% at 24 months.
Zuberitamab is an anti-CD20 antibody first approved in China in 2023 for diffuse large B-cell lymphoma.

reason: Orforglipron's weight loss is about half tirzepatide's, so the AHI effect could be smaller than expected, though it would have to fall below about 5 events/h to miss significance.
rationale: Orforglipron gives roughly 8-10% placebo-adjusted weight loss at one year. SURMOUNT-OSA (tirzepatide, about 16% net loss) cut AHI by 20-24 events/h more than placebo, and liraglutide (about 4% net) by 6, so 10-12 events/h is expected here. With about 178 per arm and SD near 23, that is z above 4; even a 7-event effect would be significant. Both sub-studies should succeed. Lilly discloses top-line data and is expected to seek the OSA indication.

assumptions.claim: In SURMOUNT-OSA study 1, AHI changed by -25.3 events/h with tirzepatide vs -5.3 with placebo at week 52, a difference of -20.0.
In ATTAIN-1, orforglipron 36 mg gave about 11-12% mean weight loss at 72 weeks vs about 1-2% with placebo.
In SCALE Sleep Apnea, liraglutide 3.0 mg reduced AHI by 12.2 vs 6.1 events/h with placebo at 32 weeks.
assumptions.source: Blackman et al., Int J Obes 2016

reason: FcRn blockade has no proven effect on skin fibrosis, and with 58 vs 29 patients the observed mRSS difference must exceed about 3 points against a placebo arm that usually improves on background therapy.
rationale: FcRn blockade is untested in systemic sclerosis; the autoantibody hypothesis for skin fibrosis is unproven, though B-cell depletion (DESIRES) gives some support. mRSS phase 2 trials have a poor record (tocilizumab, abatacept, riociguat and lenabasum all missed), with placebo arms on background immunosuppression improving 3-5 points by week 24. With 58 vs 29 patients and SD near 6.5, the observed difference must exceed about 3 points. argenx usually discloses proof-of-concept results within a few months of completion.

assumptions.claim: In focuSSced, mRSS changed by -6.14 with tocilizumab vs -4.41 with placebo at week 48, a difference that was not significant.
assumptions.source: focuSSced, Khanna et al., Lancet Respir Med 2020 (NCT02453256)

assumptions.claim: In DESIRES, mRSS changed by -6.30 with rituximab vs +2.14 with placebo at 24 weeks.
assumptions.source: DESIRES, Ebata et al., Lancet Rheumatol 2021

reason: A topical amyloid-beta modulator has no prior evidence of slowing geographic atrophy, and 55 eyes per arm can detect only a slowing of a third or more.
rationale: GAL-101 is a topical amyloid-beta aggregation modulator with no prior efficacy data in geographic atrophy; reaching effective retinal concentrations by eye drop is unproven. Even intravitreal complement inhibitors slow lesion growth only 14-22%. With about 55 per arm and between-patient SD near 1.2 mm2/year, the trial needs roughly a 35% slowing for significance.
