rationale: Individually randomized, open-label trial of app-based symptom monitoring versus usual care in about 1,458 patients on systemic therapy. PRO-TECT found a 2.4-point QLQ-C30 quality-of-life gain at 3 months and earlier trials (Basch 2016, CAPRI) were positive, while eRAPID and others were mixed. With roughly 600 evaluable per arm the standard error is near 1 point, so a true 2 to 3 point effect is significant about half to three-quarters of the time; including early-stage patients may shrink it. Still recruiting in late 2026, so results before mid-2027 are unlikely.

assumptions.claim: In PRO-TECT, electronic symptom monitoring improved QLQ-C30 health-related quality of life at 3 months by about 2.4 points versus usual care.
In the Basch single-centre trial, fewer patients on symptom monitoring had worsened health-related quality of life at 6 months than with usual care.
assumptions.source: Basch et al., J Clin Oncol 2016

reason: Dupilumab acts slowly in CSU, so the only real risk is an unexpectedly strong early response in the dupilumab arm (loading dose, active-comparator expectancy) narrowing the week 4 gap.
rationale: Novartis chose week 4 because remibrutinib acts within days (UAS7 down about 17 to 18 points by week 4 in REMIX) while dupilumab separated from placebo only gradually in CUPID, with most of its advantage arriving after week 12. I expect dupilumab near -10.5 and remibrutinib near -17.5 at week 4, a 7-point gap; with about 200 per arm and SD near 12 the standard error is about 1.2, so power is very high. Readout is likely at a mid-2027 allergy or dermatology congress or by press release.

assumptions.claim: In REMIX-1 and REMIX-2, remibrutinib reduced UAS7 at week 12 by about 20 points versus about 12 to 14 with placebo, with separation from placebo as early as week 1.
assumptions.source: REMIX-1 and REMIX-2, NEJM 2025, NCT05030311 and NCT05032157

assumptions.claim: In CUPID Study A, dupilumab reduced UAS7 at week 24 by 20.5 points versus 12.0 with placebo.
assumptions.source: LIBERTY-CSU CUPID Study A, J Allergy Clin Immunol 2024, NCT04180488

reason: The large seizure reductions seen in small open-label phase 1/2a cohorts may shrink against a sham intrathecal control with its own placebo response, leaving the week-28 difference too small to reach significance.
rationale: Zorevunersen raises Nav1.1 from the wild-type SCN1A allele; open-label phase 1/2a and extension data showed large, durable convulsive-seizure reductions on top of standard drugs, including fenfluramine. Sham or placebo arms in Dravet trials improve 10-25%. With about 85 per arm, a difference near 17 points reaches significance, so the trial succeeds unless most of the open-label effect disappears under blinding. Soticlestat's narrow phase 3 miss in Dravet is the caution. Readout after the 52-week period is expected around mid-2027, so the June deadline is close to a coin flip.
evidence: Lagae 2019, fenfluramine Study 1 in Dravet syndrome
BUTTERFLY natural history study in Dravet syndrome

assumptions.claim: Patients given 2 or 3 doses of 70 mg zorevunersen in the phase 1/2a studies had a median reduction in convulsive seizure frequency of about 85% at 3 months after the last dose.
assumptions.source: Stoke Therapeutics phase 1/2a MONARCH/ADMIRAL end-of-study data, 2024

assumptions.claim: In fenfluramine Study 1 in Dravet syndrome the placebo arm had a median reduction in monthly convulsive seizure frequency of about 19%.
In GWPCARE1 the placebo arm's median monthly convulsive seizure frequency fell by about 13%, versus about 39% with cannabidiol.

reason: The record covers only the open-label phase 2 part and still shows enrolling by invitation three months before its date; slow enrolment or adding the phase 3 part to this record would push primary completion later.
rationale: Phase 2/3 protocol whose record lists only the 24-patient open-label phase 2 part. Status is still enrolling by invitation with a 26-week primary endpoint and a January 2027 date, so either enrolment runs past the date or the sponsor updates the record with the placebo-controlled phase 3 part, which would move the date by a year or more and could add a primary outcome. BridgeBio is committed to infigratinib, so stopping is unlikely. Results posting by August 2027 is unlikely for a continuing study.

reason: Vehicle response in mild disease could be high and the molecule's potency is not well documented publicly, but a topical JAK inhibitor rarely misses EASI-75 against vehicle with 120 patients per arm.
rationale: QLM3003 appears to be a topical JAK inhibitor (JAK inhibitors are excluded as prior therapy). Topical JAK inhibitors beat vehicle on EASI-75 by 20-40 points at 4-8 weeks in the ruxolitinib and delgocitinib phase 3 trials, and Chinese vehicle-controlled dermatology phase 3 trials seldom fail. Two doses of 120 each against 120 vehicle give very high power for a 25-30 point difference. The main uncertainty is disclosure: Qilu is private and rarely posts or press-releases results quickly, so a public result by mid-2027 is unlikely.

assumptions.claim: In TRuE-AD1 and TRuE-AD2, EASI-75 at week 8 was reached by about 62% of patients on ruxolitinib 1.5% cream versus 24.6% and 14.4% on vehicle.
assumptions.source: Papp et al., J Am Acad Dermatol 2021 (TRuE-AD1/2)

assumptions.claim: In the Japanese phase 3 trial of delgocitinib 0.5% ointment, modified EASI-75 at week 4 was reached by about 26% versus about 6% on vehicle.
assumptions.source: Nakagawa et al., J Am Acad Dermatol 2020

reason: A novel epigenetic regulator added to standard symptomatic therapy is unlikely to move ADAS-cog 12 within 26 weeks; almost every add-on mechanism tested this way has failed on cognition.
rationale: ONO-2020 is a first-in-class epigenetic regulator with no published efficacy data in patients. Symptomatic add-on drugs in mild-to-moderate Alzheimer's disease, such as the 5-HT6 antagonists, have almost uniformly failed on ADAS-cog over 24-26 weeks, and placebo decline over 26 weeks is only 1-2 points, leaving little room. Two doses with about 85 per arm give some chance of a nominal hit. The trial ended in mid-2026; Ono tends to disclose outcomes in quarterly pipeline updates, where failures appear as discontinuations.
evidence: STARSHINE, STARBEAM and STARBRIGHT idalopirdine phase 3 trials, 2018

assumptions.claim: Intepirdine added to donepezil showed no significant benefit on ADAS-cog at 24 weeks in mild-to-moderate Alzheimer's disease.
Idalopirdine added to cholinesterase inhibitors did not improve ADAS-cog at 24 weeks in any of three phase 3 trials.
assumptions.source: Atri et al., JAMA 2018 (STARSHINE, STARBEAM, STARBRIGHT)

reason: Semaglutide 2.4 mg could do better than expected in this lower-BMI fatty-liver population while mazdutide 9 mg underdelivers because of titration time and diabetic participants, narrowing the gap on weight.
rationale: Mazdutide 9 mg gave about 18.6% weight loss at 60 weeks in GLORY-2; semaglutide 2.4 mg gave about 12% at 44 weeks in STEP 7's largely Chinese population. A 4-6 point gap with about 240 per arm is powered above 99%. Glucagon agonism gives mazdutide a clear edge on liver fat, so the second primary is also likely met; both must be met. Mazdutide already beat semaglutide 1 mg in DREAMS-3. Innovent usually reports phase 3 toplines within weeks of completion.

assumptions.claim: In GLORY-2, mazdutide 9 mg produced a mean weight loss of about 18.6% at week 60 versus about 3% with placebo in Chinese adults with obesity.
In STEP 7, semaglutide 2.4 mg produced a mean weight loss of 12.1% at week 44 versus 3.6% with placebo in a predominantly Chinese population.
assumptions.source: Mu et al., Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol 2024 (STEP 7, NCT04251156)

assumptions.claim: In GLORY-1, mazdutide 6 mg produced a mean weight change of about -14.8% at week 48 versus about -0.5% with placebo.

reason: Part B is still recruiting and the primary safety window runs 52 weeks per subject, so the November 2026 primary completion date cannot hold for the whole study and should move to late 2027 or beyond.
rationale: Two-part gene therapy study: Part A (45 subjects) enrolled in 2025, Part B (90 subjects) depends on drug from a second manufacturing process and the record still shows recruiting in late October 2026. Primary outcomes are adverse events through week 52, so completion for Part B subjects falls at least a year after their dosing. The registered date looks like Part A's. Pacira treats PCRX-201 as a lead pipeline asset, so stopping is unlikely; results posting by August 2027 is very unlikely.

reason: Open-label ICARS gains may partly reflect practice and placebo effects, and with about 25 patients per arm only an advantage of roughly 4-5 points or more over placebo reaches significance.
rationale: GLM101 delivers mannose-1-phosphate to bypass the PMM2 defect; an open-label phase 2 reported ICARS improvement after 24 weeks, but ataxia scales improve with repeated testing and expectation, and delivery to the cerebellum is unproven. With about 25 per arm and a between-patient SD near 7, significance needs roughly a 4-5 point advantage. I put the unconditional chance near one in three; a private sponsor is more likely to announce a positive result, which lifts the figure conditional on a public result.
evidence: GLM101 phase 2 open-label study in PMM2-CDG (Glycomine), 2024

assumptions.claim: An open-label phase 2 study of weekly intravenous GLM101 in PMM2-CDG reported improvement in ICARS total score after 24 weeks at 30 mg/kg.
assumptions.source: Glycomine phase 2 open-label study of GLM101, reported 2024-2025

assumptions.claim: In the AZATAX trial, ICARS total score improved significantly after 6 months of open-label acetazolamide in PMM2-CDG.

reason: Ulotaront's true advantage over placebo looks like 2-4 PANSS points from DIAMOND 1 and 2, below the roughly 4.5-point difference this trial needs for significance, and placebo response in acute trials stays high.
rationale: Ulotaront missed in both DIAMOND phase 3 trials: 75 mg was no better than placebo in DIAMOND 1 and 100 mg led placebo by 3.8 points in DIAMOND 2, after a 7.5-point phase 2 effect. This trial repeats 75 and 100 mg with about 179 per arm and tighter entry criteria (hospitalised, prior good antipsychotic response). With an SD near 19-20, significance needs about 4.5 points; a true effect near 3 gives roughly 25% power. Primary completion was October 2026, so a topline is likely by spring 2027.

assumptions.claim: In DIAMOND 1, PANSS total change at week 6 was -16.9 with ulotaront 50 mg and -19.6 with 75 mg versus -19.3 with placebo.
assumptions.source: DIAMOND 1 (NCT04072354) topline, Sumitomo Pharma and Otsuka, 2023

assumptions.claim: In DIAMOND 2, PANSS total change at week 6 was -16.4 with ulotaront 75 mg and -18.1 with 100 mg versus -14.3 with placebo.
assumptions.source: DIAMOND 2 (NCT04092686) topline, Sumitomo Pharma and Otsuka, 2023

assumptions.claim: In the phase 2 trial, PANSS total change at week 4 was -17.2 with ulotaront versus -9.7 with placebo.

reason: Novartis closed the study early after 7 participants; the open questions are whether the record ends as terminated or completed and how soon the small safety dataset is posted.
rationale: The record already says the study is being closed out early with only 7 randomized, and the primary outcome has been reduced to safety. Novartis usually labels sponsor-decision early closures as terminated, though an amended protocol with all enrolled participants followed to a defined end could be marked completed. Primary completion was October 2026, so results are due about October 2027; Novartis tends to post near the 12-month mark, which makes posting by end of August 2027 less likely than not.

reason: Fully enrolled vaccine trial with a fixed visit schedule and US defence co-funding; it should complete near the registered date, with results posted later than August 2027.
rationale: Healthy-volunteer phase 2 with 411 enrolled and status active, not recruiting; remaining visits follow a fixed vaccination schedule, so primary completion in February 2027 should hold within 90 days. The programme is funded with the US JPM CBRN office, which lowers the chance of a sponsor-driven stop. Results are due about a year after primary completion, so posting by 31 August 2027 is unlikely. Immunogenicity primaries are specified in detail and unlikely to change in substance.

reason: If TQB3473 is only as active as fostamatinib (durable response under 20%), dropouts and a small placebo arm could leave the difference short of significance, though this is unlikely.
rationale: TQB3473 is an oral Syk inhibitor; the class has beaten placebo on durable platelet response in chronic ITP (sovleplenib 48% vs 0% in Chinese patients, fostamatinib 18% vs 2%). Placebo durable response in pretreated chronic ITP with counts under 30 is near zero, so even a fostamatinib-sized effect should be significant with about 200 patients. The main uncertainty is this molecule's true potency and tolerability. A readout before mid-2027 is unlikely since 24-week treatment ends around March 2027.

assumptions.claim: In ESLIM-01, durable platelet response was 48.4% with the Syk inhibitor sovleplenib versus 0% with placebo in Chinese adults with chronic ITP.
In the pooled FIT-1 and FIT-2 trials, stable response was 18% with fostamatinib versus 2% with placebo.
assumptions.source: Bussel et al., Am J Hematol 2018

assumptions.claim: In LUNA 3, durable platelet response was 23% with rilzabrutinib versus 0% with placebo.

reason: Three-times-weekly vadadustat tends to give lower hemoglobin than ESA, and a gap near 0.5 g/dL would push the confidence bound past a -0.75 g/dL non-inferiority margin.
rationale: Akebia's VOCAL trial compares in-center three-times-weekly vadadustat with standard ESA; the hypothesis is most likely non-inferiority on hemoglobin change with a -0.75 g/dL margin, as in INNO2VATE and MO2DIFY. Vadadustat usually runs 0.2-0.5 g/dL below ESA, so with about 175 per arm the lower confidence bound should sit near -0.55, inside the margin but with limited room. If the hypothesis were superiority it would fail. The trial completed in August 2026, so topline is expected by early 2027.

assumptions.claim: In INNO2VATE prevalent-dialysis patients, the hemoglobin difference between vadadustat and darbepoetin at weeks 24-36 was -0.17 g/dL, within the -0.75 g/dL non-inferiority margin.
MO2DIFY compared once-daily and three-times-weekly vadadustat with ESA in hemodialysis patients using hemoglobin change with a -0.75 g/dL non-inferiority margin.

reason: Failure would need the composite response to collapse because ALT normalization lags behind viral suppression, which phase 2 data make very unlikely against a near-zero control.
rationale: Delayed-treatment controls at week 12 should have essentially no HDV RNA target-not-detected plus ALT normalization (ALT above normal is required at entry). In phase 2 SOLSTICE the monthly combination gave undetectable HDV RNA in roughly two-thirds at week 48 and ALT normalization in about half, so a composite response near 30-40% is expected. With about 124 patients this contrast is overwhelmingly significant. Vir has guided to topline around the turn of 2026/2027.

assumptions.claim: In SOLSTICE, tobevibart plus elebsiran every 4 weeks produced HDV RNA target-not-detected in about 41% of participants at week 24.
In MYR301, the delayed-treatment control arm had a combined virologic and ALT response of 2% at week 48.

reason: Six patients per arm cannot show a significant difference in parenteral support volume unless the effect is very large and consistent.
rationale: Only 18 patients are randomized across three arms (6 each), with four primary outcomes including two efficacy measures and no stated formal hypothesis. A statistically significant fall in both parenteral support volume and stool volume versus placebo is very unlikely at this size, and Jaguar/Napo typically describes such data as encouraging rather than as a met endpoint. Recruitment was still open in late 2026, so the 24-week treatment period will probably run past the registered March 2027 completion.

assumptions.claim: In STEPS, placebo patients reduced parenteral support volume by about 2.3 L/week at week 24 versus 4.4 L/week with teduglutide.
The trial randomizes 18 patients 1:1:1 to two crofelemer doses or placebo.

reason: All three co-primary endpoints must be met and any statement by mid-2027 would have to come from an interim analysis or an early stop, given the trial only began in August 2026.
rationale: Combined oral contraceptives reliably beat placebo on lesion counts and global assessment in acne (drospirenone/EE 20 mcg trials), and cyproterone is a stronger antiandrogen, so the 531-patient 2:1 trial should be positive if completed, although all three co-primaries must be met. The trial only started in August 2026 with 24 weeks of treatment, so the February 2027 completion date is not credible and a result by mid-2027 is very unlikely; an early public statement would more likely be a stop or interim outcome.

assumptions.claim: In two placebo-controlled trials of drospirenone 3 mg/ethinyl estradiol 20 mcg in moderate acne, investigator global success was 15% vs 4% and 21% vs 9% after six cycles.
assumptions.source: Koltun et al. 2008 and Maloney et al. 2008

assumptions.claim: The trial started in August 2026 and treats for six 28-day cycles, with registered primary completion in February 2027.

reason: Faricimab produces near-maximal visual gains by week 16, leaving no room for superiority and making success depend on a pre-specified non-inferiority objective in a small trial.
rationale: IBI302 (efdamrofusp alfa, VEGF/complement bispecific) is compared with faricimab on BCVA change at week 16 with about 50 patients per arm. After loading doses, strong anti-VEGF agents give similar gains (about 8-10 letters), so superiority is very unlikely; the trial counts as met only if Innovent pre-specified and reports non-inferiority, as it did in its phase 2 nAMD trial against aflibercept. I assume roughly even odds that a formal non-inferiority objective exists and is reported as met.
evidence: Innovent phase 2 IBI302 8 mg nAMD trial 2023-2024

assumptions.claim: In YOSEMITE and RHINE, faricimab every 8 weeks improved BCVA by about 10.7 and 11.8 letters at one year in DME.
Innovent reported that its phase 2 trial of 8 mg IBI302 in neovascular AMD met its primary endpoint of BCVA change non-inferior to aflibercept 2 mg.
assumptions.source: Innovent press release on the phase 2 high-dose IBI302 nAMD study, 2023-2024

reason: Enrolment is complete and follow-up is six months, so the trial should finish near the registered date, with registry results posted later than August 2027.
rationale: Small sham-controlled safety study of a single jCell injection with 6-month follow-up; enrolment (31) is closed and the registered December 2026 completion fits the follow-up window, so lateness and stopping are unlikely. Results are not due on the registry until late 2027 for an unapproved product, so posting by August 2027 is unlikely.

reason: Only if insulin dose reductions offset the glycaemic benefit, as partly happened with liraglutide, would the HbA1c difference shrink, and even then the sample is large enough to detect about 0.2 points.
rationale: Tirzepatide added to insulin in adults with type 1 diabetes and overweight should lower HbA1c by roughly 0.5-0.7 points versus placebo at 40 weeks, given large weight loss and insulin dose reductions seen in smaller studies and the 0.2-0.3 point effects of weaker GLP-1 agonists (liraglutide, semaglutide). With about 900 patients and an SD near 0.85 the trial is heavily powered. Lilly completes the trial in November 2026 and should report topline or at ADA by mid-2027.

assumptions.claim: In ADJUNCT ONE, liraglutide 1.8 mg added to insulin in type 1 diabetes lowered HbA1c by 0.20 percentage points more than placebo at 52 weeks.
assumptions.source: Mathieu et al., Diabetes Care 2016 (ADJUNCT ONE)

assumptions.claim: In ADJUST-T1D, semaglutide added to automated insulin delivery lowered HbA1c by about 0.3 percentage points versus placebo at 26 weeks.

reason: Recruitment of 49 transplant patients at four sites was still open five months before the registered completion date, so a delay beyond 90 days is about as likely as not.
rationale: Small four-site phase 2 comparing ethanol-free carmustine with BiCNU in BEAM conditioning; the primary window is only 30 days post-transplant, but the trial was still recruiting in late 2026 and small-company transplant trials often slip, so lateness is about even odds. Results posting by August 2027 is unlikely given completion in 2027.

reason: Fistula curettage and internal-opening closure in the saline arm give combined remission near 35-45%, which erased the cell-therapy effect in ADMIRE-CD II.
rationale: Local mesenchymal stem cell injection for Crohn's perianal fistulas showed a 16-point gain in combined remission in ADMIRE-CD (50% vs 34%) but no benefit in the larger ADMIRE-CD II (49% vs 46%), where the surgical-conditioning placebo response was high. With 114 per arm the trial needs roughly a 13-point observed difference. I expect a true effect near 10 points, giving somewhat under even odds. The trial was still recruiting in late 2026, so week-24 data are unlikely before late 2027.

assumptions.claim: In ADMIRE-CD, combined remission at week 24 was 50% with darvadstrocel versus 34% with placebo.
ADMIRE-CD II did not meet its primary endpoint of combined remission at week 24.

reason: Trial is already completed; the only live question is whether Boehringer's results clear registry QC within about 12.5 months of the August 2026 completion.
rationale: Record shows completed with primary completion 14 Aug 2026, so a stop is essentially excluded. Boehringer usually submits results close to the 12-month due date even for unapproved compounds; being posted by 31 Aug 2027 needs submission before mid-Aug 2027 and a clean QC pass, so somewhat under even odds. The eGFR primary is already collected; a substantive change to it is unlikely.

reason: Mechanism is unproven: the same anti-oxidised LDL antibody did not reduce vascular inflammation on FDG-PET in GLACIER, and the FAI signal rests on a small exploratory analysis in psoriasis.
rationale: Orticumab (anti-oxidised LDL antibody) failed to lower arterial FDG-PET inflammation in GLACIER; support for an FAI effect comes from an exploratory CCTA analysis in a small psoriasis phase 2a. FAI-score is a sensitive but noisy imaging biomarker and 240 patients give power only if a real effect exists, which I put near 30%. Still recruiting in late Oct 2026 with a 24-week endpoint, so completion slips past May 2027 and a readout by June 2027 is unlikely; a private sponsor would publicise mainly positive data.
evidence: Orticumab psoriasis phase 2a with CCTA substudy, 2023
Elnabawi et al., JAMA Cardiology 2019 (biologics and perivascular FAI in psoriasis)

assumptions.claim: In GLACIER, the anti-oxidised LDL antibody MLDL1278A (orticumab) did not reduce arterial FDG-PET inflammation (target-to-background ratio) versus placebo at 12 weeks.
assumptions.source: GLACIER, Lehrer-Graiwer et al., JACC Cardiovasc Imaging 2015

assumptions.claim: Biologic therapy for psoriasis was associated with a fall in perivascular fat attenuation index on CCTA at about one year, while untreated patients showed no change.
Higher perivascular FAI on CCTA predicted cardiac mortality in two independent cohorts, which is the basis for using it as an inflammation biomarker.

reason: With about 41 per arm the trial needs an observed ESSDAI difference near 2 points, more than the roughly 1.5 points I expect from APRIL-only blockade.
rationale: APRIL-only blockade is untested in Sjogren's; validated B-cell agents (ianalumab, telitacicept, dazodalibep, nipocalimab) give placebo-adjusted ESSDAI gains of about 1.5-3 points. IgG lowering should help the biological domain, so I expect a true effect near 1.5 points. With about 41 per arm and SD near 4.8, significance needs an observed difference near 2 points, giving roughly one-third power. Placebo change near -3.5 as in recent ESSDAI>=5 trials. Enrolment is complete; primary completion March 2027, so disclosure before July 2027 is unlikely.

assumptions.claim: In the dazodalibep phase 2 trial (population with ESSDAI of 5 or more), ESSDAI change at day 169 was about -6.3 with dazodalibep versus -4.1 with placebo.
assumptions.source: St Clair et al., Nature Medicine 2024; NCT04129164

assumptions.claim: In DAHLIAS, nipocalimab 15 mg/kg changed clinESSDAI at week 24 by about -6.4 versus -3.7 with placebo.
Ianalumab 300 mg gave a placebo-adjusted ESSDAI change of about -1.9 points at week 24 in the phase 2b dose-finding trial.

reason: A complete response gain is very likely, but overall survival is also registered as primary and will be immature, so a report by mid-2027 may not count as the full primary objective met.
rationale: SHR-A1912 is a CD79b ADC, the polatuzumab class; POLARGO showed pola plus R-GemOx roughly doubled CR rate (about 40% vs 19%) and improved OS (HR 0.60). With 141 per arm a 20-point CR gain is detected with high power even at a split alpha. Main uncertainty is how a dual primary (CRR plus OS, OS immature) is labelled and whether anything is public by mid-2027; Hengrui usually discloses at congresses or with NMPA filing acceptance. Control CR about 20-25% as in POLARGO and STARGLO.
evidence: Mounier et al., R-GemOx phase 2, Haematologica 2013

assumptions.claim: In POLARGO, adding the anti-CD79b ADC polatuzumab vedotin to R-GemOx improved overall survival (hazard ratio about 0.60) and raised the complete response rate to about 40% versus 19% with R-GemOx alone.
In STARGLO, the R-GemOx control arm had a complete response rate of about 22-25%.
SHR-A1912 is an antibody-drug conjugate directed at CD79b, the same target as polatuzumab vedotin.
assumptions.source: Hengrui SHR-A1912 phase 1 reports in B-cell lymphoma

reason: Enrolment is closed with a 16-week safety primary, so completion near the registered date is likely; results are not due until about a year later, and a sponsor portfolio decision is the main stop risk.
rationale: Active, not recruiting with a 16-week primary window and a 31 Dec 2026 placeholder date; modest slippage is possible but more than 90 days is unlikely. The drug is unapproved and results fall due about 12 months after completion, so posting by Aug 2027 would be unusual. A safety-count primary is unlikely to be rewritten.

reason: Failure would need an unusually high placebo resolution rate or many missing week-60 biopsies in arms of only about 60 patients.
rationale: Mazdutide is a GLP-1/glucagon dual agonist with large liver-fat reductions in obesity trials. Same-class survodutide and pemvidutide, and tirzepatide, gave MASH resolution or improvement in 45-62% vs 10-19% on placebo. With about 60 per arm and an expected 35-40 point gap, power exceeds 95%, and one of two doses suffices. A 60-week endpoint with start in June 2025 means the registered Sept 2026 primary completion is not credible; study completion July 2027 implies topline in late 2027, so disclosure by June 2027 is unlikely.

assumptions.claim: Survodutide, a GLP-1/glucagon dual agonist, gave improvement in MASH without worsening of fibrosis in 47%, 62% and 43% of patients across doses versus 14% with placebo at 48 weeks.
Tirzepatide gave MASH resolution without worsening of fibrosis in 44%, 56% and 62% across doses versus 10% with placebo at 52 weeks.
assumptions.source: SYNERGY-NASH, Loomba et al., NEJM 2024; NCT04166773

assumptions.claim: Pemvidutide gave MASH resolution without worsening of fibrosis in about 59% and 52% at two doses versus 19% with placebo at 24 weeks.

reason: A first dose-finding study in cervical dystonia may use doses too low for a full effect, and arms of about 44 leave limited power if the gain is under 5 TWSTRS points.
rationale: Every marketed botulinum toxin beat placebo on TWSTRS total at week 4 by 6-9 points (Dysport, Xeomin, Daxxify), with placebo change of about -2 to -7. IPN10200 is a recombinant long-acting BoNT with clear activity in glabellar lines. With about 44 per arm and SD near 11.5, a 7-point effect gives about 80% power per dose, and either dose suffices. Risk is conservative dosing in a first cervical dystonia study. Enrolment runs to about Feb 2027; Ipsen topline before July 2027 is unlikely.
evidence: Truong et al., abobotulinumtoxinA in cervical dystonia, 2010
Comella et al., incobotulinumtoxinA in cervical dystonia, 2011

assumptions.claim: In ASPEN-1, the TWSTRS total score change averaged over weeks 4 and 6 was -12.7 (125 U) and -10.9 (250 U) versus -4.3 with placebo.
assumptions.source: ASPEN-1, Comella et al., Neurology 2024; NCT03608397

assumptions.claim: AbobotulinumtoxinA 500 U improved TWSTRS total by 15.6 points versus 6.7 points with placebo at week 4.
assumptions.source: Truong et al., Parkinsonism Relat Disord 2010

assumptions.claim: IncobotulinumtoxinA 240 U improved TWSTRS total by 10.9 points versus 2.2 points with placebo at week 4.
assumptions.source: Comella et al., J Neurol Sci 2011

reason: The low zibotentan dose in the fixed combination gives a moderate UACR effect, and with noisy UACR and 112 per arm an unlucky sample could miss significance.
rationale: ZENITH-CKD showed zibotentan plus dapagliflozin lowered UACR by 27% (0.25 mg) to 34% (1.5 mg) versus dapagliflozin alone at 12 weeks, the same design and endpoint. Log-UACR SD about 0.8 gives a standard error near 0.11 with 112 per arm, so a 28% reduction yields about 80-85% power. High-proteinuria patients respond well to endothelin antagonists. Dapagliflozin arm starts after run-in, so its change should be small. A Russia-only registration study will probably surface through registry posting around Sept 2027 rather than a press release.

assumptions.claim: In ZENITH-CKD, zibotentan 1.5 mg plus dapagliflozin lowered UACR by about 33.7% and zibotentan 0.25 mg plus dapagliflozin by about 27.0% versus dapagliflozin plus placebo at week 12.
In ZENITH-CKD the 90% confidence interval for the 0.25 mg plus dapagliflozin UACR difference ran from about -38% to -14% with roughly 91 versus 177 patients.
A phase 3 trial of zibotentan/dapagliflozin versus dapagliflozin in CKD with high proteinuria was already registered before this round.

reason: Sham surgery produces large, durable placebo responses on diary endpoints, as in earlier transplant and gene therapy trials; before 2028 the only possible result is an early stop.
rationale: Primary endpoint is at week 78 and the trial was still recruiting in Oct 2026, so no efficacy readout is possible before 2028; the registered March 2027 date is not credible. Any public statement by June 2027 would almost certainly be a stop, which counts as not met. Longer term, phase 1 open-label data showed about 2 hours more good ON-time at high dose, but sham-controlled fetal cell and gene therapy trials in Parkinson's often failed on placebo response; I put eventual success near 35%.
evidence: Freed et al., fetal dopamine neuron transplantation, NEJM 2001
Olanow et al., fetal nigral transplantation, Ann Neurol 2003

assumptions.claim: In the open-label phase 1 exPDite study, the high-dose cohort gained about 2 hours per day of ON-time without troublesome dyskinesia at 12 to 24 months.
Two sham-surgery-controlled trials of fetal dopamine cell transplantation in Parkinson's disease missed their primary endpoints.
assumptions.source: Freed et al., NEJM 2001; Olanow et al., Ann Neurol 2003

assumptions.claim: The primary endpoint is measured at week 78 and the record still showed the trial recruiting in October 2026.

reason: Enrolment is closed and the PK primaries are read by week 18, so the February 2027 date should hold; BMS rarely posts results months ahead of the 12-month due date.
rationale: Active, not recruiting with 76 patients and PK primaries measured within 18 weeks, consistent with the registered 5 Feb 2027 primary completion. Results fall due in Feb 2028, so posting by Aug 2027 is unlikely. Stop risk is small for a fully enrolled formulation study; PK outcome lists are sometimes edited, so a modest amendment risk remains.

reason: Pembrolizumab alone already yields responses in about half of patients, so 59 per arm needs a 20-25 point ORR gain from an intralesional agent supported only by a small uncontrolled phase 1b.
rationale: Pembrolizumab alone gives ORR near 50% in first-line MCC (KEYNOTE-017 56%, KEYNOTE-913 49%); the durable-response definition trims this to roughly 42%. With 59 per arm, significance needs about a 20-25 point gain. IFx-Hu2.0 support is a small uncontrolled phase 1b in CPI-refractory patients, and intralesional add-ons to PD-1 have failed before (MASTERKEY-265). Enrollment in a rare tumour began December 2025 and the record still recruits, so a mid-2027 readout is unlikely; an early public outcome would more likely be a stop.
evidence: IFx-Hu2.0 phase 1b in advanced MCC and cSCC, 2023

assumptions.claim: First-line pembrolizumab gave an objective response rate of 56% in advanced Merkel cell carcinoma in KEYNOTE-017.
assumptions.source: KEYNOTE-017 / CITN-09, NCT02267603 (Nghiem et al., NEJM 2016; JCO 2019)

assumptions.claim: First-line pembrolizumab gave an objective response rate of 49% by central review in KEYNOTE-913.
Adding intralesional talimogene laherparepvec to pembrolizumab did not significantly improve PFS or OS versus placebo plus pembrolizumab in advanced melanoma.

reason: Bevacizumab already supplies VEGF blockade in the control arm, so the gain must come from PD-1 blockade in mostly MSS colorectal cancer, where add-on benefit has been modest (HR about 0.8) and 560 patients may not suffice.
rationale: Ivonescimab plus FOLFOXIRI gave ORR 81.8% in a small single-arm phase 2, and Akeso's ivonescimab phase 3s in lung cancer have all hit PFS. But here bevacizumab matches the VEGF arm, so benefit rests on PD-1 blockade in mostly MSS disease, where AtezoTRIBE (HR 0.69, phase 2) and CheckMate 9X8 (HR 0.81, missed) suggest HR near 0.8; 560 patients give about 50% power for that. A statement by mid-2027 would most likely be a positive interim announcement, which lifts the conditional probability.
evidence: Ivonescimab with or without ligufalimab plus FOLFOXIRI phase 2, ESMO 2024

assumptions.claim: In AtezoTRIBE, adding atezolizumab to FOLFOXIRI plus bevacizumab gave median PFS of 13.1 versus 11.5 months (HR 0.69).
In CheckMate 9X8, nivolumab added to FOLFOX plus bevacizumab did not significantly improve PFS (HR 0.81, medians 11.9 months in both arms).
Ivonescimab plus FOLFOXIRI gave an objective response rate of 81.8% in first-line MSS/pMMR metastatic colorectal cancer in a phase 2 study.
assumptions.source: Ivonescimab with or without ligufalimab plus FOLFOXIRI phase 2, ESMO 2024

reason: No prior mania data: a muscarinic agonist may be less antimanic than D2 blockers, and a week of titration inside a 3-week trial plus high placebo response could shrink the YMRS difference below the roughly 2.7 points needed.
rationale: No phase 2 in mania exists; the bet is that KarXT's robust acute antipsychotic effect (EMERGENT-2/-3, about 8-10 PANSS points) carries to mania, which responds to most antidopaminergic drugs, and M4 agonism lowers striatal dopamine. Against that: one week of titration in a 3-week trial, GI tolerability, high placebo response in mania trials, the ARISE miss, and brexpiprazole's failure in two mania trials. With 137 per arm the study has about 85-90% power for a 4-point YMRS difference; I expect about 3 points.
evidence: Brexpiprazole acute mania phase 3 trials (Vieta et al.), 2021
Cariprazine acute mania phase 3 (Calabrese et al.), 2015

assumptions.claim: KarXT lowered PANSS total score versus placebo by 9.6 points at week 5 in EMERGENT-2.
Adjunctive KarXT did not reach statistical significance on PANSS total score at week 6 in ARISE (difference about 2 points, p=0.11).
Brexpiprazole did not separate from placebo on YMRS at week 3 in two phase 3 acute mania trials.

reason: Untested mechanism in mania: muscarinic agonism may calm mania less than D2 blockade, titration takes a third of the 3-week window, and placebo response at sites in India, China and eastern Europe could be large.
rationale: Same design as BALSAM-1, so the outcomes are tightly linked. No phase 2 in mania exists; the case rests on KarXT's robust acute antipsychotic effect (EMERGENT-2/-3) and the general responsiveness of mania to drugs that damp dopamine signalling. Risks: a week of titration inside a 3-week trial, GI tolerability, the ARISE miss and brexpiprazole's two failed mania trials. Sites in India, China and eastern Europe may raise placebo response. With 137 per arm, power is about 85-90% for 4 YMRS points; I expect about 3.
evidence: Brexpiprazole acute mania phase 3 trials (Vieta et al.), 2021
Cariprazine acute mania phase 3 (Calabrese et al.), 2015

assumptions.claim: KarXT lowered PANSS total score versus placebo by 8.4 points at week 5 in EMERGENT-3.
Discontinuation for adverse events in the pooled acute schizophrenia trials was 6% on KarXT versus 4% on placebo.
assumptions.source: Cobenfy US prescribing information, 2024 (EMERGENT-2 and EMERGENT-3)

assumptions.claim: Brexpiprazole did not separate from placebo on YMRS at week 3 in two phase 3 acute mania trials.

reason: High between-patient variability of subcutaneous daratumumab exposure in myeloma, with two AUC windows that must both fall inside the equivalence margins, is the main way a true biosimilar could miss.
rationale: Celltrion's biosimilar phase 3 programmes have consistently met their equivalence endpoints, and 473 patients is a large sample chosen for the high between-patient variability of subcutaneous daratumumab exposure in myeloma. Residual risk comes from two co-primary AUC windows (first week and weeks 8-10) that must both fall within the margins, target-mediated clearance tied to tumour burden, and a new hyaluronidase co-formulation. Enrollment is complete, so week-24 data should be in hand by March 2027; Celltrion usually discloses topline several months later.

assumptions.claim: Subcutaneous daratumumab was non-inferior to intravenous daratumumab on both overall response rate and maximum trough concentration in COLUMBA.
Celltrion's CT-P43 ustekinumab biosimilar met its primary equivalence endpoint in its phase 3 trial in plaque psoriasis.

reason: Recruitment of narcolepsy type 2 patients is slow and the record still recruits a month before its completion date, so a slip of several months is likely; termination or outcome changes are unlikely.
rationale: Record still recruiting on 29 October 2026 with a 30 November 2026 completion date; NT2 is rare and hard to recruit, the design is adaptive, and participation runs up to 15 weeks, so a slip past February 2027 is about even odds. Takeda is investing heavily in orexin agonists, so termination is unlikely barring a class safety signal such as the liver injury seen with TAK-994. Takeda normally posts results near the 12-month deadline, after August 2027. A safety-count primary outcome is rarely amended.

reason: Benefit of oral SERDs over fulvestrant is concentrated in ESR1-mutated tumours; in an all-comer second-line Chinese population the blended hazard ratio may land near 0.85 and miss significance.
rationale: Oral SERDs beat fulvestrant mainly in ESR1-mutated disease: all-comer hazard ratios were 0.87 (EMBER-3), 0.81 (acelERA), 0.83 (VERITAC-2), with elacestrant at 0.70 in a fully CDK4/6-pretreated population. This Chinese trial takes all comers after 1-2 endocrine lines, so ESR1 mutation prevalence is perhaps 30% and the blended HR about 0.8; 640 patients give roughly even odds. Slight upward adjustment because the design might include a non-inferiority step and because Chinese sponsors mainly publicise positive results.

assumptions.claim: In EMBER-3, imlunestrant versus standard endocrine therapy gave a PFS hazard ratio of 0.87 in the overall population (not significant) and 0.62 in ESR1-mutated patients.
In acelERA, giredestrant versus physician's choice endocrine therapy gave a PFS hazard ratio of 0.81 that was not statistically significant.
Median PFS on placebo plus fulvestrant was 7.2 months in Chinese patients progressing after endocrine therapy in DAWNA-1.

reason: A first-in-class Wnt agonist must match monthly ranibizumab on vision; if barrier restoration alone dries the macula less completely than VEGF blockade, the BCVA difference will breach the non-inferiority margin.
rationale: Remigromig is a first-in-class Wnt agonist; support is the small open-label AMARONE study (+11.2 letters, CST -143 microns at week 12 in DME) and Merck's commitment to two pivotal trials. Monthly ranibizumab is a hard comparator (+10 to 11 letters at one year) and non-VEGF mechanisms have usually fallen short of anti-VEGF. With about 350 per arm and a likely 4-letter margin, non-inferiority needs an observed difference above about -2 letters. I treat it as a coin flip between near-equivalence and clear inferiority. BRUNELLO will read out first.

assumptions.claim: In AMARONE, DME patients given EYE103 monotherapy gained a mean 11.2 ETDRS letters with central subfield thickness reduced by 143 microns at week 12.
Ranibizumab-treated eyes gained a mean 11.2 letters at one year in DRCR Protocol T.
Aflibercept every 8 weeks gave mean gains of 10.9 and 10.3 letters at one year in YOSEMITE and RHINE.

reason: Vehicle response is high and variable in mild HS with few lesions, and a topical may not reach deep nodules, so the HiSCR75 gap could shrink well below the 29 points seen in the small phase 2.
rationale: Phase 2 (n=69) in the same mild HS population showed AN count reduction of 3.61 vs 2.42 and AN75 54% vs 25% at week 16. Discounting that 29-point gap by half still leaves about 13 points, and with about 286 per arm the trial keeps over 80% power for a 12-point difference against a vehicle rate near 26%. Risks are high and variable vehicle response in low-lesion-count disease, the stricter HiSCR75 endpoint, and limited penetration of a topical into deep nodules.
evidence: Ruxolitinib cream phase 2 in mild-moderate HS (NCT05635838), 2024

assumptions.claim: In the phase 2 trial of ruxolitinib cream 1.5% twice daily in mild HS, mean AN count change at week 16 was -3.61 versus -2.42 with vehicle.
In that phase 2 trial, 54.2% on ruxolitinib cream versus 25.0% on vehicle reached at least a 75% reduction in AN count at week 16.

reason: With about 33 patients per arm, a true 15-20 point endoscopic response gain over placebo has only around even odds of reaching significance, especially if many patients previously failed anti-TNF.
rationale: TNF blockade is validated in Crohn's (adalimumab endoscopic response about 40% at week 12 in SERENE CD) and brivekimig worked in biologic-naive hidradenitis (HS-OBTAIN), but less so after anti-TNF, and this trial allows advanced-therapy failures. Assuming about 32% response versus 12% on placebo, 33 per arm gives only about 55% power per dose at two-sided 0.05; two doses and a possibly looser phase 2 alpha help. The record still recruits with a week-16 endpoint, so completion will slip into 2027 and disclosure by mid-2027 is unlikely.

assumptions.claim: Brivekimig gave HiSCR50 in 67% versus 37% on placebo at week 16 in biologic-naive hidradenitis suppurativa.
Placebo endoscopic response at week 12 was 12% in ADVANCE and 11% in MOTIVATE.
Endoscopic response at week 12 was 43% with higher-dose and 39% with standard-dose adalimumab induction in SERENE CD.

reason: Mild HS with low lesion counts fluctuates spontaneously, so vehicle HiSCR75 could run high (vehicle response sank TRuE-PN2); the phase 2 signal came from 69 patients with uneven dropout and may shrink under non-responder imputation.
rationale: Phase 2 (n=69) showed AN75 54% vs 25% and a significant AN-count reduction; JAK inhibition is validated in HS by oral povorcitinib and upadacitinib. With 290 per arm, a true HiSCR75 gap of 10 points or more gives over 75% power, and I expect about 38% vs 25%. Risks are a high vehicle response in fluctuating mild disease, shrinkage from a small phase 2 analysed on observed cases, and limited dermal penetration. Incyte usually reports topline two to three months after primary completion, so a result by March 2027 is likely.

assumptions.claim: In the phase 2 trial of ruxolitinib 1.5% cream in mild HS, 54.2% of ruxolitinib patients and 25.0% of vehicle patients had at least a 75% reduction in abscess and inflammatory nodule count at week 16.
The phase 2 primary endpoint, change in abscess and inflammatory nodule count at week 16, was -3.61 with ruxolitinib cream versus -2.42 with vehicle (p<0.05).
Of the two identical phase 3 trials of ruxolitinib cream in prurigo nodularis, TRuE-PN1 met its primary endpoint and TRuE-PN2 did not reach statistical significance.

reason: Insulin is cut when tirzepatide starts and titrated to target in both arms, which can shrink the HbA1c difference toward the 0.2 points seen with liraglutide; even so the trial is powered to detect that.
rationale: GLP-1-based adjuncts lower HbA1c in type 1 diabetes even with insulin titrated in both arms: liraglutide by 0.2 points in ADJUNCT ONE and semaglutide by 0.3 in ADJUST-T1D. Tirzepatide gives greater weight loss and insulin-dose reduction, so I expect about 0.5 points versus placebo. With some 230 per arm and an SD near 0.8, even a 0.25-point difference would be significant. Failure would need insulin down-titration for hypoglycaemia to cancel the glycaemic gain. Lilly should disclose topline in early-to-mid 2027.

assumptions.claim: In ADJUST-T1D, semaglutide added to automated insulin delivery in adults with type 1 diabetes and obesity lowered HbA1c by about 0.3 percentage points more than placebo at 26 weeks.
In ADJUNCT ONE, liraglutide 1.8 mg added to insulin in type 1 diabetes lowered HbA1c by 0.20 percentage points more than placebo at 52 weeks.
In SURMOUNT-1, 4.3% to 7.1% of tirzepatide patients stopped treatment because of adverse events, against 2.6% on placebo.

reason: TDF is a strong comparator and each HBeAg stratum has only about 50 to 60 patients per arm, so a 20-point advantage at the 10 IU/mL cut-off may miss significance, and both strata must succeed.
rationale: Two primary outcomes, one per HBeAg stratum, and both must be met. In phase 1, ALG-000184 300 mg suppressed HBV DNA faster and deeper than historical nucleoside data, with about 60% of high-viral-load HBeAg-positive subjects below 10 IU/mL at week 48 and nearly all HBeAg-negative subjects suppressed. TDF reaches below 29 IU/mL in about two thirds of HBeAg-positive patients at week 48, fewer at the 10 IU/mL cut-off. I expect roughly 65% vs 45%, borderline with 50 to 60 per arm. The HBeAg-negative part depends on TDF's target-not-detected rate.
evidence: GS-US-320-0110, TAF vs TDF in HBeAg-positive (2016)
GS-US-320-0108, TAF vs TDF in HBeAg-negative (2016)
Study 103, TDF vs adefovir in HBeAg-positive (2008)

assumptions.claim: In the TAF versus TDF trial in HBeAg-positive chronic hepatitis B, 67% of TDF-treated patients had HBV DNA below 29 IU/mL at week 48.
In the phase 1 study, about 60% of HBeAg-positive subjects on ALG-000184 300 mg monotherapy had HBV DNA below 10 IU/mL at week 48.
In the TAF versus TDF trial in HBeAg-negative chronic hepatitis B, 93% of TDF-treated patients had HBV DNA below 29 IU/mL at week 48.

reason: Latanoprost drops lower diurnal IOP by about 7 mmHg, which intracameral prostaglandin implants have at best matched; with 25 per arm neither superiority nor a tight non-inferiority margin is within reach.
rationale: A 75-patient dose-finding study against latanoprost drops, with no stated hypothesis. Sustained-release prostaglandin implants (bimatoprost SR, travoprost intracameral implant) were shown non-inferior to timolol, a weaker comparator than latanoprost, so superiority over latanoprost is very unlikely; I expect the implant to lower IOP about 6 mmHg against about 7 for latanoprost. A 'met' outcome needs the sponsor to state that a pre-specified non-inferiority or responder goal was reached, which 25 per arm barely supports. PolyActiva is private and may release little.
evidence: iDose TR phase 3, travoprost intracameral implant vs timolol (2023)

assumptions.claim: In the AYAME trial, latanoprost 0.005% lowered mean diurnal IOP by about 6.6 mmHg from a baseline near 23 mmHg at week 4.
Bimatoprost SR was shown non-inferior, not superior, to timolol for IOP lowering over 12 weeks in its phase 3 trial.

reason: Controls stay on effective nusinersen, so the gap to gene therapy may be only 1 to 2 HFMSE points, below what 25 patients per arm can detect.
rationale: GC101 uses the same intrathecal AAV9-SMN1 dose as OAV101 IT, which gained 2.4 HFMSE points vs 0.5 with sham in treatment-naive patients (STEER) and about 1 point in patients switched from nusinersen or risdiplam (STRENGTH). Here controls continue nusinersen and should stay stable or gain slightly, so a true difference of 1 to 2.5 points is plausible; with 25 per arm and an SD near 4, significance needs over 2 points. Open-label assessment and young patients may inflate the difference. The record still says recruiting, so a readout by mid-2027 is unlikely.
evidence: STRENGTH, OAV101 IT after nusinersen or risdiplam (2025)

assumptions.claim: In STEER, intrathecal onasemnogene abeparvovec improved HFMSE by 2.39 points against 0.51 with sham at 52 weeks in treatment-naive patients aged 2 to under 18 years.
In STRENGTH, patients who stopped nusinersen or risdiplam and received intrathecal onasemnogene abeparvovec had a mean HFMSE increase of about 1 point at 52 weeks.
In CHERISH, nusinersen-treated children gained 3.9 HFMSE points while sham-treated children lost 1.0 point at 15 months.

reason: IL-1 inhibition is a weak mechanism in rheumatoid arthritis and the population is biologic-refractory; a 9-point ACR50 gain would not be significant with about 30 to 45 patients per arm.
rationale: IL-1 blockade has modest efficacy in rheumatoid arthritis: anakinra with methotrexate gave ACR50 of 17% vs 8% at 24 weeks, and lutikizumab failed in osteoarthritis. In patients who have failed one or two biologic or targeted drugs, I expect ACR50 near 20% vs 11% at week 12, which roughly 30 to 45 per arm cannot reliably separate at conventional alpha. AbbVie rarely announces phase 2 platform results; a public statement before 2028 would most likely be a congress abstract or a substudy stop.
evidence: Anakinra plus methotrexate in RA, Cohen (2004)
Lutikizumab in erosive hand osteoarthritis, Kloppenburg (2019)

assumptions.claim: Anakinra 100 mg daily added to methotrexate gave an ACR50 response of 17% against 8% with placebo at 24 weeks in rheumatoid arthritis.
assumptions.source: Cohen et al., Ann Rheum Dis 2004

assumptions.claim: Lutikizumab did not improve pain or synovitis versus placebo in its phase 2 trials in knee and erosive hand osteoarthritis.
The anti-CD40 antibody BI 655064 did not significantly improve ACR20 response versus placebo at week 12 in methotrexate-inadequate responders with rheumatoid arthritis.
assumptions.source: Visvanathan et al., Ann Rheum Dis 2019

reason: Percent change in AHI is highly variable and only about 70 patients per arm are enrolled; a lower-BMI Chinese population with more anatomical apnea could blunt the weight-loss effect.
rationale: HRS9531 is a GLP-1/GIP dual agonist with about 17 to 18% weight loss at 48 weeks in Chinese phase 3. Tirzepatide, same class, cut AHI by 51% vs 3% with placebo in SURMOUNT-OSA without PAP. Chinese patients have lower BMI and more craniofacial contribution, so I expect a somewhat smaller relative effect, about 42 points. Percent change in AHI is very variable (SD 60 or more), but 70 per arm still gives over 90% power. The record looks stale, so timing and disclosure are the main uncertainties.
evidence: HRS9531-301 phase 3 in obesity, Hengrui topline (2025)

assumptions.claim: In SURMOUNT-OSA Study 1 (patients not on PAP), AHI changed by -50.7% with tirzepatide against -3.0% with placebo at week 52.
HRS9531 6 mg produced a mean weight loss of about 17.7% at 48 weeks in Chinese adults with obesity or overweight.
In SURMOUNT-OSA Study 1, tirzepatide reduced AHI by about 20 events per hour more than placebo at week 52.

reason: With about 35 patients per arm, a 15-point remission gain over placebo is only borderline significant, and prior advanced-therapy failures may blunt a TNF-based drug.
rationale: Brivekimig blocks TNF and OX40L; TNF blockade is validated in ulcerative colitis but early remission gains were modest (golimumab 18% vs 6%, adalimumab 17% vs 9%), and the population includes advanced-therapy failures. Phase 2a in hidradenitis was positive. I expect about 25% vs 10% remission at week 16 at the top dose; with about 35 per arm that gives roughly 40% power per dose, helped by two dose arms. Sanofi tends to flag phase 2 readouts in quarterly updates, and registry results are due by December 2027.
evidence: HS-OBTAIN, brivekimig phase 2a in hidradenitis suppurativa (2025)

assumptions.claim: In PURSUIT-SC, clinical remission at week 6 was about 18% with golimumab induction against 6.4% with placebo.
In ULTRA 2, clinical remission at week 8 was 16.5% with adalimumab against 9.3% with placebo.
In the phase 2a HS-OBTAIN trial, brivekimig gave a HiSCR50 response of 67% against 37% with placebo at week 16 in biologic-naive hidradenitis suppurativa.

reason: About 50 to 60 patients per arm and an FEV1 SD near 400 mL leave moderate power for a 150 mL effect, and a population not selected for type 2 inflammation may dilute it.
rationale: PF-07275315 neutralises IL-4, IL-13 and TSLP, each a validated asthma target. Dupilumab raised pre-bronchodilator FEV1 at week 12 by 0.13 to 0.20 L over placebo, and the trial requires bronchodilator reversibility, which enriches for FEV1 responders. I expect about 150 mL at the top dose; with 252 patients over several arms, pairwise power is moderate, but a dose-response model should help. No eosinophil threshold is visible, which dilutes the effect. Pfizer seldom announces phase 2 results, so disclosure before 2028 is uncertain.

assumptions.claim: In the dupilumab phase 2b asthma trial, 200 mg every 2 weeks raised FEV1 at week 12 by about 0.20 L more than placebo in the overall population.
In QUEST, dupilumab improved pre-bronchodilator FEV1 at week 12 by 0.14 L (200 mg) and 0.13 L (300 mg) over matched placebo.
PF-07275315 is a trispecific antibody that binds IL-4, IL-13 and TSLP.

reason: Only about 55 first exacerbations are expected per dose-versus-placebo comparison, so a true hazard ratio near 0.6 would reach two-sided 0.05 only about half the time.
rationale: DPP1 inhibition is validated in bronchiectasis: brensocatib gave hazard ratios of 0.58 and 0.62 over 24 weeks in WILLOW, and the Chinese HSK31858 phase 2 roughly halved exacerbation rates. XH-S004 mirrors WILLOW with 78 per arm; at a 42% placebo event rate that yields about 55 events per comparison, so a hazard ratio of 0.6 is borderline at two-sided 0.05, though two dose arms and a possibly lenient phase 2 alpha help. Chinese sponsors disclose phase 2 data irregularly.

assumptions.claim: In WILLOW, the hazard ratio for time to first exacerbation over 24 weeks was 0.58 with brensocatib 10 mg and 0.62 with 25 mg versus placebo.
In WILLOW, 48.3% of placebo patients had an exacerbation over 24 weeks, against 31.7% and 33.3% on brensocatib 10 mg and 25 mg.
In the Chinese phase 2 trial of the DPP1 inhibitor HSK31858, annualised exacerbation rates were about 1.00 (20 mg) and 0.75 (40 mg) against 1.88 with placebo over 24 weeks.

reason: Small open-label Sanofi phase 2 needing actively hyperthyroid Graves' patients for 16 weeks; it was still recruiting about 15 weeks before the registered completion date, so some slippage is likely, and Sanofi usually posts results about a year after completion.
rationale: Thirty patients across 24 sites in 9 countries, started September 2025. With 16 weeks of treatment, the last patient had to start by late October 2026 to hit 11 February 2027, yet the record still says recruiting. Hyperthyroid patients willing to take an experimental BTK inhibitor are hard to find, so a slip past mid-May 2027 is close to even odds. Exploratory indication, so a modest chance of an early stop. Results posting within 6 months of completion is rare for Sanofi.

reason: Only 45 patients enrolled against three primary outcomes; with a between-patient SD near 17 Fugl-Meyer points the trial can only detect a gain of 10 points or more, and nothing suggests neflamapimod is that strong.
rationale: Proof-of-concept with only 45 patients enrolled (card planned 90) and three primary outcomes; round rules need all met. Fugl-Meyer change SD near 17 points gives a standard error near 5 points, so roughly a 10-12 point gain is needed for significance, more than fluoxetine's 9.8 in FLAME. Neflamapimod missed primary endpoints in Alzheimer's disease and in the double-blind phase of RewinD-LB; its stroke-recovery evidence is preclinical. Spontaneous recovery on placebo will be large, about 20 points. A small company may call trends encouraging, which counts as not met.
evidence: FLAME 2011 (fluoxetine for motor recovery after stroke)

assumptions.claim: In FLAME, Fugl-Meyer motor score improved by an adjusted mean of 24.3 points with placebo and 34.0 points with fluoxetine at day 90.
Neflamapimod did not meet its primary endpoint in the 16-week placebo-controlled phase of the RewinD-LB phase 2b trial in dementia with Lewy bodies.
The registry lists 45 participants enrolled in RESTORE, with status completed.

reason: Placebo AN-count reductions in recent HS trials run 25-35% or more; with about 82 per arm, an IL-17A-level effect of roughly 18 points sits only just above the 16 points needed for significance.
rationale: IL-17A blockade is validated in HS: secukinumab cut AN count 39-47% versus 22-24% on placebo in SUNSHINE/SUNRISE, and tibulizumab's IL-17A binder derives from ixekizumab. BAFF blockade is unproven in HS and may add little by week 16. With about 82 per arm and SD near 50-55 points, a difference of about 16 points is needed; I expect about 18, so power is 55-60% per dose, helped by two doses and a continuous endpoint, hurt by rising placebo responses in recent HS trials and multiplicity control.

assumptions.claim: In SUNSHINE, AN count fell by 46.8% with secukinumab every 2 weeks versus 24.3% with placebo at week 16.
In SUNRISE, AN count fell by 39.3% and 45.5% with secukinumab every 2 and every 4 weeks versus 22.4% with placebo at week 16.
Tibulizumab is a bispecific antibody combining an ixekizumab-derived IL-17A binder with a tabalumab-derived BAFF binder.

reason: The effect should be large, so the residual risk is 70 per arm with noisy polysomnography AHI and missing week-52 studies after PAP withdrawal; timing of any public result is the bigger uncertainty.
rationale: HRS9531 is a GLP-1/GIP dual agonist with about 18% weight loss at 48 weeks in Chinese phase 3, similar to tirzepatide, which cut AHI by 23.8 events/h versus placebo in PAP users in SURMOUNT-OSA trial 2. With 70 per arm and SD near 22, a difference near -18 gives z above 4, so failure would need a much weaker effect or heavy dropout. Lower baseline BMI and AHI in China trim the absolute effect. Timing is the main uncertainty: a 52-week trial started August 2025 probably reads out in 2027.

assumptions.claim: In SURMOUNT-OSA trial 2 (participants on PAP), AHI changed by -29.3 events/h with tirzepatide versus -5.5 with placebo at week 52, a difference of -23.8.
In SURMOUNT-OSA trial 1 (no PAP), the AHI difference versus placebo at week 52 was -20.0 events/h.
HRS9531 6 mg gave mean weight loss of roughly 18-19% at 48 weeks in Hengrui's Chinese phase 3 obesity trial.

reason: Sham eyes can improve through background or rescue anti-inflammatory therapy and fluctuating edema, and the record's CST band of 320 to under 400 microns with BCVA up to 78 letters leaves limited room for a visual gain over sham.
rationale: KSI-101 combines IL-6 and VEGF inhibition; the open-label phase 1b APEX study showed rapid drying and gains near 10 letters. Sham eyes in uveitic macular edema gain only 2-3 letters (PEACHTREE +3.0). The record restricts CST to 320 to under 400 microns and allows BCVA up to 78 letters, limiting headroom, so I expect about 5 letters over sham; with 300 patients and SD near 11 that is still well powered. Caution: Roche's intravitreal anti-IL-6 vamikibart missed in one of two phase 3 trials, and phase 1b was small and uncontrolled.

assumptions.claim: In PEACHTREE, sham-treated eyes with uveitic macular edema gained a mean of 3.0 ETDRS letters at week 24 versus 13.8 with suprachoroidal triamcinolone.
Intravitreal anti-IL-6 vamikibart met its primary endpoint in the phase 3 MEERKAT trial but not in the identically designed SANDCAT trial in uveitic macular edema.
In the phase 1b APEX study, KSI-101 produced mean BCVA gains of about 10 letters or more by week 12 in patients with macular edema secondary to inflammation.

reason: A 3,100-patient trial of a drug that halved LDL-C in phase 2b is vastly overpowered; only a conduct, supply or safety surprise, or a reporting quirk, could keep it from meeting the primary objective.
rationale: AZD0780 30 mg lowered LDL-C by 50.7% versus placebo at week 12 on statin background in phase 2b PURSUIT, with a monotonic dose response. With about 3,100 patients, a 12-week LDL-C endpoint and SD near 28 points, the trial is powered far beyond need; oral PCSK9 inhibition is validated by enlicitide's phase 3 programme. I expect slight attenuation in phase 3 (about -48 points) from adherence and treatment-policy analysis. Failure would need a conduct or safety surprise. The blind runs 52 weeks, so readout follows January 2027 completion.

assumptions.claim: In PURSUIT, AZD0780 30 mg once daily reduced LDL-C by 50.7% versus placebo at week 12 in patients on statin therapy.
assumptions.source: PURSUIT phase 2b, Koren et al., JACC 2025 (NCT06173570)

assumptions.claim: AZD0780 doses of 1, 3 and 10 mg reduced LDL-C by about 35%, 38% and 45% versus placebo at week 12 in PURSUIT.
assumptions.source: PURSUIT phase 2b, Koren et al., JACC 2025 (NCT06173570)

assumptions.claim: The oral PCSK9 inhibitor enlicitide reduced LDL-C by about 56% versus placebo at week 24 in the phase 3 CORALreef Lipids trial.

reason: PCSK9 inhibition works as well in HeFH as elsewhere and about 470 patients give essentially full power for a roughly 50-point LDL-C difference; only a conduct, safety or reporting surprise could cause a miss.
rationale: AZD0780 30 mg lowered LDL-C by 50.7% versus placebo at week 12 in phase 2b PURSUIT. PCSK9 inhibitors work as well or better in HeFH (enlicitide about -59% in CORALreef HeFH; inclisiran -47.9% in ORION-9), and placebo LDL-C tends to drift up in HeFH, widening the difference. With about 470 patients randomised 2:1 and SD near 27 points, power is effectively 100%. Failure would need a conduct or safety surprise. The blind runs 52 weeks, so the week-12 result is released after January 2027 completion.

assumptions.claim: In PURSUIT, AZD0780 30 mg once daily reduced LDL-C by 50.7% versus placebo at week 12 in patients on statin therapy.
assumptions.source: PURSUIT phase 2b, Koren et al., JACC 2025 (NCT06173570)

assumptions.claim: In ORION-9 in HeFH, LDL-C rose 8.2% with placebo and fell 39.7% with inclisiran at day 510.
Enlicitide reduced LDL-C by about 59% versus placebo at week 24 in adults with HeFH.
assumptions.source: CORALreef HeFH, Ballantyne et al., JAMA 2025

reason: A single-dose psychedelic trial in medically ill patients with adjustment disorder was still recruiting in the month before its registered completion date, so a slip of a few months is about as likely as not; posting by August 2027 is unlikely.
rationale: One hundred patients at 32 US sites since July 2025, with a day-7 primary endpoint, so enrolment can run almost to the completion date. The record still shows recruiting with completion in November 2026; finishing by end of February 2027 needs enrolment to close by mid-February. A novel population (cancer, ALS, MS, PD, IPF) and a sponsor also running a postpartum depression programme make a slip plausible. Private sponsor, so a small chance of a business-driven stop. Results are due a year after completion, after the read date.

reason: Enrolment is closed and the 6-month blinded period ends on a fixed schedule that the sponsor needs for its planned filing in toddlers, so a slip of more than 90 days is unlikely; results posting is not due until late 2027.
rationale: The record shows active, not recruiting, with a 6-month double-blind period and completion in November 2026, so the last randomised child fixes the date. DBV needs these safety data for its toddler filing, which argues against delay or a stop. The open-label extension runs to 2028, so the study stays active. Posting is due about 12 months after primary completion and can be deferred for an unapproved product, so posting by August 2027 is unlikely. A safety-events primary outcome rarely changes in substance.

reason: A small sponsor planned only six months from first patient to primary completion for 36 patients at 8 sites with strict eligibility (non-smoking household, BMI under 30, early PD on levodopa), so a slip past March 2027 is more likely than not.
rationale: Started 30 June 2026 with completion registered for 31 December 2026, which leaves under five months to enrol 36 patients given 14 days of dosing plus 30 days of follow-up. Site activation is staggered and multiple-dose cohorts usually need safety reviews between them, so finishing by end of March 2027 requires enrolment to close by mid-February. Parkinson Study Group sites and foundation funding help. A small company gives a modest stop risk. Results posting by August 2027 would be unusually fast.

reason: CD73 blockade has not yet shown a clear randomized benefit, and 150 patients give power only for a hazard ratio near 0.67, beyond what an add-on in an unselected population is likely to deliver.
rationale: Anti-CD73 add-ons have not yet produced a clear randomized win, and uliledlimab's support is single-arm response data in CD73-high tumours. With 150 patients and roughly 95 BICR PFS events, only a hazard ratio of about 0.67 or better reaches significance, while my central estimate is about 0.85 in an unselected population. Sintilimab-chemo control should give 7-8 months across histologies. A private Chinese sponsor reports selectively, so a public result is somewhat more likely to be favourable, and a relaxed phase 2 alpha is possible.

assumptions.claim: In ORIENT-11, sintilimab plus pemetrexed-platinum gave a median PFS of 8.9 months versus 5.0 months with chemotherapy alone in non-squamous NSCLC.
In ORIENT-12, sintilimab plus gemcitabine-platinum gave a median PFS of 5.5 months versus 4.9 months with chemotherapy alone in squamous NSCLC.
Uliledlimab plus toripalimab gave an objective response rate of about 63% in first-line NSCLC patients with high CD73 expression and PD-L1 of at least 1%.

reason: A MAO-B inhibitor is unlikely to produce the 2.5 to 3 point placebo-adjusted weight loss needed for significance with 22 versus 11 patients over 12 weeks.
rationale: KDS2010 is a reversible MAO-B inhibitor whose obesity rationale rests on mouse work (astrocytic GABA, GABRA5 neurons) and unpublished phase 1 signals; marketed MAO-B inhibitors do not cause meaningful weight loss. Each stage has only 22 active versus 11 placebo patients over 12 weeks, so a placebo-adjusted loss of 2.5 to 3 points is needed for significance, more than I expect. Stage 3 (240 mg) starts only after stage 2 finishes, so the January 2027 completion date is unrealistic and a public result by mid-2027 is unlikely.
evidence: Sa et al., Nature Metabolism 2023 (KDS2010 in obese mice)

assumptions.claim: KDS2010 reduced body weight in diet-induced obese mice without reducing food intake.
The record states that stage 2 (180 mg) was still being prepared for recruitment and that stage 3 (240 mg) starts only after the stage 2 week-13 safety review.

reason: The broad, mixed-aetiology DEE population may dilute the effect seen in SCN2A and SCN8A patients, leaving about 53 patients per arm short of power.
rationale: Relutrigine gave a 46% placebo-adjusted fall in motor seizures in SCN2A/SCN8A patients in EMBOLD at a lower dose, and sodium-channel blockers have precedent in Lennox-Gastaut syndrome. EMERALD tests higher doses in a mixed DEE population, where the effect should be diluted (some aetiologies, such as Dravet, may respond poorly), so I expect about 20-25 points beyond a placebo fall near 12%. With about 53 per arm that gives roughly two-thirds power, helped by having two dose arms. Praxis reports quickly, so a readout in early 2027 is likely.
evidence: Knupp et al., fenfluramine in Lennox-Gastaut syndrome (2022)

assumptions.claim: In EMBOLD cohort 1, relutrigine gave a 46% placebo-adjusted reduction in monthly motor seizures in SCN2A and SCN8A developmental and epileptic encephalopathy.
In the fenfluramine Lennox-Gastaut trial, median drop-seizure frequency fell 26.5% with 0.7 mg/kg/day versus 7.6% with placebo.
In PACIFIC, countable motor seizures fell by a median 59.8% with bexicaserin versus 17.4% with placebo in DEE patients.

reason: Failure is very unlikely; the only realistic routes are an operational problem or heavy dropout rather than lack of effect.
rationale: CagriSema beat placebo by 17 points at 68 weeks in REDEFINE 1 (20.4% versus 3.0%, treatment-policy), so superiority at 80 weeks with 609 patients is near certain. I expect 21-24% loss on CagriSema and 2-3% on placebo; the published difference depends on which estimand is quoted. Fixed 80-week visits and a March 2027 primary completion make a company announcement in the second quarter of 2027 likely. The 20% responder endpoint will clearly favour CagriSema but may appear without a formal test in the first release.

assumptions.claim: In REDEFINE 1, mean weight change at 68 weeks was -20.4% with CagriSema versus -3.0% with placebo under the treatment-policy estimand.
In REDEFINE 1, weight loss at 68 weeks was 22.7% with CagriSema versus 2.3% with placebo if all participants adhered to treatment.
In STEP 1, placebo with lifestyle intervention gave a mean weight change of -2.4% at 68 weeks.

reason: TSLP blockade failed with tezepelumab in atopic dermatitis, and the strong open-label phase 2a signal may shrink against a week-24 placebo improvement of about 35%.
rationale: Bosakitug (anti-TSLP) showed 94% EASI-75 at week 26 in a small open-label phase 2a, but tezepelumab, against the same target, failed in atopic dermatitis, so the true effect is very uncertain. With about 55 per arm and a standard deviation near 42 points, a difference of about 17 points is needed; placebo should improve about 35% by week 24. I put slightly under even odds on an effect that large. Primary completion was September 2026, so top-line data are imminent.

assumptions.claim: In the open-label phase 2a trial of bosakitug (BSI-045T) in atopic dermatitis, 94% of patients reached EASI-75 at week 26.
In ALLEGRO, EASI-50 at week 12 was 64.7% with tezepelumab plus topical corticosteroids versus 48.2% with placebo, which was not statistically significant.

reason: Topical JAK inhibition is untested in palmoplantar pustulosis, and PPPASI-75 at 16 weeks is a high bar that may leave the gap over vehicle below the roughly 13 points needed.
rationale: Delgocitinib cream is proven in chronic hand eczema, but there is no controlled evidence in palmoplantar pustulosis, a recalcitrant disease where systemic agents have missed (spesolimab phase 2b). PPPASI-75 at 16 weeks is demanding; I expect about 10% on vehicle and 22-25% on active if the drug works, against a gap of about 13 points needed with 68 per arm. The trial was still recruiting in late October 2026 against a December 2026 completion date, so it is probably late and unlikely to report by mid-2027.
evidence: Spesolimab PPP phase 2b, Burden et al. (2023)
Guselkumab PPP phase 3, Terui et al. (2019)

assumptions.claim: In DELTA 1 and DELTA 2, IGA-CHE treatment success at week 16 was 20% and 29% with delgocitinib cream versus 10% and 7% with vehicle.
The phase 2b trial of spesolimab in palmoplantar pustulosis did not meet its primary endpoint of percentage change in PPPASI at week 16.

reason: Recruitment still open six weeks before the registered completion date makes a slip likely, but the study should finish in 2027.
rationale: A 120-subject radiolabelled recovery study at two sites with 35-day storage is logistically slow; the record was still recruiting in late October 2026 against a 15 December 2026 completion, which needs the last donation by early November. I put about even odds on a slip of more than 90 days. Cerus needs the data for its red-cell submission, so a stop is unlikely. Results are not due on ClinicalTrials.gov until 12 months after primary completion, so posting by August 2027 is unlikely.

reason: The risk is not enoxaparin but the hypothesis: if the primary also requires superiority over apixaban, whose VTE rate is about 12-15%, the margin is much thinner.
rationale: Factor XI inhibitors have consistently beaten enoxaparin on venographic VTE after knee replacement (abelacimab, milvexian, osocimab), and REGN7508 gave about 7% versus 21% in phase 2. With about 667 per arm and an enoxaparin rate near 20%, power for superiority is above 99% at a relative risk near 0.4. The residual risk is the hypothesis structure: if the primary also requires beating apixaban, success is less sure. Completion is due February 2027 while still recruiting, so a readout by mid-2027 is a little under even odds.

assumptions.claim: In phase 2 (ROXI-VTE-II), VTE occurred in about 7% of patients given REGN7508 versus about 21% given enoxaparin after knee replacement.
In the abelacimab knee-replacement trial, VTE occurred in 22% of patients on enoxaparin versus 5% and 4% with abelacimab 75 mg and 150 mg.
In ADVANCE-2, VTE or death occurred in about 15% of patients on apixaban versus 24% on enoxaparin 40 mg daily after knee replacement.

reason: With 16 patients and no washout, carryover of the active effect into the placebo period and noisy diary data could leave a real effect short of significance.
rationale: B-VEC restores collagen VII and works on DEB skin wounds (GEM-3), and an ophthalmic case report showed corneal healing, so a real effect on abrasion days is biologically likely. The risks are size and design: 16 patients, a symptom-diary endpoint, and a two-period crossover with no washout, where carryover from active to placebo would shrink the measured difference. I expect about 6 symptom days a month on placebo and about 2.5 fewer on KB803, with a little over even odds of significance. Krystal will press-release the result.
evidence: Vetencourt et al., NEJM 2024 (ophthalmic B-VEC case report)

assumptions.claim: In GEM-3, complete wound healing at 6 months occurred in 67% of B-VEC-treated wounds versus 22% of placebo-treated wounds.
A patient with recessive DEB given ophthalmic B-VEC after ocular surgery had corneal healing and improved from hand-motion vision to 20/25.

reason: The trial is past its primary completion date and should close as completed, with results posting due only in October 2027.
rationale: The registered primary completion (23 October 2026) has passed with the trial active, not recruiting, so it should simply complete. Enrolment of 16 against about 48 described suggests sub-study 2 was cut back, which leaves some chance of a terminated label or of the sub-study 2 primary outcome being removed. AstraZeneca usually posts phase 2 results close to 12 months after primary completion, which falls after the 31 August 2027 read date.

reason: Earlier onabotulinumtoxinA trials in episodic migraine were negative, so the true gain over a large injection-placebo response may be about half a migraine day, less than 332 per arm can detect reliably.
rationale: Botulinum toxin A repeatedly failed in episodic migraine (2000s onabotulinumtoxinA trials; Jackson 2012 meta-analysis), with signals only in high-frequency subgroups. MINT-E enriches for 6-14 migraine days and reads out after two cycles with about 332 per arm, enough for a roughly 1-day difference. I expect a true effect near 0.5-0.6 days over a placebo change near -3.5, helped somewhat by functional unblinding. No controlled Xeomin migraine data exist. A private sponsor is likelier to publicise a win early, which lifts the conditional probability.

assumptions.claim: A 2012 meta-analysis found botulinum toxin A did not reduce headache frequency versus placebo in episodic migraine, while it did in chronic migraine.
In the pooled PREEMPT trials in chronic migraine, onabotulinumtoxinA reduced headache days by 8.4 versus 6.6 per 28 days with placebo at week 24.
assumptions.source: PREEMPT pooled analysis, Dodick et al., Headache 2010

assumptions.claim: In an exploratory onabotulinumtoxinA trial in episodic migraine the primary comparison with placebo was not significant, with benefit seen only in patients with 12 or more baseline headache days.

reason: The injection-placebo response in chronic migraine is large (about 6 days) and the toxin's margin is modest (1.5-2 days), so an effect slightly smaller than in PREEMPT would leave 269 per arm short.
rationale: OnabotulinumtoxinA reduced migraine and headache days versus placebo at week 24 in both PREEMPT trials (pooled headache days -8.4 vs -6.6), and incobotulinumtoxinA is pharmacologically similar unit for unit. With about 269 per arm and SD near 6.5, power is roughly 85-90% for a 1.8-day difference but only about half for 1.1. Risks: a larger placebo response in the CGRP era, an injection scheme or dose (unnamed Dose A) unlike PREEMPT, and no controlled Xeomin migraine data. Functional unblinding favours the active arm; early disclosure favours wins.
evidence: PREEMPT pooled analysis (Dodick et al., Headache 2010)
Cochrane review of botulinum toxins for migraine prevention, 2018

assumptions.claim: In PREEMPT 2, onabotulinumtoxinA reduced headache days by 9.0 versus 6.7 per 28 days with placebo at week 24 (p<0.001).
In PREEMPT 1 the primary endpoint (headache episodes) was not met, although headache days and migraine days were significantly reduced versus placebo.
In the pooled PREEMPT double-blind phase, 3.8% of onabotulinumtoxinA patients versus 1.2% of placebo patients discontinued because of adverse events.
assumptions.source: PREEMPT pooled analysis, Dodick et al., Headache 2010

reason: A multi-arm open-label phase 2 still recruiting four months before its registered primary completion date will probably run past it; no results posting is expected from this Chinese sponsor.
rationale: Open-label multi-arm phase 2 of a novel ADC at 17 Chinese sites, still recruiting four months before the registered primary completion date, with outcome windows of up to 24 months; such studies usually extend and add cohorts. Kelun rarely posts results on ClinicalTrials.gov. Early termination is possible if activity disappoints but unlikely within ten months. The loosely worded primary outcomes (ORR and PFS in specific arms) could be reshaped if arms change.
