reason: Enrolment is closed and the 24-week readout has passed, so the trial should complete; results are not due on ClinicalTrials.gov until about September 2027.
rationale: Enrolment is closed and the 24-week Gd-IgA1 readout has passed, so a stop is unlikely while atacicept's programme advances. Results are due about a year after primary completion (around September 2027) and small sponsors rarely post early, and a delay certificate is possible for a new dosing regimen, so posting by 31 August 2027 is unlikely. A single pharmacodynamic primary outcome leaves little reason to amend.

reason: The response criterion is undefined in the record; a strict composite or cautious echo-guided titration could shrink the gap, though myosin inhibitors have large, consistent effects in obstructive HCM.
rationale: Cardiac myosin inhibitors give large, consistent effects in obstructive HCM: mavacamten in EXPLORER-HCM (composite response 37% vs 17%; NYHA improvement 65% vs 31%) and EXPLORER-CN, aficamten in SEQUOIA-HCM. HRS-1893 is the same class and reached phase 3 after phase 2. With about 114 per arm, power exceeds 90% even for an EXPLORER-type composite; a gradient-plus-NYHA definition would give a far larger gap. The main uncertainty is the undefined response criterion and the titration scheme. Hengrui usually discloses pivotal success when an NDA is accepted.

assumptions.claim: In EXPLORER-HCM, 37% of mavacamten patients versus 17% of placebo patients met the composite primary endpoint (peak VO2 and NYHA class) at week 30.
In EXPLORER-HCM, 65% of mavacamten patients versus 31% of placebo patients improved by at least one NYHA class.
In SEQUOIA-HCM, aficamten improved KCCQ-CSS by about 7 points more than placebo at week 24.

reason: The KCCQ benefit in IMPROVE-HCM came from a post hoc subgroup, so the true effect may be 3-4 points against a needed observed gap of about 4.3 with a sizeable placebo improvement.
rationale: IMPROVE-HCM (n=67, 12 weeks) showed a significant VE/VCO2 slope benefit (-2.1) but no overall KCCQ-CSS difference (3.2 points, p=0.2); the 9.4-point gain came from a post hoc subgroup with baseline KCCQ-CSS of 80 or less. FORTITUDE enriches for limited patients, but the true effect is probably 3-5 points against a needed observed gap near 4.3 (SD about 14, 165 patients). Mavacamten missed KCCQ-CSS in non-obstructive HCM in ODYSSEY-HCM amid a large placebo response, and trimetazidine, a related metabolic modulator, failed in HCM.
evidence: Coats et al., JAMA Cardiol 2019 (trimetazidine in HCM)

assumptions.claim: In IMPROVE-HCM, ninerafaxstat improved VE/VCO2 slope versus placebo (least-squares mean difference -2.1, p=0.006).
In IMPROVE-HCM the overall KCCQ-CSS difference versus placebo was 3.2 points (p=0.2), and 9.4 points in the post hoc subgroup with baseline KCCQ-CSS of 80 or less.
In ODYSSEY-HCM, mavacamten did not significantly improve KCCQ-CSS or peak VO2 versus placebo in non-obstructive HCM.

reason: Dapagliflozin plus metformin already lowers HbA1c by about 1 point, leaving a DPP-4 inhibitor add-on effect of roughly 0.3-0.5 that must also beat the prusogliptin dual arm.
rationale: Adding a DPP-4 inhibitor to an SGLT2 inhibitor plus metformin reliably lowers HbA1c by 0.3-0.5 points: saxagliptin added to dapagliflozin/metformin (-0.35), saxagliptin plus dapagliflozin versus dapagliflozin on metformin (-0.27), empagliflozin/linagliptin versus empagliflozin (-0.4 to -0.6). Asian patients respond well to DPP-4 inhibitors and prusogliptin is approved in China. With about 163 per arm and SD near 0.9, power exceeds 90% for 0.35. The triple must also beat prusogliptin plus metformin, which SGLT2 add-on data support. Disclosure by a Chinese sponsor is the main uncertainty.

assumptions.claim: Saxagliptin added to dapagliflozin plus metformin lowered HbA1c by 0.51 versus 0.16 points with placebo at 24 weeks.
On metformin, saxagliptin plus dapagliflozin lowered HbA1c by 1.47 points versus 1.20 with dapagliflozin alone and 0.88 with saxagliptin alone at 24 weeks.
On metformin, empagliflozin 25 mg/linagliptin 5 mg lowered HbA1c by 1.19 points versus 0.62 with empagliflozin 25 mg alone at week 24.

reason: Twenty per arm, a mixed EBS population and a fluctuating photographic blister-area endpoint over 2 months make a statistically significant primary result unlikely even if the gel has some effect.
rationale: First controlled test of TolaSure in EBS, with 20 per arm, a mixed population (localized plantar disease and intermediate or severe subtypes), a fluctuating blister-area endpoint read from photographs and only 2 months of randomized treatment. No topical agent has shown a significant controlled benefit in EBS; diacerein's vehicle-controlled trial missed. Spontaneous variation and vehicle effects are large. Two-site enrolment in a rare disease will probably run late, and a small private sponsor may describe results as encouraging without a formal primary statement.
evidence: DELIVERS trial of diacerein 1% ointment in EBS (2018)

assumptions.claim: The vehicle-controlled DELIVERS trial of diacerein 1% ointment in epidermolysis bullosa simplex did not meet its primary endpoint.
assumptions.source: Castle Creek Pharmaceuticals DELIVERS phase 2 trial, results announced 2018

reason: A small single-centre cosmetic patch study is likely to finish somewhat late or leave its record stale, and is unlikely to post results.
rationale: Single-centre cosmetic-patch study run by a small Korean sponsor with an Italian CRO; the record is sparsely written and may not be kept current. Seventy-two patients with 3 months of treatment plus follow-up must all have enrolled by mid-2026 for a November 2026 completion, so slippage is plausible. Results posting is unlikely for a non-US cosmetic study, and the adverse-event primary outcome gives little reason for a substantive change.

reason: With about 69 per arm, two doses and two region-specific primaries (SALT 20 or less, and the stricter SALT 10 or less), a modest response in children with extensive loss could leave one analysis short.
rationale: Ritlecitinib 50 mg gave SALT 20 or less in 23% versus 2% with placebo at week 24 in ALLEGRO-2b/3 (ages 12 and over), with adolescents responding at least as well (about 25% vs 0%). Children 6-11 on exposure-matched dosing should respond similarly, and placebo regrowth is limited by excluding recent regrowth. With about 69 per arm, power for SALT 20 or less is above 90%, but the EU-plan primary (SALT 10 or less, about 13% vs 2% in ALLEGRO) and two-dose multiplicity lower the chance that everything reported as primary is met.
evidence: Hordinsky et al., Pediatr Dermatol 2023 (adolescent subgroup of ALLEGRO-2b/3)

assumptions.claim: In ALLEGRO-2b/3, 23% of patients on ritlecitinib 50 mg versus 2% on placebo had a SALT score of 20 or less at week 24.
Among adolescents aged 12-17 in ALLEGRO-2b/3, 25% on ritlecitinib 50 mg versus 0% on placebo had a SALT score of 20 or less at week 24.
In ALLEGRO-2b/3, a SALT score of 10 or less at week 24 was reached by about 13% on ritlecitinib 50 mg versus about 2% on placebo.

reason: The non-inferiority margin is not in the record; with 2:1 allocation and 252 patients, a 10-point margin leaves only moderate power unless HArmonyCa's month-6 responder rate is at least equal to Perlane's.
rationale: Evaluator-blinded filler trial against an approved HA filler; the hypothesis is presumably non-inferiority on month-6 MFVDS responders, as usual for NMPA registration. Both products should give roughly 80-85% responders at month 6, and the CaHA in HArmonyCa should help sustain volume. With 168 vs 84 patients, a 10-point margin gives only moderate power if the products are truly equal, so success depends on the unknown margin and on HArmonyCa doing at least as well. Large-company filler registration trials rarely fail.
evidence: Juvederm Voluma US pivotal midface trial (Jones and Murphy 2013)

assumptions.claim: Juvederm Voluma's US pivotal midface trial reported 85.6% MFVDS responders at month 6 versus 38.9% in untreated controls.
assumptions.source: Jones and Murphy, Dermatol Surg 2013 (Voluma pivotal trial)

assumptions.claim: Restylane Lyft's US midface trial reported about 89% MMVS responders at week 8 versus about 16% in untreated controls.
assumptions.source: Weiss et al., Dermatol Surg 2016 (Restylane Lyft midface trial)

reason: Selective TYK2 inhibition failed in ulcerative colitis with deucravacitinib, and a 120-patient trial split across dose groups may miss a moderate remission gain over placebo.
rationale: D-2570 is an allosteric TYK2 inhibitor that gave biologic-like PASI responses in psoriasis, suggesting deep IL-23/IL-12 pathway blockade, and IL-23 antibodies work in UC. Against that, deucravacitinib failed in UC, so selective TYK2 inhibition is unproven there. The trial is small (120 across placebo and probably two or more dose groups), so even a 15-20 point remission gain is only moderately powered against a placebo rate near 8%. Continuing from Part A into Part B suggests no early futility signal.

assumptions.claim: Deucravacitinib 6 mg twice daily did not beat placebo for week-12 clinical remission in LATTICE-UC (14.8% vs 16.3%).
D-2570 gave week-12 PASI 75 rates of about 85-90% versus 12.5% with placebo in its phase 2 psoriasis trial.

reason: An 81-patient, 12-week trial can only show a significant FVC difference if the observed gain is near 80 mL, and IL-11 blockade has no clinical proof in fibrosis yet.
rationale: First-in-patient phase 2a of BI 765423, which I take to be an anti-IL-11 antibody; the target has preclinical support only and no clinical proof in fibrosis. With 81 patients and a 12-week FVC change (SD about 170 mL), a nominally significant result needs an observed difference near 80 mL, larger than most antifibrotics show at 12 weeks. Placebo decline on background therapy should be roughly 50 mL. Boehringer may use a Bayesian criterion, which helps somewhat. Early public reporting by mid-2027 is unlikely.

assumptions.claim: In the phase 2 trial of BI 1015550, the median 12-week FVC change on placebo was -81.7 mL without and -59.2 mL with background antifibrotics.

reason: A shorter 8-week regimen may relapse more in genotype 3, cirrhotic or non-adherent patients, and a deficit of 2-3 points against SOF/VEL would breach a margin of about 5 points.
rationale: Phase 2 of BEM/RZR gave SVR12 of 98% in adherent and 95% in all evaluable patients, and DAA phase 2 results translate well. SOF/VEL should reach about 95-96% here. With about 440 per arm, the trial appears sized for a 5-point non-inferiority margin at 90% power assuming equal rates near 95%; it tolerates a true deficit of 1 point but not 3. The risks are relapse after the shorter 8-week course in genotype 3, cirrhotic or poorly adherent patients.

assumptions.claim: In phase 2, 8 weeks of BEM/RZR gave SVR12 of 98% in the per-protocol treatment-adherent population and 95% in the efficacy-evaluable population.
Sofosbuvir-velpatasvir for 12 weeks gave SVR12 of 99% in ASTRAL-1 and 95% in genotype 3 in ASTRAL-3.

reason: The primary analysis is limited to LA grade C/D patients, a fraction of the 523 enrolled, so a true 15-20 point healing gain over lansoprazole at week 4 could miss significance.
rationale: Potent acid blockers have consistently beaten lansoprazole on early healing of severe (LA C/D) oesophagitis: vonoprazan by about 18 points at week 2 and about 20 at week 8. Linaprazan glurate 50 mg twice daily gives strong 24-hour acid control, and phase 2 showed a large numerical gap in C/D. Lansoprazole should heal about 55-60% of C/D patients at week 4. The primary analysis uses only the C/D subset, perhaps 70-90 per arm, so a true gain of 15-20 points is only moderately powered, with two doses sharing alpha.

assumptions.claim: In PHALCON-EE, week-2 healing in LA grade C/D was 70.2% with vonoprazan versus 52.6% with lansoprazole.
In linaprazan glurate's phase 2 dose-finding study, 4-week healing in LA grade C/D reached about 89% in the best dose group versus 38% with lansoprazole.

reason: Two earlier phase 3 trials missed on SARA; the pooled 0.6-point advantage is smaller than the roughly 0.8-point difference this 142-patient trial needs to observe.
rationale: Rovatirelin missed the SARA primary endpoint in two earlier phase 3 trials; only a post hoc pooled analysis showed a 0.61-point advantage, and the Japanese filing based on it did not lead to approval. This third trial has 142 patients, so with a between-patient SD near 2.3 it needs an observed difference of about 0.8 points, more than the pooled estimate, which itself is likely inflated by selection. The placebo response on SARA was large before (about 1 point or more). Success requires a better-selected population giving a larger effect than seen so far.
evidence: KPS1301 and KPS1305 (Nishizawa et al., JNNP 2020)

assumptions.claim: Two phase 3 trials of rovatirelin (KPS1301, KPS1305) did not meet their SARA primary endpoints; a pooled analysis found a -0.61 point difference for 2.4 mg versus placebo (-1.64 vs -1.03, p=0.029).
assumptions.source: Nishizawa et al., J Neurol Neurosurg Psychiatry 2020

reason: Efficacy is hardly in doubt; the risk is that the trial, still recruiting at its registered completion date, has no mature 18-month PFS analysis and yields only an early or vague statement, or stops.
rationale: The design copies NETTER-1, where 177Lu-DOTATATE cut the hazard of progression by about 80% against high-dose octreotide (20-month PFS 65% vs 11%); NETTER-2 and other lutetium trials confirm a large effect. With 184 patients a true hazard ratio near 0.25 is detected almost surely. The uncertainty is operational: the trial was still recruiting weeks before its registered primary completion, so a result by mid-2027 would probably come from an interim analysis or a stop, and a vague or early statement would not count as met.

assumptions.claim: In NETTER-1, 177Lu-DOTATATE versus octreotide LAR 60 mg gave a hazard ratio for progression or death of 0.21, with 20-month PFS of 65.2% versus 10.8%.

reason: The drug effect is large and the trial well sized; failure would need a conduct problem such as heavy insulin rescue in the placebo arm, dropouts or a data-quality issue.
rationale: HRS9531 is a GLP-1/GIP dual agonist of the tirzepatide type with HbA1c falls above 2 points in Chinese phase 2. The design mirrors SURPASS-5, where tirzepatide added to basal insulin beat placebo by 1.2-1.5 points at week 40. With about 100 per arm and an SD near 1 point, a difference of that size is detected with near certainty. Failure would require an execution problem, not a weak drug. Hengrui may not publicise this supportive trial quickly.

assumptions.claim: In SURPASS-5, tirzepatide added to titrated insulin glargine lowered HbA1c by 2.11 to 2.40 points versus 0.86 with placebo at week 40.

reason: True difference should be near zero, so failure would come from chance or higher-than-assumed variability relative to the equivalence margins with only 278 patients.
rationale: QL1206 is an established denosumab biosimilar already studied in Chinese postmenopausal osteoporosis, so a true difference from Prolia in 12-month lumbar spine BMD gain should be near zero. With 278 patients and a between-patient SD of about 4 percentage points, the trial looks sized for roughly 90% power against margins near 2 points either side; tighter margins of 1.45 would cut power noticeably. Denosumab biosimilar equivalence trials have almost all succeeded. Qilu rarely publicises results quickly.
evidence: QL1206 phase 3 vs placebo in Chinese postmenopausal osteoporosis (2022)

assumptions.claim: In ROSALIA, biosimilar denosumab GP2411 met equivalence to reference denosumab on percent change in lumbar spine BMD at week 52 in 527 postmenopausal women.
assumptions.source: ROSALIA study, Jeka et al., J Bone Miner Res 2024

reason: High placebo response in a 61-site MDD trial could swamp a modest 1.5-2 point HAM-D effect typical of GABA-A modulators; six-week durability of effect is untested.
rationale: SPT-300 is an oral allopregnanolone prodrug with no prior efficacy data in depressed patients. The class is mixed in MDD: zuranolone beat placebo by only about 1.7 HAM-D points at day 15 and was not approved for MDD, and PRAX-114 failed. Six weeks of continuous dosing and HAM-D-17's sleep and anxiety items should help a sedating GABA-A modulator. With about 180 per arm and an SD near 7.5, a 2-point true effect gives roughly 65% power, and placebo response in multi-site MDD trials is high.

assumptions.claim: In WATERFALL, zuranolone 50 mg lowered HAMD-17 at day 15 by 14.1 points versus 12.3 with placebo, a difference of 1.7 points.
assumptions.source: Clayton et al., Am J Psychiatry 2023 (WATERFALL)

assumptions.claim: PRAX-114 did not separate from placebo on HAM-D-17 in the phase 2/3 Aria trial in major depressive disorder.
assumptions.source: Praxis Precision Medicines Aria study topline, 2022

reason: With about 20 patients per arm and an SPPB change SD near 1.6, only a difference of roughly 1.4 points would reach significance, more than any sarcopenia drug has shown over a placebo arm that also improves with exercise and nutrition advice.
rationale: Small dose-ranging phase 2 (about 20 per arm) from a small Korean biotech with no public efficacy data for AMC6156. No drug has convincingly improved SPPB in sarcopenia; placebo arms given exercise and nutrition advice improve about 0.5 points, and many entrants may sit near the SPPB ceiling. Detecting a difference needs roughly 1.4 points at this size. Three doses give some chance of one nominal win, and publication is more likely if positive, so I sit a little above the base rate.
evidence: Bimagrumab sarcopenia phase 2, Rooks et al. 2020

assumptions.claim: In the phase 2 trial of bimagrumab in older adults with sarcopenia, SPPB improved in both arms with no significant difference between bimagrumab and placebo.
assumptions.source: Rooks et al., JAMA Network Open 2020

assumptions.claim: The trial enrols 80 patients across three AMC6156 doses and placebo, about 20 per arm.

reason: Recruiting 87 cancer patients with adjustment disorder for psilocybin sessions at five Australian sites is slow and the sponsor is small, so the March 2027 primary completion is likely to slip by more than 90 days.
rationale: Small listed sponsor with limited cash running a three-arm psilocybin trial in cancer patients at five Australian sites. Eighty-seven patients were to be enrolled, treated and followed to week 10 within about 18 months of an October 2025 start; psychedelic-therapy trials in oncology recruit slowly, so the March 2027 primary completion will probably slip past June. Results posting on ClinicalTrials.gov by August 2027 is very unlikely. The mixed efficacy and safety primaries could be tidied, but substantive change is uncommon.

reason: A change in concentration, volume or hyaluronidase content could shift Cmax enough that its 90% interval leaves the equivalence bounds even if AUC passes.
rationale: Roche has completed the 12-week PK phase of a 193-patient parallel bioequivalence study, sized by a sponsor with extensive subcutaneous ocrelizumab PK data (OCARINA I and II). At about 96 per arm and inter-patient CV near 35%, the 90% interval is roughly plus or minus 8-9%, so success needs a true ratio within about 0.88-1.14 for both AUC and Cmax. Cmax is the more fragile parameter when the formulation changes. Formulation-bridging studies by large sponsors succeed in most cases, and failures are less likely to be publicised early.

assumptions.claim: OCARINA II met its primary endpoint: subcutaneous ocrelizumab 920 mg was non-inferior to intravenous 600 mg on AUC from day 1 to week 12.
The study enrols 193 patients in a two-arm parallel design, about 96 per formulation.

reason: Recruitment is closed in a short 50-patient PK/PD study, so it should complete on time, with results posting likely only after the read date.
rationale: Fifty-patient PK/PD study run by Galderma, already closed to recruitment with a 16-week treatment period, so the December 2026 primary completion looks achievable. Nemolizumab is approved for prurigo nodularis and atopic dermatitis and the study is short, so a stop is unlikely. Results are due 12 months after primary completion, which falls after the read date, and sponsors rarely post much earlier. Model-parameter primaries are unlikely to be changed.

reason: A more cautious icodec titration aimed at limiting hypoglycaemia in type 1 diabetes could leave HbA1c meaningfully higher than with glargine and push the interval past the non-inferiority margin.
rationale: ONWARDS 6 already showed non-inferior HbA1c for icodec in type 1 diabetes (difference 0.05, upper bound 0.23, margin 0.3) with 582 patients; ONWARDS 11 has 877, giving an interval half-width near 0.11. Failure needs an observed difference above about 0.18, plausible only if a more cautious icodec titration, meant to curb the excess hypoglycaemia seen before, costs real glycaemic control. Entry HbA1c of 7-10% and exclusion of hypoglycaemia-prone patients leave room to titrate. Novo should report headline results in spring 2027.

assumptions.claim: In ONWARDS 6 the estimated difference in HbA1c change at week 26, icodec minus degludec, was 0.05 %-points (95% CI -0.13 to 0.23), confirming non-inferiority at a 0.3 margin.
In ONWARDS 6 level 2 or 3 hypoglycaemia was more frequent with icodec than degludec (about 19.9 versus 10.4 events per patient-year).
In ONWARDS 6 mean HbA1c fell by about 0.5 %-points in both arms from a baseline near 7.6% at week 26.

reason: With roughly 40 patients per arm, a true remission gain of 15-20 points over placebo can easily miss significance, especially if placebo remission in largely biologic-naive Russian patients runs above 10%.
rationale: TL1A blockade is validated in ulcerative colitis by tulisokibart, duvakitug and afimkibart, with placebo-adjusted remission of roughly 15-27 points at weeks 12-14. BCD-261 is an unproven antibody, but Biocad has delivered follow-on biologics before, and Russian patients are largely advanced-therapy naive. At about 40 per arm a 20-point gain has only around 60% power per dose; several regimens against placebo raise the chance that one wins. A readout by mid-2027 is uncertain since the record still shows recruiting, and Biocad mostly publicises positive results.

assumptions.claim: In ARTEMIS-UC cohort 1, clinical remission at week 12 was 26% with tulisokibart versus 1% with placebo.
In RELIEVE UCCD, clinical remission at week 14 in ulcerative colitis was 36.2% and 47.8% with duvakitug 450 mg and 900 mg versus 20.45% with placebo.

reason: Dapagliflozin may lower HbA1c by about 1 point in Chinese patients with baseline near 8.5%, so HDM1002 must deliver orforglipron-like potency to show a clear advantage.
rationale: HDM1002 is an oral small-molecule GLP-1 agonist, and the design copies ACHIEVE-2, where orforglipron beat dapagliflozin on HbA1c at week 40 by 0.5-0.9 points. With 200 per arm and SD near 1.0, the standard error is about 0.1, so any true advantage of 0.3 or more wins, and one of three doses suffices. Risks are a weaker molecule than orforglipron, a strong dapagliflozin response in Chinese patients with baseline near 8.5%, and gastrointestinal dropouts. Huadong advanced to phase 3 after its own phase 2 diabetes data.
evidence: Yang et al., dapagliflozin add-on to metformin in Asian patients, 2016

assumptions.claim: In ACHIEVE-2, orforglipron lowered HbA1c by about 1.3 to 1.7 %-points at week 40 versus about 0.8 with dapagliflozin in adults on metformin.
Dapagliflozin 10 mg added to metformin lowered HbA1c by about 0.85 %-points at 24 weeks in Asian, mostly Chinese, patients, versus about 0.23 with placebo.
assumptions.source: Yang et al., Diabetes Obes Metab 2016

reason: Thirty patients randomized 2:1 with short follow-up cannot show a significant progression-free survival difference unless the hazard ratio is near 0.35 or lower.
rationale: Thirty patients randomized 2:1 give almost no power for progression-free survival: significance would need a hazard ratio near 0.35 or lower, and follow-up from a September 2025 start is short for first-line pazopanib, whose median is 8-11 months. IBR854 is an early-stage cell therapy with no randomized evidence. The study reads as exploratory, with no stated hypothesis, so any report will probably describe response rates and trends, which the round counts as not met.

assumptions.claim: Median progression-free survival with first-line pazopanib in COMPARZ was 8.4 months.
The trial plans 30 patients randomized 2:1 to IBR854 plus pazopanib or pazopanib alone.

reason: Eighty patients spread over several infection types and three primary outcomes leave each comparison far too small for significance, and best available therapy with ceftazidime-avibactam is effective.
rationale: This is a small pathogen-directed trial against best available therapy, modelled on TANGO II, with 80 patients split across urinary, pneumonia, bloodstream and abdominal infections and three separate primary outcomes. Such trials are descriptive: none of the subsets is large enough for a significance test, and the round requires all co-primaries to be met. Best available therapy in China now often includes ceftazidime-avibactam, active against the dominant KPC producers, so a large margin is unlikely. A publication by mid-2027 is also unlikely.

assumptions.claim: In TANGO II, clinical cure at test of cure among 47 patients with confirmed CRE infection was 59.4% with meropenem-vaborbactam versus 26.7% with best available therapy.
assumptions.source: TANGO II, Wunderink et al., Infect Dis Ther 2018

assumptions.claim: The trial enrols 80 patients across five infection types with three separate primary outcomes.

reason: Failure would need viral breakthrough from capsid-inhibitor resistance or poor adherence to erase a suppression advantage that phase 2 showed to be large.
rationale: Capsid assembly modulators added to nucleos(t)ide analogues reliably deepen HBV DNA suppression (vebicorvir, bersacapavir), and GST-HG141's phase 2 in low-level viraemia showed a large gain in DNA below the quantification limit. Patients still viraemic after more than a year on an analogue rarely clear on continued therapy, so the placebo rate should stay near 15-20%. With 263 per arm the trial is overpowered for any gain above 15 points. Remaining risks are resistance-driven breakthrough and how the vague 48-week endpoint is analysed.

assumptions.claim: In its phase 2 add-on trial in nucleos(t)ide-treated patients with low-level viraemia, GST-HG141 gave a much higher rate of HBV DNA below the quantification limit at week 24 than placebo.
assumptions.source: GST-HG141 phase 2 in low-level viraemia, reported 2024

assumptions.claim: Vebicorvir added to entecavir produced a greater HBV DNA decline at week 24 than entecavir alone in treatment-naive HBeAg-positive patients.
assumptions.source: Sulkowski et al., J Hepatol 2022 (vebicorvir Study 202)

reason: Failure would need an underpowered multi-arm split (171 may be three arms of 57) combined with an unusually weak HbA1c response; the class effect on this background is consistent at about -0.7 points.
rationale: SGLT2 inhibitors added to metformin plus a DPP-4 inhibitor lower HbA1c by 0.6-0.9 points versus placebo at 24 weeks (empagliflozin with linagliptin and metformin, ertugliflozin with sitagliptin and metformin, Korean ipragliflozin trial). Enrolment of 171 looks like three arms of 57 (two empagliflozin doses and placebo), sized for a 0.5-point difference with SD 0.9; even then the expected z-score exceeds 4. Failure would need a conduct problem. A public result by mid-2027 is unlikely for a Korean registration study of a combination product.
evidence: Softeland et al. 2017, Diabetes Care (empagliflozin added to linagliptin and metformin)
Han et al. 2018 (ipragliflozin added to metformin and sitagliptin, Korea)

assumptions.claim: Empagliflozin 10 mg and 25 mg added to linagliptin and metformin lowered HbA1c by 0.79 and 0.70 percentage points more than placebo at week 24.
Ertugliflozin 5 mg and 15 mg added to metformin and sitagliptin lowered HbA1c by 0.69 and 0.76 points more than placebo at week 26, with a placebo change of -0.09.
Ipragliflozin added to metformin plus sitagliptin in Korean patients lowered HbA1c by about 0.8 points more than placebo at week 24.
assumptions.source: Han et al., Diabetes Obes Metab 2018

reason: Rare-disease crossover with 29 weeks per patient and still recruiting three months before the registered completion date, so primary completion will probably slip past April 2027; no results posting expected by August 2027.
rationale: Crossover study in a rare, genetically confirmed disease: 24 patients, each followed about 29 weeks, one listed Belgian site, still recruiting three months before the registered primary completion of January 2027. For that date the last patient had to start by about June 2026, so a slip beyond April 2027 is more likely than not. Lupin is an industry sponsor with no US site here; results posting within months of completion is rare. Eight loosely worded safety primaries leave some room for edits.

reason: The exact target and potency of HRS-7249 are not public, so the main way to miss is a weaker triglyceride drop than other siRNAs in a dose arm of only about 45-55 patients with a noisy endpoint.
rationale: HRS-7249 appears to be Hengrui's injectable siRNA for hypertriglyceridaemia (probably APOC3-directed; I cannot confirm the target). The primary endpoint is triglycerides after about 24 weeks of treatment. APOC3 and ANGPTL3 siRNAs lowered triglycerides 50-60% more than placebo in phase 2 (SHASTA-2, MUIR, ARCHES-2) with about 50 patients per arm, so a 224-patient dose-ranging trial should show a clear drop at the top dose. Uncertainties are target, potency, and whether Hengrui reports before mid-2027; a phase 3 start in 2027 is plausible.

assumptions.claim: Plozasiran lowered triglycerides by about 50%, 56% and 62% more than placebo at week 24 at 10, 25 and 50 mg in mixed hyperlipidaemia.
Zodasiran lowered triglycerides by 51%, 57% and 63% more than placebo at week 24.
Plozasiran lowered triglycerides by up to 57% more than placebo at week 24 in severe hypertriglyceridaemia.
assumptions.source: SHASTA-2, Gaudet et al., JAMA Cardiol 2024

reason: No human data show that S-pindolol preserves lean mass during GLP-1 weight loss; the anabolic signal comes from cancer cachexia, and with about 40 per arm it must prevent roughly a third of the lean loss.
rationale: S-pindolol increased weight and lean mass in cancer cachexia at 10 mg twice daily (ACT-ONE), but nothing in humans shows it preserves lean mass during GLP-1 weight loss, where I expect about 0.6 kg of lean loss per 4 weeks. With roughly 40 patients per arm and a between-patient SD near 400 g per 4 weeks, the drug must prevent about a third of that loss to reach significance. Beta-blockade may also blunt fat loss. A second primary outcome after semaglutide withdrawal adds a hurdle.

assumptions.claim: Espindolol 10 mg twice daily gave a weight slope of +0.54 kg per 4 weeks versus -0.21 kg per 4 weeks on placebo in cancer cachexia.
assumptions.source: ACT-ONE, Stewart Coats et al., J Cachexia Sarcopenia Muscle 2016

assumptions.claim: About 39% of the weight lost on semaglutide 2.4 mg was lean mass in the DXA substudy.
Enobosarm 3 mg cut lean mass loss by 71% versus placebo over 16 weeks of semaglutide, the placebo arm losing 4.1% of lean mass.

reason: Statin initiation after ACS lowers LDL-C sharply in the placebo arm too, which narrows the percentage-point gap, but not nearly enough to threaten significance; only conduct problems could.
rationale: Inclisiran lowers LDL-C by about 50% versus placebo on top of statins (ORION-10/11) and by 44 points versus usual care after ACS (VICTORION-INCEPTION). In hospital-start ACS trials the placebo arm also falls as statins are begun (EVOPACS placebo -35%), so the percentage-point gap shrinks to about 35, but with 300 patients and an SD near 30 the test is overwhelmingly powered. Only an operational failure could miss. Primary completion is February 2027, so a public result by June 2027 is doubtful; ESC or AHA 2027 is likelier.

assumptions.claim: Inclisiran lowered LDL-C by 52.3% and 49.9% more than placebo at day 510.
assumptions.source: ORION-10 and ORION-11, Ray et al., NEJM 2020

assumptions.claim: In hospital-start ACS patients LDL-C fell 35.4% on placebo plus atorvastatin 40 mg and 77.1% with evolocumab at week 8.
After recent ACS, LDL-C fell 47.5% with inclisiran added to usual care versus 3.5% with usual care alone at day 330.

reason: BFB759 has no published phase 2 efficacy in atopic dermatitis; if its targets lie outside the IL-4/IL-13, OX40 or IL-31 axes, the top dose may not separate from a placebo arm improving EASI by 35-40%.
rationale: I cannot confirm BFB759's targets from memory; I believe it is an antibody also being tested in hidradenitis suppurativa. Phase 2 atopic dermatitis trials of antibodies on the IL-4/IL-13, OX40 or IL-31 axes nearly always beat placebo on EASI, while those on IL-17, IL-23, IL-33, IL-36 or IL-1 mostly failed. A 225-patient, 88-site dose-ranging trial implies backing, but no phase 2a efficacy in this disease is public. Placebo EASI falls of 30-45% are common. A private sponsor is likelier to announce a positive result quickly.

assumptions.claim: Placebo patients improved EASI by 29.4% at week 16 versus 61.5% on the best amlitelimab dose.
Dupilumab 300 mg every 2 weeks improved EASI by 68% versus 18% on placebo at week 16 in phase 2b.

reason: Still recruiting two months before the registered primary completion with a staged three-dose design, so completion is likely to move into mid-2027 or later; results posting on ClinicalTrials.gov is very unlikely.
rationale: Open-label dose-optimisation study of a PD-L1 antibody-drug conjugate in pretreated colorectal cancer, 60 patients, with a planned pause after five patients per dose. It started in September 2025 and was still recruiting in late October 2026 against a primary completion of 30 December 2026, which leaves no room for response follow-up, so a delay is likely if the record is updated. Henlius rarely posts results on ClinicalTrials.gov. Weak activity in colorectal cancer could lead to early closure.

reason: Four co-primaries (NPS and congestion, overall and eosinophilic) must all hold, and a large non-eosinophilic share in Chinese patients could dilute the overall-population effect of TSLP blockade.
rationale: TQC2731 is Chia Tai Tianqing's anti-TSLP antibody (bosakitug, licensed from Biosion). TSLP blockade with tezepelumab cut NPS by 2.07 and congestion by 1.03 versus placebo (WAYPOINT), and stapokibart cut NPS by 2.3 in a Chinese phase 3 with the same overall-plus-eosinophilic co-primary structure. With 246 patients power is high even at half of tezepelumab's effect. Risks are four co-primaries, more non-eosinophilic disease in China and lower potency. Enrolment is complete, but a public result before June 2027 is unlikely.

assumptions.claim: Tezepelumab reduced the nasal polyp score by 2.07 and the nasal congestion score by 1.03 more than placebo at week 52.
Stapokibart reduced the nasal polyp score by 2.3 more than placebo at week 24 in a Chinese phase 3 (-2.6 versus -0.3).
TQC2731 is the same anti-TSLP antibody as bosakitug (BSI-045B), licensed by Biosion to Chia Tai Tianqing for Greater China.

reason: Spontaneous resolution by day 28 can push placebo clinical cure to 35-45%, leaving boric acid, never tested against placebo under the strict cure definition, with too small a margin in about 80 culture-confirmed patients per arm.
rationale: Boric acid 600 mg has antifungal activity and cured 92% versus 64% with nystatin in a 1981 double-blind study, but it has never been tested against placebo under the strict clinical cure definition. Placebo cure was 29% and 44% in the two ibrexafungerp VANISH trials at day 8-14 and may be higher by day 28. I expect about 54% versus 35%; with about 80 culture-confirmed patients per arm that gives roughly 70% power, with two regimens to test. A private consumer company is likelier to publicise a positive result.
evidence: Van Slyke et al. 1981 (boric acid versus nystatin)

assumptions.claim: Clinical cure at the test-of-cure visit was 50.5% with ibrexafungerp versus 28.6% with placebo.
Clinical cure at the test-of-cure visit was 63.3% with ibrexafungerp versus 44.0% with placebo.
Boric acid 600 mg daily for 14 days cured 92% of patients at 7-10 days after treatment versus 64% with nystatin.
assumptions.source: Van Slyke et al., Am J Obstet Gynecol 1981

reason: Complete clearing of corneal staining is a strict binary endpoint and 40 patients per arm need a gap above about 20 points over a lubricating vehicle, which dry eye drugs rarely achieve in 28 days.
rationale: rhPRG4 (lubricin) improved signs and symptoms versus hyaluronate in a 39-patient study (Lambiase 2017), but Novartis, which licensed it as ECF843, did not take it forward after its own phase 2. The primary is strict: complete clearing of corneal staining at day 28 in Sjogren's patients with baseline Oxford grade 1-2. With 40 per arm the gap must exceed about 20 points, and the vehicle itself lubricates. Dry eye sign endpoints often fail at this size, and a small private sponsor may not report by mid-2027.
evidence: Lambiase et al. 2017 (rhPRG4 versus sodium hyaluronate)
Novartis ECF843 phase 2 dry eye trial 2020-2021

assumptions.claim: rhPRG4 150 ug/mL improved symptoms and corneal staining more than 0.18% sodium hyaluronate over 2 weeks in 39 patients with moderate dry eye.
Novartis in-licensed rhPRG4 as ECF843 for dry eye in 2017.

reason: Fifteen crossover patients must show significance on both corneal staining and total symptom VAS against a lubricating vehicle; vehicle responses in dry eye are large, and a larger vehicle-controlled dry-eye programme of rhPRG4 was not taken forward.
rationale: Two co-primary endpoints (Oxford corneal staining and total symptom VAS) must both reach significance in a 15-patient crossover with only a 14-day washout and a lubricating vehicle as comparator. Vehicle effects in dry eye are substantial and ocular GVHD is refractory. Early lubricin data against hyaluronate were encouraging, but the larger vehicle-controlled ECF843 programme was not advanced. A small Australian sponsor is unlikely to publicise a result by mid-2027; if it does, it is more likely a favourable one, which lifts the conditional probability slightly.
evidence: Lambiase 2017 recombinant human lubricin vs sodium hyaluronate in dry eye (Ocular Surface)
Novartis ECF843 (rhPRG4) vs vehicle phase 2 in dry eye disease, 2020-2021

assumptions.claim: A randomized trial of 150 ug/mL recombinant human lubricin versus 0.18% sodium hyaluronate eye drops in about 40 patients with moderate dry eye reported significantly greater improvement in symptoms and several signs with lubricin after 2 weeks.
Novartis tested rhPRG4 (ECF843) against vehicle in a phase 2 trial in dry eye disease and did not take it into phase 3.
assumptions.source: Novartis ECF843 phase 2 dry eye trial, 2020-2021

reason: Small Chinese multiple-ascending-dose study in IPF still recruiting two months before its registered completion, with adverse events followed for about a year; a completion date slipping past March 2027 is more likely than not, and results posting on ClinicalTrials.gov is very unlikely.
rationale: Forty-eight IPF patients in ascending-dose cohorts across 12 Chinese sites, started November 2025, with adverse events followed for about a year: the registered December 2026 completion looks optimistic while the record still shows recruiting in late October 2026. Sequential cohorts with safety reviews usually stretch timelines. Early-phase Chinese biotech studies are rarely terminated formally, almost never post results on ClinicalTrials.gov, and a single safety primary outcome is seldom changed in substance.

reason: If the trial tests superiority on both iPTH responder thresholds, a well-titrated double-dummy cinacalcet arm could leave a gap of about 10 points that 212 patients per arm detect only part of the time; non-inferiority would be met comfortably.
rationale: MT1013 appears to be an injectable calcimimetic-type peptide given at dialysis (hence double-dummy), so adherence is assured, as with etelcalcetide, which beat oral cinacalcet on both the >30% and >50% PTH-reduction endpoints (68% vs 58%; 52% vs 40%). Cinacalcet is capped at 100 mg in China, which helps the comparison. The record gives neither hypothesis nor margin: non-inferiority looks very likely to be met, superiority on both primaries roughly even odds with 424 patients. Chinese active-controlled registration trials following a phase 2 usually succeed, and early announcements skew positive.
evidence: Evocalcet vs cinacalcet East Asian phase 3 (2023)

assumptions.claim: In the head-to-head trial of etelcalcetide versus cinacalcet in haemodialysis patients, 52.4% on etelcalcetide and 40.2% on cinacalcet had a more than 50% reduction in PTH over weeks 20-27.
In the same trial a more than 30% PTH reduction was reached by 68.2% on etelcalcetide and 57.7% on cinacalcet.

reason: With about 85 patients per arm the pCR gap over pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy must reach roughly 14 points for nominal significance, and the phase 2 may not carry a formal superiority hypothesis at all.
rationale: Pembrolizumab plus platinum-pemetrexed should give a pCR near 20% in EGFR/ALK-negative non-squamous disease (KEYNOTE-671 18% overall, lower in non-squamous; Chinese PD-1 trials somewhat higher). IBI363, a PD-1/IL-2 alpha-biased fusion protein, has shown responses in PD-1-refractory NSCLC, weaker in adenocarcinoma than squamous, so a gain of around 10 points is plausible but unproven in immunotherapy-naive patients. With 170 patients that is borderline for significance, and IL-2-type toxicity could cost surgeries. An early congress presentation would favour a positive readout.

assumptions.claim: In KEYNOTE-671, pathological complete response was 18.1% with perioperative pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy versus 4.0% with chemotherapy alone.
In CheckMate 816, pathological complete response was 24.0% with neoadjuvant nivolumab plus chemotherapy versus 2.2% with chemotherapy alone.

reason: Failure would need bromocriptine to normalise prolactin nearly as often as cabergoline over 14 weeks, or heavy dropout; both are unlikely given the consistent historical advantage of cabergoline in efficacy and tolerability.
rationale: Cabergoline has beaten bromocriptine in every sizeable comparison: in Webster 1994 prolactin normalised in 83% versus 59% of women, with fewer discontinuations for intolerance (3% vs 12%), and meta-analyses agree. This Chinese registration study of a cabergoline tablet enrols a similar population of women aged 18-45 for 14 weeks with double-dummy dosing. A sample of 382 points to a non-inferiority design with a conservative margin, which a 15-25 point advantage clears easily; even superiority would very likely be met. The residual risk is operational.
evidence: Webster 1994 cabergoline vs bromocriptine in hyperprolactinemic amenorrhea (NEJM)
dos Santos Nunes 2011 meta-analysis of cabergoline vs bromocriptine

assumptions.claim: In 459 women with hyperprolactinemic amenorrhea, serum prolactin normalised in 83% of those given cabergoline and 59% of those given bromocriptine.
In the same trial 3% of women on cabergoline and 12% on bromocriptine stopped treatment because of drug intolerance.

reason: Tranexamic acid is already a highly effective antifibrinolytic, so a new agent is unlikely to show significantly less blood loss; success depends on whether the phase 2 defines its objective as non-inferiority or comparability rather than superiority.
rationale: Intravenous tranexamic acid cuts total blood loss after knee replacement to roughly 700-900 mL by the Gross formula, with a between-patient SD near 300 mL, leaving little room for a new haemostatic to do better; with 90 per arm a significant gain would need about 90 mL less loss. The record states no hypothesis. If the dose-ranging phase 2 tests non-inferiority or simply comparability, the high dose probably passes; if superiority, it probably fails. I weight the two about equally, and a result is unlikely to be public by mid-2027.
evidence: Fillingham 2018 network meta-analysis of tranexamic acid in total knee arthroplasty
Xie 2016 multiple-dose intravenous tranexamic acid in total knee arthroplasty

assumptions.claim: Tranexamic acid significantly reduces blood loss and transfusion in primary total knee arthroplasty compared with placebo, and no formulation or dosing regimen was clearly superior to the others.

reason: The only real threat is the short 24-week window for a strict target-not-detected endpoint after switching from bulevirtide; even a response rate of 25-30% would still clear a continued-bulevirtide arm expected to stay in single digits.
rationale: In SOLSTICE, monthly tobevibart plus elebsiran produced HDV RNA target-not-detected in about 41% at week 24 and 66% at week 48. Patients still viraemic (500 IU/mL or more) after at least 24 weeks of bulevirtide 2 mg rarely become undetectable over a further 24 weeks (MYR301: 12% undetectable at week 48 overall), so the control rate should be a few percent. With about 75 per arm a 40-point gap is overwhelmingly significant. Vir has guided to topline data around the first quarter of 2027.
evidence: SOLSTICE phase 2 of tobevibart plus elebsiran in chronic hepatitis D (week 24 data 2024, week 48 data 2025)

assumptions.claim: In SOLSTICE, about 41% of participants on monthly tobevibart plus elebsiran had HDV RNA target not detected at week 24, rising to about 66% at week 48.
In MYR301, 12% of patients on bulevirtide 2 mg had undetectable HDV RNA at week 48.

reason: A topical JAK inhibitor may clear anterior chamber cells somewhat less than intensive prednisolone acetate; a shortfall of 0.2-0.3 grade would threaten a typical 0.5-grade non-inferiority margin with 77 patients per arm, and superiority is out of reach.
rationale: Prednisolone acetate 1% lowers anterior chamber cell grade by about 1.9 at day 14 in comparable trials (difluprednate studies), a high bar. The record gives no hypothesis; a single-masked active-controlled pivotal study almost certainly tests non-inferiority, probably with a margin near 0.5 grade as in the difluprednate programme. VVN461, a topical JAK1/TYK2 inhibitor, reportedly performed similarly to steroid in its US phase 2, which motivated this design. If truly within 0.1-0.15 grade, 154 patients give good power; a larger shortfall fails. Superiority over steroid is implausible.
evidence: Foster 2010 difluprednate vs prednisolone acetate in endogenous anterior uveitis
Sheppard 2014 difluprednate vs prednisolone acetate in anterior uveitis
Loteprednol etabonate vs prednisolone acetate in acute anterior uveitis (1999)
VVN461 US phase 2 in non-infectious anterior uveitis

assumptions.claim: In endogenous anterior uveitis, mean anterior chamber cell grade at day 14 fell by about 2.1 with difluprednate 0.05% and about 1.9 with prednisolone acetate 1%, with non-inferiority judged against a 0.5-grade margin.
assumptions.source: Foster et al., J Ocul Pharmacol Ther 2010

reason: Trough office systolic pressure at 4 weeks demands a sustained effect; the drug appears to act through the nitric oxide-cGMP pathway, where reductions are modest, and 70 per arm needs about a 4.5 mmHg placebo-adjusted fall for significance.
rationale: The exclusion of nitrates, alpha-blockers and PDE5 inhibitors suggests RTN-001 works through the nitric oxide-cGMP pathway, probably a modified-release PDE5 inhibitor. Sildenafil three times daily lowered ambulatory pressure by about 8/6 mmHg in untreated hypertension, so a pre-dose placebo-adjusted office effect of 4-7 mmHg on top of 2-5 drugs is plausible. With about 70 per arm, an SD near 13-14 mmHg and placebo falls of 5-9 mmHg, power is 45-75%; three doses give more than one chance but need multiplicity control. Roughly even odds.

assumptions.claim: Sildenafil 50 mg three times daily lowered ambulatory blood pressure by about 8/6 mmHg versus placebo in untreated hypertensive patients.
In BrigHTN, seated systolic blood pressure fell by 9.4 mmHg on placebo over 12 weeks in patients with treatment-resistant hypertension.

reason: Failure would require the combination to fall far short of its phase 2 clearance rate while bulevirtide overperforms, or substantial dropout in the open-label combination arm counted as non-response.
rationale: SOLSTICE showed HDV RNA target-not-detected in about 66% of patients at week 48 on monthly tobevibart plus elebsiran, whereas bulevirtide 2 mg gave undetectable HDV RNA in only 12% at week 48 in MYR301. A 45-55 point gap makes even 100 patients more than enough for significance. The open-label design matters little for a laboratory endpoint. Enrolment is complete, the week-48 timepoint falls around the turn of 2026-27, and Vir has guided to topline data in early 2027.
evidence: SOLSTICE phase 2 of tobevibart plus elebsiran in chronic hepatitis D (week 48 data 2025)

assumptions.claim: In SOLSTICE, about 66% of participants on monthly tobevibart plus elebsiran had HDV RNA target not detected at week 48.
In MYR301, 12% of patients on bulevirtide 2 mg had undetectable HDV RNA at week 48.

reason: Only about 40 patients per arm: if the reformulated product with short incubation clears all lesions in only 25-30% of patients, as in the 2016 short-incubation study, a single-arm comparison could miss significance despite low vehicle clearance.
rationale: ALA blue-light PDT is an established AK treatment: the original Levulan trials gave about 73% versus 8% complete clearance at week 12, and short-incubation broad-area use still beat vehicle. Restricting to 4-8 lesions in a 25 cm2 field should raise complete clearance. Vehicle-PDT clearance on face and scalp is low (about 5-15%), so 40 per arm still gives good power, and two incubation arms give two chances. Residual risks are the small arms and an unknown reformulation. Sun rarely publicises such results quickly.
evidence: Piacquadio et al., Arch Dermatol 2004 (Levulan Kerastick phase 3)
Pariser et al., Dermatol Surg 2016 (short-incubation ALA-PDT, face/scalp)
Jiang et al., Dermatol Surg 2019 (ALA-PDT upper extremities phase 3)
Reinhold et al., Br J Dermatol 2016 (BF-200 ALA field-directed PDT)

assumptions.claim: In the original Levulan Kerastick phase 3 trials on face and scalp with blue light, complete response at week 12 was about 73% with ALA versus about 8% with vehicle.
With 1-3 hour broad-area incubation on the face or scalp, median AK lesion clearance at week 12 was 68-79% with ALA-PDT versus 7% with vehicle-PDT.
In field-directed BF-200 ALA PDT of patients with 4-8 face or scalp lesions, complete clearance with vehicle was about 22%.
assumptions.source: Reinhold et al., Br J Dermatol 2016

reason: The reformulated ALA would have to perform clearly worse than the original on the arms, where complete clearance was only 31% versus 13% for vehicle, for a 260-patient trial to miss.
rationale: The earlier DUSA phase 3 at the same site with a near-identical design (ALA 20%, blue light, up to two sessions, week-12 complete clearance) was clearly positive: 31% versus 13% with about 135 per arm. This trial has 130 per arm and fewer lesions per patient (4-8), which should raise clearance. Risks are a weaker reformulation or a higher vehicle response on the arms. Sun is unlikely to announce results before late 2027.
evidence: Jiang et al., Dermatol Surg 2019 (ALA-PDT upper extremities phase 3)
Pariser et al., Dermatol Surg 2016 (short-incubation ALA-PDT, face/scalp)
Piacquadio et al., Arch Dermatol 2004 (Levulan Kerastick phase 3)

assumptions.claim: In the earlier phase 3 of ALA 20% blue-light PDT on the upper extremities, complete clearance at week 12 was 31% with ALA versus 13% with vehicle.
In the same trial the mean AK lesion clearance rate at week 12 was about 80% with ALA versus about 46% with vehicle.

reason: Both first-dose and cycle-7 AUC must fall within the equivalence bounds in about 146 patients with 30-40% PK variability and dropouts before steady state, so a wide interval or a small true exposure difference could fail one co-primary.
rationale: PK-similarity studies of monoclonal antibody biosimilars usually succeed once analytical similarity is established, and Qilu has taken biosimilars through approval before. 146 patients give reasonable power for 80-125% bounds given pembrolizumab exposure variability of roughly 30-40% CV, but both first-dose and steady-state AUC must pass, and dropouts before cycle 7 shrink the steady-state sample. Patient PK is noisier than healthy-volunteer PK. Qilu rarely publicises results quickly, so a public statement by mid-2027 is unlikely.
evidence: Ahamadi et al., CPT Pharmacometrics Syst Pharmacol 2017 (pembrolizumab population PK)

assumptions.claim: Between-patient variability of pembrolizumab clearance is moderate, with a coefficient of variation of roughly 30-40% in population PK analyses.
assumptions.source: Ahamadi et al., CPT Pharmacometrics Syst Pharmacol 2017

reason: With 48 patients and a UAS7 change SD near 12, only an effect of 8-10 points reaches significance, more than TSLP or IL-13 pathway blockade has shown by week 16 in CSU.
rationale: CM512 (TSLP and IL-13 bispecific) has no CSU data. TSLP blockade alone (tezepelumab, INCEPTION) missed UAS7 at week 16, while IL-4 receptor blockade (dupilumab) gave about 8.5 points at week 24 with slow onset, so a week-16 effect near 4-6 points is plausible. With 48 patients and a UAS7 change SD around 12, only an effect near 8-10 points reaches significance. Placebo responses in CSU trials are large (about 10-13 points). Small phase 2 results may be reported only descriptively.

assumptions.claim: Tezepelumab did not significantly improve UAS7 versus placebo at week 16 in the phase 2b INCEPTION trial in CSU.
Dupilumab reduced UAS7 at week 24 by about 8.5 points more than placebo in omalizumab-naive CSU (about -20.5 versus -12.0).
assumptions.source: LIBERTY-CSU CUPID Study A, Maurer et al., J Allergy Clin Immunol 2024

reason: KLK5/7 inhibition is clinically unproven in atopic dermatitis and a systemic antibody may not change skin inflammation enough within 16 weeks to beat a 15-25% placebo response.
rationale: TRIV-509 (anti-KLK5/7 antibody) is a first-in-class barrier-targeted approach with no earlier controlled efficacy data in AD; novel non-type-2 mechanisms in AD have failed more often than not. About 48 per arm gives good power only for a dupilumab-like effect (25 points or more on EASI-75) against placebo rates of 15-25%. A private sponsor is more likely to announce a positive topline than a negative one, which raises the conditional probability slightly. The record does not define the primary response criterion.

assumptions.claim: Placebo EASI-75 at week 16 was about 15% and 12% in the dupilumab SOLO 1 and SOLO 2 monotherapy trials.
assumptions.source: Simpson et al., N Engl J Med 2016

assumptions.claim: TRIV-509 is a monoclonal antibody that inhibits kallikreins 5 and 7 and had no controlled efficacy data in atopic dermatitis before this study.

reason: Ciclosporin emulsion is an effective comparator, so a 4-week difference in corneal staining is likely to be small (about 0.2-0.3 grade) relative to the 0.4 grade needed for superiority with 60 per arm.
rationale: Active-controlled comparison against ciclosporin emulsion, an effective approved VKC therapy, with a 4-week corneal staining endpoint. T1695's composition is not public; if it is a calcineurin inhibitor or steroid suspension, small head-to-head studies suggest similar or modestly better sign improvement than ciclosporin, which 60 per arm would detect only if the difference is about 0.4 grade or more. The record does not say whether the hypothesis is superiority or non-inferiority; non-inferiority would be much easier. Thea rarely publishes quickly.
evidence: VEKTIS (ciclosporin cationic emulsion in severe VKC) 2019
Ohashi et al., J Ocul Pharmacol Ther 2010 (tacrolimus 0.1% ophthalmic suspension)
Labcharoenwongs et al., Asian Pac J Allergy Immunol 2012 (tacrolimus vs ciclosporin in VKC)

assumptions.claim: Ciclosporin 0.1% cationic emulsion four times daily improved corneal fluorescein staining versus vehicle over 4 months in children with severe VKC.
A double-masked comparison of 0.1% tacrolimus ointment with 2% ciclosporin eye drops in VKC found no significant difference in clinical improvement.
assumptions.source: Labcharoenwongs et al., Asian Pac J Allergy Immunol 2012

reason: On top of guideline triple or quadruple antiemetic prophylaxis the control delayed complete response is already about 65-70%, leaving a GIP receptor agonist with unproven clinical anti-emetic efficacy little room to add the 13 points needed.
rationale: LY3537021 is a long-acting GIP receptor agonist; anti-emetic support comes from animal models and reduced GLP-1-induced nausea in a phase 1 study, not from CINV patients. Added to guideline prophylaxis, the control delayed complete response should be about 65-70%, so roughly 13 points gain is needed for significance with 102 per arm. Olanzapine achieved that as an add-on, but this mechanism is unproven. Lilly would likely show positive data at a 2027 congress; negative data would appear later on the registry.
evidence: Navari et al., N Engl J Med 2016 (olanzapine for CINV)
Knop et al., Diabetes Obes Metab 2024 (long-acting GIPR agonist with GLP-1 RA)
Borner et al., Diabetes 2020 (GIPR agonism and emesis, preclinical)

assumptions.claim: Adding olanzapine to an NK1 antagonist, a 5-HT3 antagonist and dexamethasone raised delayed-phase complete response from 52% to 67% in highly emetogenic chemotherapy.
assumptions.source: Navari et al., N Engl J Med 2016

assumptions.claim: With olanzapine 5 mg added to triple prophylaxis for cisplatin, delayed-phase complete response was 79% versus 66% with placebo.
assumptions.source: J-FORCE, Hashimoto et al., Lancet Oncol 2020

assumptions.claim: A long-acting GIP receptor agonist reduced gastrointestinal adverse events caused by a GLP-1 receptor agonist in a phase 1 study.
assumptions.source: Knop et al., Diabetes Obes Metab 2024

reason: The 5:1 design leaves about 12 placebo patients, so the comparison could be reported descriptively or blurred by discontinuations, although the expected fat-mass difference of 15-20 points is large.
rationale: Aleniglipron produced about 11% placebo-adjusted weight loss at 36 weeks in ACCESS, so 44 weeks of treatment should cut DXA fat mass by roughly 15-20% versus near zero on placebo. Even with 12 placebo patients and dropouts, that is many standard errors. The main ways to miss are a result reported only descriptively without a statement on the primary comparison, or heavy discontinuation. The study is completed and the listed sponsor will very likely report it with other programme updates.

assumptions.claim: Aleniglipron 120 mg gave a placebo-adjusted mean weight loss of about 11.3% at 36 weeks in the ACCESS phase 2b study.
About 10% of aleniglipron-treated participants in ACCESS stopped treatment because of adverse events.
In the STEP 1 DXA substudy, semaglutide 2.4 mg reduced total fat mass by about 19% over 68 weeks.
assumptions.source: Wilding et al., J Endocr Soc 2021

reason: Placebo HiSCR response is high and variable in HS trials and each dose arm has only about 40-50 patients, so a 20-point HiSCR75 gain could miss significance in a given arm.
rationale: Brivekimig (TNF and OX40L nanobody) had a positive phase 2a in HS (HiSCR50 67% versus 37% in biologic-naive patients) and TNF blockade is validated in HS, so a real effect on HiSCR75 is likely. Risks are the variable placebo response in HS trials, small dose arms (208 patients over several arms) and inclusion of biologic-experienced patients, where effects are usually smaller. Sanofi tends to disclose phase 2b results at congresses or quarterly updates, so a statement by June 2027 is uncertain.

assumptions.claim: In the phase 2a HS-OBTAIN study, HiSCR50 at week 16 was 67% with brivekimig versus 37% with placebo in biologic-naive patients.
Placebo HiSCR75 at week 16 was about 16-18% in the bimekizumab BE HEARD I and II trials.
In the sonelokimab MIRA phase 2 trial, HiSCR75 at week 12 was about 43% with 120 mg versus about 15% with placebo.

reason: Enrolment of 1200 patients was still open about three months before the registered primary completion, so a moderate delay is plausible; early termination and results posting by August 2027 are both unlikely.
rationale: Large open-label phase 2 with a 12-week bleeding endpoint. AF anticoagulant phase 2 trials (AZALEA-TIMI 71, PACIFIC-AF) enrolled quickly and Regeneron is running its factor XI programme at pace, but the record still showed recruiting about three months before the registered primary completion, so a slip beyond 90 days is plausible. An early stop is unlikely and results posting is not due until 2028.

reason: TL1A blockade has no clinical proof of concept in RA; a modest true effect would be swamped by a 35-45% placebo ACR20 with only about 60 patients per arm.
rationale: First test of TL1A blockade in RA; no clinical proof of concept in joints, only UC/CD efficacy and preclinical arthritis data. Several IBD-validated cytokine targets (IL-23, IL-12/23) failed in RA. About 60 patients per arm needs a ~25-point ACR20 gain over a placebo rate near 35-40%, and fast multinational enrolment raises placebo-response risk. Multiple doses give more than one shot. A result public by mid-2027 (likely EULAR) is more probable if positive, so conditional p_met sits above my unconditional ~0.3.

assumptions.claim: In ARTEMIS-UC cohort 1, tulisokibart gave clinical remission at week 12 in 26% of patients versus 1% on placebo.
Placebo plus methotrexate gave an ACR20 response of about 36% at week 12 in SELECT-COMPARE.
assumptions.source: Fleischmann et al., Arthritis Rheumatol 2019 (SELECT-COMPARE, NCT02629159)

assumptions.claim: Ustekinumab and guselkumab did not significantly improve ACR20 at week 28 versus placebo in methotrexate-treated RA.
assumptions.source: Smolen et al., Ann Rheum Dis 2017 (NCT01645280)

reason: Efficacy failure is unlikely; the realistic miss is GI-driven dropouts at the top dose or a disclosure that gives no clear statement on the Part B primary.
rationale: NNC0662-0419 appears to be Novo's once-weekly GLP-1/GIP/amylin tri-agonist; the exclusion criteria and the >25% weight-loss willingness criterion point to strong expected efficacy. Any incretin-based agent at phase 2 doses separates from placebo on 36-week weight change by well over 10 points even with small arms, so statistical failure is unlikely. Residual risk: tolerability-driven dropouts at the top dose, or Novo disclosing only headline numbers or a discontinuation without stating the Part B primary was met; the multi-part primary set adds labelling ambiguity.

assumptions.claim: Subcutaneous amycretin 20 mg gave about 22% weight loss at 36 weeks while placebo patients gained about 2%.
assumptions.source: Novo Nordisk company announcement January 2025; amycretin sc phase 1b/2a (NCT06064006)

assumptions.claim: CagriSema gave 20.4% weight loss at 68 weeks versus 3.0% with placebo in REDEFINE 1 (treatment-policy estimand).

reason: A high vehicle response or a smaller IGA delta, as in PERFECT 1 (about 10 points), could leave the IGA co-primary short even though lesion counts should separate.
rationale: Trifarotene beat vehicle on all three facial co-primaries in both PERFECT trials (IGA success 29.4% vs 19.5% and 42.3% vs 25.7%), with lesion counts highly significant. This Chinese registration study of 561 (possibly 2:1) has roughly 85-90% power for IGA success at the pooled PERFECT effect; IGA is the limiting co-primary. Risks are a smaller delta as in PERFECT 1, vehicle response, or irritation-related dropouts counted as failures. A sponsor disclosure by mid-2027 is more likely if positive.

assumptions.claim: In PERFECT 1, facial IGA success at week 12 was 29.4% with trifarotene versus 19.5% with vehicle.
assumptions.source: Tan et al., J Am Acad Dermatol 2019 (PERFECT 1, NCT02566369)

assumptions.claim: In PERFECT 2, facial IGA success at week 12 was 42.3% with trifarotene versus 25.7% with vehicle.
assumptions.source: Tan et al., J Am Acad Dermatol 2019 (PERFECT 2, NCT02556788)

assumptions.claim: Truncal PGA success at week 12 was 35.7% vs 25.0% in PERFECT 1 and 42.6% vs 29.9% in PERFECT 2.
assumptions.source: Tan et al., J Am Acad Dermatol 2019 (PERFECT 1 and 2)

reason: No oral agent has reliably shrunk drusen, and drusen area over 24 weeks is noisy, so a small or absent true effect is the main way to miss.
rationale: QA108 is a TCM granule from Smilebiotek, built on the hypothesis that drusen-associated microbes drive AMD; a company phase 2 reportedly supported drusen reduction, but no oral agent has convincingly regressed drusen. Drusen area over 24 weeks is noisy with small natural change, so a real treatment effect must be sizeable; 400 patients give power for modest differences. Chinese TCM phase 3 trials that report usually report success. Still recruiting with a March 2027 completion, so a result by June 2027 is unlikely.
evidence: LEAD 2019 (subthreshold nanosecond laser in intermediate AMD)

assumptions.claim: In AREDS, antioxidants plus zinc lowered the risk of progression to advanced AMD by about 25% over 5 years in people with intermediate AMD.
In LEAD, subthreshold nanosecond laser did not significantly slow progression to late AMD overall (adjusted HR 0.61, p=0.122).

reason: Four weeks of an untested mechanism is unlikely to move BACS beyond placebo practice effects, as larger CIAS programmes have repeatedly shown.
rationale: KAT-II inhibition to lower brain kynurenic acid is untested clinically for cognition. CIAS has a long record of failures, including iclepertin's phase 3 CONNEX and luvadaxistat's ERUDITE after positive phase 2 signals. Only 28 days of dosing, about 37 per arm, and BACS practice effects on placebo mean a pairwise win needs an effect size near 0.6; three doses and a possible trend test help a little. A private sponsor is likelier to publicise a win, so conditional p_met exceeds my unconditional ~0.17.

assumptions.claim: Iclepertin did not improve cognition versus placebo at 26 weeks in the phase 3 CONNEX programme.
In phase 2, BI 425809 at 10 mg and 25 mg improved the MCCB overall composite T-score versus placebo after 12 weeks.

reason: A topical thiol may not reach basal skin cells in protective amounts, and keeping patients at grade 0 throughout is a demanding endpoint requiring a roughly 20-point gain.
rationale: Topical amifostine thiol has animal radioprotection data but no prior controlled clinical efficacy; skin penetration within minutes before each fraction is uncertain. The endpoint, staying grade 0 throughout, is strict: with 26 Gy in 5 fractions most patients develop at least faint erythema, so vehicle grade 0 is perhaps 20-25% and about 91 per arm needs a ~20-point gain. Most topical radiodermatitis preventives have failed. Two doses give two chances, and a small private sponsor will more readily publicise success.
evidence: Mometasone furoate for radiation dermatitis, Hindley 2014

assumptions.claim: In FAST-Forward, 26 Gy in 5 fractions over one week was non-inferior to 40 Gy in 15 fractions for 5-year ipsilateral breast tumour relapse.
In the FAST-Forward acute toxicity sub-study, RTOG grade 3 or worse acute skin reactions occurred in 5.8% of patients given 26 Gy in 5 fractions versus 13.6% given 40 Gy in 15.

reason: With 30 per arm and noisy CAP readings, any plausible probiotic effect on steatosis is too small to reach significance.
rationale: Sixty patients at one site with CAP as outcome: between-patient SD of CAP change is around 45 dB/m, so a significant result needs roughly a 35 dB/m difference, well above what probiotics have shown in MASLD meta-analyses. The primary bundles CAP and FAST, raising the bar if both are required. Placebo arms in such trials also improve through regression to the mean. Recruitment is ongoing with a February 2027 completion, so a public result by June 2027 is improbable.
evidence: Sharpton et al. meta-analysis of probiotics/synbiotics in NAFLD 2019
Fuentes et al. L. plantarum CECT 7527/7528/7529 trial 2013

assumptions.claim: A mixture of L. plantarum CECT 7527, 7528 and 7529 lowered LDL cholesterol versus placebo in hypercholesterolaemic adults over 12 weeks.
assumptions.source: Fuentes et al., Br J Nutr 2013

assumptions.claim: A meta-analysis of randomized trials found probiotics or synbiotics associated with modest improvements in ALT, liver stiffness and steatosis in NAFLD, with substantial heterogeneity.
assumptions.source: Sharpton et al., Am J Clin Nutr 2019

reason: Twelve weeks and about 53 per arm leave the trial short of power unless inhaled nintedanib nearly halts FVC decline.
rationale: Nintedanib is a proven antifibrotic, and inhaled delivery should raise lung exposure with fewer GI effects, but 12 weeks is short: untreated placebo patients lose roughly 50-80 mL, so even halting decline yields a ~60 mL difference against an SE near 30-35 mL with ~53 per arm. Oral nintedanib's own 12-week effect would be only ~30 mL. Success therefore needs a better-than-oral effect or a lenient phase 2 alpha. Enrolment of untreated IPF patients is slow, so readout likely slips into 2027.

assumptions.claim: In the phase 2 trial of BI 1015550, placebo patients without background antifibrotics had a median FVC change of -81.7 mL over 12 weeks versus +5.7 mL on drug.
In INPULSIS-1 the adjusted annual rate of FVC decline was -114.7 mL with nintedanib versus -239.9 mL with placebo.

reason: Equivalence would fail only if the quail-cell process changes potency or particle quality enough to shift PRNT titres outside the margins, or if assay variability widens the interval.
rationale: Same virus strain and dose, with only the production substrate changed (quail CCX.E10 cell line vs chicken embryo fibroblasts). MVA-BN has passed a phase 3 lot-consistency trial and a lyophilized vs liquid comparison on vaccinia PRNT GMTs, and about 485 per arm gives tight confidence intervals against usual equivalence margins. Residual risk is a real potency or particle-quality shift from the new substrate, or PRNT assay variability. Bavarian Nordic is listed and should announce topline soon after completion.

assumptions.claim: Three consecutive production lots of MVA-BN gave equivalent vaccinia PRNT geometric mean titres in a phase 3 trial of about 4,000 vaccinia-naive adults.
Lyophilized MVA given subcutaneously was non-inferior to the liquid formulation on peak vaccinia neutralizing antibody titres in vaccinia-naive adults.

reason: Efficacy is very likely; the main threat is GI intolerance and dropouts at the top dose blurring the estimate, or vague wording of the topline.
rationale: HM15275 is a long-acting GLP-1/GIP/glucagon triple agonist; phase 1 showed about 5% weight loss in four weeks. Retatrutide, the same class, gave 17.5% at 24 weeks and 24% at 48 weeks versus about 2% on placebo. With roughly 53 per arm and an SD near 7-8 points, even a 5-point placebo-adjusted loss would be significant, so failure on the primary is very unlikely. Residual risks are GI-driven dropouts and how clearly Hanmi words its topline.

assumptions.claim: Retatrutide 12 mg gave a mean weight change of -24.2% at 48 weeks versus -2.1% with placebo.
Retatrutide 12 mg gave a mean weight change of -17.5% at 24 weeks versus -1.6% with placebo.
In phase 1, four weekly doses of HM15275 gave mean weight loss of roughly 5% at the top dose.
assumptions.source: Hanmi HM15275 phase 1 results presented at ADA 2025

reason: Enrolment is closed and the immunogenicity primary is fixed four weeks after the last dose, so the trial should finish close to its registered date, with results posted only after the read date.
rationale: Enrolment is closed (active, not recruiting) and the immunogenicity primary is fixed four weeks after the last dose, so primary completion near January 2027 is likely; the two-part design leaves some slippage risk. It is a DoD-funded biodefence programme using an adjuvant of known safety, so a stop is unlikely even after Dynavax's change of ownership. Results are due a year after primary completion, so posting by August 2027 is unlikely. The vaguely worded primary outcomes may be reworded, but a change of substance is uncommon.
evidence: Dynavax rF1V plus CpG 1018 plague vaccine phase 2, 2023

reason: The only realistic failure route is the stringent composite, which needs a 2-grade gain on Merz's own scale from both investigator and participant at week 2, giving an active response well below the usual toxin responder rates.
rationale: Botulinum toxin A against placebo on a 2-grade composite responder endpoint has near-zero placebo response and a 30-40% active response in the onabotulinumtoxinA platysma phase 3 trials; incobotulinumtoxinA behaves similarly unit-for-unit in other aesthetic indications and its dose came from a phase 2 dose-ranging study. With 300 participants power is close to 100%. Residual risk is the stringent investigator-plus-participant composite on Merz's own scale. Merz is private and reports slowly, so disclosure by June 2027 is uncertain.
evidence: NT 201 platysma prominence phase 2 dose-ranging study, 2023

assumptions.claim: In the two phase 3 trials of onabotulinumtoxinA for platysma bands, 2% or fewer of placebo participants met the composite investigator-and-participant 2-grade responder definition at day 14.
assumptions.source: Botox Cosmetic US prescribing information, platysma bands studies M21-309 and M21-310 (2024)

assumptions.claim: Composite responder rates with onabotulinumtoxinA in those two trials were between 30% and 45%.
assumptions.source: Botox Cosmetic US prescribing information, platysma bands studies (2024)

assumptions.claim: The FDA approved onabotulinumtoxinA for moderate to severe platysma bands in October 2024.

reason: A fully enrolled pharmacokinetic bridging study whose week-24 primary date has passed should run to completion, with registry results delayed past the read date while the subcutaneous formulation is under regulatory review.
rationale: Phase 3 pharmacokinetic bridging study of subcutaneous ublituximab, fully enrolled, with the week-24 primary completion date already passed; the sponsor plans a regulatory filing on it, so a stop is very unlikely. Posting on ClinicalTrials.gov by August 2027 is unlikely because results are due in October 2027 and a delay certification for a new formulation is probable. The exposure primary could gain a co-primary measure, but a change of substance is uncommon.

reason: Failure would need subcutaneous VRDN-003 exposure to fall well short of intravenous anti-IGF-1R antibodies, cutting the proptosis response enough that a small placebo arm could blur the difference.
rationale: Anti-IGF-1R antibodies give large, consistent proptosis responses: teprotumumab 83% vs 10% (OPTIC), veligrotug 70% vs 5% at 15 weeks (THRIVE), and IBI311 about 86% vs 4% in Chinese patients. VRDN-003 shares veligrotug's binding domain with half-life extension for subcutaneous dosing. Even a 40-point difference gives near-certain significance with 108 patients. Risks are lower subcutaneous exposure and a small placebo arm if randomisation is unequal. Week-24 data mature in March 2027, so topline by June 2027 is roughly even odds.

assumptions.claim: In OPTIC, 83% of teprotumumab patients and 10% of placebo patients were proptosis responders at week 24.
In THRIVE, the proptosis responder rate at week 15 was 70% with veligrotug and 5% with placebo.
In Chinese patients with thyroid eye disease, IBI311 gave a week-24 proptosis responder rate of about 86% against about 4% with placebo.

reason: Three viral-load time points are registered as primary and day 2, one day after the first dose in patients whose virus is already falling, may not separate from placebo even if days 4 and 6 do.
rationale: S-337395 is an oral RSV L-protein inhibitor with a large viral-load effect in a human challenge study. In natural infection treated within 72 hours, viral load is already falling, and earlier antivirals (rilematovir, EDP-938 in RSVP) showed small or no RNA differences. Three time points are registered as primary; day 2, one day after the first dose, is least likely to separate, and the round requires all co-primaries. About 96 per arm with SD near 1.5 log gives good power only for differences above 0.6 log. Enrolment depends on RSV seasons, so delay is likely.

assumptions.claim: In a phase 2 human challenge study, the highest dose of S-337395 reduced RSV viral load area under the curve by about 89% compared with placebo.
assumptions.source: Shionogi press release on the S-337395 phase 2 challenge study, 2025

assumptions.claim: EDP-938 did not meet its primary endpoint in the RSVP study of otherwise healthy adults with community-acquired RSV.

reason: Sixty patients with day-21 mortality near 8% per arm cannot show a mortality difference, so the trial can only describe safety and survival rather than meet a tested efficacy objective.
rationale: A 60-patient phase 2 cannot show a mortality difference: with day-21 all-cause mortality near 8-10% in each arm, a significant result would need an implausible effect. The trial is most likely descriptive, so a 'met' label would need the sponsor to state that a primary objective was met rather than call the data encouraging. Invasive mould infection trials enrol slowly; a February 2026 start with primary completion in December 2026 is optimistic, so a late finish and no result by June 2027 are likely.

assumptions.claim: In the SECURE trial, all-cause mortality through day 42 was 19% with isavuconazole and 20% with voriconazole.
In AmBiLoad, 12-week survival was 72% with liposomal amphotericin B at 3 mg/kg per day.
assumptions.source: AmBiLoad, Cornely et al., Clinical Infectious Diseases 2007

reason: With about 50 patients per arm and a between-patient SD near 15 points of time in range, even a small true deficit against well-titrated degludec leaves the confidence bound short of the non-inferiority margin.
rationale: LY3938577 is Lilly's glucose-sensing insulin receptor agonist, tested open-label against titrated degludec with a non-inferiority primary on time in range. Treat-to-target basal insulin trials usually give similar glycaemic control, so non-inferiority is plausible if the titration algorithm for the new molecule works, but with about 50 per arm and an SD near 15 points the margin (not stated, probably near 10 points) leaves little room for a true deficit. Lilly rarely announces phase 2 insulin data early; ADA 2027 or registry posting in late 2027 are the likely routes.
evidence: Insulin efsitora alfa phase 2 vs degludec in type 2 diabetes, 2023
International Consensus on Time in Range, 2019

assumptions.claim: Lilly's clinical pipeline describes LY3938577 as a glucose-sensing insulin receptor agonist.
A change of 5 percentage points in time in range is regarded as clinically meaningful.
assumptions.source: Battelino et al., International Consensus on Time in Range, Diabetes Care 2019
