reason: A fully enrolled phase 2a safety study whose 180-day follow-up date has passed should complete, with results more likely posted at or after the 12-month deadline in September 2027 than before the read date.
rationale: Phase 2a safety study, fully enrolled, with the 180-day follow-up primary completion date already past, so little remains that could stop it; changes in government vaccine funding are a small residual risk. A small sponsor with a government-funded trial will probably post results near the 12-month deadline in September 2027, so posting by 31 August 2027 is possible but not likely. The single composite safety primary is unlikely to change in substance.

reason: Against placebo the combination should win easily; the risk is that the protocol's primary comparison is with the single agents and macupatide adds too little weight loss on top of eloralintide to show it with about 50 per arm.
rationale: Eloralintide alone gave 9.5-20.1% weight loss at 48 weeks versus 0.4% with placebo in people without diabetes; type 2 diabetes typically cuts such weight loss by about a third, and week 32 is before plateau. The combination with macupatide should still exceed placebo by roughly 10 points, which with about 50 per arm and SD near 6.5 is decisive. Remaining risk is that the protocol's primary comparison is combination versus the single agents. Lilly usually presents phase 2 obesity data at a congress, so disclosure by June 2027 is unlikely.

assumptions.claim: In its phase 2 trial in adults with obesity or overweight without diabetes, eloralintide gave mean weight loss of 9.5% to 20.1% at 48 weeks against 0.4% with placebo.
assumptions.source: Eloralintide phase 2, Lilly press release and Lancet publication, November 2025

assumptions.claim: In SURMOUNT-2 in type 2 diabetes, weight loss at 72 weeks was 14.7% with tirzepatide 15 mg and 3.2% with placebo.
In SURMOUNT-1 in people without diabetes, tirzepatide 15 mg gave 20.9% weight loss at 72 weeks.

reason: The objective needs the combination to beat stannous fluoride alone on both Schiff score and tactile threshold, and stannous fluoride by itself already gives most of the relief, leaving little for potassium nitrate to add at week 8.
rationale: The stated aim is superiority of the stannous fluoride plus potassium nitrate paste over stannous fluoride alone, potassium nitrate alone and vehicle, on both Schiff score and tactile threshold at week 8. Beating vehicle and potassium nitrate is likely; beating stannous fluoride alone on both measures is not, because tubule occlusion already gives most of the benefit and potassium nitrate adds little in 8-week trials. About 180 per active arm detects roughly 0.2 Schiff points. Haleon reports mainly through registry posting, expected around August 2027.
evidence: Schiff et al. three-dentifrice desensitizing trial, 2000
Sowinski et al. 8-week desensitizing dentifrice trial, 2000
Parkinson et al. 0.454% stannous fluoride 8-week trial, 2013
Cochrane review of potassium-containing toothpastes for dentine hypersensitivity, 2006

assumptions.claim: The registry description plans about 180 participants in each of the three active dentifrice arms and about 90 in the vehicle arm.
A dentifrice with 5% potassium nitrate and 0.454% stannous fluoride gave greater sensitivity relief at 8 weeks than a potassium nitrate-only dentifrice.
assumptions.source: Schiff et al., Compendium of Continuing Education in Dentistry Supplement, 2000

assumptions.claim: A 0.454% stannous fluoride dentifrice significantly reduced Schiff sensitivity scores against a negative control dentifrice after 8 weeks of twice-daily use.
assumptions.source: Parkinson et al., American Journal of Dentistry 2013

reason: Failure would require an operational or analysis problem, since an oral PCSK9 inhibitor plus rosuvastatin against double placebo should lower LDL-C by about 75% in untreated adults.
rationale: Enlicitide 20 mg lowered LDL-C about 56-60% versus placebo on background statin in CORALreef Lipids and up to 61% at week 8 in phase 2b; rosuvastatin alone lowers LDL-C 46-55%. Against double placebo in untreated adults the combination should give roughly a 75% reduction with about 250 per arm, so superiority is essentially certain; residual risk is operational. Short treatment keeps discontinuations low. Disclosure is likely via a 2027 congress or registry posting about a year after the August 2026 primary completion.

assumptions.claim: In the phase 2b trial of MK-0616 (enlicitide), placebo-adjusted LDL-C reductions at week 8 ranged from about 41% at 6 mg to about 61% at 30 mg.
assumptions.source: Ballantyne et al., J Am Coll Cardiol 2023 (NCT05261126)

assumptions.claim: In CORALreef Lipids, enlicitide 20 mg daily lowered LDL-C by about 56% versus placebo at week 24, mostly on background statin therapy.
Rosuvastatin 10, 20 and 40 mg lowered LDL-C by about 46%, 52% and 55% from baseline at 6 weeks.
assumptions.source: STELLAR, Jones et al., Am J Cardiol 2003

reason: Enrolling 212 children across age bands within a year looks optimistic, so primary completion probably slips past April 2027, and results posting on ClinicalTrials.gov by August 2027 is unlikely.
rationale: Paediatric study needing 212 children aged 1 to under 18 with in-unit admission, started at the end of December 2025 and still recruiting two months before its registered January 2027 completion. Paediatric bowel-preparation trials usually enrol slowly, especially in the youngest age band, so a slip beyond April 2027 is likely. A non-US sponsor with only European sites makes ClinicalTrials.gov results posting by August 2027 improbable. The descriptive primary outcome is unlikely to change in substance.

reason: Only an operational failure or a much lower dose than in PURSUIT could prevent a significant LDL-C difference, since oral PCSK9 inhibition roughly halves LDL-C on statin background.
rationale: AZD0780 30 mg lowered LDL-C 50.7% versus placebo on statin background at week 12 in PURSUIT. This Russian study repeats that comparison after a rosuvastatin run-in with 38 per arm, which gives overwhelming power for a difference near 50 points (SD about 22). Placebo change after run-in should be near zero. The trial is completed; the main uncertainty is whether and when AstraZeneca discloses results, most likely by registry posting about a year after the September 2026 completion, which falls after the main deadline.

assumptions.claim: In PURSUIT, AZD0780 30 mg once daily added to statin therapy lowered LDL-C by 50.7% versus placebo at week 12.
assumptions.source: PURSUIT phase 2b, Koren et al., J Am Coll Cardiol 2025

assumptions.claim: Lower AZD0780 doses of 1, 3 and 10 mg gave placebo-adjusted LDL-C reductions of about 35%, 38% and 45% in PURSUIT.
assumptions.source: PURSUIT phase 2b, Koren et al., J Am Coll Cardiol 2025

reason: Ritlecitinib's JAK3 and TEC-family inhibition may give a smaller UAS7 effect than dedicated BTK inhibitors, and with about 50-67 patients per arm and a large placebo response a 4-point effect would miss significance.
rationale: Ritlecitinib covalently inhibits JAK3 and TEC-family kinases including BTK; BTK inhibitors (remibrutinib, rilzabrutinib) and the JAK1 inhibitor povorcitinib improved UAS7 by roughly 6-8 points over placebo at week 12, so the mechanism is credible, though BTK coverage at 100 mg is less certain. With placebo responses of 11-14 points, SD about 13 and 50-67 per arm, power is about 70-80% for a 6-7 point effect; two doses give two chances. Primary completion looks likely to slip into 2027, so disclosure by mid-2027 is unlikely.

assumptions.claim: In REMIX-1 and REMIX-2, UAS7 change at week 12 was about -20.0 and -19.4 with remibrutinib versus -13.8 and -11.7 with placebo.
assumptions.source: REMIX-1 and REMIX-2, Metz et al., N Engl J Med 2025

assumptions.claim: Ritlecitinib (PF-06651600) irreversibly inhibits JAK3 and the TEC family kinases, including BTK.
assumptions.source: Xu et al., ACS Chem Biol 2019

assumptions.claim: The oral JAK1 inhibitor povorcitinib significantly improved UAS7 versus placebo at week 12 in a phase 2 trial in antihistamine-refractory CSU.

reason: Completed-enrolment single-dose immunobridging study; GSK usually posts results about a year after primary completion, so posting by the end of August 2027 is somewhat more likely than not.
rationale: Enrolment is complete and the Day 31 immunogenicity primary completion passed in July 2026, so stopping is very unlikely. GSK routinely posts results on ClinicalTrials.gov about 12 months after primary completion, which puts posting close to the 31 August 2027 read date; quality-control lag for a China-only study is the main uncertainty. The four immunobridging primary outcomes are fixed by the regulatory design and unlikely to change in substance.

reason: UACR is highly variable and dapagliflozin's add-on effect on top of an aldosterone synthase inhibitor may be only 15-20% in participants without diabetes, leaving 111 per arm short of power.
rationale: Both arms receive baxdrostat, so the test isolates dapagliflozin's add-on antialbuminuric effect. SGLT2 inhibition lowered UACR about 29% in DAPA-CKD (35% with diabetes, 15% without), and in CONFIDENCE adding empagliflozin to finerenone gave about 29% further reduction, so a 20-30% relative reduction is expected. With 111 per arm and log-UACR SD near 0.8, power is roughly 65-85% depending on the diabetic share. Enrolment is complete, so the December 2026 completion should hold; disclosure is likeliest at a 2027 congress or by registry posting.

assumptions.claim: In CONFIDENCE, finerenone plus empagliflozin lowered UACR at day 180 by about 29% more than finerenone alone and 32% more than empagliflozin alone.
assumptions.source: CONFIDENCE, Agarwal et al., N Engl J Med 2025 (NCT05254002)

assumptions.claim: In DAPA-CKD, dapagliflozin lowered UACR by about 29% versus placebo overall, about 35% in participants with type 2 diabetes and about 15% in those without.
assumptions.source: Jongs et al., Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol 2021

assumptions.claim: In DIAMOND, six weeks of dapagliflozin did not significantly reduce proteinuria in non-diabetic CKD.
assumptions.source: DIAMOND, Cherney et al., Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol 2020

reason: With about 22 patients per arm and highly variable F-VASI change, only a JAK-inhibitor-sized effect from an antibody with no patient efficacy data would reach significance at week 24.
rationale: EI-001 is an early-stage antibody (understood to neutralise interferon-gamma) with no patient efficacy data. The interferon-gamma/JAK axis is validated in vitiligo by oral JAK inhibitors, which improved facial VASI by about 20-35% at week 24 versus -14% to +2% on placebo, but with about 22 per arm and SD near 35 points the trial needs roughly a 21-point difference for p<0.05. I give about 40% odds of real efficacy and under 50% power even then. Still recruiting with a 24-week endpoint, so completion will slip into 2027.

assumptions.claim: In the ritlecitinib phase 2b vitiligo trial, percent change in F-VASI at week 24 was about -21% with 50 mg (with loading dose) versus about +2% with placebo.
assumptions.source: Ezzedine et al., J Am Acad Dermatol 2023 (NCT03715829)

assumptions.claim: In the upadacitinib phase 2 vitiligo trial, percent change in F-VASI at week 24 was about -36% (11 mg) and -34% (22 mg) versus about -14% with placebo.

reason: A plausible 5-10 point gain in continuous abstinence is below the roughly 13 points that 111 per arm can detect, and GI-related dropouts count as relapse.
rationale: Brenipatide is Lilly's GIP/GLP-1 agonist for addiction indications. Incretin evidence in smoking is mixed: exenatide plus patch raised short-term abstinence (46% vs 27%), dulaglutide plus varenicline did not (63% vs 65%), and observational semaglutide data suggest less tobacco use. In recent quitters, placebo 24-week continuous abstinence should be 35-40%; 111 per arm needs about 13 points for significance while a plausible true effect is 5-10 points, and GI dropouts count as relapse. Still recruiting, so the February 2027 completion probably slips and disclosure before mid-2027 is unlikely.
evidence: Yammine 2021 exenatide plus nicotine patch pilot
Wang 2024 semaglutide and tobacco use disorder emulation

assumptions.claim: Adding dulaglutide to varenicline and counselling did not improve 12-week abstinence (63% versus 65% with placebo).
Extended-release exenatide plus nicotine patch gave 46.3% abstinence at 6 weeks versus 26.8% with placebo in a pilot randomized trial.
assumptions.source: Yammine et al., Nicotine Tob Res 2021

assumptions.claim: Among smokers abstinent after 12 weeks of varenicline, 49.6% of those switched to placebo stayed continuously abstinent in weeks 13-24, versus 70.5% on continued varenicline.

reason: Intra-articular saline typically gives about 2 points of pain relief at week 4, so a single liraglutide injection would need a steroid-like effect of about 0.75 points to separate with 65 per arm.
rationale: 4P004 is intra-articular liraglutide with only phase 1 and preclinical support for analgesia. Intra-articular saline is a strong comparator: placebo arms typically improve about 2 points on a 0-10 pain scale by week 4, and most intra-articular candidates other than steroids beat saline by under 0.5 points. With 65 per arm and SD about 2.1, significance needs about 0.75 points. Synovitis enrichment might help an anti-inflammatory mechanism. The trial is completed, so topline disclosure is likely within months; a positive result is more likely to be announced, which lifts the conditional probability slightly.

assumptions.claim: In the FX006 phase 3 trial, the saline placebo arm improved average daily pain by about 2.1 points on a 0-10 scale at week 12, versus about 3.1 with extended-release triamcinolone.
assumptions.source: Conaghan et al., J Bone Joint Surg Am 2018 (NCT02357459)

assumptions.claim: 4P004 is an intra-articular formulation of the GLP-1 receptor agonist liraglutide, which reduced pain and inflammation in rodent osteoarthritis models.

reason: A large saline-injection placebo response in diagnostic-block responders could shrink the difference below the roughly 0.8 NRS points that 75 patients per arm can detect.
rationale: SL1002 is an injectable neurolytic given to patients who respond to a diagnostic genicular nerve block; that enrichment, the sponsor's decision to proceed to phase 3, and genicular radiofrequency ablation data support a real analgesic effect. But saline-injection placebo responses are large (about 2 NRS points), sham-controlled denervation evidence is mixed, and 75 per arm needs about 0.8 points (SD 2.4) for significance. Unconditional success is near 50%; a private sponsor is likelier to announce a win, raising the conditional figure. Enrolment is complete, so readout should come in early 2027.
evidence: Davis 2018 cooled radiofrequency genicular ablation vs steroid

assumptions.claim: Cooled radiofrequency ablation of the genicular nerves gave greater knee osteoarthritis pain reduction at 6 months than intra-articular steroid injection in a randomized trial.
assumptions.source: Davis et al., Reg Anesth Pain Med 2018

assumptions.claim: In the FX006 phase 3 trial, the saline placebo arm improved average daily pain by about 2.1 points on a 0-10 scale at week 12.
assumptions.source: Conaghan et al., J Bone Joint Surg Am 2018 (NCT02357459)

reason: SPN-820, the same mechanism, missed MADRS separation in a Phase 2b TRD trial; the new intermittent 2400 mg regimen rests on a small open-label study, and US adjunctive MDD trials carry large placebo responses over 4 weeks.
rationale: SPN-821 appears to continue Supernus's mTORC1 activator programme (SPN-820/NV-5138), which failed a placebo-controlled Phase 2b in treatment-resistant depression in 2025. The twice-weekly 2400 mg regimen is supported only by an open-label Phase 2a signal. With 115 per arm and SD near 10, the trial needs roughly a 2.7-point MADRS difference; I expect about 1 point against a placebo change near -11 in a 40-site US study with frequent contact. Public company, so topline should follow quickly after completion.

assumptions.claim: SPN-820 did not separate from placebo on MADRS in its Phase 2b trial in treatment-resistant depression.
assumptions.source: Supernus SPN-820 Phase 2b TRD topline announcement, 2025

assumptions.claim: An open-label Phase 2a study of SPN-820 2400 mg in MDD reported rapid reductions in depressive symptoms, with no placebo arm.
In RELIANCE I (adjunctive REL-1017 in MDD), the placebo arm improved by about 13 MADRS points at Day 28.

reason: JAK3/TEC inhibition is untested in HS; with 64 per arm and placebo HiSCR50 often 30-40%, a true gain of about 15 points gives only around half power.
rationale: Ritlecitinib blocks JAK3 and TEC-family kinases including BTK. JAK1 inhibitors (povorcitinib, upadacitinib) and the BTK inhibitor remibrutinib have shown HiSCR gains, which gives a plausible but indirect rationale. Pfizer's earlier HS Phase 2a showed brepocitinib working and two other kinase inhibitors failing against a 33% placebo rate. With 128 patients the detectable difference is about 15-17 points; unconditionally I put success near 0.42. Pfizer seldom publicises Phase 2 failures before registry posting, so results public by mid-2027 lean positive.

assumptions.claim: In Pfizer's Phase 2a HS trial of three kinase inhibitors, brepocitinib achieved HiSCR at week 16 in about 52% of patients versus 33% with placebo.
assumptions.source: NCT04092452; Kimball et al., NEJM Evidence 2024

assumptions.claim: Remibrutinib 25 mg twice daily gave a week-16 HiSCR rate of about 73% versus about 35% with placebo in a Phase 2 HS study.
Povorcitinib gave HiSCR50 at week 12 in about 40-42% of patients versus about 29-30% with placebo in the Phase 3 STOP-HS trials.

reason: Oral incretin agents reliably beat placebo on weight at 28 weeks; the residual risk is weak oral exposure at the top dose or a terse disclosure that never states the primary result.
rationale: ZT006 is a once-daily oral tablet titrated to three target doses, and I assume an incretin (GLP-1 class) mechanism, the sponsor's field. Such agents give 6-12% placebo-adjusted weight loss by 26-28 weeks (orforglipron Phase 2, oral semaglutide), far above the roughly 3.5-point difference needed with 46 per arm and SD near 6. Chinese placebo arms lose 1-3%. Main uncertainty is disclosure: a private Chinese sponsor may report by press release or at ADA/EASD 2027, or not by mid-2027.

assumptions.claim: Orforglipron produced mean weight loss of 8.6-12.6% at week 26 versus 2.0% with placebo in its Phase 2 obesity trial.
Oral semaglutide 50 mg produced 15.1% mean weight loss versus 2.4% with placebo at 68 weeks.

reason: The compound's identity and potency are not public; if type 2 blockade is incomplete or slow, week 12 may be too early for a clear EASI-75 gap in arms of about 50 patients.
rationale: I take JNJ-95597528 to be one of J&J's acquired type 2 pathway assets, most likely the IL-13/TSLP bispecific from Proteologix. IL-13 or IL-4R blockade gives EASI-75 gains of 25-40 points over placebo by week 16 (lebrikizumab, dupilumab), and placebo rates run 10-20% in monotherapy studies. A 189-patient dose-ranging trial has high power for the top dose if activity is dupilumab-like. Risks: uncertain mechanism, a 12-week readout, small arms. Enrolment finished quickly, so data could reach a 2027 congress.

assumptions.claim: Johnson & Johnson acquired Proteologix in 2024, gaining PX128, a bispecific antibody against IL-13 and TSLP intended for atopic dermatitis.
assumptions.source: Johnson & Johnson press release on the Proteologix acquisition, May 2024

assumptions.claim: Lebrikizumab monotherapy gave EASI-75 at week 16 in 58.8% and 52.1% of patients versus 16.2% and 18.1% with placebo.
assumptions.source: ADvocate 1 and ADvocate 2, Silverberg et al., NEJM 2023

reason: With about 52 patients per arm, a 90-day mRS 0-1 difference needs roughly 18 points to reach significance, far above the 8-10 points seen with late-window thrombolysis.
rationale: The design (4.5-24 h window, imaging selection, no thrombolysis or planned thrombectomy, reperfusion and recanalisation secondaries) suggests a thrombolytic-type agent. Late-window trials such as TRACE-III and HOPE gained about 9-14 points on mRS 0-1 with several hundred patients; a Phase 2 with about 52 per arm is a dose-finding study with low power on function. Control mRS 0-1 should be 20-28%. Hengrui rarely announces Phase 2 results, so publication by mid-2027 is unlikely; the completed status makes termination near impossible.

assumptions.claim: In TRACE-III, mRS 0-1 at 90 days was 33.0% with tenecteplase given 4.5-24 h after onset versus 24.2% with standard medical treatment.
In the Phase 2a trial of TMS-007 (JX10) given within 12 h of onset, mRS 0-1 at 90 days was 40.4% versus 18.4% with placebo.

reason: TKI sustained release may regress DRSS less than anti-VEGF injections (EYP-1901 missed in PAVIA); also the registered March 2027 completion is unrealistic for 930 patients followed 52 weeks, so no readout is likely by mid-2027.
rationale: The record's March 2027 primary completion cannot hold: the trial started in November 2025, was still recruiting in October 2026 and needs 52 weeks of follow-up, so a readout before 2028 is unlikely and any statement by mid-2027 would probably be a stop or an interim. On efficacy, HELIOS-1 showed 23% versus 0% two-step DRSS improvement and no worsening on drug, and the ordinal endpoint with 310 per arm is well powered if that holds (about 0.8 at a full readout). EYP-1901's PAVIA miss is the caution.

assumptions.claim: In HELIOS-1, 23.1% of OTX-TKI eyes versus 0% of sham eyes had at least a 2-step DRSS improvement at week 48, in 22 patients.
In PANORAMA, at least a 2-step DRSS improvement at week 52 occurred in 65% and 80% of aflibercept eyes versus 15% of sham eyes.
assumptions.source: PANORAMA, Brown et al., JAMA Ophthalmology 2021

assumptions.claim: The vorolanib insert EYP-1901 did not meet its primary endpoint of at least 2-step DRSS improvement in the Phase 2 PAVIA trial in NPDR.

reason: Small arms and a subjective itch endpoint: a high placebo response or early dropouts in a five-country study could blunt a real JAK-pathway effect.
rationale: ICP-332 (soficitinib) is a TYK2/JAK1-pathway inhibitor that produced large EASI and itch improvements within 4 weeks in a Chinese atopic dermatitis Phase 2. JAK inhibition works on itch in prurigo nodularis (povorcitinib Phase 2: 36-54% itch responders versus 8%). I expect about a 30-point greater percentage reduction in PP-NRS at week 16 against a placebo fall near 22%; with roughly 45 per arm and SD about 33, power is high. InnoCare usually announces Phase 2 toplines, but completion may slip past mid-2027.

assumptions.claim: In a Chinese Phase 2 atopic dermatitis trial, ICP-332 80 mg gave EASI-75 at week 4 in 64% of patients versus 8% with placebo.
assumptions.source: InnoCare ICP-332 Phase 2 AD topline, December 2023

assumptions.claim: In the povorcitinib Phase 2 trial in prurigo nodularis, a 4-point or greater itch NRS improvement at week 16 occurred in 36-54% of treated patients versus 8% with placebo.
In PRIME, 60.0% of dupilumab patients versus 18.4% of placebo patients had a 4-point or greater WI-NRS improvement at week 24.
assumptions.source: PRIME, Yosipovitch et al., Nature Medicine 2023

reason: JAK1 inhibition is proven in AS; the residual risk is an unusually high placebo ASAS40 rate in a Chinese multicentre trial.
rationale: LNK01001 is a selective JAK1 inhibitor with positive Phase 2 data in ankylosing spondylitis. The class effect is consistent: upadacitinib 52% vs 26% and tofacitinib 41% vs 13% on ASAS40, and Chinese JAK1 inhibitors have also succeeded. With 176 per arm the trial has over 95% power for a 20-point difference; I expect about 44% vs 20%. Timing is the uncertainty: the record still said recruiting in late October 2026 with a November 2026 completion date, so topline may come around mid-2027.

assumptions.claim: Upadacitinib 15 mg gave ASAS40 at week 14 in 52% of patients versus 26% with placebo in biologic-naive ankylosing spondylitis.
assumptions.source: SELECT-AXIS 1, van der Heijde et al., Lancet 2019

assumptions.claim: Tofacitinib gave ASAS40 at week 16 in 40.6% of patients versus 12.5% with placebo in its Phase 3 ankylosing spondylitis trial.
assumptions.source: Deodhar et al., Annals of the Rheumatic Diseases 2021

assumptions.claim: LNK01001 is a selective JAK1 inhibitor that met the primary endpoint of a placebo-controlled Phase 2 trial in ankylosing spondylitis in China.
assumptions.source: Lynk Pharmaceuticals LNK01001 Phase 2 AS announcement, 2023

reason: Completed single-site Australian supplement bioavailability study run by a CRO; it cannot now be stopped and registry results posting is unlikely.
rationale: The record already shows the trial completed in August 2026, so termination, suspension or withdrawal is very unlikely. The sponsor is an Australian CRO testing nutritional omega-3 oils for dsm-firmenich; such studies are not subject to US results-posting rules and are usually reported in journals or not at all, so posting on ClinicalTrials.gov by August 2027 is improbable. A change to the single primary outcome after completion is also unlikely, though late record tidying happens occasionally.

reason: Enzalutamide is an equally potent drug of the same class, so a superiority test on 6-month undetectable PSA would probably fail; success depends on the protocol testing non-inferiority, which the record does not state.
rationale: Rezvilutamide is a close analogue of enzalutamide, and both give PSA below 0.2 ng/mL in roughly two thirds of mHSPC patients (ARCHES 68%, more in low-volume disease). I expect a difference of a few points. A 206-patient trial fits either non-inferiority with a margin near 15 points, which would likely be met, or superiority assuming a 20-point gain, which would likely fail; I weight these about equally. Hengrui rarely releases toplines, so a result before late 2027 is unlikely.

assumptions.claim: In ARCHES, 68.1% of patients on enzalutamide plus ADT reached undetectable PSA (below 0.2 ng/mL) versus 17.6% on placebo plus ADT.
assumptions.source: ARCHES, Armstrong et al., Journal of Clinical Oncology 2019

assumptions.claim: Rezvilutamide plus ADT improved radiographic progression-free survival and overall survival versus bicalutamide plus ADT in high-volume mHSPC.
assumptions.source: CHART, Gu et al., Lancet Oncology 2022

assumptions.claim: In TITAN, about 68% of patients on apalutamide plus ADT reached PSA of 0.2 ng/mL or lower.
assumptions.source: TITAN PSA kinetics analysis, Chowdhury et al., Annals of Oncology 2023

reason: With about 20 patients per arm, a true HiSCR75 gain of roughly 20 points over placebo would reach two-sided p<0.05 only about a third of the time.
rationale: SCT650C is, as far as I recall, an anti-IL-17 antibody, a class with proven activity in HS: bimekizumab added about 17 points of HiSCR75 at week 16 and sonelokimab about 29 at week 12, over placebo rates of 15-18%. The drug probably works, but 60 patients in three groups give little power for a binary endpoint, and placebo response in small HS trials swings widely. Two active doses give two chances. Primary completion is March 2027 and the record still recruits, so a result by June 2027 is unlikely.
evidence: BE HEARD I and BE HEARD II 2024 (bimekizumab in HS)
Bimekizumab HS phase 2, Glatt et al. 2021

assumptions.claim: In BE HEARD I and II, HiSCR75 at week 16 was reached by about 33-36% of patients on bimekizumab every 2 weeks versus about 16-18% on placebo.
assumptions.source: BE HEARD I and II, Kimball et al., Lancet 2024

assumptions.claim: In the phase 2 MIRA trial, HiSCR75 at week 12 was 43.3% with sonelokimab 120 mg versus 14.7% with placebo.

reason: The blinded, vehicle-controlled clearance rate could fall well below the 51% seen in open-label COVE-1, especially in patients with many or large warts, though even 22% vs 10% would be significant.
rationale: Cantharidin is a long-used wart treatment, and VP-102 cleared all warts in 51% of patients on the every-21-days-with-paring regimen in open-label COVE-1, the regimen used here. In the molluscum phase 3 trials the product kept its early effect (46-54% vs 13-18%). I expect about 35% vs 9% under blinded assessment; with 151 per arm even 22% vs 10% is significant. Risks are a weaker blinded effect in patients with many or large warts, and vehicle clearance from paring, occlusion and spontaneous resolution in children. Topline is likely in early 2027.
evidence: CAMP-1 and CAMP-2 2020 (VP-102 in molluscum contagiosum)

assumptions.claim: In the open-label phase 2 COVE-1 study, about 51% of cohort 2 patients (VP-102 every 21 days with paring) had complete clearance of all treatable common warts at day 84.
In the CAMP-1 and CAMP-2 phase 3 molluscum trials, complete clearance at day 84 was 46% and 54% with VP-102 versus 18% and 13% with vehicle.
assumptions.source: CAMP-1 and CAMP-2, Eichenfield et al., JAMA Dermatology 2020

reason: Efficacy over a near-zero placebo cure rate is close to certain, so the residual risk is a safety signal (ALT flares after stopping NA, injection-site or platelet effects) or a conduct problem that prevents a clean result.
rationale: AHB-137 is an antisense oligonucleotide of the bepirovirsen type that gave higher HBsAg loss rates in phase 2 in this same population (HBeAg-negative, NA-treated, HBsAg 100-3000 IU/mL). Off-treatment functional cure on placebo plus NA is near zero, so with 577 patients any cure rate above a few percent is significant; both bepirovirsen phase 3 trials were reported positive in January 2026. I expect about 30% cure. Failure would need a safety stop or a conduct problem. Primary completion is December 2026, so a topline or an EASL 2027 presentation is likely.

assumptions.claim: In the phase 2b B-Clear trial, bepirovirsen 300 mg for 24 weeks gave sustained HBsAg and HBV DNA loss in about 9% of patients on NA therapy, mostly those with low baseline HBsAg.
In phase 2, AHB-137 300 mg produced HBsAg loss by end of treatment in a majority of HBeAg-negative, NA-treated patients with baseline HBsAg of 100-3000 IU/mL.
GSK announced in January 2026 that the bepirovirsen phase 3 trials B-Well 1 and B-Well 2 met their primary functional cure endpoint.

reason: The record still recruited ten weeks before a primary completion date that includes 6 months of follow-up, so the date will probably slip past April 2027, while stopping and early posting are unlikely.
rationale: The registered primary completion (7 January 2027) implies the last child was vaccinated by early July 2026, since follow-up is 6 months, yet the record still said recruiting in late October 2026; children with sickle cell disease at 7 sites enrol slowly. Unless the status is stale, primary completion moves past 7 April 2027. Sanofi rarely stops vaccine studies and posts results about a year after completion, so posting by August 2027 is unlikely. Five descriptive primary outcomes leave small room for amendment.

reason: Challenge cryptosporidiosis in healthy adults resolves on its own within days, so stool grade on days 3-5 may be near normal on placebo and leave little room to show benefit.
rationale: EDI048 is a gut-restricted Cryptosporidium PI(4)K inhibitor that killed parasites fast and resolved diarrhea in calves, so an antiparasitic effect in humans is likely. The doubt is the clinical endpoint: cryptosporidiosis in healthy adults is self-limited (median about 3 days of diarrhea in older challenge studies), patients are randomized only after diarrhea starts, and stool grade on days 3-5 may already be near normal on placebo. The attack rate may leave fewer than 40 per arm. Novartis seldom reports phase 2 before registry posting, so a result by June 2027 is unlikely.
evidence: Manjunatha et al. 2024 (EDI048 preclinical, Nature Microbiology)
DuPont et al. 1995 (C. parvum challenge in healthy volunteers)
Okhuysen et al. 1999 (C. parvum isolates in healthy adults)

assumptions.claim: EDI048 is a gut-restricted Cryptosporidium PI(4)K inhibitor that resolved diarrhea and reduced oocyst shedding in the neonatal calf model.
In healthy adult volunteers challenged with C. parvum oocysts, diarrheal illness was self-limited with a median duration of about 74 hours.

reason: The patient-reported ocular subscore may respond less and more noisily than generalised MG scales, and seronegative ocular patients may dilute the effect.
rationale: Telitacicept had a very large effect in the Chinese phase 3 in generalised MG (MG-ADL -5.74 vs -0.91 at week 24) with a low placebo response, and B-cell directed immunosuppression should also help ocular symptoms. With 60 per arm and an SD near 3.8 points, a difference of about 1.4 points is enough; I expect about 3. Risks: a patient-reported ocular subscale, seronegative patients included, and ocular signs often responding less than generalised ones. The record still recruits, so week-24 data probably come in the second quarter of 2027 or later.
evidence: Telitacicept phase 3 in generalised MG, China, 2025
ADAPT OCULUS (efgartigimod in ocular MG, same MGII PRO ocular endpoint)

assumptions.claim: In the Chinese phase 3 trial in generalised myasthenia gravis, telitacicept 240 mg weekly reduced MG-ADL by 5.74 points at week 24 versus 0.91 points with placebo.
assumptions.source: Telitacicept gMG phase 3, RemeGen, presented at AAN 2025

assumptions.claim: The phase 3 ADAPT OCULUS trial of efgartigimod in ocular MG also used change in the MGII PRO ocular score as its primary endpoint.

reason: With roughly 44-59 patients per arm and an SD near 38 points, a smaller-than-expected F-VASI difference at 24 weeks could miss significance.
rationale: Oral JAK inhibitors consistently improve facial repigmentation at week 24 in phase 2: ritlecitinib (-21% vs +2% F-VASI change), upadacitinib and povorcitinib all met this endpoint with about 40-50 patients per arm. Ivarmacitinib (SHR0302) is a JAK1 inhibitor approved in China for other immune diseases, and the combination arm adds topical drug. I expect a difference of 20-25 points with an SD near 38, giving about 80-90% power per arm, with more than one active arm. Hengrui rarely publicises phase 2 results quickly, so a result by June 2027 is unlikely.
evidence: Upadacitinib vitiligo phase 2, Passeron et al. 2024

assumptions.claim: In the phase 2b trial of ritlecitinib in nonsegmental vitiligo, the percent change in F-VASI at week 24 was about -21% with 50 mg after a loading dose versus about +2% with placebo.
In the phase 2 trial of upadacitinib in nonsegmental vitiligo, the 11 mg and 22 mg doses significantly reduced F-VASI at week 24 versus placebo.

reason: A probiotic lozenge is unlikely to offset three weeks of unchecked plaque by the roughly 7 points of bleeding sites that 30 per arm can detect.
rationale: Probiotic lozenges have a mixed record in experimental gingivitis: L. reuteri lozenges did not change bleeding or gingival index, while some other strains showed modest benefit. Three weeks without brushing produces heavy plaque that a salivaricin-producing S. salivarius strain is unlikely to offset by much; I expect about 2-3 points less bleeding against a rise of about 18 points, and 30 per arm can detect only about 7. The multi-timepoint primary leaves room for a favourable reading. A small company and a university site mean slow publication.
evidence: Hallstrom et al. 2013 (L. reuteri lozenges in experimental gingivitis)
Loe et al. 1965 (experimental gingivitis in man)

assumptions.claim: Lactobacillus reuteri lozenges did not significantly affect plaque accumulation, gingival inflammation or bleeding in a randomized experimental gingivitis trial.
assumptions.source: Hallstrom et al., Acta Odontologica Scandinavica 2013

reason: Daily growth hormone is an effective active control, so the higher PEG-rhGH dose is expected to match rather than significantly beat it with 24 children per arm.
rationale: A 72-patient, three-arm, open-label phase 2 comparing two weekly PEG-rhGH doses with daily GH is a dose-selection study; the record states no margin, so the card treats it as superiority over an effective active control. PEG-rhGH 0.2 mg/kg/week slightly beat daily GH in GHD, but in SGA daily GH at registered doses already gives about 10-12 cm/year at 26 weeks, so I expect near-equal growth and significance in about one case in eight; some credit is added for a possible non-inferiority claim. Publication by June 2027 is unlikely.
evidence: REAL 5 2023 (somapacitan vs daily GH in SGA, phase 2)
PEG-rhGH phase 3 in GHD, Luo et al. 2017

assumptions.claim: In the phase 2 REAL 5 trial in short children born SGA, daily GH gave an annualised height velocity at week 26 of about 10.3 cm/year at 0.035 mg/kg/day and about 11.9 cm/year at 0.067 mg/kg/day.
In the phase 3 trial in growth hormone deficiency, weekly PEG-rhGH 0.2 mg/kg gave a higher height velocity than daily rhGH 0.25 mg/kg/week (about 13.4 vs 12.6 cm/year).
assumptions.source: Luo et al., European Journal of Endocrinology 2017

reason: About 12 patients per arm and a variable biopsy gene score mean only a very large drop in interferon signature after 4 weeks would be significant.
rationale: VENT-03 is a first-in-class oral cGAS inhibitor with no patient efficacy data. cGAS-STING contributes to the interferon response in lupus skin, but TLR7/9-driven plasmacytoid dendritic cells also feed it, so the size of the drop in skin interferon signature after 4 weeks is uncertain. With about 12 per arm and a noisy biopsy-based gene score, only a large effect (over about one SD) reaches significance. A private sponsor will probably announce a positive readout quickly and a negative one late or vaguely. Enrolment of 24 across 34 sites looks slow.
evidence: Skopelja-Gardner et al. 2020 (cGAS and UV-induced interferon response in skin)

assumptions.claim: VENT-03 is an oral cGAS inhibitor that completed a phase 1 study in healthy volunteers before this trial and had no earlier efficacy data in patients.

reason: An IL-17A antibody in a 500-patient AS trial should clear ASAS40 easily; the residual risk is an unusually high placebo response or conduct problems at Chinese sites rather than lack of drug effect.
rationale: 608 is an anti-IL-17A antibody already positive in psoriasis phase 3. IL-17A blockade has consistently beaten placebo on ASAS40 at week 16 in AS (secukinumab, ixekizumab, Chinese me-too antibodies), with deltas of 20-30 points over placebo rates of 10-20%. With about 250 per arm the trial has near-complete power even for a 12-point difference. Public readout by June 2027 depends on on-time completion in January 2027 and a company announcement.

assumptions.claim: In COAST-V, ASAS40 at week 16 was 48% with ixekizumab every 4 weeks versus 18% with placebo.
assumptions.source: COAST-V 2018 (van der Heijde et al., Lancet)

assumptions.claim: In MEASURE 2, ASAS40 at week 16 was about 36% with secukinumab 150 mg versus about 11% with placebo.
608 is an anti-IL-17A monoclonal antibody whose phase 3 trial in moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis met its primary endpoints.

reason: Triglyceride changes vary enormously between severe-hypertriglyceridemia patients, so with about 60 patients a real 40-50% lowering could still miss significance, especially if chylomicron-dominant patients respond poorly to ANGPTL3 silencing.
rationale: Solbinsiran silences ANGPTL3; in PROLONG-ANG3 it lowered triglycerides substantially (roughly by half at 400 mg) in mixed dyslipidemia, and zodasiran and evinacumab show the class works when lipoprotein lipase is functional (FCS is excluded here). A 45-50% placebo-adjusted fall against an SD near 45% gives high power even with 30 per arm. Risks: skewed triglyceride data and weaker response in chylomicron-dominant patients, as the variable evinacumab sHTG phase 2 showed. Lilly usually presents phase 2 data at congresses 8-12 months after completion, so a readout by June 2027 is unlikely.
evidence: Evinacumab phase 2 in severe hypertriglyceridemia (Rosenson et al.), 2023

assumptions.claim: In PROLONG-ANG3, solbinsiran 400 mg lowered apolipoprotein B by about 14% versus placebo at day 180.
In ARCHES-2, zodasiran lowered triglycerides by 51 to 63 percentage points versus placebo at week 24.
In SHASTA-2, pooled placebo triglycerides fell about 17% from baseline at week 24 in severe hypertriglyceridemia.

reason: Small Chinese phase 2 safety study in a narrow HFpEF group; it was still recruiting five months before its registered primary completion despite 24 weeks of treatment, so a delay is likely, with no ClinicalTrials.gov results posting expected.
rationale: No efficacy goal. HRS-1893 is a cardiac myosin inhibitor tested here in a narrow HFpEF group (LVEF at least 60%, raised NT-proBNP), 48 patients, 24 weeks. The record still showed recruiting five months before the registered primary completion, which a 24-week treatment period makes hard to hold, so a delay beyond 90 days is about even odds if the record is updated. Hengrui-group sponsors rarely stop small phase 2 trials formally, almost never post results on ClinicalTrials.gov, and seldom change registered outcomes.

reason: Myostatin-pathway blockade without an incretin mainly swaps fat for lean mass, so total body weight, the registered primary, may move only 1-2% against placebo and miss significance even if body composition improves.
rationale: Taldefgrobep blocks myostatin signalling; it raised lean mass and cut fat in earlier studies but failed its SMA phase 3. Only bimagrumab, a broader ActRII blocker, has shown monotherapy weight loss (6.5% at 48 weeks); myostatin-selective agents left weight roughly flat. Over 24 weeks I expect about 1 point of placebo-adjusted weight loss, borderline for 150 patients split over two or three arms. Fat mass is likelier to separate. Biohaven is cash-constrained and will report quickly, probably by early 2027.
evidence: Bimagrumab phase 2 in type 2 diabetes with obesity (Heymsfield et al.), 2021
COURAGE (trevogrumab with or without garetosmab plus semaglutide), 2025

assumptions.claim: Bimagrumab lowered body weight by 6.5% versus 0.8% with placebo over 48 weeks in adults with type 2 diabetes and overweight or obesity.
assumptions.source: Heymsfield et al., JAMA Network Open 2021

assumptions.claim: Taldefgrobep alfa did not meet the primary endpoint of the phase 3 RESILIENT trial in spinal muscular atrophy.

reason: Failure would most likely come from low or erratic oral absorption of a weekly peptide tablet leaving exposure too low to separate from placebo with about 34 patients per arm.
rationale: Ecnoglutide is a potent cAMP-biased GLP-1 analogue with 9-13% weight loss as an injection in Chinese phase 3. A GLP-1 agonist reaching adequate exposure gives 6-9 points of placebo-adjusted loss by week 20, far above what 34 per arm needs (about 2.5 points). Phase 1 oral data supported moving to a 206-patient phase 2b with five active arms; any one Schedule A dose suffices. The trial completed in July 2026 without a readout seen yet, a mild negative signal. Verdiva is well funded and likely to move to phase 3.
evidence: Orforglipron phase 2 in obesity (Wharton et al.), 2023

assumptions.claim: Injectable ecnoglutide gave about 9% to 13% mean weight loss at week 40 versus almost no change with placebo in the Chinese phase 3 SLIMMER trial.
assumptions.source: SLIMMER 2025 (Ji et al., Lancet Diabetes and Endocrinology)

assumptions.claim: Orforglipron gave 8.6% to 12.6% weight loss at week 26 versus 2.0% with placebo in its phase 2 obesity trial.

reason: Refresh Optive is itself an effective tear, so ABBV-444 can at best match it; the objective is met only if the trial's own hypothesis is non-inferiority, as in earlier Allergan tear studies, and is reported as such.
rationale: Allergan/AbbVie artificial-tear registration studies compare OSDI change at day 90 against a marketed Refresh product with a non-inferiority margin of about 7 points; with 261 patients and an SD near 16, non-inferiority is very likely (true difference near zero). Superiority over an active tear is unlikely (under 10%). My p_met weighs about 85% odds that the hypothesis is non-inferiority and that the source states it. The trial is complete; results will mainly surface through ClinicalTrials.gov posting around August 2027 or an ARVO abstract.
evidence: Simmons et al., lipid-based versus aqueous Refresh Optive artificial tears, Clinical Ophthalmology 2015
Simmons et al., two new CMC-hyaluronate artificial tear formulations, Clinical Ophthalmology 2015

assumptions.claim: An earlier Allergan artificial-tear trial against a marketed Refresh comparator used OSDI change from baseline at day 90 as the primary endpoint, tested for non-inferiority.

reason: The drug should lower phosphorus clearly; the main threat to a responder endpoint in 100 patients is diarrhoea-driven dose limitation or discontinuation counting as non-response, or a high placebo target rate on continued binders.
rationale: TS-172 is, to my knowledge, an intestinal NHE3-type phosphate absorption inhibitor that lowered phosphorus dose-dependently in Japanese phase 2. The design copies the Japanese tenapanor add-on phase 3, where phosphorus fell about 2 mg/dL versus 0.2 with placebo over 8 weeks and far more patients reached target. Expect roughly 65-70% versus 30% reaching target, ample for 50 per arm. Taisho is private and rarely issues topline releases, so a public result by June 2027 is unlikely; JSDT or ASN abstracts are the likeliest route.
evidence: Tenapanor added to phosphate binders, Japanese phase 3 (Shigematsu et al.), 2021
TS-172 phase 2 in hemodialysis patients with hyperphosphatemia (Taisho)

assumptions.claim: In the Japanese phase 3 trial adding tenapanor to phosphate binders, mean serum phosphorus change at week 8 was about -2.0 mg/dL with tenapanor versus about -0.2 mg/dL with placebo.
assumptions.source: Shigematsu et al. 2021, tenapanor add-on phase 3 in Japanese hemodialysis patients

assumptions.claim: In AMPLIFY, tenapanor added to binders lowered serum phosphorus by 0.84 mg/dL versus 0.19 mg/dL with placebo at week 4.

reason: Semaglutide is a strong comparator, but HRS9531's phase 3 weight loss was about 5 points greater than semaglutide achieves in Chinese patients, so failure would need the semaglutide arm to overperform or the tested dose to be low.
rationale: HRS9531 is a GLP-1/GIP dual agonist; 6 mg gave 17.7% loss at 48 weeks in Chinese phase 3, similar to tirzepatide, while semaglutide 2.4 mg gave about 12% in STEP 7. SURMOUNT-5 showed dual agonism beats semaglutide by 6.5 points. With 286 per arm and SD about 8.5, a 3-point difference already gives over 95% power; open-label design favours the new drug. Hengrui announced its earlier phase 3 topline soon after completion, so a mid-2027 readout is plausible but not assured by 30 June.

assumptions.claim: HRS9531 6 mg gave 17.7% mean weight loss at week 48 in the Chinese phase 3 HRS9531-301 trial.
Semaglutide 2.4 mg gave 12.1% weight loss at week 44 versus 3.6% with placebo in STEP 7.
assumptions.source: STEP 7 2024 (Mu et al., Lancet Diabetes and Endocrinology)

assumptions.claim: In SURMOUNT-5, weight loss at week 72 was 20.2% with tirzepatide versus 13.7% with semaglutide.

reason: Twelve weeks and about 17 boys per arm give little power to show a strength gain on dynamometry, a noisy measure in 7-9 year olds, for an unproven regenerative mechanism.
rationale: SAT-3247 aims to restore muscle stem-cell asymmetric division; human evidence is an open-label phase 1b in five adults with reported grip-strength gains. A placebo-controlled 12-week comparison in 51 boys split over two doses and placebo is exploratory; DMD drugs rarely show significant strength differences this early, and boys of 7-9 on steroids are near plateau. The company will likely describe trends as encouraging, which counts as not met. Enrolment is complete, so Part 1 topline should come in the first half of 2027.
evidence: SAT-3247 phase 1b open-label cohort in adults with DMD (Satellos), 2025

assumptions.claim: An open-label phase 1b cohort of five adults with DMD treated with SAT-3247 for 28 days reported increases in grip strength.

reason: If the siRNA silences angiotensinogen less deeply or durably than zilebesiran, the month-6 ambulatory effect could shrink to a few mmHg, and with patients split over several dose arms that might miss significance.
rationale: HRS-9563 appears to be an angiotensinogen siRNA (RAAS exclusions, infrequent injection), the zilebesiran mechanism. In KARDIA-1 zilebesiran monotherapy lowered 24-hour systolic pressure 14-17 mmHg versus placebo at month 3 and 11-14 at month 6. If HRS-9563 achieves similar knockdown, a 10-12 mmHg difference against an SD near 12 gives high power even with about 48 per arm. Unknowns are potency and dose selection. Hengrui seldom discloses phase 2 results quickly; a congress presentation in the second half of 2027 is the likeliest route, and a phase 3 could follow.

assumptions.claim: In KARDIA-1, zilebesiran lowered 24-hour mean ambulatory systolic pressure at month 3 by about 14 to 17 mmHg versus placebo across doses.
In KARDIA-1, the placebo group's 24-hour mean systolic pressure rose by about 6.8 mmHg from baseline at month 3.

reason: Untreated response is near zero and phase 2 combined response on brelovitug was above 50%, so a miss would need ALT normalization to lag badly at week 24 or a report that does not state the primary endpoint.
rationale: Brelovitug gave a virologic response in essentially all phase 2 patients and a combined virologic plus ALT response of roughly 55-80% by weeks 24-48. Untreated combined response is about 0-2% (MYR301 delayed arm, 2% at week 48). With 40 versus 20 patients even 35% versus 5% is significant. ALT normalization at week 24 is the weaker component. Mirum guided the AZURE toplines for the second half of 2026 and a filing in 2027, so the result should be public early and is likely to support a BLA.
evidence: BJT-778 (brelovitug) phase 2 in chronic hepatitis D, AASLD 2024 and EASL 2025

assumptions.claim: In MYR301 the delayed-treatment arm had a combined virologic and ALT response of about 2% at week 48.
In the phase 2 trial of brelovitug (BJT-778) every dose arm reached a virologic response rate of 100% by week 48.
Combined virologic and ALT response in the phase 2 brelovitug arms at week 48 was between about 65% and 82%.

reason: The mechanism is new and unproven in a placebo-controlled trial; if the true gain over a placebo change near -35% is under about 15 points, 52 per arm will not show it.
rationale: ENV-294 is a first-in-class oral with an undisclosed mechanism; only a small 4-week phase 1b supports efficacy. Novel oral mechanisms in atopic dermatitis often fail placebo-controlled phase 2 (etrasimod, H4 antagonists). Percent change in EASI is sensitive: with about 52 per arm and SD near 36, a 20-point difference gives about 75% power. US monotherapy trials see placebo changes near -35%. Enveda is private, so a positive result is more likely to be announced than a negative one, which lifts the conditional probability slightly.
evidence: ENV-294 phase 1b in atopic dermatitis, Enveda 2025

assumptions.claim: The placebo arm's mean percent change in EASI at week 12 was about -35% in the abrocitinib phase 2b trial.
The placebo arm's mean percent change in EASI at week 16 was about -23% in the upadacitinib phase 2b trial.
assumptions.source: Guttman-Yassky et al., J Allergy Clin Immunol 2020

assumptions.claim: Enveda reported EASI improvement after 4 weeks of ENV-294 in a phase 1b study in patients with atopic dermatitis.

reason: With about 590 per arm and a 90-day placebo attack rate near 2-3%, only about 14 placebo cases are expected, so a quiet COVID period or efficacy near 60% would leave the comparison short of significance.
rationale: VYD2311 is a more potent successor to pemivibart and adintrevimab, dosed monthly for high titres. This antibody class cut symptomatic COVID-19 by 71-84% in EVADE, PROVENT and CANOPY when variants were susceptible. The main risk is event count: with about 590 per arm and a 90-day placebo attack rate near 2-3% in 2026, only about 14 placebo events are expected, so low incidence or efficacy near 60% would miss significance. Variant drift is a smaller risk. Two active regimens give two chances.

assumptions.claim: In CANOPY's placebo-controlled cohort, pemivibart lowered RT-PCR-confirmed symptomatic COVID-19 through month 6 by about 84% relative to placebo (about 2% versus 12%).
In EVADE, adintrevimab lowered symptomatic COVID-19 by about 71% versus placebo over 3 months in the pre-exposure cohort.
In PROVENT, tixagevimab-cilgavimab lowered symptomatic COVID-19 by 77% versus placebo at the primary analysis.

reason: A 50-patient US asthma study with strict lung-function and reversibility criteria at 20 sites; likely to complete, with a fair chance of finishing a few months late.
rationale: Asthma phase 2 studies that require FEV1 50-80%, reversibility, an ACQ-5 window and a recent exacerbation screen-fail often, so a December 2026 primary completion after a January 2026 start is tight; the record still showed recruiting in late October 2026 with a 16-week participation period. Enveda is well funded, so termination risk is low but not zero if the atopic dermatitis study disappoints. Small private sponsors rarely post results within eight months of completion. A safety primary outcome is rarely rewritten.

reason: The BFM scale is coarse and the population is mixed (different body regions, many on botulinum toxin cycles), so a real but modest benefit of 2-3 points could be lost in the noise with 50 per arm.
rationale: VIM0423 targets the cholinergic imbalance in dystonia, the pathway of trihexyphenidyl, which worked in a 1986 crossover trial in young patients. This is the first efficacy test, in adults with multi-region dystonia, many on botulinum toxin, using the coarse BFM scale. With about 50 per arm and SD near 8 points the trial needs roughly a 3-point difference; I put the chance the drug delivers that near 40%. Primary completion is March 2027, so a result by June 2027 is unlikely and would more often be a positive announcement.
evidence: Burke et al. 1986, high-dose trihexyphenidyl crossover trial in torsion dystonia
Kupsch et al. 2006, pallidal stimulation sham-controlled trial (sham arm BFM change)

assumptions.claim: In a double-blind crossover trial of high-dose trihexyphenidyl in 31 patients with torsion dystonia, about 71% had a clinically significant response.
Sham stimulation improved the BFM movement score by about 1.4 points (about 5%) at 3 months in the pallidal stimulation trial.

reason: Three primary outcomes (stress, anxiety, sleep quality) must all be significant in the same arm; with 60 per arm, a large placebo response on self-rated scales and floor effects on the BAI, that is unlikely.
rationale: Three primary outcomes (PSS, BAI, sleep quality) are registered with no hierarchy, and the round requires all to be met by the same arm. Lavender oil has support in anxiety (Silexan trials) and sleep quality, but in mildly stressed healthy adults with 60 per arm, placebo responses on the PSS are large (about 4-5 points) and floor effects limit the BAI. The chance of one arm winning on all three is low. The sponsor is a contract research organisation that publishes late and rarely posts results, so a result by June 2027 is unlikely.
evidence: Kasper et al. 2010, Silexan in subsyndromal anxiety disorder
Kasper et al. 2014, Silexan versus paroxetine and placebo in generalized anxiety disorder
Rao et al. 2021, palmitoylethanolamide (Levagen+) sleep trial

assumptions.claim: Silexan 80 mg daily lowered the HAM-A total score by about 16 points versus about 9.5 points on placebo over 10 weeks in subsyndromal anxiety disorder.
assumptions.source: Kasper et al., Int Clin Psychopharmacol 2010

assumptions.claim: The record registers three primary outcomes (PSS, BAI and sleep quality) and 60 participants per arm.

reason: About 20 per arm can only detect a PCL-5 difference near 10 points, while an anxiety-sensitivity app is expected to beat an active comparator app by about 5.
rationale: A 40-person single-site pilot of an anxiety-sensitivity app (Florida State CAST lineage) against a comparator app. Earlier CAST trials cut anxiety sensitivity clearly but PTSD symptoms only modestly (d about 0.3-0.5). With about 20 per arm and a PCL-5 change SD near 14, the trial needs a difference near 10 points, so power is about 20-30%. The comparator app will also improve by several points. Results will most likely appear as a ClinicalTrials.gov posting around the NIH one-year deadline (July 2027) or a later paper.
evidence: Schmidt et al. 2014, Cognitive Anxiety Sensitivity Treatment (CAST) randomized trial
Short et al. 2017, brief anxiety sensitivity intervention and PTSD symptoms
Schmidt et al. 2017, anxiety sensitivity intervention and suicide risk

assumptions.claim: A brief computerized anxiety sensitivity intervention (CAST) lowered anxiety sensitivity more than a health-education control in a randomized trial.
assumptions.source: Schmidt et al., J Consult Clin Psychol 2014

assumptions.claim: The trial enrols 40 participants across two arms at a single site.

reason: A 100-patient, 8-week US social anxiety study at 11 sites with a safety primary outcome; it should complete, with a moderate chance of slipping a few months past January 2027.
rationale: Social anxiety studies at US psychiatric research sites usually enrol about one patient per site per month, which fits 100 patients in 11 sites between December 2025 and late 2026, but the record still showed recruiting at the end of October 2026 and exclusion of daily psychotropics slows screening. Newleos is venture funded with several programmes, so an early stop is unlikely. Private sponsors seldom post results within months of completion. The primary outcome is adverse events; a switch to the LSAS efficacy measure is possible but not likely.

reason: The class effect is so large that a miss is implausible on efficacy; the residual risk is a public report that calls the result positive without stating the primary endpoint, or an operational problem.
rationale: Kylo-11 is a GalNAc-siRNA against LPA. Every siRNA in this class (olpasiran, lepodisiran, zerlasiran) lowered Lp(a) by 80-100% versus placebo in phase 2 with tiny p-values, and Kylo-11's phase 1 reductions were of the same order. Placebo Lp(a) is stable, within a few percent. With about 200 patients across dose arms the top dose cannot plausibly miss. The only risks are operational or a report that does not state the primary endpoint. A private Chinese sponsor will probably present at a congress in 2027.

assumptions.claim: Olpasiran at 75 mg or more every 12 weeks lowered Lp(a) by more than 95% versus placebo at week 36.
Lepodisiran 400 mg lowered time-averaged Lp(a) from day 60 to day 180 by about 94% versus placebo.
The placebo arm's Lp(a) rose by about 4% at week 36 in OCEAN(a)-DOSE.

reason: ANGPTL3 blockade lowers triglycerides by about half, so an efficacy miss is implausible with about 180 per arm; the residual risk is operational or a public statement that does not address the primary endpoint.
rationale: SHR-1918 is an anti-ANGPTL3 antibody. ANGPTL3 inhibition (evinacumab, zodasiran) lowers triglycerides by about 50%, and SHR-1918's phase 2 showed reductions of that order. With about 180 per arm and SD near 30 points, a 40-50 point difference is overwhelmingly significant. Enrolment is already complete, so primary completion in March 2027 is credible. Hengrui units seldom announce phase 3 toplines; the result will probably surface through an NDA notice or a congress late in 2027 or after, so publication by June 2027 is unlikely.
evidence: Evinacumab phase 2 in severe hypertriglyceridemia, Rosenson 2023

assumptions.claim: Zodasiran lowered triglycerides by about 51-63% versus placebo at week 24 in mixed hyperlipidemia.
SHR-1918 lowered triglycerides by more than 40% at its higher doses in the phase 2 trial in patients with hyperlipidemia.
The trial was already active, not recruiting by late October 2026, seven months after its March 2026 start.

reason: Only 32 per arm against active latanoprost after a latanoprost run-in: an add-on effect of 1.5-2 mmHg sits at the edge of what this sample can detect, and the record does not state the hypothesis.
rationale: QLS-111, a KATP channel opener that lowers episcleral venous pressure, added roughly 3 mmHg from a latanoprost-treated baseline in the phase 2 Apteryx trial, part of it regression to the mean. Here both arms start from a latanoprost run-in with IOP of 19 mmHg or more, so I expect a control fall near 1 mmHg and a net difference near 1.8 mmHg. With 32 per arm and SD about 2.8 mmHg, power is roughly 60-70%. A small private sponsor is more likely to publicize a positive result, and the hypothesis is not stated.
evidence: Apteryx phase 2 of QLS-111 added to latanoprost (Qlaris, 2025)

assumptions.claim: In MERCURY 1 the netarsudil/latanoprost fixed combination lowered IOP 1.3-2.5 mmHg more than latanoprost alone over three months.
Qlaris reported that QLS-111 added to latanoprost gave about 3 mmHg of further IOP lowering from baseline in the phase 2 Apteryx trial.
assumptions.source: Qlaris Bio press release on Apteryx, 2025

reason: Office SBP is noisy (SD about 13 mmHg) with a sizeable placebo fall, so a GLP-1 driven effect of 5-6 mmHg at 20 weeks, part of it spent in titration, could miss significance with about 80 per arm, or fewer if several doses are tested.
rationale: VCT220 is an oral small-molecule GLP-1 agonist with clear weight loss in a Chinese phase 2. GLP-1 based drugs lower office systolic pressure by 5-7 mmHg in obesity trials and more in hypertensive patients. At 20 weeks, part of it titration, I expect about 6 mmHg beyond a placebo fall near 7 mmHg. With 80 per arm and SD 13 mmHg, power is about 75-80%; unknown dose arms and background therapy lower it a little. Chinese phase 2 sponsors mostly publicize positive results.

assumptions.claim: In SURMOUNT-1 pooled tirzepatide lowered systolic blood pressure by 7.2 mmHg against 1.0 mmHg with placebo at 72 weeks.
In STEP 1 semaglutide 2.4 mg lowered systolic blood pressure by about 6.2 mmHg against about 1.1 mmHg with placebo at 68 weeks.

reason: Failure is unlikely; the only real risk is an ESS-based loss-of-response definition noisy enough for patients kept on drug to cross the threshold, or too few randomized patients, which would blur a very large true effect.
rationale: Oveporexton replaces missing orexin signalling in NT1. In phase 2b and both phase 3 trials ESS fell by roughly 9-14 points against 2-3 on placebo, and a short half-life agonist loses its effect within days of stopping. In a randomized withdrawal of responders nearly all placebo patients should lose response within one to two weeks while few on drug do, so the hazard ratio should be near 0.05. About 40 randomized per arm is ample. Takeda will probably present at a sleep congress or post results in 2027.

assumptions.claim: In the phase 2b trial in NT1, mean ESS change at week 8 ranged from about -8.9 to -13.8 across TAK-861 doses against -2.5 with placebo.
assumptions.source: TAK-861 phase 2b, Dauvilliers et al., NEJM 2025

assumptions.claim: Takeda reported in 2025 that both phase 3 trials of oveporexton in NT1, FirstLight and RadiantLight, met their primary and all secondary endpoints.

reason: Enrolment is closed and follow-up is fixed at about 7 months, so the trial should complete near its registered date; results posting by August 2027 is unlikely for an unlicensed vaccine.
rationale: Enrolment is closed and follow-up is fixed at about 7 months, so completion past June 2027 is unlikely; the registered March 2027 date probably includes assay time. Vaxcyte's VAX-31 phase 3 programme is well funded, so termination risk is minimal. Results are due a year after primary completion and can be deferred for an unlicensed vaccine, so posting by August 2027 is unlikely. The six primary outcomes are standard immunogenicity ratios and safety tables; small edits are possible but substantive change is unlikely.

reason: A single specialised German centre with 60 women and 84 days of treatment should finish near the registered date; the recruiting status looks stale, and results posting by August 2027 is unlikely.
rationale: Ovulation-inhibition studies of this kind run at one specialised German unit, usually on schedule: 60 women, a pre-treatment cycle and 84 days of treatment fit between December 2025 and November 2026. The recruiting status probably reflects a record not updated since registration. A delay beyond February 2027 would need slow recruitment into autumn 2026. No US site and a primary completion in late 2026 make results posting by August 2027 unlikely. The descriptive primary outcome should not change.

reason: Enrolment is closed and the primary window is 28 days, so completion by December 2026 is likely; a thinly funded sponsor adds a small chance of an early stop, and results posting is unlikely for an Australian-only study.
rationale: The trial is already closed to enrolment with a 28-day primary window, so completion by December 2026 is likely. Traws is a thinly funded microcap, which adds a small chance the record is closed as terminated. It is an Australian-only phase 2a, outside US posting rules, and the sponsor has little history of posting results. Safety primaries in a descriptive study rarely change.

reason: Remifentanil already keeps most ventilated patients at target analgesia, so a dose-exploration study of about 40 per arm cannot show superiority, and no non-inferiority margin is stated.
rationale: Tegileridine is a biased mu-opioid agonist approved in China for postoperative pain; for ICU analgesia it should perform much like remifentanil, with success near 90% in both arms. The record states no hypothesis, so a 'met' call needs superiority, which is implausible with about 40 per arm, or a prespecified non-inferiority test that the sponsor reports. Hengrui seldom publishes phase 2 data within a year of completion, so a public result by mid-2027 is unlikely and would probably be descriptive.
evidence: Tegileridine phase 3 trials in postoperative pain (China, 2023)

assumptions.claim: Tegileridine fumarate injection was approved in China in January 2024 for moderate to severe pain after abdominal surgery.
The trial's registry record states no superiority or non-inferiority hypothesis against remifentanil.

reason: The durable CSBM responder endpoint is strict and gains over placebo in CIC are near 10 points; if tenapanor's bowel effect in CIC is smaller than in IBS-C (the 6/12-week CSBM component of T3MPO-1 was not significant), about 173 per arm could miss.
rationale: Tenapanor 50 mg BID is approved for IBS-C, where durable 9/12-week responder rates were clearly above placebo in T3MPO-1 and T3MPO-2. NHE3 inhibition retains sodium and water in the gut and acts directly on stool frequency. Linaclotide and plecanatide won in CIC with gains of 8-11 points over placebo rates of 5-10%. I expect about 17-18% against 7%, giving roughly 85-90% power with about 173 per arm, and three doses give extra chances. Topline probably follows the 26-week completion, after June 2027.

assumptions.claim: In T3MPO-1 the 6/12-week combined responder rate was 27.0% with tenapanor 50 mg BID and 18.7% with placebo.
Plecanatide 3 mg gave a durable overall CSBM responder rate of 21.0% against 10.2% with placebo in a 12-week CIC phase 3 trial.
Linaclotide 72 mcg gave a 12-week CSBM overall responder rate of 13.4% against 4.7% with placebo in CIC.

reason: DLCO% varies widely in patients recovering from radiation pneumonitis on steroids, placebo patients also improve, and a mixed population with checkpoint pneumonitis may dilute a modest antifibrotic effect.
rationale: Pirfenidone is an antifibrotic with an earlier phase 2 signal on DLCO in radiation lung injury from the same sponsor and investigators. DLCO% is noisy (SD about 11 points), placebo patients on steroids also recover, and adding checkpoint pneumonitis broadens the population. With about 99 per arm, a true gain of 3 points gives only about 45-50% power. The registered December 2026 completion is not feasible for a 24-week endpoint with 298 patients enrolling from March 2026, so a result by mid-2027 is very unlikely.
evidence: Phase 2 trial of pirfenidone in radiation-induced lung injury (Sun Yat-sen University, 2023)

assumptions.claim: In ASCEND 14.4% of pirfenidone patients and 10.8% of placebo patients stopped treatment because of adverse events over 52 weeks.
The record requires baseline DLCO from 40% to below 80% of predicted and lung injury of less than 2 months' duration.

reason: A triple agonist should separate from placebo easily; the remaining risk is tolerability-driven dropout at the top dose in small arms, or a headline that gives no clear statement on the Part B primary endpoint.
rationale: UBT251 is a GLP-1/GIP/glucagon triple agonist. A Chinese phase 1b showed 15.1% weight loss at 12 weeks and the Chinese phase 2 about 20% at 24 weeks; retatrutide, the same class, gave 17.5% at 24 weeks against 1.6% on placebo. A 28-week Part B should show 15-20 points over placebo, far beyond what any plausible arm size could miss. The residual risk is how the headline is worded. Novo usually reports phase 2 headline data in company announcements within months of completion.

assumptions.claim: Retatrutide 12 mg reduced body weight by 17.5% at 24 weeks against 1.6% with placebo in its phase 2 obesity trial.
In a Chinese phase 1b trial the top dose of UBT251 reduced body weight by 15.1% at 12 weeks while placebo patients gained 1.5%.
assumptions.source: United Laboratories and Novo Nordisk licence announcement, March 2025

assumptions.claim: The Chinese phase 2 trial of UBT251 in obesity reported weight loss of up to about 19.7% at 24 weeks.
assumptions.source: Novo Nordisk and United Laboratories announcement, 2026

reason: Recruitment closed at 8 of about 40 planned, so the 24-week follow-up should end close to the registered date, with a modest chance the sponsor labels the curtailed pilot terminated.
rationale: Enrollment shows 8 against about 40 planned, and the record is already active, not recruiting, so the last 24-week visit should fall near the registered February 2027 date. A sponsor that curtails a pilot may still label it completed. Results would be due in early 2028, so posting by August 2027 is unlikely. Seven unranked primaries leave little reason to amend.

reason: With about 80 per arm the trial needs a gain of roughly 15 percentage points in mRS 0-1, more than a kallikrein-type neuroprotectant is likely to deliver.
rationale: Phase 2b dose-finding with about 80 per arm needs roughly a 15-point absolute gain in mRS 0-1 to reach p<0.05. QHRD106 is, I believe, a PEGylated pancreatic kallikrein from the maker of pancreatic kininogenase; human urinary kallidinogenase is used in China for stroke but its evidence is low quality, so a true gain of 3-8 points is my central case. Placebo rates in Chinese trials with the same NIHSS 6-20 entry rule run near 45-55%. Three doses give several chances, and domestic stroke trials often read positive, which keeps the probability near 0.2.

assumptions.claim: In TASTE-SL, which used the same NIHSS 6-20 and limb-score entry rule, 54.7% of placebo patients reached mRS 0-1 at day 90 against 64.4% on sublingual edaravone dexborneol.
In TASTE, mRS 0-1 at day 90 was 67.2% with edaravone dexborneol and 59.0% with edaravone alone.
Human urinary kallidinogenase, a kallikrein preparation, is approved in China for acute ischaemic stroke.
assumptions.source: Zhang C et al., J Evid Based Med 2012 (systematic review)

reason: The regular fluoride toothpaste arm may also improve over three weeks of brushing, and organoleptic scoring is subjective, though a zinc effect on breath odour is well established.
rationale: Colgate's zinc toothpastes have repeatedly beaten regular fluoride toothpaste on overnight breath odour, and zinc ions directly bind volatile sulphur compounds. With 40 per arm, trained judges and subjects selected for high baseline scores, even a half-point difference on the organoleptic scale is easily significant. The study is completed and designed to support a claim. The main way it scores as not met is a posted result without a clear statistical statement, or a regular toothpaste arm that also improves over three weeks of regular brushing.
evidence: Navada 2008 (zinc toothpaste and oral malodor, J Clin Dent)
Young 2003 (zinc and volatile sulphur compounds, Eur J Oral Sci)

assumptions.claim: A zinc-containing toothpaste reduced breath volatile sulphur compounds more than a control fluoride toothpaste in a Colgate-run study.
assumptions.source: Navada R et al., J Clin Dent 2008

assumptions.claim: Zinc salts inhibit orally produced volatile sulphur compounds.
assumptions.source: Young A et al., Eur J Oral Sci 2003

reason: Arms of 12 to 24 patients leave little margin if the Chinese placebo response on EASI is high, although IL-4R alpha blockade usually separates clearly.
rationale: IBI3002 is Innovent's bispecific antibody against IL-4R alpha and TSLP. IL-4R alpha blockade is the most reliable mechanism in atopic dermatitis: dupilumab cut EASI by about 70% against 31-38% on placebo in SOLO, and stapokibart did similarly in China. A difference near 35-40 points with SD about 35 gives over 80% power even with 24 against 12-24 patients, and any dose can win. Risks are the small arms, a high Chinese placebo response, and an unproven molecule.

assumptions.claim: In SOLO 1 and SOLO 2, EASI fell by 72.3% and 67.1% with dupilumab every two weeks against 37.6% and 30.9% with placebo at week 16.
In the stapokibart phase 3 trial in Chinese adults, EASI-75 at week 16 was 66.9% against 25.8% with placebo.
assumptions.source: Zhao Y et al., Allergy 2024 (stapokibart phase 3)

assumptions.claim: IBI3002 is a bispecific antibody that blocks IL-4R alpha and TSLP.

reason: The study is already completed; results are not due on the registry until September 2027 and the sponsor may certify a delay.
rationale: The trial is completed, so a stop is nearly excluded. Results are due on the registry twelve months after the September 2026 primary completion, after the read date, and small sponsors of unapproved drugs often certify a delay. Safety primaries on a completed study are rarely changed.

reason: If the 50 mg dose does not suppress oestradiol enough, the bleeding response could fall short in arms of only 30 patients.
rationale: I take CMS-D002 to be China Medical System's oral GnRH receptor antagonist (an assumption; the record does not say). That class gives large, fast drops in fibroid bleeding: 70-85% responders against 9-35% on placebo for elagolix, relugolix and linzagolix. With 30 per arm, a gap of about 25 points is significant, and three doses give more than one chance. The remaining risk is a top dose that does not fully suppress oestradiol, or a noisy 12-week blood-loss measure.

assumptions.claim: In Elaris UF-1 and UF-2, 68.5% and 76.5% on elagolix with add-back met the bleeding responder definition against 8.7% and 10% on placebo.
In LIBERTY 1 and 2, 73% and 71% on relugolix combination therapy responded against 19% and 15% on placebo.
In PRIMROSE 1 and 2, placebo responder rates at 24 weeks were 35.0% and 29.4%.

reason: Twenty patients with a very rare lymphoma at one listed site will probably take longer than ten months to enrol, so completion is likely to slip past March 2027.
rationale: Primary vitreoretinal lymphoma is very rare, the record lists one site and the plan was 20 patients in under a year, so slippage past March 2027 is more likely than not. Aldeyra's funding depends on other programmes, which gives a modest stop risk. Posting by August 2027 would need on-time completion and early submission.

reason: A small, late-registered phase 2a that was still recruiting two months before its registered completion is about as likely as not to finish more than 90 days late.
rationale: A 24-patient phase 2a from a small Beijing biotech, registered after it started and still recruiting two months before its registered completion. An 8-week treatment period means the last patient had to start by October 2026 to finish on time, so a delay past March 2027 is about even odds. Chinese biotechs seldom post results on ClinicalTrials.gov.

reason: A TRPV1 antagonist is likely to lower post-PRK pain by under 1 point on a 10-point scale, which a parallel trial of about 43 per arm detects only about half the time.
rationale: BL1332 is probably the second-generation TRPV1 antagonist that Bausch + Lomb bought from Novartis as OJL332 (my inference). The first-generation drug, libvatrep, lowered post-PRK pain by about 1 point on a 10-point scale in a crossover study. In a parallel design with about 43 per arm and SD near 2.3, the difference must reach about 1 point, so power is 35-65% if the drug matches libvatrep. Two doses give two chances. Rescue analgesia and a bandage lens blunt the vehicle arm's pain.

assumptions.claim: Libvatrep 2.5% lowered VAS ocular pain after PRK by about 11 mm at 6 hours and about 9 mm on average over 12 hours against vehicle.
assumptions.source: Thompson et al., Transl Vis Sci Technol 2023

assumptions.claim: Bausch + Lomb acquired libvatrep and OJL332, a second-generation TRPV1 antagonist, from Novartis together with Xiidra in 2023.

reason: Drugs for ARDS have rarely improved ventilator-free days, and this trial needs a gain of about 2.4 days to reach significance.
rationale: Drug trials in ARDS rarely move ventilator-free days: in SAILS, in sepsis-associated ARDS, both arms had 15.1 days, and HARP-2 and the sivelestat STRIVE trial were also neutral. YD0743's mechanism is not stated in the record. With SD about 10.5 days and about 155 per arm the trial needs a gain of roughly 2.4 days, more than most agents achieve. A mixed population of ventilated and non-ventilated patients adds noise. An enrolment of 309 suggests three groups, which would lower power further.

assumptions.claim: In SAILS, mean ventilator-free days to day 28 were 15.1 in both the rosuvastatin and placebo arms of patients with sepsis-associated ARDS.
In HARP-2, ventilator-free days were 12.6 with simvastatin and 11.5 with placebo, not significantly different.
In STRIVE, sivelestat did not change ventilator-free days or 28-day mortality in acute lung injury.
assumptions.source: Zeiher et al., Crit Care Med 2004

reason: Failure is unlikely for a botulinum toxin versus placebo; the residual risk is the strict composite needing a 2-grade gain on both investigator and subject scales, or a release that does not state the primary result plainly.
rationale: Every botulinum toxin tested against placebo in glabellar lines has met the FDA composite, with placebo responders near 0-2% and active rates of 50-75% (daxibotulinumtoxinA 74%, prabotulinumtoxinA 68-70%). IPN10200 beat placebo in phase 2 LANTIC. With about 300 patients power is essentially complete. Enrolment is closed and the week-4 visits are done or nearly so; Ipsen should issue a topline release in the first half of 2027, probably jointly with LAURITE 2.
