A filing by end-2027 needs long-term repeat-dose data, so it is possible but not the base case.

assumptions.claim: DaxibotulinumtoxinA 40U reached the 2-grade composite investigator-plus-subject response at week 4 in 73.6% and 74.0% of patients versus 0% and 1.0% on placebo.
assumptions.source: SAKURA 1 and SAKURA 2, Carruthers et al., Plast Reconstr Surg 2020

assumptions.claim: PrabotulinumtoxinA 20U reached the 2-grade composite response at day 30 in 67.5% and 70.4% of patients versus 1.2% and 1.3% on placebo.
assumptions.source: EV-001 and EV-002, Beer et al., Dermatol Surg 2019

assumptions.claim: IPN10200 met its week-4 primary endpoint versus placebo in glabellar lines in the phase 2 LANTIC trial.

reason: Enrolment is closed and the 30-week follow-up ends within weeks of the registered date, so the trial should complete on time; results posting within nine months is unlikely for an unapproved drug.
rationale: Active, not recruiting, with primary completion two weeks after the snapshot and a short fixed follow-up, so a slip beyond 90 days is unlikely. Regeneron rarely posts phase 2 results for unapproved drugs before the 12-month deadline and may certify a delay. Four safety and drug-level primaries leave little reason for a change in substance.

reason: An on-demand sublingual SERT inhibitor taken 15 minutes before intercourse may not reach effective levels fast enough, so the IELT gain over placebo could be small in a 40-man crossover.
rationale: Serotonin reuptake inhibition reliably delays ejaculation, and dapoxetine on demand roughly doubles the placebo gain in IELT, so the class effect is real. A crossover of 40 men has good power for a dapoxetine-sized effect but not a smaller one. KH-001 has no public efficacy data and dosing 15 minutes before intercourse is ambitious. The record still showed recruiting at its registered completion date, so a result by June 2027 is doubtful, and a small private sponsor is more likely to announce a positive result.
evidence: Pryor et al., dapoxetine phase 3, Lancet 2006
Buvat et al., dapoxetine, Eur Urol 2009
McMahon et al., dapoxetine pooled phase 3 analysis, J Sex Med 2011

assumptions.claim: On-demand dapoxetine 30 mg and 60 mg raised mean IELT from about 0.9 minutes at baseline to 2.78 and 3.32 minutes at week 12, versus 1.75 minutes with placebo.

reason: Failure is unlikely for a botulinum toxin versus placebo; the residual risk is two region-specific primaries that must both be reported as met, or a release that does not state the primary result plainly.
rationale: Same drug, endpoint and timing as LAURITE 1 in a larger, multi-region double-blind phase. Botulinum toxins have always beaten placebo on the 2-grade composite (placebo 0-2%, active 50-75%), and the EU primary of a 2-grade investigator-rated gain is easier still, so both regional primaries should be met. Enrolment is closed with primary completion in December 2026; a joint topline release with LAURITE 1 in the first half of 2027 is likely. The open-label repeat-dose phase runs to 2028, which may hold a filing announcement beyond 2027.

assumptions.claim: DaxibotulinumtoxinA 40U reached the 2-grade composite investigator-plus-subject response at week 4 in 73.6% and 74.0% of patients versus 0% and 1.0% on placebo.
assumptions.source: SAKURA 1 and SAKURA 2, Carruthers et al., Plast Reconstr Surg 2020

assumptions.claim: PrabotulinumtoxinA 20U reached the 2-grade composite response at day 30 in 67.5% and 70.4% of patients versus 1.2% and 1.3% on placebo.
assumptions.source: EV-001 and EV-002, Beer et al., Dermatol Surg 2019

assumptions.claim: IPN10200 met its week-4 primary endpoint versus placebo in glabellar lines in the phase 2 LANTIC trial.

reason: With about 35 patients per arm and a placebo response in CLASI-A that has ranged from roughly -15% to -50% across cutaneous lupus trials, a real TYK2 effect could still miss significance.
rationale: ICP-488 is an allosteric TYK2 inhibitor with strong phase 2 psoriasis data; TYK2 blocks type I interferon signalling, central to cutaneous lupus, and deucravacitinib gave large CLASI-50 gains in the PAISLEY SLE trial. Litifilimab showed a 24-33 point placebo-adjusted CLASI-A drop at week 16. Two dose arms give two chances. Against that, 35 per arm is thin and placebo response is variable. Enrolling 105 biopsy-proven patients since April 2026 probably pushes completion past March 2027, so a result by June 2027 is unlikely.
evidence: LILAC part B (litifilimab in cutaneous lupus, 2022)
Iberdomide phase 2 in SLE, cutaneous analysis (2022)

assumptions.claim: In PAISLEY, CLASI-50 response at week 48 was 69.6% with deucravacitinib 3 mg twice daily versus 16.7% with placebo.
assumptions.source: PAISLEY, Morand et al., Arthritis Rheumatol 2023

assumptions.claim: In LILAC part B, CLASI-A changed by -14.5% with placebo at week 16 versus -38.8% to -47.9% with litifilimab.
assumptions.source: LILAC, Werth et al., N Engl J Med 2022

assumptions.claim: ICP-488 6 mg and 9 mg once daily gave PASI 75 at week 12 in 77.3% and 78.6% of psoriasis patients versus 11.6% on placebo.

reason: A 155-patient safety study with a week-16 primary and a year-end 2026 date; the main uncertainty is whether enrolment closed early enough to keep primary completion within 90 days of that date.
rationale: Started December 2025 with primary completion registered for 31 December 2026; the status still showed enrolling by invitation in late October, so a slip of a few months is plausible but more than 90 days is less likely. A small company is unlikely to post results within eight months of completion. The single safety primary could be reworded when the record is updated, but a change in substance is uncommon.

reason: The record states no formal superiority hypothesis, so a report may describe recovery times without declaring the primary objective met, or HRS-9190 may not recover clearly faster than cisatracurium.
rationale: Choosing recovery time after stopping the infusion as primary, against intermediate-acting cisatracurium, suggests HRS-9190 is a shorter-acting blocker, in which case a difference of 20 minutes or more would be significant even with about 33 per group. Cisatracurium needs roughly 40-55 minutes to reach a train-of-four ratio of 0.9 from deep block. The trial completed in July 2026, but Hengrui seldom reports phase 2 results quickly, so a public statement by June 2027 is unlikely. A phase 3 registration in 2027 is plausible.
evidence: Belmont et al., cisatracurium pharmacodynamics, Anesthesiology 1995

assumptions.claim: Cisatracurium has a 25-75% spontaneous recovery index of about 13 minutes that does not lengthen with infusion duration.

reason: Ten women per arm means only a very large difference, about 60% against 10%, reaches significance on a strict 90% Lactobacillus threshold.
rationale: FB301 is Freya's vaginal microbiome therapeutic; comparable products (LACTIN-V, donor microbiome transplants) do shift the microbiome, and spontaneous conversion to 90% Lactobacillus within 16 days should be rare on placebo, though oestrogen priming may raise it. But with 10 per arm a Fisher test needs roughly 6-7 responders against 0-1. Enrolment started in July 2026 and was still open at the registered completion date, so a result by June 2027 is uncertain; a private sponsor is more likely to announce a favourable one.
evidence: Lev-Sagie et al., vaginal microbiome transplantation, 2019

assumptions.claim: LACTIN-V (Lactobacillus crispatus CTV-05) given after metronidazole cut bacterial vaginosis recurrence by week 12 to 30% versus 45% with placebo.
assumptions.source: Cohen et al., N Engl J Med 2020

reason: No prior human evidence that oleoylethanolamide lowers imidazole propionate, a highly variable microbial metabolite, so a real effect in healthy adults over 8 weeks is unlikely.
rationale: Imidazole propionate is produced by gut bacteria from histidine and varies widely between people and with diet. Oleoylethanolamide acts mainly on PPAR-alpha and appetite; an effect on this metabolite is a new hypothesis without human data. With 45 per arm only a moderate standardised effect would be detected. The trial completes around March 2027 and supplement trials of this kind usually publish a year or more later, so a statement by June 2027 is unlikely. Variability assumes plasma levels in nmol/L.
evidence: Koh et al., imidazole propionate and insulin signalling, Cell 2018
Molinaro et al., imidazole propionate in type 2 diabetes, Nat Commun 2020

assumptions.claim: Imidazole propionate is a microbially produced histidine metabolite that is higher in people with type 2 diabetes and impairs insulin signalling.

reason: With about 30 patients per arm and blood-pressure change SD near 14 mmHg, a placebo response larger than expected or a modest dose could leave a real effect short of significance.
rationale: Primary aldosteronism is the population where blocking aldosterone action or synthesis lowers blood pressure most: esaxerenone cut systolic pressure about 18 mmHg in this setting, against a placebo fall of roughly 3-8 mmHg. HRS-1780 is an aldosterone-pathway agent from Hengrui, so a placebo-adjusted fall near 10-14 mmHg is expected, which 60 patients detect with roughly 80% power. Completion is due November 2026, but Hengrui subsidiaries seldom disclose phase 2 results quickly; a congress abstract by mid-2027 is possible but unlikely.
evidence: Esaxerenone phase 3 in primary aldosteronism (Satoh et al., 2021)
Parthasarathy et al., spironolactone versus eplerenone in primary aldosteronism, 2011

assumptions.claim: Esaxerenone lowered sitting systolic blood pressure by about 17.7 mmHg at 12 weeks in Japanese patients with primary aldosteronism in a single-arm phase 3 study.
In BrigHTN, systolic blood pressure fell by 9.4 mmHg with placebo and by 20.3 mmHg with baxdrostat 2 mg at 12 weeks.
assumptions.source: BrigHTN, Freeman et al., N Engl J Med 2023

reason: Enrolment is closed and treatment lasts 20 weeks, so the trial should complete close to its registered date; the sponsor seldom posts results on ClinicalTrials.gov.
rationale: Small two-site Chinese phase 2 (102 patients) that started in April 2026 and is already active, not recruiting; with a 20-week treatment period the last visits fall around the registered December 2026 or shortly after. Stopping a fully enrolled short study is unlikely. Jiangsu HengRui almost never posts results on ClinicalTrials.gov, and a single safety primary outcome is unlikely to be changed.

reason: Failure is very unlikely for a PCSK9 antibody on LDL-C at week 12; the residual risk is a disclosure that only calls the result positive without a statement on the primary endpoint.
rationale: Tafolecimab is an approved PCSK9 antibody; CREDIT-1, CREDIT-2 and CREDIT-4 showed placebo-adjusted LDL-C reductions of roughly 57-65%, and monotherapy trials of other PCSK9 antibodies (MENDEL-2, REMAIN-1) show similar effects without statins. With 198 patients and an SD near 20 points, power is essentially complete. Placebo change after a 4-week run-in should be near zero to -6%. The uncertainties are which regimen the result is read on (Q4W or a longer interval) and whether Innovent discloses the result by mid-2027.

assumptions.claim: In CREDIT-4, tafolecimab 450 mg every 4 weeks changed LDL-C at week 12 by -68.9% versus -5.8% with placebo, a difference of about -63%.
In CREDIT-1, tafolecimab lowered LDL-C at week 48 by 65.0% (450 mg Q4W) and 57.3% (600 mg Q6W) relative to placebo.
assumptions.source: CREDIT-1, Lancet Regional Health Western Pacific 2023

assumptions.claim: In MENDEL-2, evolocumab monotherapy lowered LDL-C at week 12 by about 55-57% more than placebo.

reason: Enrolment closed within about four months and the endpoint is at week 12, so completion should be on time; results posting is not due until about a year after primary completion.
rationale: Regeneron enrolled 438 participants at 34 US sites between June and October 2026 and the record is already active, not recruiting; a 12-week endpoint puts last visits at or just after the registered 29 December 2026. Alirocumab is an approved, well-tolerated drug, so a stop is unlikely. Results are due on ClinicalTrials.gov about 12 months after primary completion, after the read date, and a delay certification for a new regimen is possible. The LDL-C primary outcome is standard and unlikely to change.

reason: Nine registered primary outcomes in a 24-patient single-dose crossover make it very unlikely that all are met, and the sponsor may only describe the data as supportive.
rationale: Exploratory single-dose crossover in 24 unmedicated GAD patients with nine registered primary outcomes spanning fMRI, behavioural tasks and self-report. Under the round's rules all primaries must be met, which is very unlikely for a first-in-patient pharmacodynamic study of a novel endocannabinoid reuptake inhibitor; even amygdala reactivity alone would be roughly a one-in-three shot at this size. A small private sponsor is likely to describe results as positive or supportive rather than state that every primary endpoint was met. Single-site recruitment of unmedicated patients able to undergo MRI makes delay plausible.

assumptions.claim: The registry record lists nine primary outcomes for a two-way crossover in 24 participants given a single dose per period.

reason: Recruiting 120 women with symptomatic bacterial vaginosis at two German research units on a menstrual-cycle-timed schedule is likely to run somewhat behind plan, but the study should finish without stopping.
rationale: Open-label four-arm phase 2 of a live biotherapeutic at two contract research sites. The plan needs about 11 patients a month with Nugent score 7 or above and regular cycles through early 2027, which leaves little slack; a slip of more than 90 days is a real possibility. The sponsor is a small private company, so funding is the main stopping risk. European early-phase sponsors rarely post results on ClinicalTrials.gov within months of completion. The microbiome primary outcome is specific and unlikely to change in substance.

reason: With about 150 children the trial is powered only for a large acceleration of symptom resolution, and zelicapavir's clinical benefit has so far been modest outside the highest-risk adults.
rationale: Zelicapavir has shown antiviral activity in children (RSVPEDs, about 1.4 log greater viral-load decline at day 5), but clinical benefit is unproven: the adult RSVP trial failed and RSVHR missed its primary endpoint in the overall population while showing faster complete symptom resolution in the highest-risk subgroup. With 150 children and roughly 100-110 resolution events, the trial has good power only for hazard ratios near 1.6; for a plausible 1.2-1.3 it has 20-35%. RESOLVE-P is a new instrument, adding endpoint risk. Enanta should report topline promptly if enrolment finishes in the 2026 Thai season.

assumptions.claim: In Part 2 of the paediatric RSVPEDs study, zelicapavir produced a viral-load decline at day 5 about 1.4 log greater than placebo.

In the RSVHR phase 2b study in high-risk adults, the primary endpoint of time to resolution of lower respiratory tract disease symptoms was not statistically significant in the overall efficacy population.
In the phase 3 AIRFLO trial, ziresovir significantly improved the Wang bronchiolitis score at day 3 in hospitalised infants with RSV compared with placebo.

reason: TL1A blockade has no clinical proof in psoriatic arthritis, and small dose arms need a difference of about 20 points in ACR20 to reach significance.
rationale: TL1A blockade is validated in ulcerative colitis and Crohn's disease but has no randomized efficacy data in psoriatic arthritis; support is genetic and preclinical (TNFSF15, Th17 amplification). With about 35-47 patients per arm, significance needs a roughly 20-point ACR20 difference over a placebo rate near 33%, so a moderate true effect gives only about even odds, though several dose arms help. I put unconditional success near 0.42; a result public by June 2027 is more likely a termination or pipeline removal than a congress presentation, which lowers the conditional probability. Enrolment is complete, so timing risk is small.

assumptions.claim: In the phase 2 trial of deucravacitinib in psoriatic arthritis, the ACR20 response at week 16 was 31.8% with placebo.
assumptions.source: Mease et al., Ann Rheum Dis 2022 (deucravacitinib phase 2 PsA)

assumptions.claim: In ARTEMIS-UC, clinical remission at week 12 occurred in 26% of patients on tulisokibart versus 1% on placebo in the first cohort.
No randomized efficacy result for tulisokibart in psoriatic arthritis had been published before this trial started in April 2026.

reason: The main risk is that the AND017 dosing algorithm leaves hemoglobin lower than with ESA in a mixed naive and ESA-treated population, although the HIF-PHI class has reliably shown non-inferiority.
rationale: Oral HIF-PH inhibitors have consistently matched ESAs on hemoglobin in non-dialysis CKD (roxadustat, daprodustat, enarodustat, desidustat, vadadustat), and AND017 completed phase 2 dose-finding before this trial. With titration to a 10-12 g/dL target in both arms, the between-arm difference should sit within about 0.3 g/dL, well inside a usual margin of 0.75-1.0. Risks are an unvalidated dosing algorithm, a mixed naive and ESA-treated population, and open-label conduct. The record still shows recruiting with a 27-week endpoint, so primary completion will slip into 2027 and a public result by June 2027 is unlikely.

assumptions.claim: In ASCEND-ND, daprodustat was non-inferior to darbepoetin alfa for change in hemoglobin, with a between-group difference of about 0.08 g/dL.
In DREAM-ND, desidustat was non-inferior to darbepoetin for hemoglobin change at weeks 16-24 (about 1.95 versus 1.83 g/dL).
In SYMPHONY ND, mean hemoglobin in the evaluation period was about 10.96 g/dL with enarodustat and 10.87 g/dL with darbepoetin alfa.

reason: A large placebo response on background therapy, as in the HALO trial of baxdrostat, could erase the difference with only about 65 patients per arm.
rationale: The design copies the baxdrostat programme (uncontrolled and resistant strata, diuretic background, potassium and eGFR limits), so QLS1410 is most likely an aldosterone synthase inhibitor; this is an inference, not stated in the record. That class lowered seated SBP by about 8-11 mmHg over placebo in BrigHTN, BaxHTN, Target-HTN and Launch-HTN. With about 65 per arm and an SD near 14 mmHg, a difference of about 5 mmHg is significant, giving roughly 80-90% power per dose for a class-typical effect. HALO shows a large placebo response can erase the signal in phase 2.

assumptions.claim: In BrigHTN, baxdrostat 2 mg changed seated systolic blood pressure at week 12 by -20.3 mmHg versus -9.4 mmHg with placebo, a difference of -11.0 mmHg.
In BaxHTN, the placebo-adjusted change in seated systolic blood pressure at week 12 was -9.8 mmHg with baxdrostat 2 mg, and the placebo arm fell by 5.8 mmHg.
In the phase 2 HALO trial, baxdrostat did not separate from placebo on seated systolic blood pressure, with a placebo fall of about 16.6 mmHg.

reason: A smaller liver-fat effect at 26 weeks than in the 61-day study, compounded by dropouts at the highest dose, is the most likely way to miss one of the two efficacy primaries.
rationale: HU6 lowered liver fat by a relative 33-43% in the 61-day phase 2a NAFLD trial, and Rivus reported that the six-month M-ACCEL trial in MASH met its liver-fat primary endpoint. A placebo-adjusted reduction near 25-30 points with an SD near 32 gives over 90% power at about 45 per arm, and the 30% responder co-primary should follow. Risks are dropouts from flushing or gastrointestinal effects, a weaker effect at 26 weeks, and reporting that does not state both efficacy primaries. The record still shows recruiting, so completion will likely slip to mid-2027.

assumptions.claim: In the 61-day phase 2a trial in adults with NAFLD and high BMI, HU6 reduced liver fat by a relative 33.0%, 43.0% and 35.6% at 150, 300 and 450 mg, significantly more than placebo.
assumptions.source: Noureddin et al., Lancet Gastroenterol Hepatol 2023

assumptions.claim: Rivus reported that the six-month phase 2 M-ACCEL trial of HU6 in MASH met its primary endpoint of liver-fat reduction versus placebo.
The phase 2a HuMAIN trial of HU6 in obesity-related HFpEF met its primary endpoint of body-weight reduction versus placebo.

reason: A titration scheme that leaves mean haemoglobin clearly below the ESA arm, or an unusually tight margin, is the main way an ESA-conversion HIF-PHI trial misses non-inferiority; the larger practical risk is that this small sponsor reports late or not at all.
rationale: AND017 is an oral HIF-prolyl hydroxylase inhibitor; every approved member of the class (roxadustat, daprodustat, vadadustat, enarodustat, desidustat) held haemoglobin non-inferior to ESA in dialysis conversion trials using dose titration to a target range. Open-label titration makes Hb maintenance close to mechanical, and 150 per arm gives ample power for a 0.75-1.0 g/dL margin with SD near 1.1. Residual risks: an untested dosing regimen, an undisclosed margin and a small sponsor's reporting habits.
evidence: Roxadustat China dialysis phase 3, Chen et al. NEJM 2019 (NCT02652806)

assumptions.claim: In the Chinese dialysis phase 3 trial, roxadustat was non-inferior to epoetin alfa, with mean haemoglobin change of 0.7 versus 0.5 g/dL over weeks 23 to 27.
In ASCEND-D, daprodustat was non-inferior to ESA for haemoglobin change (difference 0.18 g/dL) against a margin of -0.75 g/dL.
In INNO2VATE, vadadustat met haemoglobin non-inferiority versus darbepoetin in dialysis patients against a margin of -0.75 g/dL, with differences of about -0.2 to -0.3 g/dL.

reason: Failure would need the older-adult stratum or the seroconversion co-primary to fall short of the regulatory thresholds, or Moderna to describe the data without stating that the endpoints were met.
rationale: Immunogenicity-only phase 3 judged against licensure thresholds for pandemic vaccines (lower 95% bound for HAI >=1:40 of 70% in adults under 65, 60% in older adults). In the phase 1/2 study 97.8% of recipients reached HAI >=1:40 at Day 43 with a 44.5-fold rise from a near-naive baseline (2.1%). A two-dose mRNA regimen, a large sample and essentially seronegative placebo recipients make success very likely; residual risks are older adults, assay differences and both HAI co-primaries needing to pass.
evidence: FDA guidance on pandemic influenza vaccine licensure, 2007

assumptions.claim: In the phase 1/2 study of mRNA-1018, 97.8% of participants had HAI titres of 1:40 or higher at Day 43, three weeks after the second dose.
Baseline HAI titres of 1:40 or higher were present in about 2% of participants in that phase 1/2 study.
FDA licensure criteria for pandemic influenza vaccines require the lower 95% bound for the share with HAI >=1:40 to reach 70% in adults under 65 and 60% in those 65 and older.
assumptions.source: FDA Guidance for Industry: Clinical Data Needed to Support the Licensure of Pandemic Influenza Vaccines, 2007

reason: Only an event rate far below the 40-55% seen in earlier lung fluorescence-imaging trials, or disputes over what counts as a clinically significant event, would sink a single-arm threshold test; slow enrolment is the bigger threat to a timely readout.
rationale: The primary is a within-patient event rate tested against a low pre-specified threshold, not a between-arm comparison. In the phase 2 efficacy study about 43% of evaluable patients had at least one clinically significant event, the first phase 3 (VISUALIZE) was reported as meeting its primary endpoint, and pafolacianine's ELUCIDATE lung trial showed 53% against a 10% threshold. With 115 evaluable patients a true rate near 40% clears any plausible threshold. Main uncertainties are enrolment speed and reporting timing.

assumptions.claim: In the phase 2 efficacy study of VGT-309, roughly 4 in 10 evaluable patients (about 43%) had at least one clinically significant event.
The first phase 3 trial of abenacianine in lung surgery, VISUALIZE, was reported by the sponsor as meeting its primary endpoint.
In ELUCIDATE, pafolacianine with near-infrared imaging produced a clinically significant event in 53% of lung surgery patients against a pre-specified threshold of 10%.
assumptions.source: ELUCIDATE, Sarkaria et al., J Thorac Cardiovasc Surg 2023 (NCT04241315)

reason: The large HbA1c effects came from small subgroups of COVALENT-111, so regression toward the modest whole-trial effect (about 0.4 points) would leave 64 patients underpowered.
rationale: COVALENT-111 gave a pooled per-protocol placebo-adjusted HbA1c change of only -0.36 points at week 26; the -1.47 point figure for 100 mg over 12 weeks came from a small insulin-deficient subgroup. This trial uses BMI <=32 and a non-incretin background as a proxy for that phenotype and reads out 14 weeks off drug. With about 32 per arm and SD near 1.1, significance needs roughly -0.6 points. I expect a true effect near -0.4, so power is about one in three.

assumptions.claim: In COVALENT-111 the pooled per-protocol placebo-adjusted HbA1c reduction with icovamenib at week 26 was 0.36 percentage points.
In the insulin-deficient subgroup of COVALENT-111, 100 mg once daily for 12 weeks gave a placebo-adjusted HbA1c reduction of 1.47 percentage points at week 26.
At week 52 of COVALENT-111, severe insulin-deficient patients given icovamenib for 12 weeks kept a placebo-adjusted HbA1c reduction of about 1.2 percentage points.

reason: Vehicle drops usually improve corneal staining by 1.5 to 2 points over 12 weeks, leaving little room for an untested compound to separate.
rationale: First sizeable efficacy trial of a Dompe compound with undisclosed mechanism, labelled exploratory. First phase 2 attempts on dry eye sign endpoints succeed about a third of the time because vehicle responses are large and variable (corneal staining SD near 2.8). Enrolment of 417 (3 x 139) suggests three arms, so each comparison has about 139 per arm and needs a 0.65-point difference; active drugs usually deliver 0.3-0.8. A private sponsor makes a public statement before mid-2027 unlikely.

assumptions.claim: In ESSENCE-2, total corneal fluorescein staining (NEI 0-15) fell by 4.0 points with water-free cyclosporine 0.1% and 3.6 points with vehicle at day 29, a difference of 0.4.
assumptions.source: ESSENCE-2, Akpek et al., JAMA Ophthalmol 2023

assumptions.claim: In GOBI, total corneal fluorescein staining fell by about 2.0 points with perfluorohexyloctane and 1.0 point with saline control at day 57.

reason: Molecular remission needs about eight months of therapy per patient and 150 newly diagnosed APL patients take years to enrol, so no remission result can be mature by mid-2027; anything public by then is an early stop or a partial pharmacokinetic statement.
rationale: IV arsenic trioxide plus ATRA yields molecular remission in nearly all evaluable low/intermediate-risk patients, and oral arsenic matched IV arsenic in a randomized Chinese trial, so non-inferiority is likely once the trial completes. But the registered March 2027 primary completion cannot cover remission in 150 patients enrolled from June 2026; it fits only the PK co-primary. Conditional on something public by June 2027, the statement is about as likely to be an early stop or partial PK readout, hence p_met near one half.
evidence: Zhu et al., oral arsenic RIF vs IV arsenic trioxide, Lancet Oncol 2018
ORH-2014 oral arsenic trioxide phase 1, Ravandi et al. 2020
AML17 APL comparison, Burnett et al. Lancet Oncol 2015

assumptions.claim: In APL0406, all 77 evaluable patients given ATRA plus IV arsenic trioxide achieved complete remission, and 2-year event-free survival was 97%.
Oral arsenic (realgar-indigo naturalis formula) plus ATRA was non-inferior to IV arsenic trioxide plus ATRA in non-high-risk APL, with 2-year event-free survival of 97% versus 94%.

reason: THR-beta agonists lower liver fat but have not reduced body weight in people, so the body-weight primaries are unlikely to separate from semaglutide alone over 11 weeks.
rationale: Five primaries must all be met under the round's rules: two on body weight and three on liver fat. Liver-targeted THR-beta agonists reliably cut MRI-PDFF (resmetirom, VK2809), but resmetirom produced no weight change in MAESTRO-NASH. Adding ECC4703 to escalating semaglutide for 11 weeks with about 50-75 per arm would need roughly 1.2-1.6 points of extra weight loss; I expect about 0.3. Eccogene is private, so disclosure is uncertain and may be selective.

assumptions.claim: Resmetirom did not change body weight relative to placebo over 52 weeks in MAESTRO-NASH.
In MAESTRO-NASH, resmetirom 100 mg reduced MRI-PDFF liver fat by about 47% at week 52 versus about 9% with placebo.
In STEP 1, semaglutide 2.4 mg gave a mean weight change of -14.9% at week 68 versus -2.4% with placebo.

reason: Antisense knockdown of angiotensinogen is reliable, so the threats are a week-4 reading taken before monthly dosing reaches full effect in an unstable post-discharge population, and a two-part trial that will not finish on the registered schedule.
rationale: The Part B primary is a pharmacodynamic biomarker: percent change in plasma angiotensinogen at week 4. Liver-targeted antisense against AGT lowered plasma AGT by 54-67% versus placebo in Ionis phase 2 studies with modest between-patient spread, so a significant difference is close to assured even with about 50 per arm. Blood pressure, the harder question, is only secondary. Recruiting recently hospitalised patients at 13 sites makes the December 2026 completion date unrealistic, and a private sponsor will probably wait for a congress.
evidence: IONIS-AGT-LRx phase 2 studies, Morgan et al. JACC Basic Transl Sci 2021

assumptions.claim: IONIS-AGT-LRx 80 mg weekly lowered plasma angiotensinogen by 54% as monotherapy and 67% as add-on therapy versus placebo in two phase 2 hypertension studies.
assumptions.source: Morgan et al., JACC Basic Transl Sci 2021

assumptions.claim: Blood pressure reductions with IONIS-AGT-LRx in those phase 2 studies were not statistically significant.
assumptions.source: Morgan et al., JACC Basic Transl Sci 2021

assumptions.claim: Zilebesiran, an siRNA against angiotensinogen, lowered serum AGT by more than 90% and 24-hour systolic pressure by about 14-17 mmHg versus placebo at month 3 in KARDIA-1.

reason: The mechanism is undisclosed and a single oral dose must act within hours; a slow-onset or modestly effective agent would not separate from placebo before rescue medication blurs the comparison.
rationale: Third molar extraction is the most sensitive acute pain model: low placebo response, and about 50 patients per arm detect a 1-point NRS difference; with dose-ranging any dose can succeed. LY4515100's mechanism is not public. Lilly bought SiteOne's Nav1.8 inhibitor STC-004 in 2025; if this is that asset, suzetrigine shows the class works in acute pain, though modestly and with slow onset. Blending a Nav1.8 scenario (55-60%) with an unknown-mechanism scenario (about 35%) gives just under one half.

assumptions.claim: Suzetrigine beat placebo on SPID48 after abdominoplasty and bunionectomy (differences of 48.4 and 29.3) but was not superior to hydrocodone-acetaminophen.
assumptions.source: Suzetrigine phase 3 trials, Vertex 2024; Bertoch et al., Anesthesiology 2025

assumptions.claim: Eli Lilly agreed in 2025 to acquire SiteOne Therapeutics and its Nav1.8 inhibitor STC-004 for pain.
assumptions.source: Lilly and SiteOne Therapeutics announcement, May 2025

reason: P2X3 antagonism has no clinical proof in IBS and has disappointed in other non-cough indications, while placebo typically cuts abdominal pain by nearly 2 points.
rationale: First test of a P2X3 antagonist in IBS, so the prior is a novel mechanism in a condition with high placebo response. Placebo arms in IBS pain trials improve by about 1.5-2 points on the 0-10 scale; established drugs add 0.3-0.7. Olorinab's phase 2b missed on the same abdominal pain endpoint, and P2X3 blockade has not worked outside cough. With roughly 105-140 per arm, significance needs about 0.5 points. GSK rarely announces phase 2 results quickly, so disclosure by June 2027 is unlikely.
evidence: Eluxadoline phase 3, Lembo et al. NEJM 2016

assumptions.claim: Olorinab did not meet its primary endpoint of change in average abdominal pain score at week 12 in the CAPTIVATE phase 2b trial in IBS-C and IBS-D.
In SOOTHE, camlipixant 50 mg and 200 mg twice daily reduced 24-hour cough frequency by about 34% versus placebo, with taste adverse events in under 7% of patients.
assumptions.source: SOOTHE phase 2b, NCT04678206; BELLUS Health topline December 2021

reason: With 18 women per arm a cure-rate gap of about 35 points is needed for significance, and occidiofungin gel has no prior human efficacy data to suggest an effect that large over a placebo gel.
rationale: First efficacy test of occidiofungin gel; no human efficacy data. With 18 per arm, significance needs roughly a 35-point cure gap. Placebo cure with symptom score 0 ran 29-44% at later test-of-cure visits in the VANISH trials and is likely lower at day 8. Topical antifungals can reach 55-65%, but a novel class is discounted. The primary spans three visits plus safety, so a clean statement that it was met is less likely. Small private sponsor, single site.

assumptions.claim: In VANISH-303, clinical cure at test-of-cure was 28.6% with placebo versus 50.5% with ibrexafungerp.
In VANISH-306, clinical cure at test-of-cure was 44.0% with placebo versus 63.3% with ibrexafungerp.

reason: Tirzepatide is the strongest marketed comparator and HDM1005 is in the same GLP-1/GIP class, so a gap of more than 2 points in its favour, needed for superiority with 93 per arm, is unlikely unless the top dose is pushed well beyond tirzepatide-equivalent exposure.
rationale: HDM1005 is a GLP-1/GIP dual agonist of tirzepatide's class, so parity is the default; beating tirzepatide by the roughly 2.3 points needed with 93 per arm is unlikely unless dose level 3 exceeds tirzepatide-equivalent exposure. Open-label design and a sponsor-chosen comparator dose help somewhat. The hypothesis may be non-inferiority, which would be easier, and three doses give three chances. SURMOUNT-CN gave -17.5% at 52 weeks for 15 mg, so about -16% at week 40. Huadong may announce topline only after week 52.

assumptions.claim: In SURMOUNT-CN, tirzepatide 15 mg gave a mean weight change of -17.5% at week 52 versus -2.3% with placebo in Chinese adults with obesity or overweight.
In SURMOUNT-CN, tirzepatide 10 mg gave a mean weight change of -13.6% at week 52.
HDM1005 is a once-weekly GLP-1 and GIP receptor dual agonist, the same mechanism class as tirzepatide.

reason: M4 positive allosteric modulation has not held up in schizophrenia: emraclidine failed two phase 2 trials, so the true effect of NS-136 may be only a few PANSS points, too small to detect with 50 patients per arm.
rationale: NS-136 is an M4 positive allosteric modulator. Emraclidine, the same mechanism, failed both EMPOWER phase 2 trials; the M4 agonist NBI-1117568 worked at one dose only. Chinese inpatient 5-week trials usually show a modest placebo response (about -11) and decent signal detection, and two doses give two chances. With 50 per arm and SD near 18, an observed gap of about 7.5 points is needed. Expected true effect is about 4 points.

assumptions.claim: Emraclidine, an M4 positive allosteric modulator, did not separate from placebo on PANSS total at week 6 in either EMPOWER-1 or EMPOWER-2.
assumptions.source: EMPOWER-1 NCT05227690 and EMPOWER-2 NCT05227703, AbbVie announcement November 2024

assumptions.claim: In EMERGENT-2, PANSS total changed by -11.6 with placebo and -21.2 with xanomeline-trospium at week 5.
NS-136 is an M4 muscarinic receptor positive allosteric modulator.

reason: The 15-minute endpoint should be met easily, but the co-primary at 14 hours after a single dose asks for a duration beyond the 8 hours shown for low-dose brimonidine, and the late effect may be too small to reach significance.
rationale: Apraclonidine is an alpha agonist with well-known conjunctival blanching; the 15-minute endpoint is near certain, as brimonidine 0.025% showed about a 1-point gap early after dosing. The risk is the co-primary at 14 hours, beyond brimonidine's 8-hour claim, the day after a single dose. Alcon sized the trial (115 per arm) for a small late effect and presumably has phase 2 duration data. Both co-primaries must be met. Alcon rarely announces such readouts, so publication by mid-2027 is unlikely.
evidence: Ackerman 2019, integrated analysis of four brimonidine 0.025% trials

assumptions.claim: Brimonidine 0.025% significantly reduced investigator-assessed ocular redness versus vehicle from 5 minutes through 8 hours after a single dose.
Vehicle-treated eyes in the brimonidine 0.025% redness trials showed only a small fall in redness score after instillation, well under half a point.
assumptions.source: Ackerman 2019 integrated analysis of four trials

reason: The mechanism of HSK55718 is not disclosed and each arm has only about 40 patients; if its analgesic effect is modest, rescue opioid use in the placebo arm can narrow the SPID gap below significance.
rationale: Haisco analgesic of undisclosed class tested against placebo with morphine as active reference, which suggests opioid-like efficacy is expected. Chinese placebo-controlled trials after abdominal surgery with rescue analgesia have almost always separated active analgesics from placebo (anrikefon, tegileridine, oliceridine). Three doses, about 40 per arm, one sufficient. Uncertainty: unknown mechanism, small arms, and rescue opioid in the placebo arm narrowing the SPID gap. Haisco seldom announces phase 2 results.

assumptions.claim: Haisco's HSK21542 (anrikefon) met its primary SPID 0-24 h endpoint against placebo for pain after abdominal surgery in its Chinese phase 3 trial.
assumptions.source: HSK21542 phase 3 trial in abdominal surgery, Haisco, 2023-2024

assumptions.claim: Oliceridine was superior to placebo on its primary analgesic endpoint over 24 hours after abdominoplasty.

reason: With 25 patients per arm, significance on IHS4-55 needs a gap of roughly 35-40 points over placebo, more than established HS biologics achieve, so even an active drug would probably miss.
rationale: Biologic of undisclosed target in a first HS proof-of-concept. With 25 per arm, two-sided significance needs roughly a 35-40 point gap in IHS4-55, more than adalimumab or IL-17 blockers produce over placebo on HiSCR (15-30 points). Placebo IHS4-55 at week 12 should be about 25-30%. A proof-of-concept design may use a looser success criterion, which lifts the chance slightly. Almirall would probably mention topline in results presentations during 2027.

assumptions.claim: In PIONEER I and II, HiSCR at week 12 was reached by 26.0% and 27.6% of placebo patients versus 41.8% and 58.9% on adalimumab.
assumptions.source: PIONEER I and II, NCT01468207 and NCT01468233

assumptions.claim: IHS4-55 was developed and validated as a dichotomous outcome using the PIONEER I and II adalimumab trial data.
assumptions.source: Tham 2022, J Eur Acad Dermatol Venereol

reason: The symptom benefit in TNFR1 genotype carriers rests on small subgroup analyses of earlier trials and may shrink on replication, while dry eye symptom scores improve a lot on vehicle alone.
rationale: Licaminlimab improved ocular discomfort in a Novartis phase 2 trial, and a TNFR1 genotype subgroup responded more; the RELIEF phase 2b trial supported the genotype mainly on signs. The symptom effect in carriers comes from small subgroups, so shrinkage is expected. Dry eye symptom endpoints fail often because of vehicle response; the artificial-tear run-in helps. The genotype-positive primary set may be well under 160. Enrollment is complete, so topline should come in early 2027.

assumptions.claim: In the phase 2 trial of licaminlimab (LME636), global ocular discomfort improved significantly more than with vehicle at day 29.
Oculis reported that in the phase 2b RELIEF trial the treatment effect on signs was larger in patients carrying a specific TNFR1 genotype.
assumptions.source: RELIEF phase 2b topline, Oculis press release, 2024

reason: Twenty patients against ten on placebo cannot show a significant difference in treatment failure unless the gap is about 45 points or more, larger than adalimumab achieved in VISUAL I.
rationale: The design copies VISUAL I and NEPTUNE: steroid taper with failure counted from week 6. Placebo failure by week 24 should be 60-75%. Even a brepocitinib-like result (about 30% failure) gives only borderline significance with 20 versus 10 patients. The mechanism of FXS5626 is not given in the record, and a phase 2 this small may have no formal hypothesis. The trial was still recruiting four months before a primary completion that needs 24 weeks of follow-up.

assumptions.claim: In VISUAL I, median time to treatment failure was 13 weeks with placebo and 24 weeks with adalimumab.
In NEPTUNE, treatment failure at week 24 occurred in 29% of patients on brepocitinib 45 mg and 44% on 15 mg.

reason: A 24-patient dose-comparison trial run by a small company across six sites, with outside adjudication of every eligibility decision, is likely to enrol slowly and finish after its January 2027 target.
rationale: Tiny single-blind dose-comparison trial by a small company at six US sites; mild infected diabetic foot ulcers with external adjudication of eligibility slow enrollment, and the trial started only in August 2026 with completion planned for January 2027. Slippage past May 2027 is close to even odds. Posting within months of completion is rare for small sponsors. The record carries leftover template text, so edits are likely, but changes of substance to the primary outcomes are uncommon.

reason: Lacripep missed its primary endpoints in its only earlier controlled trial, and patients entering at the top of the staining scale will improve on vehicle alone, leaving little room for the half-grade gap that 27 per arm requires.
rationale: Lacripep missed its primary endpoints in a 204-patient phase 2 trial in Sjogren's dry eye, with only post hoc signals. Stage 1 neurotrophic keratitis patients enter at the scale maximum (central staining grade 3), so the vehicle arm will improve through regression and lubrication. With 27 per arm and SD near 0.9, about a 0.5-grade gap is needed. Lacritin biology (epithelial and nerve support) is plausible but clinically unproven. Enrollment of this narrow population may run late.
evidence: Lacripep phase 2 in primary Sjogren's syndrome (NCT03226444), 2023

assumptions.claim: Lacripep did not meet its primary endpoints in the phase 2 trial in dry eye associated with primary Sjogren's syndrome.

reason: With about 22 women per arm, frequent spontaneous normalisation of ASC-US/LSIL cytology within weeks, and two efficacy primaries (cytology regression and hr-HPV clearance) that must both be significant, this proof-of-concept study has little power even if the suppository has some activity.
rationale: Tiny single-site proof-of-concept (45 women) with safety plus two efficacy primaries, all of which must be met. ASC-US/LSIL cytology often reverts to normal on repeat sampling within months, so placebo regression near 35% is plausible, while hr-HPV clearance seven weeks after baseline is uncommon. EGCG evidence is mixed: a small Korean study with untreated controls was positive, but the randomized oral Polyphenon E trial was null. Significance needs roughly a 40-point difference in each endpoint, so success on both is unlikely.
evidence: Garcia et al., Polyphenon E in persistent hr-HPV and low-grade CIN, Gynecol Oncol 2014
Ahn et al., green tea extracts in cervical lesions, Eur J Cancer Prev 2003

assumptions.claim: In a randomized phase 2 trial, oral Polyphenon E (green tea catechins including EGCG) did not improve hr-HPV clearance or regression of low-grade CIN versus placebo.
About 65% of untreated controls with ASC-US/LSIL had normal cytology with concordant colposcopy at 6 months in the Paloma trial.
assumptions.source: Paloma trial, Serrano et al., J Low Genit Tract Dis 2021

assumptions.claim: Green tea extract preparations gave a 69% response in cervical lesions versus 10% in untreated controls in a small Korean study.
assumptions.source: Ahn et al., Eur J Cancer Prev 2003

reason: Fifteen patients per arm cannot detect much less than a 2-point mVSS difference, and anti-IL-11 efficacy in established scars is unproven; 12 weeks may also be too short to remodel mature scar tissue.
rationale: First patient study of an anti-IL-11 antibody in pathological scars, 30 patients, with safety and PK as much the aim as efficacy. Established scars (stable for six months, mVSS 9 or more) change little on placebo, but remodelling within 12 weeks from systemic IL-11 blockade is speculative; clinical proof of anti-IL-11 efficacy in any fibrotic disease is still lacking. Significance needs a roughly 2-point mVSS gap. Publication by mid-2027 is unlikely and would skew positive.
evidence: Schafer et al., IL-11 in fibrosis, Nature 2017

assumptions.claim: IL-11 drives fibroblast activation and fibrosis in preclinical models, and blocking it reduces fibrosis in mice.

reason: The 15-minute endpoint is near-certain for an alpha-agonist vasoconstrictor; the risk is the co-primary at 600 minutes, where the drug-vehicle gap will be small and must still reach significance with 89 per arm.
rationale: Apraclonidine is an alpha-agonist that blanches conjunctival vessels; low-dose brimonidine 0.025% beat vehicle by about 0.9 units across 5 to 240 minutes in its trials, so the 15-minute primary should be met easily. Both primaries must be met, and the 600-minute one tests duration beyond the 8 hours claimed for brimonidine. Alcon presumably chose 10 hours from earlier data, and 178 subjects can detect about 0.25 units, but a fading effect makes this the real hurdle.
evidence: Ackerman et al., integrated analysis of brimonidine 0.025%, 2019
Torkildsen et al., brimonidine 0.025% for ocular redness, 2018

assumptions.claim: Across brimonidine 0.025% trials, mean investigator-assessed redness over 5 to 240 minutes after instillation was about 0.62 with brimonidine versus 1.49 with vehicle.
assumptions.source: Ackerman et al., Clin Exp Optom 2019 (integrated analysis)

assumptions.claim: The brimonidine 0.025% phase 3 efficacy trial showed significantly lower redness than vehicle at every time point from 5 to 240 minutes on Day 1.

reason: The hypothesis comes from a post-hoc age subgroup of a phase 2a that missed in the overall population; with large intra-articular placebo responses, the true effect is probably too small for both WOMAC pain and function to reach significance.
rationale: Enlivex's phase 1/2a missed significance in all patients at 3 months; the benefit was confined to older patients with age-related primary OA, which this trial now enrols (age 64 and over). Subgroup-derived effects usually shrink on replication, and three intra-articular placebo injections give a large response (about 9 of 50 points). Both WOMAC pain and function must be significant. With 91 per arm and SD near 11, a true difference of about 4.5 points is needed for good power; I expect about 2.
evidence: Enlivex Allocetra knee OA phase 1/2a topline, 2025
Saltzman et al., intra-articular saline placebo meta-analysis, 2017

assumptions.claim: In Enlivex's phase 1/2a knee OA trial, the 3-month pain benefit of Allocetra over placebo was not statistically significant in the overall population and was significant only in the age-related primary OA subgroup.
Intra-articular saline placebo produces a clinically meaningful improvement in knee OA pain lasting up to 6 months.
assumptions.source: Saltzman et al., Am J Sports Med 2017

reason: Failure would need an unexpectedly weak or short-lived knockdown, or very noisy triglyceride values in a 40-patient study; APOC3 silencing has reliably halved triglycerides in this population.
rationale: RBD5044 is a GalNAc siRNA against APOC3. The class is validated: plozasiran and olezarsen cut triglycerides by about 50 to 60% against placebo in moderate hypertriglyceridemia, and RBD5044's early studies showed deep apoC-III lowering. Week 16 falls four weeks after the second dose, near peak effect. Even with 40 patients and SD near 30%, a 50-point difference is overwhelmingly significant. Main uncertainty is whether and when a Chinese sponsor reports. LDL-C, the key secondary, is usually unchanged.

assumptions.claim: Plozasiran lowered fasting triglycerides by roughly 50 to 62% versus placebo at week 24 in mixed hyperlipidemia.
assumptions.source: MUIR, Ballantyne et al., N Engl J Med 2024

assumptions.claim: Olezarsen lowered triglycerides by 49 and 53 percentage points versus placebo at 6 months with 50 mg and 80 mg.
assumptions.source: Bridge-TIMI 73a, Bergmark et al., N Engl J Med 2024

reason: Vehicle gels improve mild-to-moderate eczema by a quarter or more in four weeks; if skin delivery of VC005 is modest or the 120 patients are split over several dose arms, the EASI gap may not reach significance.
rationale: VC005 is a JAK1-selective inhibitor formulated as a gel. Topical JAK inhibitors have been reliably effective in mild-to-moderate atopic dermatitis: ruxolitinib cream and delgocitinib ointment separated from vehicle on EASI within four weeks by wide margins. With 60 per arm, a 2-point EASI difference (SD about 3.5) gives high power. Risks are formulation or potency shortfalls, strong vehicle response, and splitting patients across dose arms. Public reporting by mid-2027 is unlikely for this sponsor.
evidence: Nakagawa et al., delgocitinib ointment phase 3, 2020

assumptions.claim: Ruxolitinib 1.5% cream twice daily improved EASI by 71.6% at week 4 versus 15.5% with vehicle in mild-to-moderate atopic dermatitis.
assumptions.source: Kim et al., J Allergy Clin Immunol 2020 (NCT03011892)

assumptions.claim: Delgocitinib 0.5% ointment changed modified EASI by about -44% at week 4 versus about +2% with vehicle.
assumptions.source: Nakagawa et al., J Am Acad Dermatol 2020

reason: KCNT1 epilepsy is ultra-rare, so the randomized part will be small and slow; seizure counts vary widely, and any statement by mid-2027 will probably be open-label Part 1 data, not a Part 2 efficacy test.
rationale: The efficacy primary sits in Part 2, a 12-week placebo-controlled part that follows an open-label Part 1 in an ultra-rare paediatric epilepsy with two US sites. A January 2027 completion is implausible for Part 2; anything public by June 2027 is likely Part 1 safety or uncontrolled seizure data, which would not count as met. A selective KCNT1 inhibitor is rational for gain-of-function variants, but quinidine failed in a controlled test and about 20 per arm gives weak power.
evidence: Mullen et al., quinidine in KCNT1 epilepsy, Neurology 2018

assumptions.claim: Quinidine, a non-selective KCNT1 blocker, did not reduce seizures in a randomized crossover trial in KCNT1-related epilepsy.

reason: The only real risk is a small single-centre sample meeting a strong brushing (Hawthorne) improvement in the control arm, or the plaque index missing while gingivitis is met.
rationale: Stannous fluoride toothpastes consistently beat regular fluoride toothpaste on gingivitis and plaque in six-month examiner-blinded trials, including Colgate's own stabilized SnF2 formulas, with gingival index reductions near 20 to 25% against control. Colgate's standard design of about 42 per arm is sized for this effect and between-subject variation is small (SD about 0.2). Both gingival and plaque indices must be significant, which they usually are. Reporting is the main uncertainty; journal publication typically takes over a year.
evidence: Hu et al., stabilized stannous fluoride dentifrice 6-month trial, JADA 2019

assumptions.claim: A stabilized stannous fluoride dentifrice gave statistically significant reductions in both gingival and plaque indices versus a regular fluoride dentifrice at 3 and 6 months.
assumptions.source: Hu et al., J Am Dent Assoc 2019

reason: Failure would need bempedoic acid to perform far better than in CLEAR or obicetrapib far worse than in BROADWAY; the expected 15-point LDL-C gap is many standard errors wide with 426 patients.
rationale: Obicetrapib 10 mg lowered LDL-C by about 30 to 36% on top of statins in BROADWAY, BROOKLYN and TANDEM; bempedoic acid gave about 15 to 17% at week 12 in CLEAR Harmony and Wisdom, less on high-intensity statins. An expected gap near 15 points, SD about 27 and 213 per arm gives a standard error under 3, so superiority (or non-inferiority, if so designed) is very likely. Non-HDL-C should follow. Timing depends on enrolling 426 patients.

assumptions.claim: Obicetrapib 10 mg changed LDL-C by -29.9% at day 84 versus +2.7% with placebo on top of maximally tolerated lipid-lowering therapy.
assumptions.source: BROADWAY, Nicholls et al., N Engl J Med 2025

assumptions.claim: Bempedoic acid changed LDL-C by -16.5% at week 12 versus +1.6% with placebo on top of maximally tolerated statins.
assumptions.source: CLEAR Harmony, Ray et al., N Engl J Med 2019

assumptions.claim: Bempedoic acid changed LDL-C by -15.1% at week 12 versus +2.4% with placebo.
assumptions.source: CLEAR Wisdom, Goldberg et al., JAMA 2019

reason: A short crossover safety study in stable asthma run by GSK should enrol and finish close to schedule; results are due on the registry within a year of completion, so posting by August 2027 is possible but not the default.
rationale: Primary outcome is adverse events only, so no efficacy call. 110 stable asthma patients across 18 sites and an eight-week crossover should complete near February 2027. GSK rarely stops such supportive propellant studies and usually posts results close to the 12-month deadline, which falls after the read date.

reason: A novel TRPM8 mechanism backed by a single phase 2b could regress to a placebo-adjusted gain too small on 2-hour pain freedom or on the most-bothersome-symptom co-primary.
rationale: Elismetrep is a first-in-class oral TRPM8 antagonist; its phase 2b was reported positive on 2-hour pain freedom and most-bothersome-symptom freedom at the top dose, which is why an 1,800-patient US phase 3 followed. With about 900 per arm the trial detects a 4-point pain-freedom difference, so a gepant-like 6-9 point gain would pass both co-primaries comfortably. The risk is a single phase 2b for a novel mechanism regressing in phase 3. Placebo pain freedom in recent US single-attack trials runs 11-15%.
evidence: Kallyope elismetrep (K-304) phase 2b in acute migraine, 2025

assumptions.claim: In ACHIEVE I, 2-hour pain freedom was 11.8% with placebo versus 19.2% with ubrogepant 50 mg and 21.2% with 100 mg.
In rimegepant Study 303, 2-hour pain freedom was 21.2% with rimegepant orally disintegrating tablet versus 10.9% with placebo.
Kallyope reported that the phase 2b trial of elismetrep in acute migraine met its 2-hour pain freedom and most-bothersome-symptom endpoints at the highest dose.
assumptions.source: Kallyope press release on the elismetrep (K-304) phase 2b trial, 2025

reason: A 108-patient crossover loses power if patients fail to treat both attacks or if lung delivery from the dry-powder inhaler gives a smaller 2-hour pain-free gain than MAP0004 did.
rationale: Orally inhaled DHE has proof of concept: MAP0004 gave 28% versus 10% 2-hour pain freedom in FREEDOM-301, whereas the slower nasal powder STS101 missed this endpoint twice. ASY202 is a dry-powder inhaled DHE at 2.0 mg, and its 10- and 30-minute pain-relief secondaries suggest fast absorption. A crossover of 108 patients gives about 80% power for a 15-17 point difference if around 90 treat both attacks; attrition, period effects or lower lung delivery than MAP0004 would erode this.

assumptions.claim: In FREEDOM-301, orally inhaled DHE (MAP0004) gave 2-hour pain freedom of 28.4% versus 10.1% with placebo.
The DHE nasal powder STS101 did not reach significance on 2-hour pain freedom in the phase 3 SUMMIT trial.

reason: Short descriptive Pfizer vaccine study likely to finish close to schedule, with results posted near the 12-month deadline rather than by August 2027.
rationale: Pfizer descriptive safety and immunogenicity study of RSVpreF for Indian registration: one vaccination with 3 months of SAE follow-up, so the January 2027 date holds if enrolment of 540 closed by late October 2026. Pfizer keeps registry dates current and usually posts results near the 12-month deadline, so posting by August 2027 is unlikely. Descriptive safety and immunogenicity outcomes rarely change, and a stop is improbable for a licensed vaccine.

reason: A large placebo fall in blood pressure, as in the HALO trial of baxdrostat, could hide the effect in arms of about 63 patients.
rationale: SAL0140 is an aldosterone synthase inhibitor; the class lowers office systolic pressure about 8-11 mmHg beyond placebo at 12 weeks (baxdrostat BrigHTN and BaxHTN, lorundrostat Launch-HTN). With 63 per arm and SD near 13 mmHg, the trial has over 90% power for a 9 mmHg effect and one significant dose suffices. Risks are a large placebo fall as in HALO, an unproven molecule and dose choice. A Chinese phase 2 seldom reports publicly within months.

assumptions.claim: Baxdrostat 2 mg lowered seated systolic pressure 11.0 mmHg more than placebo at 12 weeks in BrigHTN, where placebo fell 9.4 mmHg.
The phase 2 HALO trial of baxdrostat missed its primary endpoint, with placebo systolic pressure falling about 16.6 mmHg.
Lorundrostat 50 mg lowered automated office systolic pressure 9.1 mmHg more than placebo at week 6 in Launch-HTN.

reason: hsCRP is highly variable and arms are small, so only poor exposure, adherence or tolerability at the tested doses would prevent a significant reduction.
rationale: BGE-102 is an oral NLRP3 inhibitor; BioAge reported hsCRP reductions around 86% after two weeks in phase 1 participants with obesity and raised hsCRP, and the class (VTX3232) held about 78% reductions over 12 weeks. With 40 per arm and effects of this size, at least one dose should be clearly significant on percent change in hsCRP. Dosing ends by late 2026 and BioAge, a listed company, should release topline quickly. Residual risks are tolerability, adherence and hsCRP variability.
evidence: VTX3232 phase 2 in obesity with cardiovascular risk factors, 2025

assumptions.claim: BioAge reported a median hsCRP reduction of about 86% after 14 days of BGE-102 in phase 1 participants with obesity and elevated hsCRP.
assumptions.source: BioAge Labs BGE-102 phase 1 press release, 2026

assumptions.claim: The NLRP3 inhibitor VTX3232 lowered hsCRP by roughly 78% versus placebo over 12 weeks in participants with obesity and cardiovascular risk factors.

reason: Oral bioavailability of the peptide tablet may give weight loss well below the injection, though even a few percent beyond placebo should be significant.
rationale: BGM0504 is a GLP-1/GIP dual agonist whose injection produced placebo-adjusted weight loss up to about 18% at 24 weeks in Chinese phase 2. The tablet needs only a few percent placebo-adjusted loss to be significant with 40 per arm over 20 weeks, and oral incretins (oral semaglutide 50 mg, orforglipron) reach 8-12% by then. The uncertainty is oral exposure and the size of the effect, not its existence. BrightGene usually discloses phase 2 topline by exchange filing, but perhaps after June 2027.

assumptions.claim: BGM0504 injection 15 mg gave placebo-adjusted weight loss of about 18.5% at 24 weeks in its Chinese phase 2 obesity trial.
Orforglipron reduced body weight by 8.6% to 12.6% at week 26 versus 2.0% with placebo in its phase 2 obesity trial.
Oral semaglutide 50 mg reduced body weight by 15.1% versus 2.4% with placebo at 68 weeks in OASIS 1.

reason: A herbal extract with thin independent evidence faces a sizeable placebo response on self-rated fatigue during chemotherapy, and both fatigue scales must be met.
rationale: Nuvastatic is a standardised Orthosiphon stamineus extract; an earlier company-sponsored phase 2 reported better BFI and visual analogue fatigue scores than placebo. Independent evidence for herbal agents in cancer fatigue is thin, placebo responses are sizeable and both fatigue measures must be met. Patients are starting chemotherapy, so fatigue may worsen in both arms. Anything public by June 2027 would probably be a favourable company statement, so the conditional chance is near even despite a doubtful true effect.
evidence: Nuvastatic (C5OSEW5050ESA) phase 2 trial in cancer-related fatigue, about 2023
NCCTG N07C2 (American ginseng for cancer-related fatigue), 2013

assumptions.claim: An earlier randomized, double-blind phase 2 trial reported that Nuvastatic 1000 mg three times daily improved Brief Fatigue Inventory and visual analogue fatigue scores versus placebo in patients with solid tumours.
assumptions.source: Nuvastatic (C5OSEW5050ESA) phase 2 cancer-related fatigue trial publication, about 2023

assumptions.claim: American ginseng 2000 mg daily improved fatigue versus placebo at 8 weeks in a trial of 364 patients.

reason: The primary is a single-dose 3-hour pain reduction on the last radiotherapy day, when opioid use, attrition and lozenge intolerance in severe mucositis can blur the difference from lidocaine.
rationale: Bupivacaine is long-acting while viscous lidocaine relieves mucositis pain for under an hour, so a 3-hour summed pain reduction favours the lozenge pharmacologically; the open-label design with self-rated pain adds to this. The phase 2 trial showed about 14 mm lower oral pain versus standard care including lidocaine. Risks: only about 75 per arm with attrition before the last radiotherapy day, heavy opioid use blunting differences, and lozenge tolerability in severe mucositis. OncoZenge is listed and must disclose topline promptly. Variability assumes summed pain difference in NRS point-hours.
evidence: Mogensen et al., bupivacaine lozenge phase 2 in oral mucositis, Pain Reports 2017
Mogensen et al., single-dose bupivacaine lozenge in head and neck cancer patients, 2016

assumptions.claim: In a randomized phase 2 trial in head and neck cancer, oral cavity pain was about 14 mm (0-100 VAS) lower with bupivacaine lozenges than with standard pain treatment including topical lidocaine.

reason: Failure would require WD-890 to be much less active than other TYK2 inhibitors on sPGA 0/1 or PASI 75, which its progression from phase 2 makes unlikely.
rationale: WD-890 is an oral TYK2 inhibitor tested against placebo with sPGA 0/1 and PASI 75 at week 16 as co-primaries. Deucravacitinib achieved about 54% versus 7% and 58% versus 13% in POETYK PSO-1, and larger gaps in the Asian PSO-3 trial; placebo rates in Chinese trials are below 10%. With 375 patients, any active TYK2 inhibitor that passed phase 2 clears both endpoints. The uncertainty is whether a private Chinese sponsor makes a public statement by mid-2027.

assumptions.claim: In POETYK PSO-1, sPGA 0/1 at week 16 was reached by 53.6% on deucravacitinib versus 7.2% on placebo, and PASI 75 by 58.4% versus 12.7%.
In POETYK PSO-3 in Asian patients, PASI 75 at week 16 was 68.8% with deucravacitinib versus 8.1% with placebo.

reason: If GQ1005 is less active than deruxtecan-type conjugates, a 228-patient trial against T-DM1 could miss, and slow accrual against reimbursed T-DXd delays the readout.
rationale: GQ1005 is a site-specific HER2 antibody-drug conjugate, believed to carry a topoisomerase I inhibitor payload; newer HER2 conjugates have repeatedly beaten T-DM1 on PFS (DESTINY-Breast03 hazard ratio about 0.3 with T-DM1 median 6.8 months; trastuzumab botidotin about 0.39 in China). 228 patients suffice for hazard ratios up to about 0.6. The trial was still recruiting in late 2026 against reimbursed T-DXd, so readout is probably late 2027 or after; an earlier statement would most likely be a positive interim analysis.
evidence: Trastuzumab botidotin (A166) vs T-DM1 phase 3 in China, 2025

assumptions.claim: In DESTINY-Breast03, trastuzumab deruxtecan versus T-DM1 gave a PFS hazard ratio of 0.28 at the interim analysis, with a T-DM1 median PFS of 6.8 months.
Trastuzumab botidotin (A166) improved centrally assessed PFS over T-DM1 in a Chinese phase 3 trial, with a hazard ratio near 0.39.
assumptions.source: Trastuzumab botidotin vs T-DM1 phase 3, ESMO 2025

assumptions.claim: In EMILIA, median PFS with T-DM1 was 9.6 months.

reason: With 68 per arm and strong background therapy, an effect smaller than the adult -1.3 points (noisy adolescent diaries, large placebo response, possibly patients with low eosinophils) could leave the 2-week rTNSS difference short of significance.
rationale: Stapokibart's adult phase 3 (PHECDA, eosinophils >=300) showed a 2-week rTNSS difference of about -1.3 (SD ~2), which would give >95% power here with 68 per arm; allowing shrinkage to about -1.0 and adolescent diary noise gives ~80%. The earlier all-comer phase 2 (MERAK) missed its primary, so enrichment matters. The 4-week design mirrors the adult trial. Season-bound enrolment (autumn 2026) is the main operational risk; Keymed usually announces pivotal readouts and sNDA acceptances.
evidence: PHECDA 2025 (stapokibart phase 3, adult seasonal allergic rhinitis)

assumptions.claim: In the adult phase 3 PHECDA trial, stapokibart improved mean daily rTNSS over 2 weeks by about 1.3 points more than placebo (about -3.6 vs -2.3).

The phase 2 MERAK trial of stapokibart in seasonal allergic rhinitis did not meet its primary endpoint in the overall population; benefit was seen post hoc in patients with blood eosinophils of 300 cells/uL or more.
PHECDA randomised 108 adults with blood eosinophils of 300 cells/uL or more within a single autumn pollen season.

reason: If the population is not enriched for high eosinophils, the IL-4Ra effect on 2-week rTNSS may be only about -0.6 points, as in the stapokibart all-comer phase 2, against a large placebo response in a short pollen-season trial.
rationale: SHR-1819 is an IL-4Ra antibody like stapokibart, which gained about -1.3 rTNSS points at 2 weeks in eosinophil-high adults (PHECDA) after an all-comer phase 2 failed. With 110 per arm and SD ~2.1, power is ~85% for -0.8 and >95% for -1.0. Enrolment is complete (active, not recruiting) within the 2026 autumn pollen season, so the trial should finish on time; Hengrui rarely publishes toplines before an NDA acceptance notice.
evidence: PHECDA 2025 (stapokibart phase 3, adult seasonal allergic rhinitis)

assumptions.claim: In the adult phase 3 PHECDA trial, the anti-IL-4Ra antibody stapokibart improved mean daily rTNSS over 2 weeks by about 1.3 points more than placebo.
The phase 2 MERAK trial of stapokibart in seasonal allergic rhinitis without eosinophil enrichment did not meet its primary rTNSS endpoint in the overall population.

reason: A magnesium salt oral spray has only small exploratory support for cough suppression; with about 30 per arm and highly variable cough counts, only an unusually large placebo-adjusted effect (roughly 35%) would reach significance.
rationale: Pilot phase 2 from a small company, about 30 per arm after a run-in, objective cough frequency by Hyfe monitor over 3 weeks. P2X3 antagonists achieve only 15-30% placebo-adjusted reductions in far larger trials, and the salt/hydration mechanism is supported only by small exploratory work. With a log-scale SD of change near 0.6, the detectable effect is about 35%. The chance of a statistically significant primary is low; a selective 'positive' release is possible.
evidence: Abubakar-Waziri et al. 2024 (exploratory study of alkaline hypertonic divalent salts in refractory chronic cough)

assumptions.claim: In COUGH-1, gefapixant 45 mg reduced 24-hour cough frequency by about 18% relative to placebo at 12 weeks, with a placebo-arm reduction of roughly half from baseline.
Clinical evidence for alkaline hypertonic divalent salt aerosols in refractory chronic cough comes from one small exploratory study of about a dozen patients.
assumptions.source: Abubakar-Waziri H et al., exploratory study of SC001 in refractory chronic cough, 2024

reason: Modern phacoemulsification in mostly grade 3 nuclear cataract causes modest endothelial loss (about 8-10%), leaving little room for a topical antioxidant to show a significant difference when the between-patient SD is near 300 cells/mm2.
rationale: Evidence for topical ascorbic acid protecting endothelium comes from laboratory work and small single-centre Taiwanese reports in hard nuclear cataract. Expected vehicle loss is ~200-250 cells/mm2 with SD ~300; with ~90 evaluable per arm a difference of ~90 cells/mm2 (over a third of the loss) is needed. Aqueous ascorbate is already high, so the incremental effect is uncertain. I put the true effect near 40 cells/mm2, giving about 30% chance of significance. The timeline (200 patients, 12-week follow-up, completion January 2027) looks optimistic.
evidence: Bourne et al. 2004 (endothelial cell loss after phacoemulsification)
Lee et al. 2019 (perioperative topical ascorbic acid, case reports and review)

assumptions.claim: Mean central endothelial cell loss after uncomplicated phacoemulsification is roughly 10% in the first year, and is higher with harder nuclei.
Case reports and a literature review from Chang Gung Memorial Hospital proposed perioperative topical ascorbic acid to limit phacoemulsification-related corneal endothelial damage.
assumptions.source: Lee CY et al., World J Clin Cases 2019

reason: With about 87 per arm, a 10-15 point gain in 72-hour complete response over palonosetron alone gives only about 30-55% power per dose; rescue use driven by nausea dilutes an NK1-type benefit that is mainly on vomiting.
rationale: HRS5580 is taken to be an injectable NK1 antagonist. Adding NK1 blockade to a 5-HT3 antagonist reliably cuts vomiting but improves complete response less (aprepitant versus ondansetron trials; fosaprepitant add-on trial in China). High-risk patients on palonosetron alone should reach about 55-60% complete response over 72 hours; I expect about +12 points. Two dose arms give two chances, so about 50% that one is significant. Hengrui phase 2 results are seldom public quickly.
evidence: Fosaprepitant for PONV after laparoscopic gastrointestinal surgery, Br J Anaesth 2023
Gan et al. 2007 (aprepitant vs ondansetron for PONV)
Diemunsch et al. 2007 (aprepitant vs ondansetron for PONV)

assumptions.claim: Adding fosaprepitant to dexamethasone and palonosetron lowered the 24-hour incidence of postoperative nausea and vomiting from about 49% to about 32% after laparoscopic gastrointestinal surgery.
assumptions.source: Fosaprepitant for PONV in laparoscopic gastrointestinal surgery, Br J Anaesth 2023

assumptions.claim: Oral aprepitant 40 mg was superior to ondansetron for preventing vomiting after surgery but not for complete response in the first 24 hours.
assumptions.source: Gan TJ et al., Anesth Analg 2007

reason: Percent change in F-VASI is noisy (SD about 40) and 50 per arm gives only about 65% power per dose for a 20-point difference at 24 weeks; a high placebo response in a single-country trial would erode it further.
rationale: QY201 is taken to be an oral JAK1/TYK2 inhibitor. Oral JAK inhibitors have consistently beaten placebo on F-VASI percent change at week 24 in phase 2 (ritlecitinib, upadacitinib, povorcitinib), with differences near 20 points. Three active doses against placebo give several chances, offset by small arms and possible multiplicity control. The record was registered late with status recruiting, so week-24 completion by December 2026 looks unlikely.

assumptions.claim: In the ritlecitinib phase 2b vitiligo trial, percent change in F-VASI at week 24 was about -21% with 50 mg after a loading dose versus about +2% with placebo.
assumptions.source: Ezzedine K et al., J Am Acad Dermatol 2023 (NCT03715829)

assumptions.claim: In the upadacitinib phase 2 vitiligo trial, the difference from placebo in percent change in F-VASI at week 24 was about -21 points for 11 mg and about -20 points for 22 mg.
Povorcitinib improved T-VASI by about 16-19% at week 24 versus a small worsening on placebo in its phase 2b vitiligo trial.

reason: Arms are small (60 patients split across dose groups and placebo), so a PASI 100 rate near 25-30% at week 12 could miss significance against a near-zero placebo rate.
rationale: PASI 100 at week 12 is near 0% on placebo in every biologic trial, while potent IL-23 or IL-17 class antibodies reach 25-45% in Chinese patients. Choosing PASI 100 as primary and the very long contraception window suggest a potent, long-acting antibody with phase 1 patient data behind it. With arms of 15-30, a 35% rate against 0-3% is significant about three times in four. Hengrui psoriasis trials enrol fast, so week-12 data by end-2026 is plausible.

assumptions.claim: In UltIMMa-1, PASI 100 at week 16 was reached by about 36% of risankizumab patients and 0% of placebo patients.
In BE READY, PASI 100 at week 16 was reached by about 68% of bimekizumab patients and about 1% of placebo patients.

reason: Whether a GIP receptor antagonist adds weight loss to semaglutide in humans is unproven; over 13 weeks with semaglutide only up to 1.0 mg, an extra loss under about 1.2 points would not be significant with 50 per arm.
rationale: AT673 is taken to be Antag's once-weekly GIP receptor antagonist. Support comes from animal combination data, human genetics and MariTide, not from a clean add-on trial. Semaglutide titrated to 1.0 mg in type 2 diabetes yields about -3.5% at 13 weeks (SD ~3). With 50 per arm the detectable difference is ~1.2-1.5 points; I expect about -0.9, so about 35-40% that a dose is significant. A private sponsor will likely release toplines quickly if positive.

assumptions.claim: Semaglutide 1.0 mg weekly produced about 4.5 kg mean weight loss at 30 weeks in type 2 diabetes versus about 1 kg with placebo.
Maridebart cafraglutide, which combines GIP receptor antagonism with GLP-1 agonism, gave up to about 20% weight loss at 52 weeks in obesity and up to about 17% in people who also had type 2 diabetes.
assumptions.source: MariTide phase 2 trial, N Engl J Med 2025

reason: Small safety and immunogenicity vaccine study that is already fully enrolled; follow-up to 240 days after dose 2 should finish close to the registered date, and results posting is unlikely before late 2027.
rationale: No efficacy goal. Enrolment is closed (active, not recruiting) and the last safety visit is fixed by the schedule, so lateness beyond 90 days is unlikely unless the adaptive design adds a cohort. Small Canadian sponsor with academic partners: posting on ClinicalTrials.gov within seven months of completion is rare. The six safety primaries are standard and unlikely to change.

reason: Non-inferiority would fail only if the chosen HRS-9190 dose gives slower or weaker block at the intubation time point, since rocuronium yields good or excellent conditions in nearly all patients.
rationale: Phase 3 non-inferiority on intubating conditions against rocuronium: with modern induction, 95-100% of rocuronium patients score good or excellent, and a dose of the new blocker chosen from phase 2 at 2-3 times ED95 should match it. With 160 per arm and a margin near 10 points, power is high. Hengrui anaesthesia phase 3 trials enrol in weeks and usually succeed; public results typically come with the NDA acceptance notice.
evidence: Cooper et al. 1992 (rocuronium vs suxamethonium intubating conditions)

assumptions.claim: Rocuronium 0.6 mg/kg gives good or excellent intubating conditions in about 95% of patients at 60 seconds and in nearly all at 90 seconds.
assumptions.source: Cooper R et al., Br J Anaesth 1992

reason: With 15 patients per arm and two co-primary endpoints that must both be significant, the trial needs an implausibly large advantage over a lubricating vehicle to succeed.
rationale: Tiny pivotal trial (15 per arm) with two co-primary endpoints that must both reach significance; that needs roughly a 1-SD advantage on both corneal staining and OSDI over a lubricating vehicle, which itself improves symptoms in dry-eye trials. d-MAPPS, a placental/amniotic-derived biologic drop, has only uncontrolled case-series support. Stable background therapy and a low staining entry threshold (grade 1 or more) limit room to improve. A small sponsor reporting quickly would likely spin results positively, but a formal double win is unlikely.
evidence: Harrell CR et al., d-MAPPS ocular case reports and series, 2019-2022

assumptions.claim: The record plans 30 participants in total and lists two co-primary endpoints, change in Modified Oxford corneal staining and change in OSDI total score, both at day 90.
Published clinical support for d-MAPPS eye drops consists of case reports and uncontrolled series rather than randomized controlled trials.
assumptions.source: Harrell CR et al., d-MAPPS publications 2019-2022

reason: A large placebo fall in office systolic pressure, as in HALO, or weak dose selection could blur separation when each arm has only about 64 patients.
rationale: The design copies BaxHTN (uncontrolled on 2 drugs or resistant on 3 or more, diuretic required), so SAL0120 is presumed to be an aldosterone synthase inhibitor; that class has given 8-11 mmHg placebo-adjusted office SBP falls at 12 weeks. With about 64 per arm and SD near 13, a 9 mmHg effect gives over 95% power, and any of three doses can win. The trial is completed and was registered late, suggesting presentable data. Risks: big placebo response, weaker molecule, vague public reporting.

assumptions.claim: In BaxHTN, baxdrostat 2 mg lowered seated systolic pressure about 9.8 mmHg more than placebo at week 12, with placebo falling about 5.8 mmHg.
In BrigHTN, baxdrostat 2 mg lowered systolic pressure 11.0 mmHg more than placebo at 12 weeks in resistant hypertension, with placebo falling 9.4 mmHg.
In Launch-HTN, lorundrostat 50 mg lowered office systolic pressure about 9.1 mmHg more than placebo at week 6.

reason: The oral formulation might give too little exposure for a clear separation by week 20, or the result may be disclosed only as positive without an explicit primary-endpoint statement.
rationale: MWN109 is an incretin-class peptide from Minwei (Lepu Medical). Oral incretins reliably beat placebo on weight within 20-26 weeks (orforglipron, oral semaglutide), and with about 50 per arm a placebo-adjusted loss of only 2-3% is enough. The sponsor also launched tablet studies in type 2 diabetes and weight maintenance, implying phase 1 activity. Four titrated doses give several chances. Uncertainties are oral exposure, tolerability-driven dropout, and a public statement lacking a clear primary-endpoint result.

assumptions.claim: In the phase 2 orforglipron obesity trial, mean weight change at week 26 ranged from -8.6% to -12.6% across doses versus -2.0% with placebo.
In OASIS 1, oral semaglutide 50 mg gave a mean weight change of -15.1% versus -2.4% with placebo at week 68.
The sponsor registered a separate phase 2 trial of MWN109 tablets in type 2 diabetes with placebo and oral semaglutide 14 mg controls.

reason: Failure would need an unexpectedly weak drug or heavy dropout in arms of about 31, or a public statement that only calls the result positive without a primary-endpoint finding.
