rationale: Injectable multi-agonist incretins give 12-18% placebo-adjusted weight loss by 24-52 weeks in Chinese trials (tirzepatide, mazdutide, HRS9531), so even 31 per arm is ample at 36 weeks. The tablet maintenance extension enrolled 71 participants who had lost at least 5% in the MWN109 injection phase 2, implying that most active-arm patients responded. Failure would need an unexpectedly weak drug or heavy dropout; the residual risk is vague disclosure.

assumptions.claim: In SURMOUNT-CN, tirzepatide 15 mg gave a mean weight change of about -17.5% versus -2.3% with placebo at week 52 in Chinese adults.
In GLORY-1, mazdutide 6 mg gave a mean weight change of about -14.0% at week 48 versus +0.3% with placebo in Chinese adults.
The MWN109 tablet maintenance extension lists 71 participants and requires a weight loss of at least 5% at the end of treatment in the MWN109 injection phase 2 study.

reason: Inadequate oral exposure at the tested doses, or a strong placebo response on background metformin, could shrink the HbA1c gap in arms of about 40 patients.
rationale: GLP-1-based agents lower HbA1c by 1.0-1.7 points versus placebo within 20-26 weeks at baseline HbA1c near 8.5% (oral semaglutide, orforglipron), and 40 per arm with SD about 1.0 detects 0.7 points with good power. Four MWN109 doses give several chances. Primary completion is March 2027, so a result public by June would most likely be a positive topline. Risks: inadequate oral exposure, strong placebo response, vague reporting.

assumptions.claim: In PIONEER 1, oral semaglutide 14 mg lowered HbA1c by about 1.4 points versus 0.3 points with placebo at week 26.
assumptions.source: PIONEER 1, Aroda et al., Diabetes Care 2019

assumptions.claim: In the phase 2 orforglipron type 2 diabetes trial, HbA1c fell by up to 2.10 points versus 0.43 points with placebo at week 26.
The record plans about 240 participants across four MWN109 dose arms, placebo and oral semaglutide 14 mg, with HbA1c at entry between 7.5% and 11.0%.

reason: The 24-week extension has passed its registered primary completion and should close quietly, with no results posted on ClinicalTrials.gov, as is usual for Chinese phase 2 sponsors.
rationale: Open-label maintenance extension comparing daily and weekly tablet schedules, already active not recruiting with primary completion registered for September 2026, so there is little reason to stop it. Chinese biotech sponsors rarely post results on ClinicalTrials.gov, and a record registered around completion seldom changes its primary outcome.

reason: With 30 patients per arm, the modest edge of an anti-inflammatory drop over a lubricating vehicle on corneal staining is unlikely to reach significance.
rationale: TJO-087 is presumed to be Taejoon's cyclosporine nanoemulsion. Cyclosporine's advantage over vehicle on corneal staining is small (about 0.4 NEI points in ESSENCE-2, needing hundreds per arm), and lubricating vehicles improve staining by about 2 points. With 30 per arm and SD near 2.6, only a difference above roughly 1.3 points reaches significance. Two active arms give two chances and small Korean studies sometimes show larger effects, but power is low.
evidence: Sall et al. cyclosporine emulsion phase 3, 2000

assumptions.claim: In ESSENCE-2, water-free cyclosporine 0.1% improved total corneal fluorescein staining (NEI 0-15) by about 4.0 points versus 3.6 with vehicle at day 29, a difference of about 0.4 points.
assumptions.source: ESSENCE-2, Akpek et al., JAMA Ophthalmol 2023

assumptions.claim: The record plans 90 participants across two TJO-087 arms and one vehicle arm and requires an NEI corneal staining score of at least 4.

reason: Coartem cures about 95-99% of children on PCR-corrected day-29 response, so a single-dose combination cannot show a statistically significant improvement in a 120-patient cohort.
rationale: Cohort C2 is an open-label phase 2 estimation cohort with no registered hypothesis; the card treats it as superiority over Coartem, whose PCR-corrected day-29 cure rate is about 94-99% in African children, leaving no room for a significant gain with about 60 per arm. A single-dose cipargamin plus ganaplacide-lumefantrine regimen is more likely to match or trail a 3-day ACT. Met would require the sponsor to report a prespecified threshold criterion as achieved.

assumptions.claim: In KALUMA, the PCR-corrected cure rate was 97.4% with ganaplacide-lumefantrine versus 94.1% with Coartem under the estimand analysis, and 99.2% versus 96.7% per protocol.
assumptions.source: KALUMA phase 3, Novartis press release November 2025

assumptions.claim: In the first phase 2 study of KAE609 (cipargamin), median parasite clearance time was about 12 hours.
The record describes an open-label two-arm cohort of 120 children aged 2 to under 12 years and states no hypothesis or non-inferiority margin.

reason: A high rate of spontaneous anterior chamber cell clearing by day 14 in untreated micro-incision cataract eyes could shrink the gap, and both the inflammation and pain endpoints must be met.
rationale: Depot steroids given at surgery consistently beat placebo for anterior chamber cell clearing and pain (Dextenza, Dexycu), and 4 mg subconjunctival triamcinolone performed comparably to topical prednisolone in large cohort data. With 125 per arm the trial detects gaps of about 15 points. Both co-primaries must be met; pain-free rates usually separate well because rescued patients count as failures. The main risk is a high sham clearing rate after micro-incision surgery, as in the second Dextenza trial.
evidence: Shorstein et al. subconjunctival triamcinolone cohort, 2024
Paganelli et al. sub-Tenon triamcinolone after cataract surgery, 2004

assumptions.claim: Across the three Dextenza phase 3 trials, absence of anterior chamber cells at day 14 was 33.1%, 39.4% and 52.3% with the insert versus 14.5%, 31.3% and 31.1% with placebo vehicle.
assumptions.source: Dextenza prescribing information; Tyson et al., J Cataract Refract Surg 2019

assumptions.claim: In the Dexycu phase 3 trial, anterior chamber cell clearing at day 8 was 60% with dexamethasone 517 micrograms versus 20% with placebo.
The record lists two primary outcomes, no anterior chamber cells at day 14 and no ocular pain at day 8, and states the trial will support a supplemental New Drug Application.

reason: If the tested doses give less angiotensinogen knockdown than zilebesiran, or patients stay on background therapy, the office systolic effect could shrink toward the roughly 5 mmHg seen in KARDIA-3.
rationale: GW906 is presumed to be an angiotensinogen-targeting siRNA like zilebesiran, which cut office SBP about 9-12 mmHg versus placebo at month 3 in KARDIA-1. With 319 patients (probably several dose arms of about 64) and SD near 13, a 9 mmHg effect gives high power. Salubris runs hypertension trials routinely and the week-12 primary is complete. Risks: background therapy blunting the effect as in KARDIA-3, insufficient knockdown, a large office placebo response, or vague disclosure.

assumptions.claim: In KARDIA-1, zilebesiran lowered 24-hour mean ambulatory systolic pressure at month 3 by at least 14 mmHg more than placebo (14.1 to 16.7 mmHg across regimens).
In KARDIA-2, zilebesiran added to indapamide, amlodipine or olmesartan lowered 24-hour systolic pressure at month 3 by about 12.1, 9.7 and 4.0 mmHg more than placebo.
In KARDIA-3, zilebesiran 300 mg lowered office systolic pressure at month 3 by about 5 mmHg versus placebo, which did not meet the prespecified significance threshold.

reason: All three indices (gingivitis, bleeding, plaque) must be significant for the same arm; plaque, or a required win over the active 67% bicarbonate paste, is the least certain, and a result posted without a clear statement on the primary outcomes would also count as not met.
rationale: Colgate single-site 6-month plaque and gingivitis studies against a regular fluoride toothpaste almost always report significant gains for stannous fluoride on gingivitis, bleeding and plaque; with about 40 per arm and tight whole-mouth mean scores, power is high. The risk sits in the rules: three co-primary indices, a possible superiority claim over the bicarbonate paste, and a registry posting with no clear statement. A public result by June 2027 is unlikely: completion is January 2027 and Colgate usually posts about a year later.
evidence: Hu et al. 2019, stabilized stannous fluoride dentifrice 6-month plaque and gingivitis RCT (J Am Dent Assoc)
Jose et al. 2018, 67% sodium bicarbonate toothpaste 6-month gingivitis RCT (J Clin Dent)
Parkinson et al. 2018, 0.454% stannous fluoride dentifrice 24-week gingivitis RCT (Am J Dent)

assumptions.claim: A zinc phosphate-stabilized 0.454% stannous fluoride toothpaste gave significantly lower plaque and gingival index scores than a regular fluoride toothpaste after 3 and 6 months.
assumptions.source: Hu et al. 2019, J Am Dent Assoc 150(4 Suppl):S32-S37

assumptions.claim: A 67% sodium bicarbonate toothpaste significantly reduced Modified Gingival Index and bleeding versus a regular fluoride toothpaste at 24 weeks.
assumptions.source: Jose et al. 2018, J Clin Dent

reason: Adults with epidermolysis bullosa and paired chronic wounds of 10-40 cm2 are scarce in Taiwan, so enrolling 24 in five months with one site listed is unlikely; expect the completion date to slip well past June 2027 and no results posted by the read date.
rationale: Rare disease, narrow lesion criteria (paired, size-matched, 21 days to 9 months old, away from joints), adults only, Taiwan only and one site listed against a five-month window that opened in October 2026: delay is the base case. The sponsor is a small Taiwanese company, so a stop by August 2027 is possible but not likely. The safety primary outcome is simple, so a change in substance is unlikely. Posting results within months of completion would be unusual for a non-US phase 2.

reason: Fifteen patients per arm leave little margin: if placebo withdrawal is milder than expected in pain patients on 50-90 MME, or the rescue adjustment narrows the gap, a real 3-point difference in peak COWS would miss significance.
rationale: Cebranopadol is a potent mu-opioid and NOP agonist with a long half-life; 800 micrograms a day should cover 50-90 MME, so substitution should blunt spontaneous withdrawal much as other full agonists do. Placebo patients are enriched for withdrawal and go 48 hours without opioid, so a peak COWS near 11 is expected against roughly 5-6 on drug. With 15 per arm and SD about 4, power is good only if the difference exceeds about 4 points. Slow Tmax, opioid-type nausea and sweating scored on COWS, and rescue handling are the threats.
evidence: Christoph et al. 2017, cebranopadol phase 2b in chronic low back pain

assumptions.claim: Cebranopadol 400 micrograms once daily met its primary pain endpoint against placebo after bunionectomy in ALLEVIATE-2.
Cebranopadol is an agonist at both the nociceptin (NOP) and mu-opioid receptors, with full agonism at the mu receptor.
assumptions.source: Linz et al. 2014, J Pharmacol Exp Ther

assumptions.claim: In the lofexidine USWM-LX1-3002 trial in opioid-dependent adults, withdrawal scores on placebo peaked within the first two to three days after stopping opioids.
